descriptions.NUR17757: The complex system of structures comprising water sources and water-collecting features, with ingenious channels, and a rectangular building in isodomic masonry.
descriptions.NUR12187:
Megalithic tomb consisting of a burial corridor bounded by two parallel rows of orthostats.

A single large, well-finished quadrangular slab of the roofing remains, resting on the side walls at the far end of the tomb.

For the enhancement and public use of the monument, the surrounding pertinent area has been fenced and linked to the municipal road network by a path bordered by dry-stone walls.
descriptions.NUR12839:
Dolmenic burial with an apsidal corridor.

Located in the territory of the comune of Narbolia (OR)
descriptions.NUR11634: An allée couverte is also present at Chinzana. It is a tomb consisting of a rectangular corridor with a surviving length of 5.20 m and a width of 0.95 m, formed by slabs set on edge, seven of which are still in situ; the covering slabs have disappeared. Around the tomb, on the NW, W and SW sides, some stones of the peristalith emerge.
descriptions.NUR11655: Different tomb nucleus scattered along the islet.
descriptions.NUR21176: The front part has collapsed, while the rear part is fairly well preserved. The rectangular burial corridor is bounded on one side by a slab, while the side walls consist of a series of blocks supporting small stones. The surviving height is about 130 cm. The entire upper surface is covered with a myriad of cupmarks (small cavities with magic-sacred functions).
descriptions.NUR17997: A kind of ceremonial altar of uncertain period. Located in the immediate vicinity of the nuraghe and the homonymous Nuragic village.
descriptions.NUR11890: The whole area between the domus de janas necropolis and the church of Santo Stefano is rich in tafoni rocks adapted into niches and large niches, where it is often difficult to distinguish the action of nature from that of man. In particular, around the church five sites with carved rocks can be identified:
descriptions.NUR12989: Sacred area, probably pre-Nuragic in date. It consists of a stone bench with niches, hollows, and artificial recesses. The summit of the hill is covered by stones fallen from a nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR14262: Stone worked with hammers on the outer surface. Probably a prehistoric altar.
descriptions.NUR17166: Rock bench with stairs and cupolas.
descriptions.NUR10720: The site might relate to a courtyard for animals used in the last centuries; however, an even earlier origin cannot be ruled out.
descriptions.NUR17782: Village, giants' tomb, menhir and remains of a nuraghe in the middle of the agricultural farm
descriptions.NUR16330: The archaeological area includes Nuragic tomb circles at 990 m above sea level, and later structures, among them old cattle enclosures and old sheepfolds called "Pinnetus".
descriptions.NUR13547: A sanctuary area consisting of several rooms surrounded by an irregularly elliptical enclosure. One of these buildings has a perfectly circular plan with a floor paved with limestone slabs fitted together with absolute precision. The accuracy of the construction and the existence of an original design plan are shown by the traces of the circular layout mark of the first course on the floor, drawn with a kind of compass.
descriptions.NUR2072: The Punic settlement arose on the site of an earlier Nuragic village, since the structures brought to light by excavation show the reuse of several structural elements of the indigenous settlement. A megalithic enclosure and a nuraghe that was adapted and incorporated into a wall circuit, which in turn appears to be surrounded by a fortified line, are currently visible.
descriptions.NUR7010: Domus de janas inside the Phoenician-Punic settlement of Pani Loriga, later repurposed.
descriptions.NUR7041: Domus de janas inside the Phoenician-Punic settlement of Pani Loriga, later repurposed.
descriptions.NUR7040: Domus de janas inside the Phoenician-Punic settlement of Pani Loriga, later repurposed.
descriptions.NUR5531: The archaeological area consists of the ruins of a Punic fortress and a complex nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR19529: Archaeological area comprising various remains among which Cart Ruts; menhir; different types of cairns.
descriptions.NUR14933:
It lies within the municipal territory of Donori.

Archaeological features of protohistoric and historic date; the archaeological area is partly damaged, with overlapping cultural phases presumably attributable to the Nuragic, Punic and Roman periods. There is a large quantity of cyclopean boulders entirely of grey granite, indicating the presence of the village and the cemetery.
descriptions.NUR12223: Several remains of circular buildings, terraces and massive megalithic curtain walls are visible, while on the highest point stands a complex-plan structure of granite blocks, in which a quadrangular tower can be seen. The settlement is crossed by the seasonal stream Riu Bidd'e Mores, a tributary of the Riu Gutturu Mannu.
descriptions.NUR19840: Tomb circle built of polyhedral boulders of various sizes. The structure is circular, formed by superimposing one or two rows of polyhedral boulders. The upper part consists of 13 boulders arranged in a circle (diameter about 150 cm), of which: the tallest, placed to the east in the circle, is triangular and stands out from the others; to the south and north of it are two boulders set on edge with their dressed faces visible; seven boulders of various shapes and sizes follow, completing the circle.
descriptions.NUR19842: A tomb circle built by stacking polyhedral boulders of various sizes. The upper part consists of 10 large boulders arranged in a circle about 150 cm in diameter. Some fallen boulders lie at the edges and probably belonged to the original structure. The circle is filled with earth and rubble.
descriptions.NUR19844: A tomb circle built of large, semi-worked slab-like boulders of various shapes, mostly triangular. It differs from the others in the size of the slabs. The circular structure is broken on the north-west side, where presumably three or four boulders are missing. Nine boulders remain in their original position, covering three-quarters of the construction. Some recumbent slabs lie at the edges and very probably originally closed the circle.
descriptions.NUR17839: In this area there are 11 menhirs and a cup-marked stele, most of them in granite. None of them has kept its original position; almost all are broken, probably knocked over by machinery during land improvements.
descriptions.NUR2019: It includes remains of a nuraghe and a village, the entire structure "correctly" transformed into dry stone walls.
descriptions.NUR10791: During excavation it revealed two (perhaps three) sacred wells opening onto a large open paved area, and a hut whose paving has a hole through which flowing water can be seen.
descriptions.NUR16216: The area consists of a enclosure enclosing a megaron temple.
descriptions.NUR1049:
The Punta Unossi complex is one of the most important in the Florinas area.

It consists of an extensive settlement within which a large circular building stands out (external diameter 11 m, internal diameter 7.60 m) displaying typical features of the so-called "meeting huts": a circular bench against the walls and a central circular base on which a tower baetyl originally stood.
descriptions.NUR15175:
At the foot of the hill, a short distance away, lies a lake basin, an important water source for the nearby village.

The banks show clear signs of human regularisation, with blocks and boulders carefully arranged to frame the so-called “Nuragic pond”.
descriptions.NUR10128: This is the original location of the menhirs now at sa Figu. Here they were heaped in disorder, perhaps as a result of land-improvement works, as reported by local herders.
descriptions.NUR21011: A massive single-tower nuraghe, of imposing diameter, built with large, roughly worked granite blocks. The entrance faces south and is three-quarters covered. The tholos is almost intact. Inside there are as many as three niches, cut into the wall thickness. Moreover, a spiral staircase starts from the wall to the left of the entrance corridor and certainly led to the upper floor, but is unfortunately blocked by collapse; opposite the stairwell there is a further niche.
descriptions.NUR6765: Baetyls placed near the Corbos nuraghe, used as posts for a metal gate.
descriptions.NUR6770: Prof. Ercole Contu reported in 1992, about twenty large baetyls lying halfway up the south-east slope of Monte Cachile. I consulted some geologists who partly ruled out a natural geological formation. The site has been known to local people since time immemorial, and a legend is handed down orally that first-time mothers were brought there to give birth.
descriptions.NUR6763: To be brought to a scholar's attention. They appear in random order, and if they ever had one it is not the present one. It is clear that they were put to a use connected with the herdsman's needs.
descriptions.NUR6771: It is a monolith of brown trachyte roughly shaped and poorly finished, about two metres high. It has the form of a pyramidal prism with holes.
descriptions.NUR19827: It has an irregular pyramidal shape with the face oriented to the south-south-east. The boulder retains the natural roughness of the rock from which it was hewn in places, but shows traces of working. The slightly rounded upper part bears signs of working and smoothing.
descriptions.NUR6772: Baetyl with two concavities almost on the "head". Probably for the attachment of lithic horns.
descriptions.NUR6762: Unfortunately, numerous damages—often unconscious—have been caused by human activity aimed at reclaiming a few square metres of pasture.
descriptions.NUR15631: Two nuraghi (no longer existing and/or buried) located in the territory of Ussana and reported by Taramelli (see "Ussana - Scoperte di tombe di età incerta in territorio del Comune, regione di Salomea", in Notizie degli Scavi, 1906, pp. 57-58). The first was probably situated in the centre of the village at Bruncu Sa Turri, more or less corresponding to the old municipal aqueduct (Via Aldo Frau).
descriptions.NUR19860: Hut with enclosure. The structure is built of small- and medium-sized polyhedral boulders, dry-stone bonded and laid in more or less regular courses. It was very probably altered and reused up to the last century.
descriptions.NUR17911: Hut of which only the first level of dentilled ashlar blocks is preserved. Near the same-named giants' tomb and a probable village.
descriptions.NUR21134: Taramelli had already described the hut: "The remains of a circular construction were evident, which after excavation proved to be a Nuragic enclosure about 8 m in diameter … The narrowness of the wall in relation to the size of the interior space does not allow us to say it was a true nuraghe."
descriptions.NUR10922: Nuragic huts along the south-west coast within the municipality of Arbus. Very little remains visible, but it is an important testimony of this civilization.
descriptions.NUR19659: Nuragic hut with the remaining ground-level circular enclosure. Located at the edge of the plateau above the hill, Monte Crastu, it dominated the area of the probable village of Badde Cannalza.
descriptions.NUR19858: Nuragic hut. It is circular, built of flat stones of various sizes laid one on another in courses that corbel inwards towards the centre. The wall is conical: about 150 cm wide at the base and about 70 cm wide at the top, with a surviving height of about 130 cm. To the south-east the wall breaks off for about 100 cm (perhaps the entrance) where the structure has collapsed, probably because of wild olive and mastic trees.
descriptions.NUR9816: A few metres from the two tombs of Sa Perda e s'Altare are the foundations of a circular hut (diam. 10.70 – wall th. 0.50) which, given its dimensions and type of construction, appears to be Nuragic; unfortunately only the basal course remains.
descriptions.NUR10171: The complex, datable between 1600 and 900 BC, comprises a sacred well set inside an irregular courtyard, a 'megaron' temple surrounded by an elliptical enclosure, and a large circular hut with an entrance room and an inner chamber. This was a 'communal' building, the so-called 'meeting hut' typical of Nuragic villages. Pilgrims would usually stop here, perhaps for an audience with the priests.
descriptions.NUR10134: The complex, datable between 1600 and 900 BC, comprises a sacred well set inside an irregular courtyard, a 'megaron' temple surrounded by an elliptical enclosure, and a large circular hut with an entrance room and an inner chamber. This was a 'communal' building, the so-called 'meeting hut' typical of Nuragic villages. Pilgrims would usually stop here, perhaps for an audience with the priests.
descriptions.NUR10173: The complex, datable between 1600 and 900 BC, comprises a sacred well set inside an irregular courtyard, a 'megaron' temple surrounded by an elliptical enclosure, and a large circular hut with an entrance room and an inner chamber. This was a 'communal' building, the so-called 'meeting hut' typical of Nuragic villages. Pilgrims would usually stop here, perhaps for an audience with the priests.
descriptions.NUR12444: Two huts with sacred functions are present. Structure A has a semicircular shape and is considerably larger than structure B.
descriptions.NUR12739: Remains of a nuragic hut near Mount Margherita or the Manu mountains.
descriptions.NUR19642: This is a site where the ruins of two single-tower nuraghi (huts) are found; of both, the base survives to a maximum height of one metre and a diameter of about 6
descriptions.NUR8047: On the Monte Narcao plateau, the remains of some prehistoric huts, built with large stones, still stand. Around the area, fragments of obsidian are frequently found.
descriptions.NUR8048: Neolithic huts of circular form characterised by large stones up to 1.00–1.20 metres high, resting on the rocky stratum.
descriptions.NUR5528: The Carrarzu Iddia nuragic complex stands on a low rise bounded by a curtain wall that encloses a proto-nuraghe and a nuraghe that appears to be of the tholos type; between the two buildings is a small cluster of circular huts, some of them still well preserved. A few dozen metres away is the eponymous dolmen, and a little farther off the nuraghi of Pranu 'e Ruos and Tittiriolos.
descriptions.NUR5023:
In the 1990s it was discovered that the Zapata palace had been built over the well-preserved remains of a Nuragic settlement that the archaeologist Giovanni Lilliu named Nuraxi 'e Cresia.

Thanks to an architectural restoration project of great scenic impact designed by the architect Pietro Reali, both the baronial palace and the underlying nuraghe, duly brought to light, have become the seat of a museum complex, inaugurated on 29 July 2006.
descriptions.NUR19423: Su Stampu de su Turrunu o de su Turnu is a remarkable swallow hole and resurgence, formed by the rio e Spinedda, whose waters pour out in a cascade from a hole in the rock, falling into the centre of a delightful pool.
descriptions.NUR15262: The site is called Su casteddu de Adeva, named after the mountain behind it, Monte Adeva or Is concas de Adeva. It is a single-tower nuraghe with an outer courtyard, bounded by a wall face that joins the tower structure, on the summit of a rocky spur with which the natural rock is partly integrated.
descriptions.NUR19829: To the north-north-west, beside the rocky ridge on which the northern tower of the nuraghe stands, there are two semi-circular natural cavities, about 200 cm deep, closed off by an ellipsoidal enclosure built of polyhedral boulders of various sizes.
descriptions.NUR10027: On 10 July 1205 Maria de Thori, wife of the nobleman Pietro de Maronju and aunt of Comita, judge of Torres, gave the church of S. Maria di Orria piccinna, near Chiaramonti, together with the nearby church of S. Giusta, with servants, houses, woods, lands and animals to the hermitage of Camaldoli, and for it to the prior Martino, granting, among other things, to him and his successors the free election of the rectors of the donated churches and the burial of the monks.
descriptions.NUR4723: It is identified as a megalithic circle because there is a single row of unworked cyclopean ashlars arranged in a circle. Diameter about 11 m. It is currently used as a sheepfold. Two menhirs are reported nearby.
descriptions.NUR10200: It is the uniqueness of the place in seeing so many ceremonial circles that one might believe in a constructive exaggeration without any purpose. It is thought instead that the importance of the place derives precisely from so many ceremonial circles where there was certainly a numerous population.
descriptions.NUR10345: The ceremonial circle of sa Ortija appears almost suddenly in all its majesty. It is oriented to the major northern lunistice. It consists of small and medium-sized polygonal boulders. Vaguely ovoid in shape, its major radius is 33.00 metres. Sacred functions linked to initiation were performed here, and rites and events connected with the seasons and the years of men and women were propitiated.
descriptions.NUR3853: Reduced to a massive ruin. The basal circle of pink trachyte, with vaguely squared boulders, can be made out. Contrary to what has been believed until now, this is not a nuraghe but an important sacred foundry circle of which several forms are evident. One of these, of historical and religious value, consists in its visible part of three steps with a basin. Mu
descriptions.NUR20277: At a point on elevated ground relative to a natural depression, a circle of stones is visible, which could be the base of a partially buried nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR19619: Megalithic circle composed of 16–18 large boulders standing upright on a natural rock base. Five of them lie fallen along the perimeter; three lie fallen inside it. The boulders, covered in mosses and lichens, have irregular shapes and clear signs of working.
descriptions.NUR19621: A smaller circle than the previous one, it is oval in shape and consists of 12 boulders of various sizes, almost all lying flat on the ground. The boulders, covered in moss and lichen, have irregular shapes and clear signs of working.
descriptions.NUR12836: Large megalithic circle a short distance from the Sacred Well Mitza Salamu.
descriptions.NUR20540: Composed of ten parallelepiped-shaped megaliths placed side by side (an eleventh is found in the centre), thus forming a semicircle about 10 metres across. Some pottery fragments found on the site are attributable to the Monte Claro Culture period, therefore the Eneolithic.
descriptions.NUR9222: Megalithic circle located on Monte Ladu. It is situated near a small allée couverte.
descriptions.NUR9271:
The circle, irregular in shape, has been destroyed by agricultural work that has compromised its original form.

The monument consists of about 40 trachyte boulders of various sizes forming an irregular ellipse with a major axis of 17 m and a minor axis of 15 m. Archaeological excavations have brought to light an unspecified number of polished stone axes that have allowed the circle to be dated to the Late Neolithic, placing it within the Ozieri Culture (4th millennium BC).
descriptions.NUR19814: About 350 m from the menhir Sa Perda de s'Omini there is a tomb circle about 150 cm in diameter, formed by boulders of various shapes and sizes arranged in a circle, and by three trachyte slabs set into the ground, one of them, the tallest, with a triangular tip. To the south of this slab the circle breaks off abruptly and resumes after about 50 cm, a gap that was very probably occupied originally by the two trachyte slabs that lie there recumbent.
descriptions.NUR21123: Composed of a pseudo-rectangular trench about 1 m deep, lined with three courses of stones. Closed with a flat band of three slabs of slate, each 25 cm thick. Single burial with Monte Claro ceramics.
descriptions.NUR10886: These are the ruins of a structure built of large blocks, completely buried; only a few remains appear on the surface. Some years ago a farm vehicle removed one of the large surface boulders, revealing an opening through which it was possible to enter the structure. It is, in all probability, a silo for water storage or provisions. The shape is a truncated cone with a bulge at the bottom. Diameter at the base 1.55 m; height 2.73 m.
descriptions.NUR11475:
They lie in the municipality of Fonni (NU).

The site comprises 5 tombs, of which 2 are well preserved. Four tombs are close together while a fifth (in very poor condition) lies about 400 metres to the north-west.
descriptions.NUR6754: There is no direct connection, yet it is identical to the contemporary Mesopotamian temples and embodies the 'orientalising' belief in the union of heaven and earth: sacred areas on hilltops were regarded as the meeting point between humans and the divine. The temple of Monte d'Accoddi, dating back five thousand years, is a ziggurat unique in Europe for the singularity of its architectural types. It was discovered in the mid-20th century by excavating a small hill that appeared 'artificial' in the middle of a plain.
descriptions.NUR5686: It is a proto-nuraghe of the corridor type, located within an area where remains of a larger village are visible.
descriptions.NUR1340:
It lies in the municipality of Montresta (OR).

In the centre of the delimited area, on a rocky outcrop, stands what was long considered a Nuragic construction. It is most probably, instead, a Carthaginian fortress of quadrangular shape, at the base of which traces of masonry that completed the defensive structure are visible.
descriptions.NUR20327: Un censito nuragic area archaeologica, segnalata da Davide Arzu, estesa per tutta la macchia dove non si vedono alberi. Composta da vari nuraghi e capanne.
descriptions.NUR21180: The rock shelter of "Sa Conca Frabica" preserves as many as seven archaeological excavation layers that attest to uninterrupted use from the Middle Neolithic to the Iron Age. The site was used to deposit the dead, alongside whom a funerary assemblage was placed, consisting mainly of ceramic objects but also of bronze and obsidian.
descriptions.NUR21181: Possible Nuragic huts near the spring source
descriptions.NUR5399: A very unusual building, unique in shape. Known as the rectangular nuraghe. It stands on a stratified limestone outcrop shaped like a reproductive organ, around which the stream makes a loop. It may be a temple with buildings serving communal gatherings.
descriptions.NUR4662:
Santa Vittoria is one of the most important cult complexes of Nuragic Sardinia. Covering more than three hectares, it is protected to the south/south-west by a natural cliff and to the north-west by a wall that follows the rocky edge.

The sanctuary has four main groups of buildings: the two temples and the "priest's hut", the "festival enclosure", the "double baetyl" enclosure group, and the east-south-east group
descriptions.NUR11884: Three giants' tombs are present at the site, all built with schist stone.
descriptions.NUR10581: The Piscina Caboni archaeological complex belongs to the Circles Culture of the Arzachena territory, which until a few years ago appeared to be confined to the Gallura region. In the absence of excavation data, the site's occupation can be placed from the 3rd millennium BC.
descriptions.NUR20119: Megalithic astronomical clock, built in the early Nuragic period, before the 15th–18th century BC. It is circular and built of large boulders with open spaces to let sunlight pass onto a central boulder covered with white pebbles that favoured the reflection of the sun's rays at different times — equinoxes, solstices — and in the lunar phases it reflected moonlight in specific directions.
descriptions.NUR2692: Composed of a complex nuraghe and a Nuragic settlement
descriptions.NUR4664: Complex nuraghe, consisting of a central tower and four added towers. The building, datable to 1400–1000 BC, lies on the boundary between the municipalities of Oristano and Villaurbana. Surrounded by scrub and vegetation, it is not easily accessible or visitable.
descriptions.NUR13609: Unfortunately not much remains, but those few surviving ashlars are enough to let us understand this temple. It has circular ritual huts, where benches run all round the inside circumference. Countless parallelepiped ashlars of basalt and trachyte tuff, shaped like a T, cover the whole site; they are perfectly worked and finished. In a sudden flashback this brings me back to other Sardinian sanctuaries.
descriptions.NUR2533: Complex nuraghe consisting of a primitive tower and a bastion, perhaps four-lobed. The entire outline of the central tower survives, although hidden by vegetation and collapse. The structures of two chambers belonging to the central tower survive. A curvilinear curtain wall forms the link between two peripheral towers oriented NNW and ENE. The NNW tower is connected by a curtain wall to another tower oriented WSW, of which much of the outer outline survives.
descriptions.NUR739: The complex contains a sacred well with a paved area, a temple on a rectangular plan, a corridor building, and some stretches of cyclopean walls. The nuraghe Cherchizza stands at the western end, along the edge of the plateau. The site would have served as a landmark for the population of a wide surrounding area. Excavations have yielded bronze artefacts, including a figurine of the mother goddess, as well as amber objects.
descriptions.NUR13598:
The complex consists of a nuraghe with a settlement, a giants' tomb, and a spring.

The nuraghe, built on a rock outcrop, belongs to the complex type: it comprises a main tower to which three secondary towers have been added in a frontal-lateral arrangement.
descriptions.NUR8743:
The Lu Brandali nuraghe is of mixed type, with features of both a corridor nuraghe and tholos nuraghi.

The entrance opens in the north-western part of the latter, its length marked by several watchtowers that make use of rock outcrops.

Outside the curtain wall the village extends; Michele Careddu's 1967 survey recorded 36 huts, mostly circular. Period between the 14th and 10th centuries BC.
descriptions.NUR6200: The Orconale complex has a towered bastion with a courtyard. The main tower has an ogival corridor. All around lie the remains of a large Nuragic settlement with a megaron temple where a model of a nuraghe was found, perhaps belonging to a basin similar to that of Su Monte Sorradile.
descriptions.NUR13080:
The site underwent two main building phases: the first in the Middle Bronze Age and the second in the transition period between the Bronze Age and the Early Iron Age.

The complex consists of a megaron temple, about 17 metres long, surrounded by an enclosure known as a temenos and by other cult and residential buildings, including actual workshops for metal smelting; a complex nuraghe with a trilobate plan lies nearby.
descriptions.NUR3890:
The site underwent two main building phases: the first in the Middle Bronze Age and the second in the transition period between the Bronze Age and the Early Iron Age.

The complex consists of a megaron temple, about 17 metres long, surrounded by an enclosure known as a temenos and by other cult and residential buildings, including actual workshops for metal smelting; a complex nuraghe with a trilobate plan lies nearby.
descriptions.NUR8119: The Romanzesu nuragic complex lies at 750 m above sea level in the locality "Poddi Arvu" (the white poplar), in the cork-oak forest of the Sa Serra granite plateau, in the province of Nuoro. It is a Nuragic village covering more than seven hectares, dating to the Bronze Age, near the source of the Tirso river, and comprises a sacred well, about a hundred huts, two megaron temples, a rectangular temple, a stepped elliptical amphitheatre, and a large labyrinthine structure.
descriptions.NUR13722: Set on a trachyte plateau at 152 m above sea level, from which a vast territory can be controlled, Monte Baranta consists of a pre-Nuragic settlement characterised and protected by a tower-enclosure, a long and massive wall that encloses a group of rectangular huts, separating them from a sacred area with menhirs and a megalithic circle.
descriptions.NUR10069: In total ruin. The oldest villagers remember its existence, even if only a few basal circles remained. When the Sassari–Tempio dual carriageway was built, the earthworks for it affected more than one site, in total disregard for the enormous historical value they represented.
descriptions.NUR9836: It is a marvel to see so many little cups all placed in rows of four by four. And some are grooved with channels for water or something else to flow? Perhaps. And others again are circular and oval in shape with another little cup in the middle to receive the offering made to the god or for reasons of offering to the dead or for the propitiation of the initiation of young men and young women.
descriptions.NUR7136: It is the prehistoric necropolis that gave its name to the first phase of the Early Bronze Age in Sardinia, the so-called Bonnanaro Culture (1800–1600 BC). It consists of seven hypogea, one of which, Domus I, the most important, lies about 600 metres to the north-west (outside this polygon). Two of the above hypogea are more properly burials in rock shelters.
descriptions.NUR7179: It is the prehistoric necropolis that gave its name to the first phase of the Early Bronze Age in Sardinia, the so-called Bonnanaro Culture (1800–1600 BC). It consists of seven hypogea, one of which, Domus I, the most important, lies about 600 metres to the north-west (outside this polygon). Two of the above hypogea are more properly burials in rock shelters.
descriptions.NUR7164: It is the prehistoric necropolis that gave its name to the first phase of the Early Bronze Age in Sardinia, the so-called Bonnanaro Culture (1800–1600 BC). It consists of seven hypogea, one of which, Domus I, the most important, lies about 600 metres to the north-west (outside this polygon). Two of the above hypogea are more properly burials in rock shelters.
descriptions.NUR10232: Clear traces of a hut or circular structure in the area of su Pagliaco. The heavily anthropised zone has several buildings that are, moreover, closely linked in a single complex such as is not found elsewhere in our territory.
descriptions.NUR16436: It could refer to the construction of a giants' tomb or to a nuragic hut associated with the nearby homonymous nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR10295: Rock shelters provided ancient man with a safe refuge for himself and his clan. The cave was divided into small rooms, in particular one for daytime use and, further back against the rock wall, one for the night. These rooms often served as burial places as well. Until the 1950s and 1960s they were inhabited by whole family groups who carried out agro-pastoral activities.
descriptions.NUR10296: Rock shelters provided ancient man with a safe refuge for himself and his clan. The cave was divided into small rooms, in particular one for daytime use and, further back against the rock wall, one for the night. These rooms often served as burial places as well. Until the 1950s and 1960s they were inhabited by whole family groups who carried out agro-pastoral activities.
descriptions.NUR10582:
The Piscina Caboni archaeological complex belongs to the Circles Culture of the Arzachena territory, which until a few years ago seemed to be confined to the Gallura region.

In the absence of excavation data, the site's occupation can be placed from the 3rd millennium BC.
descriptions.NUR6816:
The complex consists of a "cromlech" and other menhirs. In the surrounding area, an underground necropolis attests to the intensive occupation of the territory in prehistory.

The "cromlech" is made of large rounded boulders (trachyte, grey granite and pure white quartz) transported from considerable distances.

The complex is attributable to the Final Neolithic (3200–2800 BC, Ozieri culture) and the Early and Middle Chalcolithic (2800–2400 BC, Filigosa and Abealzu cultures).
descriptions.NUR20098: It is slightly elliptical, with a diameter varying from 20 to 30 m. Some stones no longer stand in line along the perimeter but lie fallen inside or outside the circle; however, most of them are still well aligned with each other and some are still perfectly upright. It is astonishing that, despite thousands of years having passed, the state of preservation is still relatively good.
descriptions.NUR10394: Until halfway through the last century, remains of various nuraghes could be seen, together with many basaltic ashlar of different shapes and sizes.
descriptions.NUR8642:
The archaeological area of Cuccuru Sa Cresia Arta, in the territory of Soleminis, lies on a hillock about 40 metres above the level of the farm track that gives access to it, roughly 250 metres south-west of Soleminis, in the hinterland of the Gulf of Cagliari.

The archaeological excavation, funded by the municipal administration, forms part of a wider programme to enhance the archaeological areas of the municipality of Soleminis, agreed long ago with the Superintendency.
descriptions.NUR7173: Unfortunately, the destructive action of treasure hunters has endangered most of the sites in the municipality of Chiaramonti. The loss of further historical and artistic evidence impoverishes its cultural heritage even more. The legacy left by our ancestors must be part of our history to help us better understand the path to follow for the future.
descriptions.NUR9813:
The dolmen has a circular burial chamber (1.57 x 1.26 x 0.52 m high above the fill) bounded by ten orthostats of various sizes (measurements of two slabs: 0.68 x 0.27 x 0.50 m high – 0.70 x 0.25 x 0.52 m high), while two slabs placed on one side of the entrance, oriented to the north-east, suggest the existence of a short corridor now destroyed.

The capstone is vaguely pentagonal (2.40 x 2.25 m) and has a maximum thickness of 0.55 m tapering to a minimum of 0.48 m.
descriptions.NUR9814: Dolmen II at Arbu, on the other hand, consists of a rectangular corridor (1.84 x 0.78/0.72 m) bounded on the long sides by carefully levelled natural rock and by an orthostat at the end; above it lies the covering slab (1.70 x 1.22 x 0.45 m thick).
descriptions.NUR6877:
The dolmen lies about 250 metres north-west of Nuraghe Arghentu and less than 500 metres south-east of Nuraghe Interenas, on stony ground with abundant shrub vegetation.

The tomb, built partly on a basalt outcrop, now consists of three orthostats that enclose a quadrangular space (1.16 x 1.26 m; height 0.92 m) and support a large covering slab, now slightly tilted to one side.
descriptions.NUR6884:
Small dolmen consisting of two upright slabs supporting a well-shaped covering slab.

The back wall is instead made of two base stones on which small stones rest to close the chamber.

For the enhancement and public use of the monument, the surrounding area belonging to it has been fenced and linked to the municipal road network by a fenced path as well.
descriptions.NUR16988:
Funerary megalithic structure consisting of three vertical stone slabs orthogonal to each other.

It has been interpreted by archaeologists as a dolmen, although like all the other surrounding monuments it requires more thorough scientific investigation.
descriptions.NUR14468: Built of granite as a collective burial and, at the same time, a place of worship, it is a classic example of the megalithic culture that characterised Europe, and the island in particular, during the Copper Age (3rd millennium BC). The dolmen is constructed using the trilithic system (from Greek tri, three, and lithos, stone) – the oldest known architectural scheme – characterised by vertical load-bearing elements that support others laid horizontally.
descriptions.NUR9754:
Partially incorporated into a dry-stone wall, it still preserves only three orthostats in situ (0.35 x 0.22 thick – h. 0.50; 0.80 x 0.30 thick – h. 0.50; 0.60 x 0.15 thick – h. 0.50) and the capstone (1.70 x 1.52 x 0.52/0.40 thick); another orthostat can be made out beneath the wall.

Numerous slabs scattered around the burial on Sunday indicate the existence of a peristalith of which no other trace now remains.
descriptions.NUR20384: Genetically attributable to the Ozieri culture, 3500–2700 BC, it is a simple tomb structure of rectangular shape with the entrance facing east. It has a trapezoidal chamber 2.65 m long and 2.20 m wide. The side walls consist of a stone slab topped by packing material, while the back wall is formed by a single flat quadrangular orthostat that projects beyond the side walls by almost half a metre.
descriptions.NUR6863: Simple dolmen, with a rectangular plan and the entrance facing north-east. The right-hand wall consists of a rectangular slab, the left-hand wall of two roughly worked boulders resting on natural rock. The capstone is flattened on its underside and left natural on the upper surface. DATE: Ozieri Culture (3500–2700 BC).
descriptions.NUR10595: Likely giants' tomb, dolmenic, completely collapsed
descriptions.NUR17885: It is a small, still intact dolmen.
descriptions.NUR6873: The dolmen consists of four surviving orthostatic slabs enclosing a polygonal space (1.86 x 1.40 m) bounded above by a large, fairly roughly dressed slab of varying thickness and with a rounded profile.
descriptions.NUR11748: Small dolmen closed on three sides with a single covering slab.
descriptions.NUR6858: The Prunaiola dolmen is a funerary archaeological monument situated on a small plateau in the territory of Torralba, in north-western Sardinia. It lies a short distance from the Carlo Felice state road 131 and in the immediate vicinity of the Cabu Abbas giants' tomb and two domus de janas, in an area rich in archaeological evidence documenting the continuity of human settlement from prehistory.
descriptions.NUR12388:
It is of tufaceous trachyte (L 5, W 2.50, H 2.70 m), consisting of a rectangular chamber (4.18 x 1.14 m) bounded on the sides by two orthostats, by a front slab with an entrance hatch with rounded corners facing south-east, and by a flat covering slab.

Inside the western lateral orthostat a rectangular niche opens (L 1.22, W 0.88, D 0.50 m). To the left of the monument's front slab there is a small niche, cut into the thickness of the western orthostat.
descriptions.NUR6903: The chamber, roughly circular with a maximum diameter of 1.80 metres on a north–south axis, is enclosed by four orthostatic slabs, though seven can be ideally reconstructed to complete the circuit with the entrance to the south-east. Three of the four surviving slabs support the capstone.
descriptions.NUR12361: Formed by stones driven into the ground that support a slab measuring 3 x 2 m, surrounded by an elliptical stone enclosure. The Elcomis Dolmen appears to have been built about three centuries after Su Laccu, since its orientation (azimuth 161.9; declination –46.75) would also point towards alpha of the constellation Musca, but in 2100 BC.
descriptions.NUR14780: Sa Turricula is recognised as the first phase of the Nuragic civilization. The site includes the nuraghe, the village, and at a short distance, in the territory of the comune of Osilo (locality Funtana 'e Casu), a dolmen.
descriptions.NUR6878: The dolmenic tomb stands on a modest rocky rise, about 200 metres north-west of the giants' tomb of the same name and less than 500 metres south-east of the Nuraghe Cherbos. The burial chamber, of a vaguely quadrangular shape, is bounded by five stones set on edge that appear to rest directly on the outcropping rock. The cover consists of a polygonal slab, now slightly tilted by the fall of an orthostat and with widespread chipping, thinner than the supports.
descriptions.NUR14465: The dolmen is made of a row of squared boulders and roughly worked slabs set upright to form a rectangular chamber about six metres long. Above it, at a height of about 2.20 metres, two more slabs laid flat close the burial chamber; one of them is the second largest of its kind in the whole Mediterranean basin: it measures 4.80 x 3.42 m and is about 45 cm thick.
descriptions.NUR15231: General location in the area of Li Casacci
descriptions.NUR14237: Dolmen composed of a large horizontal slab placed on a dry-stone wall of cyclopean masonry.
descriptions.NUR13073: Dolmen composed of a large covering slab supported by three vertical orthostats
descriptions.NUR6901:
The structure consists of a large horizontal basalt slab resting on seven smaller stones that form a polygonal chamber. Around it is a circle of stones that must have retained the earth forming the covering mound.

The construction of this funerary monument is dated to the third millennium BC.
descriptions.NUR6898: Dolmen located near the homonymous nuraghe
descriptions.NUR11650: Dolmen with a lapidary slab on megalithic walls
descriptions.NUR6905:
Remains of a megalithic tomb which, from what can be seen, appears to be decidedly a dolmen.

Only one orthostat remains in situ (width 1.52 – thickness 0.40 – visible height 1.10), while numerous other slabs lie overturned in the area in front of the exedra. The capstone lies broken in several fragments; the existence of the peristalith can be inferred.
descriptions.NUR7051: Two tombs partially collapsed and eroded beneath a striking natural dolmen
descriptions.NUR6894: The dolmen stands on a basalt outcrop on the northern bank of the Riu Coraggiu, about 200 metres north of the Nuraghe Nela. The burial chamber is now bounded by three orthostats, on which a large covering slab rests.
descriptions.NUR6870:
The dolmen has a burial chamber of a vaguely polygonal shape (1.51 x 1.20 x 0.71 m high) and still preserves six orthostats in their original position, on which the large polygonal covering slab, worked with some care, rests (2.20 x 1.90 x 0.50 m thick).

Around the monument, among numerous overturned stones, three orthostats still in situ can be seen maintaining an alignment parallel to the perimeter of the tomb and forming part of its peristalith.
descriptions.NUR11647: Two small dolmen already described by Taramelli
descriptions.NUR12350: It is located in the municipality of Buddusò. It is situated within an area managed by the Forest Service, known for its scenic landscape.
descriptions.NUR12183: The giants' tomb of S'Ena 'e Sa Vacca is particularly interesting for certain architectural features that in the past led scholars to regard it as a dolmenic structure. The distinctive feature of this burial is the large covering slab, completely unworked, which covers the entire tomb chamber and gives the monument the appearance of an elongated dolmen or "allée couverte".
descriptions.NUR15380: One of the very many dolmens found in Sardinia. Dolmens (from the Breton tol-men, stone table) are funerary monuments erected presumably during the Late Neolithic and Early Chalcolithic (3400–2700 BC).
descriptions.NUR20398: The dolmen is located at Berchiddeddu. The dolmenic chamber has an almost square plan; the covering slab, which is the largest element, measures about 1.60 x 1.20 m. Near the dolmen there is also a menhir, as well as traces of other destroyed structures and fragments of Ozieri Culture pottery.
descriptions.NUR6895: Also known as S'Aspru, it stands on the southern slopes of Monte Bardia, a short distance from the Roccia de Monte Longu, at an altitude of 513 m above sea level, overlooking the broad valley that looks towards the centre of Cala Gonone. It can be reached by a short trek. Rectangular in plan and built of limestone, it consists of four parallelepiped slabs (originally there must have been five) that enclose a large chamber roofed by a pentagonal slab.
descriptions.NUR18818: Prehistoric megalithic funerary structure. Of the monument, the part not concealed by vegetation shows only two vertical slabs at right angles to each other.
descriptions.NUR6893: To reach it, follow the SP 63 from Sindia towards Scano di Montiferro for about 4 km until you see the beautiful single-tower nuraghe Serrese on the right. The dolmen lies 750 metres north of the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR12362: Sos Monimentos is circular in plan, with a chamber measuring 1.80 x 1.00 m, surrounded by a dry-stone wall of granite. At the entrance to the structure two rectangular slabs stand about 0.60 m high. On these slabs rests the roughly circular covering slab, measuring 2.50 x 2.25 m. Its possible astronomical orientation has not yet been recorded.
descriptions.NUR12363: It lacks the covering slab and is covered by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR6855: Dolmen I consists of a large slab resting on stones that originally must have been set on edge to support the roof. Of Dolmen II the ceiling slab and a few wall boulders survive. In the same area about sixty hemispherical hollows are also recorded, clearly artificial and perhaps linked to ancient cult practices connected with the prehistoric monuments just described.
descriptions.NUR12080: It is a dolmen later adapted by shepherds as a sheepfold. It has a trapezoidal plan (3 m in length, 1.80 m in width, 2.20 m in height).
descriptions.NUR6853: Area around which, besides the dolmen Su Crastu Covaccadu, there is also the giants' tomb Sa Pedra Coveccada, of which only the arched stele remains, broken at the base.
descriptions.NUR12024: The elongated ('allée couverte') dolmen of 'Tramassumele' is probably a monument of transition between Neolithic dolmen and the 'giants' tombs of the Bronze Age.
descriptions.NUR7747: Multicellular domus with a dromos probably collapsed. Inside the main chamber there is a pillar with carved capitals.
descriptions.NUR10025: These are Domos belonging to the complex-architecture type. The layout of the rooms cannot be understood because Mother Earth preserves the site almost entirely. Access is possible thanks to the collapse of the vault of one of the chambers. Inside, clear construction details, fittings and petroglyphs can be seen. Mu
descriptions.NUR6989: Initially, probable rock shelters became domus de janas as needed, with the addition of the appropriate modifications. Others remain to be recorded. The surrounding area is rich in fossils and limestone formations. Photo Mario Unali
descriptions.NUR7367: They are on the left bank of the Rio Oloitti. They develop in an L-shape, numbering three chambers with an antechamber. The photograph showing the King's throne "sa trona de su Re" is not far away and arouses curiosity for its shape, which ergonomically suits the substantial backside of a commander.mu
descriptions.NUR7426: It is also known by the place name of the adjacent land, "sas Damas", which I believe is the older and more appropriate one, since it is closely linked with sa Domos de sas Fadas which by extension becomes Dama = lady. It was found by chance during extension work on a house, now the Agriturismo Sas Damas Doneddu-Murgia, and was rich in grave goods that were donated to the local museum in Perfugas SS.
descriptions.NUR10256: A jewel among the jewels in the archaeological treasure chest of our municipality of Chiaramonti. It is a Domus that the womb of Mother Earth still preserves intact. Only the antechamber is visible, rich in petroglyphs of rare beauty. mu
descriptions.NUR10257: Interesting reading of the representations contained. It is still intact in the womb of Mother Earth. mu
descriptions.NUR7049: Domus de janas with clear signs of its reuse in the 20th century.
descriptions.NUR7269: The entrance is severely collapsed, blocking access to the domus, which is arranged in various rooms surrounding a central chamber.
descriptions.NUR7262: This domus de janas takes its name from the bas-relief carving of a ram's protome on one of the interior walls. The other distinctive feature is the dolmenic corridor in front of the entrance.
descriptions.NUR7502: It is a domus de janas necropolis overlooking the Gulf of Carbonara at the locality Spiaggia del Riso. Of the whole necropolis only one tomb has remained intact: it is a truly fascinating monument that projects the territory back in time by about six thousand years.
descriptions.NUR7313: The necropolis, situated along the southern slopes of Monte Corona 'e Teula, consists of 11 domus de janas distinguished by the complexity of their ground plans and decorative schemes. Only one of them is single-chambered, while the others are composed of several cells arranged in an increasingly complex layout.
descriptions.NUR7408: The necropolis, situated along the southern slopes of Monte Corona 'e Teula, consists of 11 domus de janas distinguished by the complexity of their ground plans and decorative schemes. Only one of them is single-chambered, while the others are composed of several cells arranged in an increasingly complex layout.
descriptions.NUR7344: Single-cell domus de janas especially eroded
descriptions.NUR7722: The domus de janas at Bonorchis is a single-chamber tomb, very small, with a wide and well-crafted entrance portal.
descriptions.NUR7490: The domus de janas of Bruncu s'Allegau or Sa Domu 'e s'Orku was probably cut from an original natural cavity later adapted for funerary purposes. It consists of a single chamber extending horizontally with an irregular elliptical plan, 2.65 m long, 3.9 m wide and 1.5 m high from the present floor level; the ceiling still shows the small parallel grooves and hollows left by the prehistoric stonecutters.
descriptions.NUR7584: Group of domus de janas situated on the calcareous escarpment overlooking the Bunari valley (Abealzu culture)
descriptions.NUR7079: At certain times of the year, due to high water levels in the reservoir, it becomes inaccessible.
descriptions.NUR7057: This underground tomb, cut from a block of erratic rock, is located about 300 m from the village's sports field. Nearby, other rock blocks with cups can be observed.
descriptions.NUR7076: Single-cell domus de janas on a calcareous massif
descriptions.NUR7067: Single-cell domus de janas on a calcareous massif
descriptions.NUR7093: Single-cell domus de janas on a calcareous massif
descriptions.NUR7297:
The underground chamber is cut into a schist rock, and on the side opposite the entrance—i.e., the northern side—there is a clear indication of a previous excavation, likely from another underground chamber. Access to the domus de janas is via a door with a drainage groove cut into the threshold:

the door is characterized by the presence of a frame surmounted by a lintel, formed by carving the rock, to highlight this architectural element.
descriptions.NUR7626: The necropolis consists of 33 hypogea of the domus de janas type cut into the tuff and divided into two groups. The site, datable to the Neolithic, was used by the peoples of the Ozieri, Abealzu-Filigosa, Monte Claro, Beaker and Bonnanaro cultures, and also by the Nuragic people of Iloi in the Middle Bronze Age, with re-use in the medieval period.
descriptions.NUR7743: The necropolis consists of 33 hypogea of the domus de janas type cut into the tuff and divided into two groups. The site, datable to the Neolithic, was used by the peoples of the Ozieri, Abealzu-Filigosa, Monte Claro, Beaker and Bonnanaro cultures, and also by the Nuragic people of Iloi in the Middle Bronze Age, with re-use in the medieval period.

descriptions.NUR7648: The hypogeum is cut into an isolated basalt boulder. The doorway opens at some height above ground level and is surmounted by two deep grooves cut horizontally and parallel in the rock. The doorway still shows a clear rebate for the closing slab. A narrow groove cut into the thickness of the doorway outlines all four sides. The oval chamber is of the oven type. The tomb was explored in 1927 by A. Taramelli, who found it already violated and emptied long before.
descriptions.NUR7466:
The funerary site, datable to the 3rd millennium BC and used until the early centuries of the 2nd millennium BC, consists of thirteen domus de janas. The finds recovered are attributable to the Ozieri, Abealzu-Filigosa, Monte Claro, Beaker and Bonnanaro cultures and are now largely preserved in the Villa Sulcis Museum in Carbonia.

A single-tower nuraghe stands on the summit of the hill on which the necropolis is situated.
descriptions.NUR4347:
The funerary site, datable to the 3rd millennium BC and used until the early centuries of the 2nd millennium BC, consists of thirteen domus de janas. The finds recovered are attributable to the Ozieri, Abealzu-Filigosa, Monte Claro, Beaker and Bonnanaro cultures and are now largely preserved in the Villa Sulcis Museum in Carbonia.

A single-tower nuraghe stands on the summit of the hill on which the necropolis is situated.
descriptions.NUR7096: Group of three pruricellular domus de janas
descriptions.NUR7208: Group of three pruricellular domus de janas
descriptions.NUR7085: Group of three pruricellular domus de janas
descriptions.NUR7613: Cemetery composed of three nuclei, one of which contains a tomb decorated internally with a carved spiral.
descriptions.NUR7267: Cemetery composed of three nuclei, one of which contains a tomb decorated internally with a carved spiral.
descriptions.NUR7424: Cemetery composed of three nuclei, one of which contains a tomb decorated internally with a carved spiral.
descriptions.NUR7783: Group of three domus de janas of particular interest. Featuring a carved doorway in the basalt rock and a rectangular exedra situated below ground level.
descriptions.NUR7310: The hypogeum lies at the southern edge of a small plateau, characterised by dense woodland. The burial is cut into a block of heavily fractured granite, so that part of the antechamber has completely broken away and now lies right next to the entrance. The entrance to the cell is about 0.70 m above ground level; it has jambs and a lintel carved in relief, with carefully finished surfaces.
descriptions.NUR7266: It is a single cell cut inside a prominence of friable limestone. In the immediate vicinity considerable working is evident from the presence of other outcrops that were abandoned or on which the work was never finished.
descriptions.NUR7080: In a private plot. There are decorations in the form of probable bull's-head protomes.
descriptions.NUR7107: In a private plot. There are decorations in the form of probable bull's-head protomes.
descriptions.NUR7083:
It is a small artificial cave cut into a single rounded block of limestone. The oven-mouthed entrance faces south-east and leads into a longitudinally developed space, divided into several chambers, which must have formed the rooms of a hypogeal burial.

The tomb shows no decorative motifs and has yielded no grave goods. It is dated to the Late Neolithic and demonstrates the occupation of the territory from the pre-Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR7518: 2 domus de janas with architectural façade, typical funerary architecture very present in Sassari.
descriptions.NUR7392: Domus de janas located on the hill facing the Ortali 'e su Monte complex, beneath a smaller nuraghe similarly named.
descriptions.NUR12346:
Multi-chambered tomb with a centripetal layout. It was emptied long ago. It yielded material of the Ozieri culture (3200–2500 BC) and of the early medieval period (7th century AD). The former are kept in the "G. A. Sanna" Archaeological Museum in Sassari; the latter in the Nuoro Civic Museum.

Inside the domus de janas, cut into a rock outcrop, access is through a hexagonal doorway; all around the antechamber, with its perfectly worked ceiling, five cells open where the dead were laid.
descriptions.NUR7451: It is a tomb with an architectural façade, greatly modified and reused in medieval and modern times, blending the features of domus de janas and giants' tombs.
descriptions.NUR7658:
The necropolis comprises 18 domus de janas, all multi-chambered with up to 12 rooms, richly adorned with pilasters, panels, false doors, bull's-head protomes, chevrons and other spiral or wolf's-tooth motifs.

Seven tombs reproduce pre-Nuragic dwellings: single- or double-pitched roofs, horizontal or sloping, with or without central beams and side rafters, supported or not by pillars, all carved in the rock. One has an architectural façade with a carved arched stele.
descriptions.NUR7640:
The necropolis of Sos Laccheddos is an archaeological site in the territory of Sassari, in north-western Sardinia. It is divided into two groups of tombs lying a short distance from each other, located between state road 127 bis and the new provincial road to Anglona a few kilometres east of the town, in the direction of Osilo.

To the 32 tombs recorded in the aforementioned work, another 19 were added following more recent investigations.

It is divided into two groups of tombs lying a short distance from each other, located between state road 127 bis and the new provincial road to Anglona a few kilometres east of the town, in the direction of Osilo.

To the 32 tombs recorded in the aforementioned work, another 19 were added following more recent investigations.

descriptions.NUR7299:
It is cut into an erratic limestone boulder, worked on the outside as well, roughly trapezoidal in shape. On the main façade, which has an entrance, an arched stele almost 4 metres high was carved, on top of which three small baetyls were originally placed. On the rear façade another small entrance can be seen, perhaps from an earlier period.

The material culture found during the excavations is of the Bonnanaro type (Early Bronze Age).
descriptions.NUR7322:
There are two hypogea at the site: the first tomb is the more interesting because it shows a series of incisions above the entrance hatch; the second lies a little further on, near the edge of the road, and its interior is almost completely flooded.

Both burials are pit graves and would date to about 3000 BC.
descriptions.NUR7324:
There are two hypogea at the site: the first tomb is the more interesting because it shows a series of incisions above the entrance hatch; the second lies a little further on, near the edge of the road, and its interior is almost completely flooded.

descriptions.NUR7545: Situated on the slopes of the Còrongiu Sènes hill. It has a longitudinal layout. Chambers built in progressive heightening from the entrance inwards, consisting of an antechamber and two cells with entrances almost perfectly aligned. The domus is entered through an elliptical opening. The first cell has a sub-rectangular plan, where traces of working consisting of slight vertical grooves are evident. The second cell is sub-elliptical in shape with traces of working.
descriptions.NUR7286: The tomb is cut into a bank of granitic rock; it consists of a dromos and a chamber in which a small niche has been carved. The hypogeum opens on a gentle slope a few centimetres above ground level.
descriptions.NUR7549:
The “Domus de Janas” is cut into a modest, irregularly rounded granite outcrop that barely rises above the surrounding plain.

The plan is reduced to a single cell of modest size; the entrance, which opens to the south, is preceded by a short dromos cut into the rock face, characterised by a sub-trapezoidal plan and bounded laterally by vertical walls that decrease in height from north to south.
descriptions.NUR7092: Single-cell domus de janas built within a "trovante"
descriptions.NUR7376: "Domus de gianas of Gianna Oria Porru or Solottos; a short distance from the bed of Rio Mannu or Rio Posada, on the opposite bank from Nuraghe Eritta (no. 5). Two small chambers cut into the limestone, each with a low doorway with a raised border. Empty. In the land of Antioco Sanna" (Taramelli, 1933).
descriptions.NUR7210: Both burials have their entrances oriented to the south-west. Inside the first domus, about 5 x 3 m, the remains of two columns that once adorned the chamber are still visible in both the ceiling and the floor. The second tomb, similar to the first, has an antechamber with two raised steps on either side, and the rectangular burial chamber contains two raised lateral benches.
descriptions.NUR7212: Both burials have their entrances oriented to the south-west. descriptions.NUR7207: "Domus de giana of Su Adu 'e Sa iana, a short distance from the village, at the ford of Rio Minori, was in the past a hypogean cell, which disappeared many years ago, but the village elders still remember it. On land belonging to Pasqua Sanna, daughter of Isidoro"
descriptions.NUR7060: Single-cell domus de janas partially collapsed
descriptions.NUR7214: The domus has an ESE-facing entrance and a cruciform ground plan. The tomb structure consists of a trapezoidal doorway leading into a sub-rectangular antechamber and then into a rectangular main chamber, on three sides of which are three raised parietal niches. The niches are oriented SSW, NNW and NNE. Originally they were decorated with small pilasters set in the centre of each niche.
descriptions.NUR7573: In the broad and complex picture of the island's hypogean architecture, the majestic necropolises of Mesu 'e Montes, S'Adde 'e Asile, S'Isterridolzu, Noeddale, Su Littu, and the Tomb of Littos Longos have provided extremely significant data for understanding the phenomenon of hypogeism. The entrance is characterised by a long dromos cut into the limestone. Inside, bull's-head protomes and other carved decorations.
descriptions.NUR7152:
They are located in the territory of the comune of Busachi (OR).

At least 4 domus de janas are visible.

The necropolis should include at least  8 domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR7461:
It is an architectural-façade tomb, that is, a hypogeal tomb that reproduces in rock the external façade of a Nuragic giants' tomb, with an arched stele and an exedra.

In the early medieval period it was reused as a rock-cut chapel (its dedication is unknown).
descriptions.NUR7551:
It consists of a series of chambers opening onto the western flank of a low limestone hill. The main nucleus, the result of various transformations relating to different phases of use over the centuries, comprises three large cells linked together and arranged in succession from north to south.

The chambers look out onto a narrow terrace; the rock face has two narrow flights of steps by which the plateau above can be reached.

descriptions.NUR7248: A short distance from the town of Sassari, the domus of Oredda reveals its decorative beauties only to those who go in search of the mystery that characterises the domus de janas. We went in pursuit of this jana in a field, from which you would expect anything except to find a ditch, and then to go inside and hold your breath at the art concentrated within it.

descriptions.NUR7588: The complex, datable between the Late Neolithic (Ozieri culture, 3200–2800 BC) and the Chalcolithic, stands on a broad outcrop of tuff and consists of 26 domus de janas. The domus de janas are arranged on the ridge at different levels and are multi-chambered, i.e. composed of several rooms; most have a dromos entrance (a corridor cut into the rock) while only a few have direct access.

descriptions.NUR7618: The entrance was later modified by the construction of a wall to form a kind of shelter for domestic animals.
descriptions.NUR7088: Domus de janas with a sacred well placed at the entrance to the park on the south side
descriptions.NUR7359: The Pranu Narbonis cemetery consists of a group of three domus still in excellent conservation, dug out from a single large granite block emerging from the ground.
descriptions.NUR7383: Leaving the village of Irgoli towards Onifai/Orosei, just before a small bridge, turn onto the road for Capo Comino. After only 300 m, at the junction for the bypass, a municipal asphalt road begins on the right. Follow this road for about 5 km until you see two prominent granite pillars on the left. Walk on until you reach the Domus de Janas Sa Conca 'e mortu.
descriptions.NUR7375:
The necropolis, situated on the southern slopes of Monte Corona 'e Teula, consists of 11 domus de janas distinguished by the complexity of their ground plans and their decorative schemes.

The Tomb of the Hourglasses, on the other hand, comprises 10 chambers; the walls display geometric motifs in relief.
descriptions.NUR7510: The necropolis consists of eleven domus de janas, both single- and multi-chambered. The largest originally had five chambers, now a single space after the partition walls were demolished. It is distinguished by two distinct phases of use: the first in the Neolithic and the second in the Middle Bronze Age (1700–1300 BC), when at least three hypogea were converted into "domus a prospetto architettonico".

descriptions.NUR7492: It is located in the territory of the comune of San Vito (CA), inside the church of the same name.
descriptions.NUR7530: The domus de janas, existing in the immediate vicinity of the nuraghe, marks the continuity of human occupation of the site over the millennia.
descriptions.NUR7528: Single-cell domus de janas carved out of granite
descriptions.NUR7099:
Three hypogeic tombs on the slope of a small rise (244 m). The first has a single elliptical oven-shaped cell. The second consists of an atrium, an antechamber and a quadrangular burial chamber with a niche on the right-hand wall. On the left a wider raised cell with two small niches and a relief decoration depicting two human faces.

The third tomb, further downhill than the other two, is of the more regular type with atrium, antechamber and cell.
descriptions.NUR7181: The antechamber is quadrangular; the walls are concave while the ceiling and floor are flat, and the height of the chamber is almost the same as that of the doorway. In the back wall is the doorway leading to the main chamber, which is sub-quadrangular in shape and set irregularly in the wall. The main chamber is sub-ellipsoidal (1.80 x 1.24 m); the walls are concave and the ceiling is flat.
descriptions.NUR7396: Single-cell domus de janas located near Riu fruscu
descriptions.NUR7505: The archaeological site, dating to about 3500 BC, lies near the provincial road and consists of three tombs. The first, isolated, was cut into a rock outcrop that rises behind a small building; the other two, close together, are instead situated further south in a granite monolith that runs alongside the road. All three domus de janas are of simple type without an antechamber and have a rebate in the entrance doorway.
descriptions.NUR7366: The archaeological site, dating to about 3500 BC, lies near the provincial road and consists of three tombs. descriptions.NUR7582: The stone of Sant Eliseo is a large erratic boulder on the lower slopes of Monte Santu, in the territory of Mores. Used in various periods, it was first a Prehistoric Tomb of the Neolithic, then adapted by the Romans, and finally became a Byzantine church dedicated to Sant Eliseo. The domus has a ground floor and a first floor, reminiscent of the houses of the fairies (in Sardinian, precisely, Domus De Janas).
descriptions.NUR7245: Domus de janas with superimpositions on the stele
descriptions.NUR7407: Small domus de janas with two cells
descriptions.NUR7729: The Tracucu Necropolis is a beautiful and extensive archaeological site about three kilometres from Lotzorai, along the road to Talana. It consists of thirteen domus de janas, marked by wooden signs, which can be admired by following a guided path through the granite rocks and dense vegetation.

descriptions.NUR7524: The cemetery includes seven very unusual and strikingly beautiful domus de janas, dug into erratic stones, and one in particular, with natural cup-like formations adjacent to the doorway.
descriptions.NUR7260: The cemetery includes seven very unusual and strikingly beautiful domus de janas, dug into erratic stones, and one in particular, with natural cup-like formations adjacent to the doorway.
descriptions.NUR7277: The cemetery includes seven very unusual and strikingly beautiful domus de janas, dug into erratic stones, and one in particular, with natural cup-like formations adjacent to the doorway.
descriptions.NUR20341: A small isolated domus de janas, particularly notable for the presence of a rock-cut terraced basin (ancient vats for pressing grapes to extract wine) carved into the rock.
descriptions.NUR7314: Dug into a calcareous rock outcrop stained pink by iron veins. Single-chamber tomb.
descriptions.NUR7425: The Luzzanas domus de janas lie near the river and can only be entered from above through a shaft entrance. Once you have gone down you find yourself in a chamber with two hatches leading to two tombs, one of which consists of an antechamber plus three cells, only two of which are accessible. In this domus there is a very unusual carving depicting a labyrinth, but it may have been made in the Roman period.
descriptions.NUR21144: Neolithic burial composed of two chambers connected by a door, which has, above it, a probable bull's-head protome.
descriptions.NUR7111: The domus de janas of Scala Coperta lies a few hundred metres from the Roccia dell'Elefante, in the locality of Pedra Sciolta. Cut into an erratic trachyte boulder, it consists of an antechamber and four small cells arranged in a cross. On the outside, on top of the boulder, there are three holes for housing small baetyls; a fourth hole is set slightly further back than the others and is now barely visible because of the vegetation.
descriptions.NUR7095: There are about ten tombs of various forms, from the simplest single-chambered ones with an antechamber and a single cell, to those with a circular plan with several loculi, a hearth, and small pillars separating the cells. They are cut into the soft tuff rock. Threatened by clandestine archaeological excavations,
descriptions.NUR7304:
The domu is partially collapsed, but the incised and low-relief decorations (with the double-horn motif) that adorn the walls are still appreciable. Traces of red paint are also present.

A few metres to the right another partially buried domus, equally dilapidated.
descriptions.NUR7188: Group of two single-cell domus de janas with façade.
descriptions.NUR7205: Group of two single-cell domus de janas with façade.
descriptions.NUR7239:
The domus is cut into a limestone face that is almost sheer above the valley below. It has a façade 2.60 m high depicting a simple stele. On the stele are the three typical recesses.

Like most architectural-façade domus created from scratch, it has a single chamber; this has a semi-elliptical plan. Inside, on the left, a wide niche opens whose function is unclear but which was presumably used for depositing votive objects.
descriptions.NUR7428: Single-cell domus de janas with a façade
descriptions.NUR7385: Single-cell domus de janas with a façade
descriptions.NUR7362: Single-cell domus de janas with a façade
descriptions.NUR9114: A small domus de janas about a hundred metres from the Nuraghe Orgurù. Nine have been recorded in the area. This small domus is cut into a natural boulder and is not immediately visible because the view is initially blocked by other rocks.
descriptions.NUR12424: Domus carved out of granite. Composed of an access corridor and a central chamber opening into a small cell.
descriptions.NUR12423: Small domus whose entrance was once walled up for use as a sheepfold.
descriptions.NUR20076: Domus de janas to be verified, unnamed
descriptions.NUR11883: Domus de janas on the junction of SS125
descriptions.NUR7728:
Single-tower nuraghe built of sandstone boulders. The main chamber has three asymmetrical niches.

From the corridor, a staircase with 15 steps starts on the right. Maximum height of the tower 9.15 m.

Nearby are the remains of the settlement and two domus de janas.
