descriptions.NUR6956: Abandoned mine located in the municipality of Padria. (possibly a domus de janas)
descriptions.NUR7221: The imposing hypogeum of Sas Puntas, cut into a low limestone bench a short distance from the settlement, reproduces a giants' tomb in full, both in its exedra façade and inside, with an elliptical burial chamber. The tomb belongs to the category of tombs with an architectural façade, also known as "Nuragic domus", that is, hypogeal burials cut into the rock, often by reusing pre-existing Neolithic domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR6931: A natural cavity adapted as a domus de janas that hosted the games of several generations of children from the village of Uri, now left to itself as times have changed. It is entered from above by a fairly dangerous "manoeuvre", about 6/7 metres above the ground.
descriptions.NUR14312: It lies in the municipality of Putifigari (SS). A hypogeal tomb (domus de janas) with a deeply buried entrance, about two metres below the level of the road and the surrounding ground. It consists of a main pillared cell and three smaller lateral cells. The double-pitched roof is still remarkable.
descriptions.NUR17350: It is a domus excavated at the base of a trachytic rock outcrop.
descriptions.NUR19963: Domus de janas reported via the Nurnet page by an anonymous contributor. From the photos it appears to be a two-cell tomb, used by the landowner for storing livestock.
descriptions.NUR6933: Two multi-chambered domus de janas are cut into the limestone ridge that bounds the Baddenare plateau. Both have an antechamber, a main chamber and two side cells. One is entered through a long dromos, the other through a raised doorway above ground level. The domus with the dromos entrance preserves two fine columns in the main chamber and an incised inscription (L M S), probably Roman or medieval in date.
descriptions.NUR20258: Domus de janas reported to the Nurnet editorial office. From the video it appears to be a rocky massif where a larger necropolis may be present.
descriptions.NUR8695: Group of domus de janas immediately beneath the road embankment. It is suspected that other domus de janas may lie beneath or have been destroyed by the works for road construction.
descriptions.NUR7006:
The rock face of this hypogeum has the peculiarity of bearing, above the doorway, a bull sign consisting of a line (1.14 m) incised with its ends turned upwards (height 0.18 m).

It is a representation of the bull deity drawn in an extremely elementary and rough manner, which is nevertheless of considerable interest because it is the only known example in the area. Chamber measurements: depth 1.24 m; width 1/1.18 m; height 0.70/0.94 m.
descriptions.NUR9758: Short antechamber (depth 0.45 – width 0.77) leading to the door (height 0.48 – thickness 0.18 – width 0.40). The chamber measures: depth 0.98 – width 1.16/0.90 – height 0.44/0.80.
descriptions.NUR14943: Domus de janas with a chamber having a collapsed ceiling.
descriptions.NUR7483: A rectangular niche cut into the sedimentary rock, set against a quadrangular space bounded by four large upright stones with dry-stone walls. In the lowest Bell Beaker levels three cist structures were identified, sealed by limestone slabs and containing human skeletal remains attributable to several individuals. Above these lay further deceased individuals accompanied by grave goods such as objects in ceramic, metal, stone, bone and a gold necklace.
descriptions.NUR14663: Domus de janas located inside a granite quarry. Pruricellulare with an internal double pillar.
descriptions.NUR14144: Located on the southern edge of the Corraile plateau (480 m a.s.l.), (Ozieri Culture). The eight tombs that make it up, together with a small natural cave, share architectural features similar to those of the main necropolises in the area. Some tombs stand out for their monumentality and for the presence of symbolic elements closely linked to the cult.
descriptions.NUR7202: An area with a small single-tower nuraghe around which there is a small necropolis of four domus de janas, in which there are decorations of carved bull's-head protomes.
descriptions.NUR12074: Small underground chamber in an isolated stone.
descriptions.NUR7998: It is a domus de janas, a burial of the "double oven" type, attributable to a period spanning from the third to the second millennium BCE.
descriptions.NUR6957: It consists of four domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR7649: This domus de janas is single-chambered with a pseudo-quadrangular room and curvilinear walls. The domus de janas lies against the perimeter wall of the cemetery with its opening facing that wall. The nature of some apparent "reliefs" on the ceiling should be investigated further. A second tomb is present next to it.
descriptions.NUR7279: It is a pair of hypogea: a two-cell domus and a three-cell domus.
descriptions.NUR7124: Domus de janas with architectural façade, interesting the graffiti.
descriptions.NUR7003: Visible from the road, they are domus with modified entrances set slightly above the countryside level and located within the sheepfold.
descriptions.NUR7717: These are four tombs at Chighizzu, above the tunnels along the SS 131, Sardinia's main highway. The steep slopes and the void beneath are truly dizzying, and those who excavated these domus de janas were undoubtedly very brave.
descriptions.NUR7791: These are four tombs at Chighizzu, above the tunnels along the SS 131, Sardinia's main highway. The steep slopes and the void beneath are truly dizzying, and those who excavated these domus de janas were undoubtedly very brave.
descriptions.NUR7748: These are four tombs at Chighizzu, above the tunnels along the SS 131, Sardinia's main highway. The steep slopes and the void beneath are truly dizzying, and those who excavated these domus de janas were undoubtedly very brave.
descriptions.NUR7139:
It is a two-chambered domus de janas, oriented south-east, with a largely broken-in ceiling (opening 1.06 x 0.86 m) and lacking the partition that separated the two chambers, demolished in recent times to create a single, more spacious room.

The hypogeum is entered through a quadrangular hatch (height 0.44 m – width 0.50 m – thickness 0.22 m) finely shaped and fitted with a triple frame for the cover slab.
descriptions.NUR7404: The necropolis consists of two multi-chambered domus de janas cut into the limestone, plus a third one that was started (only the dromos was cut) and never finished. One of the two tombs opens in the rock face near the cemetery, while the second, together with the unfinished tomb, opens on the edge of the plateau to the south-east.
descriptions.NUR7074: They lie on a slight rise at 184 m. The four rock-cut chambers are hewn in sandstone and each consists of a single elliptical cell with a vaulted roof. The many artificial cuttings, clearly visible in the rock face that flanks the domus de janas on the right-hand side for a stretch of 12 m, are clear signs of ancient quarrying that has largely destroyed the original layout of the site.
descriptions.NUR9755: It is a domus de janas cut into a flat rock outcrop and consists of two roughly circular chambers – on the same axis and opening to the south-east – separated by a partition with a hatch; the walls are carefully finished while the ceiling is slightly hemispherical.
descriptions.NUR12073: Single-chambered, carved out of a granite monolith.
descriptions.NUR14659: Domus de janas submerged by the Omodeo flood. It preserves a unique bull's-head protome in high relief.
descriptions.NUR7027:
It consists of 18 domus de janas arranged in three groups about 200 m apart. The first group has five hypogea aligned on an east–west axis; the second group, south of the first cluster, has three aligned on a north–south axis; the third group, 250 m to the east, comprises ten small rock-cut chambers that are difficult to reach and interpret.

The burials are of the horizontal-projection type with entrances between east and south. A system of channels cut into the rock protected the tomb interiors.
descriptions.NUR7048:
It consists of 18 domus de janas arranged in three groups about 200 m apart. The first group has five hypogea aligned on an east–west axis; the second group, south of the first cluster, has three aligned on a north–south axis; the third group, 250 m to the east, comprises ten small rock-cut chambers that are difficult to reach and interpret.

The burials are of the horizontal-projection type with entrances between east and south. A system of channels cut into the rock protected the tomb interiors.
descriptions.NUR7039:
It consists of 18 domus de janas arranged in three groups about 200 m apart. The first group has five hypogea aligned on an east–west axis; the second group, south of the first cluster, has three aligned on a north–south axis; the third group, 250 m to the east, comprises ten small rock-cut chambers that are difficult to reach and interpret.

The burials are of the horizontal-projection type with entrances between east and south. A system of channels cut into the rock protected the tomb interiors.
descriptions.NUR15235: It is one of the various domus de janas located in the municipality of Alghero. Inside there is a carved hearth in the stone foundation.
descriptions.NUR7435:
The necropolis comprises 11 domus de janas, generally multi-chambered, some of which are characterised by architectural decorations in relief.

The most interesting burial consists of 11 chambers arranged in an irregular layout.
descriptions.NUR7257: On the external wall there is a domus; another one has been carved inside the cave, about 3 m from the entrance on the left side.
descriptions.NUR17859: Two other domus de janas are visible in the vicinity.
descriptions.NUR7042: It consists of three domus de janas partially eroded and in very poor condition.
descriptions.NUR7421:
The massive excavation work, the architecture of this monumental hypogeum, dates to the period of the first spread of metals on the island. In this "domus de janas" one sees the result of an evolution and it denotes the consequences of the formation of powerful family nuclei under tribal chiefs, capable of imposing a greater volume of work on their dependants.

The cells opened at a considerable height above the flat rock floor, inaccessible without a ladder.
descriptions.NUR7026:
On the hill of San Giovanni a Punic fortified complex has been identified on the remains of a pre-existing Nuragic village.

Opposite are the Domus de Janas of Burdaga.

In Giuseppa Tanda's recent publication it is stated that, among the various types of Domus de Janas, there is one characterised by the fact that the necropolis is carved into pre-existing rock shelters, perhaps enlarged by artificial excavation, almost as if the overhang could provide shelter for the sacred remains of the dead.
descriptions.NUR20352: Located inside a private property, among the very numerous domus de janas of the Ozieri area, they are the largest in the territory and beyond; they are also the only ones that display symbols of the bull god carved in such a clear manner.
descriptions.NUR7134: Eight domus de janas scattered along the period indicated on the map and a few taphouses.
descriptions.NUR15783: The domus, multicellular, is in a precarious state of conservation and consists of a antechamber and four cells.
descriptions.NUR6990: The domus de janas necropolis is cut into a basalt outcrop overlooking the Riu Mannu valley, along the provincial road from Suni to Pozzomaggiore, in the Planargia region of north-western Sardinia. The hypogean complex comprises 12 single-chamber and multi-chamber burials, almost all accessed through a vestibule.
descriptions.NUR7086: The two domus, between which a large tree stands, are located about 1 km from the village of Goni and are carved into a rocky formation situated about 4 metres above the walking surface.
descriptions.NUR6959: “Sa Pedraia” consists of five hypogea set close together on a short rock face. One of them has an antechamber with a sloping roof and grooves showing the run of the beams. In the same chamber two bull’s-head protomes have been carved naturalistically to show that the fertility god would guarantee rebirth in the new life. The adjacent domus on the left has a cell with a central pillar and a raised lying-in floor.
descriptions.NUR7380: It is located in the municipality of Florinas and is composed of three hypogea.
descriptions.NUR6951: Subterranean burial with 10 domus de janas. A site worthy of in-depth study, containing 10 convex chambers.
descriptions.NUR7109:
It is known for giving its name to an important culture of the Sardinian Chalcolithic, the Filigosa culture, which is closely linked to the Abealzu culture, so much so that the term Abealzu-Filigosa culture is often used. The necropolis consists of four multi-chambered domus de janas, cut into a tuff hillock and characterised by the presence of long entrance dromoi.

It was used from the 3rd millennium BC until the early centuries of the 2nd millennium BC;
descriptions.NUR6914: The Fund'e Monti necropolis (also known as Tracucu) consists of 15 hypogean tombs, locally known as Domus de Janas (fairy houses). The tombs, both single-chambered and multi-chambered, have entrances marked by an access corridor (dromos) up to 5 m long, or by an antechamber. The doorways are the most carefully finished elements, finely carved with frames (to hold the stone doors) and rebates (for draining liquids).
descriptions.NUR7019:
The necropolis consists of 14 domus de janas, considered among the most beautiful in Sardinia for their architectural conception.

Twelve of them are cut into the rock in a horizontal row, the other two opposite the first ones. The façades are striking for their monumentality and the precision of the workmanship: in particular that of tomb 3. A drainage channel cut into the rock, still visible, protected the burials from rainwater infiltration.
descriptions.NUR7758:
It has a single chamber.

Another domus de janas should be located nearby.
descriptions.NUR21142: The necropolis includes 4 domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR7234: It is located in the territory of the comune of Buddusò (OT) at a lower elevation than the road passing through the granite quarry.
descriptions.NUR7222:
It is a Neolithic burial cut into a schist ridge near a watercourse.

The burial consists of a single cell with a sub-circular plan. Traces of the entrance hatchway can be seen.

To the right on entering there is a small niche/cupboard. There is no chronological evidence, either because no finds were recovered or because the structure was used several times, even in recent times, and has been completely disturbed; indeed it lacks a floor.
descriptions.NUR7192: It is an enormous rock that contains a funerary hypogeum of the 4th–3rd millennium BC. The site saw an extraordinary continuity of use lasting five thousand years, from the Neolithic to the 19th century. It now houses the museum of the ethnographic traditions of Anglona, which illustrates agro-pastoral culture, the life of local communities, history and archaeology, starting from the Neolithic tomb that forms the oldest level of the Rocca: six cells of varying sizes and shapes, two of which are merged into a single chamber.
descriptions.NUR7187: Prehistoric underground cemetery composed of 6 tombs.
descriptions.NUR7302: This tomb, cut into trachyte, shows – in the antechamber and the main chamber – a painted ceiling reproducing the roof of a hut according to two different typological schemes. Of particular interest is the “reticulated” motif running along the walls of the main cell.
descriptions.NUR11879: A multi-chambered domus de janas with false windows, defined by incised grooves bearing traces of red paint, and straight raised beams radiating on the ceiling to evoke a wooden roof. In the main chamber there is a sub-rectangular pilaster, of which only the lower and upper parts survive, the latter bearing an incised bull's-head protome. A Nuragic village can be sensed in the surrounding area.
descriptions.NUR6970:
The area includes a dolmen, a domus de janas and remains of a megalithic circle.

A distinctive area marked by the megalithic enclosure within which the dolmen stands. About 20 m from the dolmen lies the single-chamber Domus de Janas with a dolmenic corridor, added at a later period to create another tomb. Datable between the 3rd and 2nd millennium BC from the municipal information board.
descriptions.NUR19729:
The domus de janas consists of three sub-rectangular chambers opening onto five smaller elliptical or semi-circular cells.

The tomb is entered through a rectangular vestibule whose ceiling reproduces a double-pitched roof with a central beam (20 x 5 cm deep) from which the side rafters (eight on each side) spring, alternating with broad flat bands (20–30 cm).
descriptions.NUR15895: Cemetery composed of domus de janas repurposed in the Roman period.
descriptions.NUR6950:
In an initial phase several villages of quadrangular huts belonging to the Ozieri culture settled in the area; they are associated with a necropolis of hypogean domus de janas tombs and a probable sanctuary with menhirs, stone slabs for sacrifices and stone spheres.

It consists of 8 hypogea, among which the "tomba del Capo" stands out for its importance.
descriptions.NUR8002: Domus de janas entirely excavated in shale, consisting of a single chamber with lateral benches.
descriptions.NUR7009: Excavated in an amphitheatre of trachyte rock on the southern flank of the 'silent' hill of sa Pranedda, it consists of over 40 tombs of various sizes and plans, aligned along the rock face in a symmetrical arrangement that appears pre-planned. The necropolis of Montessu is one of the most significant and fascinating pre-Nuragic testimonies on the Island, in use for a millennium and a half, from the Late Neolithic (3200–2800 BC) to the Early Bronze Age (1800–1600 BC).
descriptions.NUR7735: Three domus de janas. Featuring an imposing column inside and carved bull's-head protomes on the walls. Very difficult to locate.
descriptions.NUR7158: On the flank of Monte Cumida. It consists of eight domus de janas, variously articulated and characterised by decorative motifs on the walls. In Tomb VI, which has seven chambers, a false door of trapezoidal shape is carved into the back wall of one of the cells. In Tomb VIII, the main cell has a double-pitched ceiling and, on the front wall above the hatch giving access to one of the secondary chambers, double horns are carved in low relief, now barely legible.
descriptions.NUR14691: The two domus de janas lie in the municipality of Silanus (NU), 40 metres north of the former SS 229, a short distance from the nuraghi Ordari and s'Aspru, which stand on rocky spurs at a higher elevation.
descriptions.NUR14194: The construction is unique in that it also embodies elements typical of the hypogean sphere. It is a domus de janas reused in the Nuragic period, when the stele and the corridor were built. It represents a distinctive architectural-façade tomb.
descriptions.NUR7606: They lie within the municipal territory of Sassari. They are two Abealzu culture hypogea cut into the limestone, a short distance from each other, on the left side of the SS131 heading towards Porto Torres. The entrances of the domus are barely perceptible to anyone walking along the track that runs alongside them and leads into a built-up area, because they are completely overgrown with spontaneous vegetation.
descriptions.NUR7306:
Two domus de janas about 2 m apart. An antechamber with a semi-elliptical plan and an irregularly flat ceiling. In the back wall of the antechamber a quadrangular doorway, also with a rebate, gives access to a chamber with a flat ceiling.

A doorway with a rectangular opening and a rebate for a closing slab gives access to an antechamber with a sub-elliptical plan and a flat ceiling.
descriptions.NUR7022: (very difficult to locate, but it exists)
descriptions.NUR7174: It should include at least five hypogea.
descriptions.NUR7068: Composed of two rooms of square plan dug into compact granite.
descriptions.NUR6998: On the Punta Sas Baddes plateau lies the domus de janas of Funtana 'e Furru, the only one with access via a small well, a single-cell structure with a chamber shaped like a "oven".
descriptions.NUR8033: Domus de janas fractured and covered with debris
descriptions.NUR7035: Domus de janas fractured and covered with debris
descriptions.NUR6932: A necropolis with nine hypogeal tombs, in an area with rock outcrops on the surrounding ground. The tombs were found by chance during recent excavation work. The site is thought to have been used from the Late Neolithic (3500 BC).
descriptions.NUR7165:
The hypogeum lies about 750 metres south-west of the Nuraghe s'Infurcadu, while some fifty metres to the north-west there are two menhirs and traces of ancient occupation that have unfortunately been swept away by uncontrolled stone-clearing work.

The domus de janas, cut into a bank of basalt rock, consists of a short vestibule leading into a cell with a niche.
descriptions.NUR7320:
It is located within the territory of the comune of Cagliari.

Final section of a domus de janas (Neolithic underground tomb), near the cave of the same name, destroyed by the limestone quarry.
descriptions.NUR7043: It is two underground chambers of domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR17728: A short distance from the Sant'Andria nuraghe, to the north-west, lies the domus de janas, cut into a granite outcrop. The entrance has collapsed, so the hypogeum is reached through an irregular opening that leads into a small antechamber from which the second chamber opens. Fragments and flakes of lithic material can be found around it.
descriptions.NUR7384: In an irregularly shaped granitic rock ledge, two single-chambered domus de janas have been cut. The surrounding area is characterised by a dense oak wood. The two hypogeal burials, about 1 m apart, are cut respectively into the north and west sides of a granitic ledge.
descriptions.NUR6939: Domus de janas restored and used as a pastoral and agricultural refuge.
descriptions.NUR7066: It consists of two single-cell tombs, side by side, each with a rectangular entrance.
descriptions.NUR7104: The archaeological area comprises a village and two domus de janas on a granite tor partly surrounded by the Tèscere river. The complex nuraghe is distinguished by natural cavities incorporated into wall structures. The two domus are cut into two boulders. The first, single-chambered, is reached through a raised entrance preceded by a short vestibule. The second consists of a single chamber ruined by the collapse of the boulder in which the entrance opened.
descriptions.NUR4151: The archaeological area comprises a village and two domus de janas on a granite tor partly surrounded by the Tèscere river. The complex nuraghe is distinguished by natural cavities incorporated into wall structures. The two domus are cut into two boulders. The first, single-chambered, is reached through a raised entrance preceded by a short vestibule. The second consists of a single chamber ruined by the collapse of the boulder in which the entrance opened.
descriptions.NUR6934: They are four small underground burials dug out in an isolated rock outcrop.
descriptions.NUR7185: It includes three hypogea, of which the first (with 7 cells) should also be called "Sa Spelunca de Nonna".
descriptions.NUR7169:
A particularly evocative domus de janas necropolis adjoining part of a larger site that includes a nuraghe with a village and a dolmen.

One of the finest domus de janas at Sirilò, until a few years ago it was still entirely underground. From the small entrance you enter the large chamber, inside which there are three more entrances leading to three other chambers.
descriptions.NUR11474: A particularly evocative domus de janas necropolis adjoining part of a larger site that includes a nuraghe with a village and a dolmen. One of the finest domus de janas at Sirilò, until a few years ago it was still entirely underground. From the small entrance you enter the large chamber, inside which there are three more entrances leading to three other chambers.
descriptions.NUR7059: Domus de janas carved out of granite, particularly striking for its double door set between a pillar.
descriptions.NUR14912: Cut into a basalt wall, the tomb has its entrance facing west, 0.80 m below ground level; it is rectangular and well carved, set within a deep recess. The threshold has a drainage channel, and along the wall thickness, beside the jamb, there are two opposite recesses, perhaps to allow the closing slab to slide more easily. The chamber, irregularly semi-circular in plan, has a flat floor and a domed roof with curved walls.
descriptions.NUR15545: On the slopes of Monte Santo three separate boulders hold ancient Neolithic tombs along an uphill path. Three erratic boulders in which the tombs were cut. In the first boulder encountered on the way to the summit, Su Crastu de Santu Eliseu, which gives the site its name, the domus de janas has been reused as a Christian place of worship. Next comes Su Crastu de Santu Elia and finally Su Crastu de Santu Enoch, which has a domus de janas with two fine bull's-head protomes.
descriptions.NUR15543: On the slopes of Monte Santo three separate boulders hold ancient Neolithic tombs along an uphill path. Three erratic boulders in which the tombs were cut. In the first boulder encountered on the way to the summit, Su Crastu de Santu Eliseu, which gives the site its name, the domus de janas has been reused as a Christian place of worship. Next comes Su Crastu de Santu Elia and finally Su Crastu de Santu Enoch, which has a domus de janas with two fine bull's-head protomes.
descriptions.NUR7201: Pluricellular, extensively modified and used as a shepherd's shelter.
descriptions.NUR6996: Single-cell domus de janas dug into trachyte
descriptions.NUR7443:
Nearby is the domus de janas of the same name. The nuraghe is very ruined.

A short distance from the Florinas–Banari provincial road; the service track of a disused sand quarry lets you get even closer to the site.
descriptions.NUR3899:
Nearby is the domus de janas of the same name. The nuraghe is very ruined.

A short distance from the Florinas–Banari provincial road; the service track of a disused sand quarry lets you get even closer to the site.
descriptions.NUR18937: It consists of six single-cell domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR19616:
Isolated domus with reuse.

Excerpt from the publication "Archaeological research in Marghine-Planargia" by Moravetti
descriptions.NUR7409: Domus de janas with the particularity of a double door on two opposite sides, with the roof collapsed on the vault.
descriptions.NUR19039: The domus is very deeply buried and entry into it is practically impossible.
descriptions.NUR7241: It is a multicompartments underground chamber.
descriptions.NUR7433: The pre-Nuragic necropolis of S'Elighe Entosu consists of eight very distinctive domus de janas: for example, one preserves in its cell a circular stone hearth carved into the floor, a ceiling carved with a double pitch replicating the timbering of a wooden roof, and on the sides a reproduction of the walls of prehistoric huts. Another, called "delle Sette Stanze", has medieval graffiti along the entrance corridor and seven small cells arranged around the main chamber.
descriptions.NUR6915: The pre-Nuragic necropolis of S'Elighe Entosu consists of eight very distinctive domus de janas: for example, one preserves in its cell a circular stone hearth carved into the floor, a ceiling carved with a double pitch replicating the timbering of a wooden roof, and on the sides a reproduction of the walls of prehistoric huts. Another, called "delle Sette Stanze", has medieval graffiti along the entrance corridor and seven small cells arranged around the main chamber.
descriptions.NUR7638: The complex consists of six hypogeal tombs cut into large isolated blocks of limestone, erratic boulders. Tombs I and IV stand out for their decorative ornaments, represented by spiral motifs carved in relief with the direct pecking technique, and architectural elements typical of contemporary dwellings, such as beams and joists (reproducing a double-pitched roof), frames, pilasters, plinths, steps and false doors, carved in bas-relief.

descriptions.NUR6910: The complex consists of six hypogeal tombs cut into large isolated blocks of limestone, erratic boulders. Tombs I and IV stand out for their decorative ornaments, represented by spiral motifs carved in relief with the direct pecking technique, and architectural elements typical of contemporary dwellings, such as beams and joists (reproducing a double-pitched roof), frames, pilasters, plinths, steps and false doors, carved in bas-relief.
descriptions.NUR1258: Two small domus de janas visible from the road
descriptions.NUR9756:
The hypogeal tomb opens in a rachitic outcrop, about 150 metres east of the Borore–Silanus municipal road.

The hypogeum, oriented south-west, consists of two sub-circular cells arranged along the longitudinal axis; the walls are carefully smoothed and the ceiling is slightly hemispherical.
descriptions.NUR9757:
The hypogeal tomb opens in a rachitic outcrop, about 150 metres east of the Borore–Silanus municipal road.

The hypogeum, oriented south-west, consists of two sub-circular cells arranged along the longitudinal axis; the walls are carefully smoothed and the ceiling is slightly hemispherical.
descriptions.NUR7469: The evidence for this period dates no earlier than the Final Neolithic. The very simple domus de janas at Campu Estius should belong to the Ozieri culture. "and the handle of a volcanic rock, the smallest of those from Perda Longa (Lilliu, 1975 p. 3; Lilliu, 2003 pp. 98-99), like a sacred rock, witness to the artificial holes made in it and to the finds of stone rings, of green stone and of discs found whole"
descriptions.NUR14950: Domus de janas of which no photographs exist and whose condition is unknown
descriptions.NUR6975: It is located in the territory of the comune of Nuoro. It is a single-cell domus, well finished internally. Difficult to identify due to dense vegetation. It opens onto a low granite bank.
descriptions.NUR7763: The necropolis of Iscala Mugheras consists of six domus de janas. In particular, the fourth, fifth, and sixth have been used as sheepfolds by the landowner in whose territory they are located.
descriptions.NUR7690: The necropolis of Iscala Mugheras consists of six domus de janas. In particular, the fourth, fifth, and sixth have been used as sheepfolds by the landowner in whose territory they are located.
descriptions.NUR7691: The necropolis of Iscala Mugheras consists of six domus de janas. In particular, the fourth, fifth, and sixth have been used as sheepfolds by the landowner in whose territory they are located.
descriptions.NUR7120: The necropolis of Iscala Mugheras consists of six domus de janas. In particular, the fourth, fifth, and sixth have been used as sheepfolds by the landowner in whose territory they are located.
descriptions.NUR7110:
Cut into a tufa cliff inside a narrow valley traversed by a tributary of the Rio Mannu, just outside the village, to the right of the road to Allai.

The domus de janas lie on private property, fenced and closed by a gate; the owner is very often working in the vegetable garden and will not hesitate to let you in and accompany you to the site.
descriptions.NUR7290: They are carved from a rock composed almost entirely of white quartz pebbles. The origin of these pebbles can be traced to a fluvial-deltaic environment dating back to about 166 million years ago.
descriptions.NUR17692: The domus consists of three large rooms with a single entrance.
descriptions.NUR15886: It is a small single-chambered underground chamber.
descriptions.NUR6945: Moderate in scale (about 51 metres with a negative elevation drop of 10 metres), easily accessible.
descriptions.NUR13986:
In a wooded area, carved into trachytic rock. The interior is decorated with a false door and a probable bull's-head protome above.

It includes 7 hypogea in total and known.
descriptions.NUR6923: Cemetery consisting of 25 tombs dug into granite. No sculptural decorations are present on the walls.
descriptions.NUR12033: Domus de janas that was begun but never completed, only the entrance and a partial excavation of the interior are visible.
descriptions.NUR6940:
Administratively it belongs to the municipality of Thiesi, province of Sassari, from which it is about 10 kilometres away.

The necropolis consists of four domus de janas cut into a trachyte outcrop on the slopes of Monte Ittiresu. Among them, Tomb III stands out for its importance; also known as the "Painted Tomb", it is considered one of the most interesting testimonies of the Sardinian Neolithic. Because the site has been left abandoned, the frescoes are undergoing continuous and rapid deterioration.
descriptions.NUR12135:
They are two hypogea.

They lie just outside the settlement, about 800 m away. They are reached via the farm track that leads towards Murruzzone and Su Lu'e. Only one of the two is in good condition, but its interior is small; it stands on an isolated rock outcrop with its entrance facing east, the first in the photo. The other appears heavily damaged and overgrown with brambles, as shown in the image below. The two 'oncheddas are about 100 m apart.
descriptions.NUR12136: Second domus de janas. in poor condition due to the overgrowth of brambles.
descriptions.NUR7231: The archaeological site, dating to the Late Neolithic, consists of five domus de janas set at different heights along the mountain slope and is easily reached by a path a short distance from the Nuoro–Siniscola provincial road; the first domus opens directly onto the path while the others lie in the vegetation above it.
descriptions.NUR7114: It consists of four underground chambers. Probable location.
descriptions.NUR7381: The chamber is single-celled, with a sub-elliptical plan and an entrance offset to the left of the chamber's median axis. It has a flat floor and a curvilinear vault, almost oven-shaped. It shows two phases of construction: in the original layout the chamber and the rectangular doorway, marked by a groove, were cut; later a small dolmenic corridor was added.
descriptions.NUR11471:
This domus came to light during the flood of 18-11-2013.  

Until then, it had been covered by vegetation and was likely known to the local herders. Above it lies a road.
descriptions.NUR7263: Once you have “crawled” your way inside, the tomb reveals itself in all its beauty: the column, the bas-relief protomes, the cells, the antechambers, the door to the afterlife, the symbols and signs of an archaic devotion that intoxicate both soul and spirit.
descriptions.NUR7112: A beautiful domus de janas necropolis consisting of eight domus, four of which are grouped together (5-6-7-8); Domus IV lies near the group of four tombs, Domus III about 200 metres to the south, and Domus I and II close together about 100 metres east of the third.
descriptions.NUR7232: A beautiful domus de janas necropolis consisting of eight domus, four of which are grouped together (5-6-7-8); Domus IV lies near the group of four tombs, Domus III about 200 metres to the south, and Domus I and II close together about 100 metres east of the third.
descriptions.NUR7371: A beautiful domus de janas necropolis consisting of eight domus, four of which are grouped together (5-6-7-8); Domus IV lies near the group of four tombs, Domus III about 200 metres to the south, and Domus I and II close together about 100 metres east of the third.
descriptions.NUR1356: It is a small cemetery composed of 5 domus de janas, one of which is barely outlined and hardly visible because hidden by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR12070: There are three isolated tombs in the municipality of Mamoiada.
descriptions.NUR7098: The domus de janas, cut into the flank of the basalt hill, are five in number, all attributable to the Ozieri Culture and excavated between 3100 and 2900 BC. The pre-Nuragic village, also dating to the Ozieri Culture, lies at the foot of the hill.
descriptions.NUR20012:
The Domus lies inside a private garden and is cut into a huge oval outcrop of granite, on top of which a small pit has been hollowed out with two channels running from it.

The Domus consists of an antechamber giving access to a large chamber, on the right of which opens the entrance to a further chamber.
descriptions.NUR9803:
The hypogeum, oriented to the north-east, consists of a short rectangular antechamber (depth 0.45 m – width 0.56 m – height 0.66 m) which, through a quadrangular doorway (width 0.38 m), leads into the burial chamber.

The chamber has a vaguely elliptical plan (depth 0.78/1.08 m – height 0.62 m – width 1.70 m) with an irregular profile, carefully smoothed walls and a slightly hemispherical ceiling.
descriptions.NUR7204: This is Domus I, the most important and easily visible of a prehistoric necropolis consisting of 7 hypogea. The other tombs lie on private land, about 600 metres away as the crow flies to the south-east. Two of the hypogea mentioned above are more properly burials in rock shelters. Prehistoric necropolis that gave its name to the first phase of the Early Bronze Age in Sardinia (1800–1600 BC), the so-called Bonnanaro Culture.
descriptions.NUR7230:
Situated between the Sas Pireddas area to the east and Riu Mortu to the south, the Domus di Istiolai is a hollow carved out of a single granite block, consisting of an atrium and a burial chamber with a rounded floor plan; the latter has a small, unnatural pit cut into the floor, probably used for votive offerings.

The entrance faces north-north-west, and the workmanship is very careful, especially at the entrance.
descriptions.NUR7292:
The Sas Arzolas de Goi necropolis dates to the Ozieri Culture period (3200–2800 BC).

Five domus de janas have been identified so far; they lie on the slope of a trachyte hill that has been extensively affected by quarrying.

Tomb 1 is particularly interesting because it displays two complete bull's-head protomes, with ears and head, carved above the entrance hatch and on the pillar inside the burial chamber. The horns at the entrance are carved in convex relief.
descriptions.NUR7235: This domus de janas is part of the larger Abealzu-Calancoi complex, which contains dozens of domus de janas. It lies on the mid-slope of a limestone hillside, facing south, and is difficult to reach on foot. Its state of decay is considerable, due to the crumbling of the limestone and later reuse.
descriptions.NUR7429: The site is characterised by a quadrangular courtyard that was originally the main chamber, now collapsed. It is entered through a granite arch of rare beauty, and from there into what remains of the original domus de janas: two chambers, one quadrangular and aligned with the entrance, the other irregular in shape on the right.
descriptions.NUR6987:
The tomb is part of the Campu Majore necropolis, composed of 24 domus de janas, which lie on private property and are not accessible without permission.

The entrance of this domus de janas faced the village of Busachi; during the Second World War it was altered with a reinforced concrete wall and adapted by the owners as a shelter against bombing.

It is now used as a water reservoir.
descriptions.NUR7154: On the edge of the named height: a very ruined tomb, possibly the only underground chamber remaining from a small necropolis.
descriptions.NUR7137: The Coroneddu necropolis (Bosa – OR) consists of three hypogea, two of them side by side and a third set further apart. It opens on a rocky spur on the southern slope of a limestone hill that extends into the Modolo valley. Probable location
descriptions.NUR6961: The necropolis consists of six domus de janas in poor condition. One, however, has two pillars carved in the rock with herringbone decoration. The ceiling, also carved, represents the roof of the hut.
descriptions.NUR7402: Single-cell domus de janas located near the municipal road
descriptions.NUR6958: It consists of 6 hypogea, of which 4 have been destroyed.
descriptions.NUR7142: Inside there is a pillar on which a bull's-head protome is carved in high relief.
descriptions.NUR7261: Three domus de janas built on a limestone cliff, monocellular, later decorated with carved stelae set against the rock face.
descriptions.NUR7295: Three domus de janas built on a limestone cliff, monocellular, later decorated with carved stelae set against the rock face.
descriptions.NUR7446: Three domus de janas built on a limestone cliff, monocellular, later decorated with carved stelae set against the rock face.
descriptions.NUR7527: Dug in a low trachytic formation, it features a bull's-head protome in the antechamber.
descriptions.NUR6983:
A group of domus de janas, spread over about 200 metres along the limestone channel.

The largest, beneath the road embankment, contains inside: Su laccu: a vat presumably used to make must.

The domus is so large that it looks more like a dwelling than a tomb.

Recesses of various sizes in the walls. Storage niches of various kinds and articulated hypogean chambers, lower and adjoining the main chamber.
descriptions.NUR7364:
The necropolis lies within a wider archaeological context that includes a village of dry-stone huts with fortifications – a few hundred metres away – and a megalithic circle (diameter 3.00 m) about 600 m distant.

The funerary complex comprises nine domus de janas with variously articulated ground plans. Tomb I is multi-chambered and has eleven successive chambers.
descriptions.NUR7116: Six hypogea of the domus de janas type. The immediate proximity of a tuff quarry, on the edges of which a few traces of other hypogea can be seen, suggests that the site originally extended further than it does today. Of the six domus present, one is almost completely destroyed, three were converted into farm buildings in historical times after substantial alterations to their plans, and only the last two (Tombs V and VI) have preserved their original structure.
descriptions.NUR7016: The "Domus de janas" are hypogean (underground) burials of the pre-Nuragic period, datable to 3500–3000 BC, consisting of one or more chambers and used up to the Nuragic age. On Monte Arista, in the municipality of Cardedu, there is a necropolis composed of ten carefully made tombs in an excellent state of preservation. The tombs are cut into isolated blocks of granite. The hypogea are of two types, single-chambered and double-chambered, and have a longitudinal layout.
descriptions.NUR7255: Multicellular domus de janas containing carved decorations depicting a bull's-head protome. At the centre there is a pillar cut out by removal of rock.
descriptions.NUR7017: On Monte Zara there are nine domus de janas, including a pair known locally as Is ogus de monti, "the eyes of the mountain". A majestic staircase of about sixty steps cut entirely into the rock leads to the summit, from which there is a broad view of the Cagliari coast. Here lies a Nuragic sacred area dating to the 7th century BC, with an altar and several cisterns for collecting rainwater.
descriptions.NUR7025: On Monte Zara there are nine domus de janas, including a pair known locally as Is ogus de monti, "the eyes of the mountain", a truly fitting nickname. A majestic staircase of about sixty steps, entirely cut into the rock, leads to the summit, from which there is a broad view of the Cagliari coast. Here lies a Nuragic sacred area dating to the 7th century BC, with an altar and several cisterns for collecting rainwater.
descriptions.NUR6930: The Museddu necropolis lies within the Petroglifi Park. It consists of 18 domus de janas with simple ground plans: a quadrangular cell preceded by a small antechamber, or two or three cells arranged longitudinally.
descriptions.NUR6974: The well-known necropolis of Noeddale lies on the western edge of a saddle that drops steeply to the west towards the Sae valley. It consists of six hypogea, three cut into a gently sloping limestone outcrop, one into a low rock face below, and two more into a higher rock face. Two hypogea are preceded by short dromoi.
descriptions.NUR7113: Single-cell domus de janas carved in limestone
descriptions.NUR7278: Single-cell domus de janas carved in limestone
descriptions.NUR6949: The cemetery consists of three domus de janas, among which the tomb I stands out for its size and decorations.
descriptions.NUR7045: Domus de janas built around a central acrocoro on which the traces of a hut or megalithic circle are evident.
descriptions.NUR7033: A large natural cave on whose eastern side several smaller cavities open; their morphological features would lead one to classify them as domus de janas, a hypothesis supported by the presence on the summit of the cave of channels and cupmarks used for both functional and ritual purposes.
descriptions.NUR7064: The two domus de janas are hard to see from the provincial road because their entrances are hidden by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR6966:
It can be counted among the most extensive of those known and is rich in particular architectural symbolism. Hewn from a rocky plateau of red trachyte, it consists of at least twenty hypogea.

The domus de janas very often reproduce the ground plans and certain details of the dwellings of the living.

In some of them anthropomorphic petroglyphs are carved, known as “capovolti” because they are thought to represent the souls of the dead returning to mother earth.
descriptions.NUR7161: It is a group of six domus de janas tombs, five of which, of the single-chamber oven type, are in very poor condition, while the sixth has a sub-square antechamber giving access to the adjoining rectangular cell.
descriptions.NUR7115: It is one of two hypogea in the Campu Marinu area. In the past, a dolmen (presumably destroyed) also existed at the site.
descriptions.NUR6984: Cemetery consisting of four domus de janas dug into erratic boulders
descriptions.NUR7225: They are three underground cists dug into a low limestone cliff face.
descriptions.NUR6947:
The necropolis consists of 18 domus de janas, cut into three superimposed horizontal levels starting from the base line of the ridge, for a maximum height of 3 m above the ground.

The finds recovered during the excavations have allowed the burials to be dated to a period ranging from the Late Neolithic (San Michele culture, 3200–2800 BC) to the Early Bronze Age (Bonnanaro culture, 1800–1600 BC).
descriptions.NUR7197: The necropolis consists of five hypogea and numerous cavities that were probably domus de janas, but now appear destroyed or incomplete. One domus (the first) has an interesting column in the main cell.
descriptions.NUR7132: Domus de janas of which no description is available
descriptions.NUR7509: It is located within the territory of the comune of Florinas. It consists of two underground chambers.
descriptions.NUR7089: Next to the village, two single-cell domus de janas dug out in a calcarean cave.
descriptions.NUR7056:
Probable location.

It consists of two underground chambers.
descriptions.NUR11644:
It is a domus de janas in basalt. It consists of an antechamber and an adjoining chamber.

A small niche is cut into the right-hand wall of the antechamber. The floor has a well-made "hearth".

It lies on a low basalt ridge in the shade of some holm oaks. Easily reached a few dozen metres from the road.
descriptions.NUR12034: It is an incomplete domus located within a granite monolith.
descriptions.NUR12071:
The small necropolis of Ovau consists of three small domus de janas. The first is the one with the largest chamber and a doorway frame; the third, on the other hand, is very small inside.

Nearby are two unusual superimposed menhirs, very well worked. The first menhir
descriptions.NUR12649: Group of domus de janas hidden in the undergrowth
descriptions.NUR9770: It is a small single-chamber tomb of the oven type, circular in plan (depth 0.55 m – width 0.62 m), entered through a finely shaped doorway (width ….. – height 0.42 m – thickness 0.12 m) preceded by a short antechamber (depth 0.32 m – width 0.75/0.48 m). The orientation is to the south, the walls are perfectly smoothed and the ceiling slightly hemispherical.
descriptions.NUR15931: The cemetery consists of three domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR14005: Domus de janas on a trachytic cliff, internally decorated with a false door and a possibly carved hearth.
descriptions.NUR7316: Typical single-cell domus de janas with a carved stele facing the limestone.
descriptions.NUR7121: Six domus de janas at the locality Sas Concheddas de Pianu Edras, cut into a rocky outcrop, this time of trachyte tuff, are the six Domus de Janas of the Prehistoric Hypogean Necropolis of Pianu Edras, among which the Domus delle Cappelle is worth noting.
descriptions.NUR6962: There are four (but one is destroyed).
descriptions.NUR7539: It consists of a rectangular doorway leading into a small antechamber originally roofed. This is followed by a doorway with four rebates arranged like steps to receive the closing slab. The tomb is single-chambered and the walls are carefully worked. In the small antechamber, on the right-hand wall and in the ceiling of the left-hand side, there are traces of red ochre that must originally have coloured the whole chamber. Copper Age material (Monte Claro culture) comes from this domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR6922: It consists of at least 19 tombs, including one barely outlined.
descriptions.NUR15083: The condition of the tomb is unknown.
descriptions.NUR10541: A group of domus de janas, the most important of which bears a chequerboard motif, bordered on one side by a zig-zag band, representing the depiction of fabric hangings found in the dwellings of the living and reproduced in the houses of the dead.
descriptions.NUR6952: The cemetery includes 21 domus de janas. Visible from the bridge on SS131.
descriptions.NUR20266: During construction a spring was found beneath the site, which keeps the domus full of water even in times of drought. For this reason it became a temple dedicated to fertility, so much so that the female reproductive organ was carved into the rock around the entrance of the domus and, above it, the male reproductive organ. These are joined by a small channel cut in the rock, signifying fertilisation.
descriptions.NUR7372: Neolithic rock-cut burial, typologically perhaps attributable to the Filigosa culture (about 2500 BC). The monument is hard to read because it is covered by dense vegetation. The burial consists of an entrance corridor (dromos), an antechamber and a chamber. The narrow corridor leads into the roughly circular antechamber. The chamber proper, smaller and roughly rectangular in plan, is reached through a roughly rectangular/trapezoidal doorway.
descriptions.NUR20017:
These are three hypogea cut into a trachyandesite outcrop inside a private property.

Domus I has a short dromos entrance, an antechamber that opens onto two successive cells along the same axis. The Domus has no particular decoration.

Domus II and III: the first is full of water, but its wide entrance can be admired; the second is completely overgrown with vegetation to the point that it was not possible to explore it.

There are probably other hypogea.
descriptions.NUR7327: It lies near the country church of San Pietro, about one kilometre from the village. Its name, S'Acqua 'e is dolus, means "the water of sorrows", from an old folk belief that the water in this small cave has miraculous powers; a legend also tells that during one of his journeys San Pietro took shelter in this artificial grotto and prayed there for so long that the imprint of his knees was left forever in the rock.
descriptions.NUR7318: The complex consists of two domus de janas carved into a rocky outcrop of sandstone exposed to the south, located in a south-eastern position relative to the new church of San Giovanni.
descriptions.NUR7339: The complex consists of two domus de janas carved into a rocky outcrop of sandstone exposed to the south, located in a south-eastern position relative to the new church of San Giovanni.
descriptions.NUR7094: The complex consists of two domus de janas carved into a rocky outcrop of sandstone exposed to the south, located in a south-eastern position relative to the new church of San Giovanni.
descriptions.NUR13966: In one tomb a large bull's-head protome and traces of paint can still be seen. Six single-chamber domus de janas in poor condition can be identified. Two other tombs lie about 500 metres away to the south-east.
descriptions.NUR12308:
Domus 1 has a multi-chambered layout, with a semicircular antechamber giving access to a first trapezoidal cell that features a central pillar. An opening cut into the top of the pillar leads to an upper level with two small chambers superimposed on the one below.

Domus 2 has a multi-chambered layout, with a corridor, an elliptical cell, a roughly rectangular central chamber with a niche, and a third quadrangular cell.
descriptions.NUR19989: Domus de janas reported by a hiker.
descriptions.NUR7719: The sculptures of the bull's head can be admired, representing the head of the male god, worshipped by the populations of the Neolithic period, who buried their dead in these artificial caves.
descriptions.NUR12727: The sculptures of the bull's head can be admired, representing the head of the male god, worshipped by the populations of the Neolithic period, who buried their dead in these artificial caves.
descriptions.NUR13691: The context is unusual because the rock-cut stone appears “isolated”, surrounded by holm oaks that camouflage it; the entrance faces south-west, the chamber is circular and its walls contain squared niches, the surrounding ground slopes, and a few metres away to the west there is a fine rocky escarpment.
descriptions.NUR7664: Remains of a domus de janas
descriptions.NUR7781: In the countryside of Osilo there is a very large domus de janas, greatly modified, located beneath the foundations of a church now reduced to ruins.
descriptions.NUR7237: The underground chamber is cut into a limestone cliff. "The whole appears carefully organised and balanced in proportion, producing a powerful compositional harmony" (Giuseppa Tanda).
descriptions.NUR7430: The underground chamber is cut into a limestone cliff. "The whole appears carefully organised and balanced in proportion, producing a powerful compositional harmony" (Giuseppa Tanda).
descriptions.NUR7199: Four domus de janas spaced apart
descriptions.NUR6916:
You crawl through that opening; the space is tight, the ceiling low because of all that millennia-old earth, and you go on advancing on your elbows, slowly. It consists of at least 12 hypogea, cut into the limestone and provided with various decorations and bull protomes.

These are domus that move you, because their beauty lies in everything they hold.

Then, in the darkness, a shaft of light illuminates a magnificent triple-framed decoration on a doorway still almost completely buried.
descriptions.NUR6942: The domus de janas that make up this necropolis, one of the most extensive and important in Sardinia, are cut into the vertical face and the plateau of a trachyte outcrop — about 10 m high and facing south — and consist of some twenty burials arranged mostly at a certain height above the surrounding ground level.
descriptions.NUR20041:
The Domus de Janas of Sant'Andrìa are in the municipality of Mara (Sassari), in the rural locality of "Sant'Andrìa", from which they take their name.

They consist of a single "niche", set in dense vegetation.

They are easy to find; they can be seen from the road to Bonu Ighinu, high up on the left.
descriptions.NUR6968:
A small necropolis with intercommunicating chambers and traces of red ochre still visible.

They lie on the SP 15 towards Sorradile, clearly visible at the junction leading to the lake.

The doorway is very well carved; the collapse of the antechamber is obvious, and there were certainly other chambers, since clear traces are visible in the ground in front.
descriptions.NUR12644: The Santu Pedru necropolis is a pre-Nuragic archaeological site. The necropolis lies on the east slope of the trachyte hill of Santu Pedru, in a position commanding a broad view over the valley below, in the Nurra, a region of north-western Sardinia. The complex comprises about ten tombs with an entrance corridor ("dromos") and a multi-cellular ground plan.
descriptions.NUR6911: A group of seven or more domus de janas on the pass, towards the Mariani farm, from which the Santa Lucia plain and the underlying Sant'Andrea Priu necropolis and the valley of the nuraghi of Torralba can be seen. Tomb seven, with the double spiral in red ochre, has recently been restored.
descriptions.NUR17694: The first chamber has collapsed upon itself, and access to the smaller chamber must be gained by crawling through the ruins.
descriptions.NUR7571: A jewel set among the mountains of Padria, where the Ancient Sardinians carved the rock and sculpted extraordinary bull's-head protomes across an entire wall, enigmatic guardians watching us in silence.
descriptions.NUR7258: Single-cell domus de janas on a rocky outcrop, isolated and rising above the terrain
descriptions.NUR7119: Domus de janas enriched with various bull's-head protomes carved in limestone
descriptions.NUR7118:
It lies in the municipality of Orani (NU). It consists of 17 domus de janas and 2 rock shelters (probably used as burials). A text by Chiara Chisu states there are 15 domus, but I have recorded at least 17 (some may have been missed because of the dense vegetation).

They must not be confused with those at Oniferi which are called Sas Concas.
descriptions.NUR9224: Two domus de janas sites located on the slopes of the mountain known as "Sas Monzas". Excavated in Miocene limestone.
descriptions.NUR6980: The complex consists of 13 hypogea situated in a panoramic position on Lake Omodeo.
descriptions.NUR13341: Domus de janas located near the provincial road. Excavated on limestone, featuring particular bull's-head protomes in relief.
descriptions.NUR7236: It consists of five hypogea, one of which is buried and one of which is difficult to identify.
descriptions.NUR19920:
The entrance, about 110 cm x 60 cm, is at floor level. There is a single oval chamber about 150 cm high, 250 cm deep and 130 cm wide, apparently undecorated. At the back of the chamber a pit occupies about two-thirds of the short side and is about 3 m deep; it has not been explored and contains a large niche within the same cavity.

Around the domus de janas cut into the limestone there are rectangular basins that look like quarrying for building material, almost as if the site had been used as a quarry.
descriptions.NUR7711: Serra is Araus is a multi-layered site, known for a rock-cut necropolis (domus de janas) of the Neolithic (Ozieri Culture), Chalcolithic (Monte Claro Culture) and Early Bronze Age (Bonnanaro). The 2013 excavation brought to light two new hypogea and the first evidence of the Nuragic village. In particular, traces of a building were found inside which a large model of a nuraghe had been placed.
descriptions.NUR20362: Four domus de janas, side by side, cut into the sandstone. The first one consists of a single chamber, the others of several chambers. The first domu is not connected to the others; the others are interconnected.
descriptions.NUR19663: The domus de janas was cut into a rock outcrop situated halfway up the hill known as Serra Nuarxis. The tomb has a Greek-cross plan and consists of a rectangular vestibule, a quadrangular doorway leading to the actual chamber, and the chamber itself. The chamber, semi-circular in plan, contains three niches, slightly raised above the floor level, oriented to the south-west, north-west and south-east. The niches have arched walls and rectangular bases.
descriptions.NUR9636: It is a two-chambered domus de janas with a short antechamber cut into a trachyte outcrop. The chambers are arranged along the longitudinal axis and have carefully smoothed walls and slightly hemispherical ceilings; the entrance faces south-east.
descriptions.NUR6963: Among the evidence of funerary hypogeism in the Usini area, the Iscala de Sa Figu necropolis, although mentioned in the literature for its five domus de janas, has not yet been the subject of specific analysis. Following detailed reports, research and surveys using different methodologies, both traditional and innovative, were carried out at the site. These operations made it possible to identify two further hypogea and to verify previously undocumented symbols.
descriptions.NUR7217: The cemetery is located in the municipality of Usini. It consists of three domus, one of which has bull's-head protomes and another repurposed as an underground church.
descriptions.NUR6979: The cemetery is located in the municipality of Usini. It consists of three domus, one of which has bull's-head protomes and another repurposed as an underground church.
descriptions.NUR7224: The site is interesting for a whole series of structural and typological considerations regarding the Domus de Janas. It is a true necropolis: the domus are both simple and complex. They range from one with an antechamber and a single cell to the most complex, with many well-made chambers. The vault of some has collapsed, but a careful visit is still possible.
descriptions.NUR11414: Single-chamber domus de janas located underneath an artwork on the S.S.131 heading N.O.
descriptions.NUR7168:
It consists of two single-chambered hypogea dug into a trachytic bed at an elevation of 190 metres.

Surrounded by dense and impenetrable vegetation, it is very difficult to locate.
descriptions.NUR11929: A short distance from the Rio Su Hannavagliu and about a few hundred metres from the nuraghe Luduruju.
descriptions.NUR20145: Noted to the Nurnet editorial office by a resident of Osilo. Single-cellular, situated on a calcareous pedestal from which it takes its name, located near the settlement of Santa Vittoria.
descriptions.NUR7271: It is a large domus de janas necropolis, built on a mass of limestone. Around it, interesting Cart Ruts are visible. Some tombs are decorated with bull's-head protomes.
descriptions.NUR12494: A few steps from the centre of Gonnesa, in a channel in the schist walls, we find the Domus de Janas. The tomb is very simple, with a round plan, and consists of a single burial chamber. The vegetation around the site is lush, so it is possible that the channel conceals other burials.
descriptions.NUR20334: This is probably the Domus reported by the engineer Melis in the census of archaeological sites in Mamoiada; the locality should be Locu Lenardu, although today the whole area is called Su Dovaru. It is a single-chambered Domus cut into a granite bench.
descriptions.NUR7596: Small tomb with a antechamber and a small chamber.
descriptions.NUR11281: Single-cell tomb that represented the place of entertainment for young people of "an earlier time", known as "su Furreddu".
descriptions.NUR12271: Less than 50 metres from the right bank of the Riu Vacchetta, 250 metres from the railway and about 800 metres SW of the Protonuraghe Gazza, two small artificial caves lie a few metres apart.
descriptions.NUR15086: The condition of the domus de janas is unknown.
descriptions.NUR7666: Domus de janas at the edge of the village, next to which a dwelling has been built.
descriptions.NUR7498: Situated near the S'Urri valley (where other domus de janas are found), in the Su Linnarbu gorge, on some outcropping rock faces small rock-cut chambers were excavated, of which only slight traces remain because the large natural inlet was used as a dump for inert materials by Italcementi. However, cut into the upper edges that bound the rocky plateau, a few small cavities are still just visible, attributable to prehistoric tombs of the pre-Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR15859: The domus has an ESE-facing entrance and a cruciform ground plan like the previous one, but with a different structure. It has a dromos raised above ground level that leads to a rectangular vestibule giving access to the main chamber. The chamber is rectangular, and on its three sides, oriented SSW, NNW and NNE, there are three parietal niches raised above the floor that originally had a central pilaster.
descriptions.NUR20413:
The split rock, a narrow, low space, dark and dusty, that forces you to kneel as if to remind you that you are in a sacred place.

But it is when you turn on the light that everything lights up, the rock takes shape, and the ancient symbols seize you and carry you back in time.
descriptions.NUR18660: In the locality "Su Tiriarzu" we find two domus de janas, about 80 metres apart.
descriptions.NUR19640: Common toponym in Sardinia referring to places where rock-cut tombs existed. Indeed, at the site there are two pre-Nuragic bicellular domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR18504: Small and single domus de janas
descriptions.NUR7147: Complex of 5 domus de janas in the Canyon of the Rio Mannu. Carved into Miocene limestone. Some have suffered collapses.
descriptions.NUR13958: In cell c the rock-cut rendering of the rectangular hut appears very faithful. The central beam, the side rafters resting on it and on two horizontal beams parallel to it, and the two symmetrically placed pillars are all reproduced.
descriptions.NUR13344: It faces the road from Alghero to Uri; the tomb is very ruined but still retains within it the typical elements of the false door and the overhanging parts, possibly bull's-head protomes.
descriptions.NUR7311: Group of domus de janas containing petroglyphs "of the overturned" very similar to other analogous ones, and in particular to those of Oniferi Sas Concas.
descriptions.NUR7713: Group of domus de janas containing petroglyphs "of the overturned" very similar to other analogous ones, and in particular to those of Oniferi Sas Concas.
descriptions.NUR6912: Group of domus de janas containing petroglyphs "of the overturned" very similar to other analogous ones, and in particular to those of Oniferi Sas Concas.
descriptions.NUR7195: The complex consists of several hypogean tombs cut into large isolated blocks of limestone, erratic boulders. Among them Tombs I and IV stand out for their decorative ornaments, represented by spiral motifs carved in relief with the direct pecking technique, and architectural elements typical of contemporary dwellings, such as beams and joists (reproducing a double-pitched roof), frames, pilasters, plinths, steps and false doors, carved in bas-relief.
descriptions.NUR6948: Various domus de janas of which no description has been found
descriptions.NUR7437: It includes two complete domus and a third that is just beginning.
descriptions.NUR7176: Domus de janas inside the settlement of Buddusò, excavated in a granite outcrop with a cross-shaped plan.
descriptions.NUR7220:
The site, situated at 270 m above sea level, lies on the shores of Lake Omodeo and consists of a nuraghe, a village and two giants' tombs; nearby is also the Ispiluncas necropolis, made up of about thirty domus de janas that have yielded abundant material of the pre-Nuragic period.

The nuraghe, perhaps a palace, is of mixed type with a three-lobed bastion and dates to the Middle-Recent Bronze Age.
descriptions.NUR3418:
The site, situated at 270 m above sea level, lies on the shores of Lake Omodeo and consists of a nuraghe, a village and two giants' tombs; nearby is also the Ispiluncas necropolis, made up of about thirty domus de janas that have yielded abundant material of the pre-Nuragic period.

The nuraghe, perhaps a palace, is of mixed type with a three-lobed bastion and dates to the Middle-Recent Bronze Age.
