descriptions.NUR7369: Group of four single-cell domus de janas with façade.
descriptions.NUR7291: Group of four single-cell domus de janas with façade.
descriptions.NUR7223: Group of four single-cell domus de janas with façade.
descriptions.NUR7256: Group of four single-cell domus de janas with façade.
descriptions.NUR7005: Typical domus de janas with a façade featuring a carved arched stele on the calcare wall.
descriptions.NUR20100: Noted to the Superintendent of Ca’ Or on 17 May 2021 by the Nurnet Foundation
descriptions.NUR11470: The exedra of the Giants' Tomb was cut into pieces and used in the construction of the dry stone wall.
descriptions.NUR10251: It lies a short distance from the beautiful eponymous nuraghe of s'Enalonga, now covered in brush and thorny bushes. A small spring of water still emerges here, which in ancient times must have fed the fountain. No particular masonry is visible.
descriptions.NUR14769: Nuragic spring included in a small municipal park, carved into the rock
descriptions.NUR13595: The temple was built in isodomic masonry, that is, with blocks of basalt expertly squared and dressed with the appropriate slope where needed. The rocks in the surrounding area consist mainly of schists or granites, and the volcanic rock used was brought to the site from rather distant locations, probably from the territory of Dorgali.
descriptions.NUR16368: Sacred well that shows features of both a well and a Nuragic sacred well. Notable is the presence of a stone with a hollow inside.
descriptions.NUR10759: Large complex nuraghe comprising three defined structures dedicated to water cults. The Supervising Office identifies the third as possibly a nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR10757: Large complex nuraghe comprising three defined structures dedicated to water cults. The Supervising Office identifies the third as possibly a nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR10760: Large complex nuraghe comprising three defined structures dedicated to water cults. The Supervising Office identifies the third as possibly a nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR10259: There are not enough elements to provide a reasoned classification, yet despite the most recent modifications, I consider it to be a Nuragic source.
descriptions.NUR10789: The complex consists of two sacred wells, a large hut, and other rooms. The various structures are surrounded by dry stone walls built in a "spine of the fish" pattern.
descriptions.NUR10792: The complex consists of two sacred wells, a large hut, and other rooms. The various structures are surrounded by dry stone walls built in a "spine of the fish" pattern.
descriptions.NUR10790: The complex consists of two sacred wells, a large hut, and other rooms. The various structures are surrounded by dry stone walls built in a "spine of the fish" pattern.
descriptions.NUR4237: The complex consists of two sacred wells, a large hut, and other rooms. The various structures are surrounded by dry stone walls built in a "spine of the fish" pattern.
descriptions.NUR20314: It has architectural features similar to those of sacred wells with a pointed-arch entrance. The inner basin is spacious and still collects the sacred water. As of July 2022 its state of preservation is very poor, and the well is not widely known.
descriptions.NUR11751: It has a feature never described before: it is built "in the round": the water collects in an apsidal rear body. "The structure, built in isodomic masonry using basaltic and trachytic ashlars, survives for a substantial portion of its base (Fig. 1), which reveals an oblong ground plan, articulated into a straight entrance forecourt and an apsidal rear body containing the spring-water collection cell."
descriptions.NUR9871: It appears ruined and covered by thick patches of brambles and thorny bushes.
descriptions.NUR2411: Source very likely of Nuragic origin.
descriptions.NUR19145: The sacred well is in good condition, despite its basic architectural elements having been tampered with several times. It is built of medium and large trachyte blocks and has a corridor paved with regular boulders, 5.10 m long, leading to a circular tholos chamber with a domed vault that encloses the water vein. The corridor was originally fitted with benches along the side walls.
descriptions.NUR11034: The territory, today almost entirely devoid of vegetation, must have been greener and richer in water at the time of the nuraghi: the springs, now neglected, were clean and well kept until thirty years ago. Even then it is likely that small circular structures were built around many of them, made of large blocks and covered by small vaults with an opening for the water, to keep them clean, as we can see in the remains of Funtana Gureu.
descriptions.NUR11631: Typical nuragic well with stakes made of ashlar stones and a lintel closure. Interior features a water collection basin.
descriptions.NUR14673: The spring has no steps and is in an almost perfect state of preservation[1]. The wall structure, entirely of granite, is completely preserved and the entrance to the inner chamber consists of a large vaulted opening. The spring is covered with two granite slabs. It encloses a spring vein, still active, and has a large threshold stone at the front with a channel cut into it for the water to drain away.
descriptions.NUR10717: Small nuragic spring with remains of the original cell built over the spring's source and faint traces of the atrium.
descriptions.NUR15306: In its upper part the corridor appears to have been cut by excavating into the sandstone rock. Below it is covered with soil; the depth is unknown but the distance between the walls is certainly greater further down. Of the conical structure of the well proper, parts made of worked ashlars are visible, especially on our left and in the upper part straight ahead, while the part on the right and the central lower part seem to have been emptied of ashlars, as if they had been taken for other uses or had collapsed. The lower part of the spring is covered with mud.
descriptions.NUR12845: The Nuragic spring of Su Musuelu lies about 600 m east of the Nuragic sacred spring of Is Molineddus. From the little information Spano was able to gather, its temple consisted of a rectangular building with the entrance on the western side, built of large blocks laid dry. Behind the building a spring rose from the rock and collected in a round well, also made of large stones.
descriptions.NUR9811:
The remains of what appears to have been a classic-type Nuragic sacred well lie against a dry-stone wall marking the boundary between the territories of Birori and Borore, a few metres from the Bau Cannas hypogea.

At present only the circular base profile (diam. 1.40 m) and a masonry of two courses of well-worked stones are visible; the bottom, as far as can be seen through the standing water, seems to have paving slabs.
descriptions.NUR20062: The Sos Muros complex occupies an area of over twenty hectares, showing clear signs of circular huts and this sacred well.
descriptions.NUR13426: The S'Ulumu spring (Dorgali) has a circular cell with a short external vestibule, built in horizontal courses and covered by a tholos. Precisely because of its simple architectural and structural appearance, it had an essentially functional character as a water supply for the nearby village.
descriptions.NUR8419:
The archaeological area lies on the south slope of Monte Senes, in the Baronia, the region of Sardinia's east coast. The spring preserves the catchment basin of the natural spring, still fed, and the west part of the monumental façade.

A stretch of the enclosure-terrace wall oriented north-south also survives, built on the outcrop of the granitic rock.
descriptions.NUR21151: Cyclopean masonry circuit with typical features of Nuragic sources
descriptions.NUR10545: Sacred well nuragica, located a short distance from the complex nuraghe of Ardasai.
descriptions.NUR10749: The spring is located within the archaeological area of S'Orgioloniga, where the remains of a Nuragic settlement also exist.
descriptions.NUR10694: The spring consists of a main horseshoe-shaped body and a front enclosure of which a semicircular sector survives. The spring was already frequented in the pre-Nuragic period, as shown by some stemmed obsidian arrowheads and especially a ceramic fragment decorated in the Ozieri style.
descriptions.NUR14324:
A monument of exceptional value belonging to the final Nuragic period, when towers were no longer built and various "federal sanctuaries" were created, which frequently included sacred wells built of isodomic ashlars and enriched with architectural sculptural elements.

Unfortunately the sacred well is not looked after and is not kept constantly clean.
descriptions.NUR20053: It lies about 300 metres below the associated nuraghe. It is built of isodomic ashlar blocks. In the vestibule in front of it there are stone benches, and in front of the entrance a hole cut in the rock acts as an overflow for the threshold level. The spring is still active and functioning. A temporary structure of concrete blocks has been built all around the spring to protect it from the weather, vegetation and animals.
descriptions.NUR13086: The structure has a constant internal diameter of 4.30 m; the walls currently measure 2.80 m in height from the present floor, which is choked with rubble, up to the highest course of boulders, located opposite the entrance, from where the height decreases towards the entrance itself. Externally, walking around the building only the topmost row of boulders is visible; the rest is completely buried in sand deliberately piled there to form a truncated cone.
descriptions.NUR10068: It is not clear exactly what it is, perhaps a unique monument that combines a giants' tomb, a trilithic dolmen, and a Nuragic fortress. It was certainly a very important place for the defence of the territory and the clan. It is a sacred site in every sense, and it is no exaggeration to think of the crag there as the place where the rite of the Accabadora was performed. mu.
descriptions.NUR1328: It is a fine example of a fortress with a wall of large polygonal boulders following a vaguely circular course in broken lines from north round through west to south. To the east it takes advantage of the steep, almost vertical, inaccessible ridge overlooking the Ozieri plain. To the north there is a fine large dolmenic trilithon with a lintel. The entrance to the south is smaller. mu
descriptions.NUR5520: Dr Aste maintains that Su Doladorgiu was originally the fortress he has reconstructed, which was equipped with towers and a nuraghe. For strategic defence reasons it was built in the Nuragic period to keep watch over the whole valley, since attacks by enemies and invaders were feared from the sea.
descriptions.NUR5489:
The complex consists of an extensive settlement defended by a wall (length 120 m; maximum height 5.00 m): the north-eastern end is better preserved, where a tower is incorporated. In the central sector, probably protecting the entrance to the acropolis.

Halfway up the slope are the remains of a second fortification, built of large squared blocks. The village extends over the summit of the plateau and has numerous huts; the complex is datable to 1400–1000 BC.
descriptions.NUR2191:
The fortress was built by the Carthaginians, making use of a pre-existing Nuragic building; behind the wall traces of buildings can be seen that were probably Nuragic at first and later occupied by the Carthaginians.

The fortress is dated to the mid-4th century BC.
descriptions.NUR8733:
The temple consists of a small vestibule, a narrow descending staircase covered by a stepped lintel roof, and a circular chamber covered by a tholos.

The standing structures are now limited to the keyhole-shaped perimeter wall enclosing the atrium and the well drum. The vestibule, partly paved, has a rectangular plan: the bench-seat is absent. The staircase leading down to the well chamber, with vertical walls, is made up of 12 steps.
descriptions.NUR10071: The area has been fitted out as a rest and picnic spot with a large car park by the local poet Bainzeddu Truddaiu, who passed away recently. Together with his family and other friends he devoted himself to organising this space, where anyone can stop and refresh themselves.
descriptions.NUR9872: It is a bilobate structure of which only a portion remains, although several collapses have affected most of the structure. The trilithic and flat-laid junction is clearly visible and very interesting. mu
descriptions.NUR9873: At the level of ruin, with disconnected circles of large stones fallen in great disorder. Only a very reduced portion remains, indicating the presence of the site. mu
descriptions.NUR6760: The investigations have identified traces of human presence at the site dating from the period between the Late Neolithic (3300–2700 BC) and the Chalcolithic (2700–1700 BC). The most monumental evidence consists of the menhirs present at the site: single, in pairs, in triads, in spectacular alignments formed by as many as 20 menhirs, and in circles. Walking through the site one can see menhirs lying on the ground everywhere, whole or in fragments. The site must originally have been larger than it appears today.
descriptions.NUR6768: The investigations have identified traces of human presence at the site dating from the period between the Late Neolithic (3300–2700 BC) and the Chalcolithic (2700–1700 BC). descriptions.NUR19419: Sa Ohe (the mouth) connects through submerged passages with the nearby Su Ventu cave. It is mistakenly known as Sa Oche, wrongly translated as "the voice", and has been known and visited since very ancient times.
descriptions.NUR19673: A small karst cavity damaged by illegal excavators. Following excavations carried out during the last years of the 1800s, the site yielded a series of metal artefacts, including a bronze boat, two swords and an iron dagger, an iron horse bit, four cups and a bronze cup, a bronze vessel and a ceramic olla containing twenty-two copper fragments. A boat depicting a bovine head found during the 1960s.
descriptions.NUR14424: The cave is about 130 metres long and consists essentially of three chambers. Important archaeological finds have been made inside, in particular some human remains dated to about 20,000 years ago, which constitute the earliest evidence of Homo sapiens in Sardinia. The famous Sardinian bandit Giovanni Corbeddu took refuge in this cave, from which it takes its name.
descriptions.NUR8173: A complex cave with three entrances (two of them artificial), heavily disturbed and stripped of its formations because it was partly used in the past as an onyx quarry and as a wartime shelter. It was frequented during the Early Bronze Age. A small park has been laid out at the entrance, managed by an association that periodically organises guided tours.
descriptions.NUR8188: A natural cave characterised by a large hall used as a sacred area where various votive offerings (lamps and miniature pots) were found on a natural rock altar shaped like a bench. It was frequented from the Neolithic to the Iron Age and includes the San Ciriaco, Bonannaro and Nuragic cultures.
descriptions.NUR16542: Connected with the Grotta di sa Ucca de su Tintirriolu. It opens through a tiny gap among stones and then earth (hard to find), followed by a deep, dangerous shaft 28 m deep. Exploration is NOT RECOMMENDED! even for experienced cavers, because the shaft does not open into solid rock.
descriptions.NUR19609: At the foot of the nuraghe, beneath a rocky outcrop, there is a cave used as a water cistern. The cave entrance has been narrowed by the construction of masonry structures, built by superimposing trachyte boulders of various shapes and sizes, which thus increased the capacity of the water cistern. Its interior is full of stones and mud.
descriptions.NUR19948: An important natural cavity called Grotta de su Mrajani, which has yielded evidence (pottery) of Early Neolithic man, even before cultures such as Bonu Ighinu or San Michele di Ozieri.
descriptions.NUR8244: Natural cave used as a storehouse for large containers for foodstuffs dating to the Middle Bronze Age, with items found on site completely intact.
descriptions.NUR12924: Cave used during the early phases of the Nuragic civilization, known for the discovery of three, older, "Mother Goddess" bone statuettes.
descriptions.NUR8186: Natural cave with a wide entrance opening onto a small chamber, followed by a drop leading to a deeper inner chamber. Inside, material datable from the Neolithic (especially Bonannaro) has been found, indicating that the cave was inhabited.
descriptions.NUR8187: Natural cave with a wide entrance followed by a step and an underlying chamber. Inside, Neolithic and Bronze Age material, belonging to the Bonannaro culture, has been found.
descriptions.NUR19801: The Nuragic structures that closed the two entrances to the Domusnovas cave were already described in 1840 by Angius. He says that at the first entrance, on the left, there are the remains of a cyclopean wall that closed it off. A small doorway by the cave wall is as high as the ordinary stature of a man; to the left of the doorway a staircase 1.30 m wide led up onto the rampart where there were merlons and loopholes. At the exit there is another wall 3.20 m thick.
descriptions.NUR16544: It is the largest and most important cave of Bonu Ighinu. It has recently been connected with the overlying Grotta del Pozzaccio. Morphologically the cavity can be divided into two main parts: the fossil branch, which is the initial one, and the active branch, crossed along its entire length by a stream; the large hall in the innermost part is also fossil. Overall the cave is 740 m long and its spatial development is 1500 m.
descriptions.NUR8182: Large cave composed of a single chamber used from the early Middle Bronze Age, where materials belonging to the Bonannaro culture have been found.
descriptions.NUR19675:
A large cavern extending for about 40 metres, with an archaeological deposit disturbed by guano diggers and clandestine excavators.

From the disturbed layers come ceramic materials ranging from the second half of the 5th millennium BC to the Republican period.
descriptions.NUR10914:
The visitable part consists of numerous chambers adorned with concretions, stalactites and stalagmites (the tallest measures 11 metres), columns rising up to 15 m, aragonite crystals and underground lakes.

Inside, the remains of several oil votive lamps of Nuragic origin and artefacts of Phoenician and Roman date have in fact been found.
descriptions.NUR19677: The cave contains internal wall remnants and artefacts; it is not ruled out that it was used as a smelting site.
descriptions.NUR8287: Natural cave composed of a single chamber within which prehistoric fragments are visible. The cave has been severely damaged by illegal excavation activities.
descriptions.NUR8285: A natural cave used in prehistoric times as a mass burial site. It has a shaft entrance and some artificial steps. Outside, a wall remnant is still visible, badly damaged by quarrying. The area is fenced off; visiting is not recommended and is dangerous.
descriptions.NUR19938: In 1968, about 150 metres from the entrance, the Treasure Chamber was found: hundreds of bowls were stacked in three large piles. A broken stalagmitic column served as an altar: a bronze tripod, a votive boat, several daggers, bracelets and rings were placed on it. Beside the altar was the hearth, where animal bones were found, evidence of ritual sacrifices. The C14 dating falls between 820 and 730 BC.
descriptions.NUR8032: Series of natural caves used in the Neolithic for collective burials. Remains of the Monte Claro culture.
descriptions.NUR6944: It is an artificial cave cut into the tufa and altered over the centuries, most likely from a domus de janas into a building for the grape harvest or a store for agricultural produce or a shelter for tools. There are many clues pointing to such a sequence.
descriptions.NUR19571: Of particular importance is the cave known as "Su Stampu VI", where pre-Nuragic and Nuragic artifacts have been found.
descriptions.NUR21138: Artificial grotto with access, pseudo-quadrilateral and large.
descriptions.NUR12896: Natural with modifications, it dates to the Bonnanaro culture period (2200–1800 BC). Used as a burial site.
descriptions.NUR12143: A scattered group of menhirs on the ground.
descriptions.NUR19476:
These natural cavities are among the largest and most beautiful in Sardinia: their rectangular entrance is set in a lush holm-oak forest.

The caves, easily visited, were according to ancient legend the dwelling of three janas (fairies) who were turned to stone by God for killing a friar.

The cave walls are covered with marble-like flows and draperies. From the ceiling it seems almost as if a storm of white stalactites hangs over the visitor.
descriptions.NUR14665:
Uncertain location, to be defined. Single petroglyph

It overlooks the upper part of the settlement of Baunei and echoes the name of the domus de janas. It is a depiction consisting of a total of 18 shallow channels that branch from a main basin several centimetres deep, joining various terminal cupmarks arranged without any apparent order.
descriptions.NUR639: From the information I have, it should be a single-tower nuraghe of which only a few traces remain.
descriptions.NUR16209: These are the remains of a nuraghe that is difficult to classify typologically; the collapses and the dense shrub vegetation growing on the exposed masonry do not allow a proper survey. However, the data gathered during repeated inspections of the site, which among other things made it possible to locate the entrance facing north-west, lead me to hypothesise that it may belong to the class of so-called corridor nuraghi with an associated settlement.
descriptions.NUR11746:
The Nuragic village-sanctuary of Abini is one of the most famous and important in Nuragic Sardinia.

It consists of numerous huts and a sacred well protected by an enclosure. The huts are predominantly circular in plan.
descriptions.NUR18619: The interpretation of these buildings is that during festivals the Nuragic people (and not only them?) traded all kinds of goods, taking advantage of the large influx of people. Besides the "stands" there are two circular meeting huts and a livestock enclosure.
descriptions.NUR12965: Nuragic settlement or sacred site, reused up to the Roman period. Basements of different structures from various historical periods are present.
descriptions.NUR11727: The area, located on the north-western slope of the comune of Giave, includes the remains of a nuraghe, possibly a giants' tomb, and an attached settlement.
descriptions.NUR18908: About 200 m from the rise in the ground that marks the nuraghe, to the north-north-east, a settlement is visible covering an area of 600–700 sq m and showing a series of rooms with a quadrilateral plan bounded by large trachyte boulders.
descriptions.NUR5611: About 200 m from the rise in the ground that marks the nuraghe, to the north-north-east, a settlement is visible covering an area of 600–700 sq m and showing a series of rooms with a quadrilateral plan bounded by large trachyte boulders.
descriptions.NUR17821:
Remains of a building divided into several rooms (vaguely rectangular in plan) bounded by walls built of medium-sized stones and clay mortar. In particular, seven steps of a staircase that linked floors at different levels survive.

Among the surface finds, Phoenician pottery fragments and Nuragic vessel forms of the Early Iron Age have been identified.
descriptions.NUR18886:
North-west of the Muntone nuraghe, from which they can be reached by a path, lie first a settlement and then the megalithic tomb of Tanca Noa.

The settlement, which appears to extend for about 400 sq m, consists of the remains of structures whose ground plans are not easily defined; the wall structures, of which only the basal course survives, are built in the double-skin technique, using trachyte and dry-stone construction.
descriptions.NUR18880: About 100 metres west of the nuraghe, a small settlement has been recorded, consisting of the remains of a cluster of at least five circular huts and a rectangular building. South of the nuraghe, about 500 metres away, the basal courses of two circular huts and other short stretches of curvilinear walls in trachyte are visible, while about 400 metres south-west of the nuraghe lie the remains of a circular hut.
descriptions.NUR10627: Situated at about 176 m above sea level, marked on the topographic map as Nuraghe. This complex of dry-stone walls has a variable height between 40 and 110 cm. The plan of these walls is circular in some rooms and squared in others.
descriptions.NUR19200: A dozen circular huts and enclosures.
descriptions.NUR16328: Name inspired by which the director Mauro Aragoni drew for his short film "Nuraghes S'Arena"
descriptions.NUR12532:
It is located within the municipal territory of Monastir (CA).

The archaeological area was discovered during excavation works for the 131.
descriptions.NUR11375: It is the "father of all the nuraghes", the proto-nuraghe Madugui (local name) or Maduli (archaeological designation), which projects prominently on the south-eastern edge of the upland. Today its walls are four metres and a half high, though they were once taller. It is one of the most significant examples of proto-nuraghe architecture (or pseudo-nuraghe) – a prototype of the "corridor nuraghes", later evolving into towers or clusters of towers closed in a false dome (tholos).
descriptions.NUR4886: It is the "father of all the nuraghes", the proto-nuraghe Madugui (local name) or Maduli (archaeological designation), which projects prominently on the south-eastern edge of the upland. Today its walls are four metres and a half high, though they were once taller. It is one of the most significant examples of proto-nuraghe architecture (or pseudo-nuraghe) – a prototype of the "corridor nuraghes", later evolving into towers or clusters of towers closed in a false dome (tholos).
descriptions.NUR11027: The archaeological site of Bruncu Suergiu lies in the Giara Park. Hidden by vegetation and hard to reach. Traces of ancient routes, a large settlement with production facilities, and defensive structures characterise the site. Besides the huge quantity of material, a broad terrace looks out over the Campidano, offering a breathtaking view. Only the panorama repays the long and difficult walk. The archaeological area, which is protected, covers about 11 hectares.
descriptions.NUR10882: The settlement consisted of a complex nuraghe with the village around it, whose clear ruins are preserved by a thriving thicket of mastic and wild olive. The most important nucleus of the ancient settlement developed around a circular depression in the ground that served as a small catchment basin for rainwater in the winter and spring months.
descriptions.NUR5060: The settlement consisted of a complex nuraghe with the village around it, whose clear ruins are preserved by a thriving thicket of mastic and wild olive. The most important nucleus of the ancient settlement developed around a circular depression in the ground that served as a small catchment basin for rainwater in the winter and spring months.
descriptions.NUR12234: The site comprises the nuraghe and the remains of an extensive village. The presence of two burials is also reported: a giants' tomb and a burial known as "dei gigli" because lilies appear to grow there in abundance.
descriptions.NUR18091: Originally it was intended to form, together with that of the nearby N.ghe Ena Ortu, a single extensive settlement.
descriptions.NUR8168: A settlement of which few traces remain, situated on the hill facing Monte Cannas in a place not recommended for visits because it was affected in the 1930s and 1940s by quarrying activity with unfenced dangerous areas. The settlement can be dated between the Bronze Age and the Roman period, passing through the Nuragic culture.
descriptions.NUR11621: Remains of a Nuragic village composed of about fifty huts. Communication took place through underground passages, many of which are still unexplored today. One notes the presence of the "meeting hut", conspicuously restored.
descriptions.NUR11620: It includes some tafons, which are thought to have been used both in funerary and domestic contexts.
descriptions.NUR2404: complex nuraghe with a village nearby
descriptions.NUR12443:
It is located within the municipal territory of Orosei (NU).

In the area there should also be a rudimentary sacred well.
descriptions.NUR17387:
It is a village of considerable size; dozens of circular structures can be made out on the ground, mainly to the south-west of the nuraghe of the same name.

Given the presence of four other nuraghi within a radius of just a few kilometres and an exceptional view over the Gulf of Asinara (on clear days ships off Porto Torres are clearly visible), the village probably played a strategic role.
descriptions.NUR10778: At the Sa Brèca site two buildings are currently clearly distinguishable: the Sacred Well Temple and a sub-circular hut with benches along the walls. The whole complex appears to be enclosed by a temenos that must have separated the Sacred Area from the nearby settlement (not yet investigated by excavation sondages).
descriptions.NUR18726:
The site includes a corridor nuraghe, a circular tower nuraghe with a tholos, two giants' tombs, a sacred well, a Roman necropolis and the ruins of a country church.

The country church preserves only a wall of two square metres. The circular nuraghe and everything else listed above are practically invisible. The corridor nuraghe is entirely covered by dense vegetation, so only a few stones can be seen. Unfortunately, as of April 2013, a visit is not recommended.
descriptions.NUR11047: The building consists of a central tower and a four-lobed bastion with an internal courtyard. The outer wall face of the main tower, of which only a single course belonging to the first-floor chamber is visible, is built in isodomic masonry with sandstone blocks. Inside, the opening of the mural staircase can be seen to the south.
descriptions.NUR10441: The village that arose in the subsequent Late Bronze Age phase (1365–1200 BC) is characterised by numerous wells dug next to dwellings, some of them sunken into the ground, others provided with a masonry plinth. At present, after the recent excavations, the area has been entirely covered over.
descriptions.NUR12405:
In the Sas Seddas area, not far from the eponymous megalithic tombs site, some ceramic finds of certain Nuragic attribution have been recovered.

No structural traces are visible at the site. The owner of the pinnetta reports that during excavation work an unspecified “channel” cut into the rock came to light, of unknown length and depth; it has since been reburied. The ceramic material consists mainly of cooking-pot fragments.
descriptions.NUR19551: Remains of the Nuragic village Siseri Alto embedded in the vegetation
descriptions.NUR12412: Inside an olive grove, ploughing has brought to light numerous ceramic finds of various periods; among the prehistoric coarseware, fragments of typically Nuragic vessels such as cooking pots and baking trays can be identified without any doubt. No obvious structures are visible, as the site has undergone constant agricultural changes.
descriptions.NUR12217:
It lies in the municipality of Nuxis (CI).

It was linked to the nearby Nuragic well, as is found at other archaeological sites (Santa Vittoria di Serri, Sant'Anastasia a Sardara, Su Putzu ad Orroli, etc.).
descriptions.NUR11923: It is a Nuragic village on Monte Tiscali inside a doline, destroyed by the Romans and by tomb robbers; the bases of the huts can be seen, and of one a part of the walling still stands. It is very difficult to reach — 45 minutes' walk — because you have to climb a steep mule track strewn with stones and pass through a fissure in the rock if you come from Oliena; in compensation you will enjoy a view over the limestone mountains of the Supramonte.
descriptions.NUR1274: The settlement, which originally must have extended as far as to merge with that of N.ghe Maiore, consists of numerous building remains that still await investigation by experts. As at nearby Maiore, remains of rectangular-plan dwellings can be seen.
descriptions.NUR11176: Remains of a possible Nuragic settlement currently located at the centre of a road ramp.
descriptions.NUR18102: Settlement belonging to the single-tower nuraghe with outer wall
descriptions.NUR10696:
On the illustrative map of Tharros and at the archaeological site it is marked with number 15.

The tophet was established by the Phoenicians and then the Carthaginians, who had already found the Nuragic structures present.
descriptions.NUR3374: The site consists essentially of two parts: the first, formed by the well temple, a sacred well dating to the Nuragic period, with structures attached to it: a meeting hut, an enclosure, and other smaller huts. The second part of the complex, about two hundred metres to the south-west, consists of a single-tower nuraghe, some elongated stone huts of uncertain date, and a Nuragic village, still to be excavated, of which only a few emerging elements are visible.
descriptions.NUR10718: Remains of some Nuragic huts with curved plans, adjacent to one another, rise within an old courtyard built with dry-stone masonry.
descriptions.NUR12866:
The site is distinguished by the presence of a Nuragic-period settlement documented by the discovery, during private building work, of wall structures attributable to the Iron Age.

It consists of a stretch of a structure in isodomic ashlars of tufaceous marl datable to Early Iron Age, whose function has not yet been clarified.
descriptions.NUR14835: It was the earliest settlement in the Villanovaforru area. A short distance from a spring, unfortunately no traces of it remain. A Bonnanaro Culture tomb was found, dated to the Early Bronze Age between 1700 and 1600 BC, together with fragments of a tripod vase and obsidian arrowheads; no osteological remains or tomb structures were recovered. The isolated find is to be interpreted as an open-air site or a funerary deposition.
descriptions.NUR11365: Pre-Nuragic/Nuragic settlement. Remains of two huts were still present up to twenty years ago, but one of the two was dismantled to make room for ploughs.
descriptions.NUR12458: In the light of all this, an area adjacent to the village of Puisteris must have been established at Serra Neba, probably used for livestock breeding and perhaps also for agriculture. The archaeological material recovered, securely attributable to the Ozieri culture, attests to the occupation of the area during the final phases of the Neolithic.
descriptions.NUR11173: The discovery of the Monte Idda hoard (Decimoputzu), which took place towards the end of 1914, was described by Taramelli as “perfectly accidental”, and on this subject the famous archaeologist wrote that “two shepherds from Desulo, who were grazing their herds on the mountain known as Sa Idda, found under some loose granite boulders, inside the remains of a terracotta vessel, a mass of bronze weapons and tools, together with ingots and ingot fragments, slag and scrap pieces of the same metal…”.
descriptions.NUR12887: The Tomba di Bau su Matutzu (3rd millennium BC) is located within an olive grove inside the Ecoserdiana dump.
descriptions.NUR12835: In this hypogeum dating to the Middle Neolithic (4600–4000 BC) several interesting finds were recovered, including a tetrapod limestone dish with a bull's-head protome. This is described as one of the oldest depictions of a bucranium in Sardinia. A bucranium is the figure of an animal head with the horns pointing upwards. On display at the Cagliari Archaeological Museum.
descriptions.NUR19516: Hypogeic temple in the Pitzu 'e toni area. It faces south. A wide entrance two metres long leads to a fork: the right branch is narrow, the left one wider. The name itself recalls its function. In the early 1960s, during an inspection, Prof. Lilliu found a little necklace made of round animal bone beads.
descriptions.NUR21155: Externally two small windows are visible, 1.6 m above the floor level, about 35 cm square. The entrance opening, 1.60 m high and 1.30 m wide, has a step down of 35 cm leading into the chamber. About 4 m wide, 3 m deep and 2.5 m high, it has at its centre a circular pit 60 cm across and 10 cm deep, set slightly to the right of the entrance.
descriptions.NUR10294: Perhaps a Neolithic burial site; Roman and medieval tombs have been identified there over time. Witnesses report that in the 1940s and 1950s, while ploughing with a wooden plough, numerous human bones and fragments of tegulae and imbrices came to light. This was even more evident when the same person (my father Giovanni, almost a centenarian, now deceased) ploughed with an iron Birindelli plough, which turned the soil at a greater depth.
descriptions.NUR12881: Monte Claro culture underground chamber discovered during works at "nuova 554". It consists of two underground chambers with vertical access shafts and various funerary furnishings.
descriptions.NUR19566: Columnar basalts are majestic basalt formations whose presence indicates submarine eruptive activity or the existence of ancient, now extinct volcanoes in the area. Is Aruttas Santas are a typical example of these basalt formations; we are on Monte Arci in the territory of Villaurbana.
descriptions.NUR10341: When the Rio Murrone joins the Rio Oloitti, several hundred metres further downstream, it drops about twenty metres, forming a waterfall of foaming, roaring water in a wild and captivating setting of unspoilt, primordial nature. The river has a winter torrent character, ceasing altogether in the driest summers.
descriptions.NUR19831: North-west of the nuraghe there is a small pond fed by spring water, which is present even in summer, albeit in very small amounts. The pond has a completely natural, irregular triangular shape. The deepest point reaches the overflow level at about 120 cm.
descriptions.NUR19740: In the Is Noccus area there are two ponds, the first at the foot of the nuraghe and the other about 200 m away. The first, at the south-west base of the nuraghe, was created by using a natural lake basin. The pond is circular and shows clear signs of human intervention aimed at catching rainwater and increasing its storage capacity; boulders of various sizes can be seen placed around the edges of the basin for most of its perimeter.
descriptions.NUR16247: Near the nuraghe, scattered over an extensive area (about 12 hectares), the remains of numerous structures with circular plans (generally over 7 m in diameter) and rectilinear plans can be seen, attributable to the ancient settlement and probably also belonging to a sacred area. The wall profiles are double-faced, built with large and medium-sized blocks of basalt or trachyte. To the south-east, at a distance of about 90 metres from the nuraghe, a plateau stands out
descriptions.NUR8473: It is a anthropomorphic rock whose appearance is likened to the face of the Egyptian sphinx.
descriptions.NUR19885: The Tomb of the Three Hundred is the most remarkable monument and part of a larger necropolis discovered during construction of the SS 131. It takes its name from the number of skeletons found inside the walls surrounding the inhumation area.
descriptions.NUR13409: Tomb II, particularly grand, has its entrance, antechamber and burial chamber cut into two separate rock blocks that were brought to the site and laid on a carefully prepared rubble bed; the fine stonework, done with a pick, and the architectural and planimetric design faithfully echo domus de janas burials.
descriptions.NUR14994: The tomb is considerably disturbed in parts, also due to illegal excavations; it preserves (a rare case for the area) a (likely) large fragment of the central stele of the exedra.
descriptions.NUR10191: In the territory of sa Loca, on the border with that of sa punta de Bonanotte, the farming family, besides cultivating a few arable fields, an orchard and an olive grove, also ran a vineyard that needed a place for the grape harvest. So, on the hard limestone they cut the treading vat (in Sardinian su lacu) for pressing and the drainage vat for collecting the must in a smaller tank (in Sardinian s'ischintorzu).
descriptions.NUR10196: It is an isolated, tree-covered hillock shaped like a cone on a plateau, on which various boulders of different shapes, from conical-prismatic to parallelepiped, are set. The setting is evocative, and stories are told of events that take place during sacred or initiatory-propitiatory ceremonies.
descriptions.NUR19862: Stone forming part of a group of five stone blocks. It is characterized by a flat anterior surface and a convex posterior surface.
descriptions.NUR21120: A massive wall structure (16.25 x 10.35 m; 168 m²) with a double wall face (4–2.2 m thick) encloses an open internal space accessed through a corridor roofed with slabs. The detail of the staircase leading to the top of the wall is a strong point of analogy with Monte Baranta.
descriptions.NUR2125: This structure is marked as a nuragic well and is located near a livestock water trough.
descriptions.NUR20291: Originally the menhir complex consisted of 12 menhirs arranged in a circle. Today only one remains, about two metres high. The others have disappeared, possibly removed for construction work.
descriptions.NUR6850: It is located near the homonymous nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR6820:
150 m from the second group of domus de janas, at the foot of Monte Corru Tundu, stands a colossal monolith of trachyte tuff with a truncated top (surviving height 5.75 m). The menhir, one of the largest in Sardinia, is strongly tapered, with one face flattened and the other rounded; on the latter three circular cup-marks appear to be visible.

The monolith and the necropolis served the settlement of Monte Padrillonis. (San Michele culture, 3200–2800 BC).
descriptions.NUR6809: The Cuili Piras site behind M. Su Crobu. The surrounding land is ploughed and reaching the place is rather difficult. Unfortunately, not long ago the area was devastated by an extensive fire. It lies inside a private property and it is best to inform the landowners of your presence.
descriptions.NUR6798: The Boeli stele, also known as Sa Perda Pintà, is a large statue-menhir of granite (height 2.67 m). It bears motifs consisting of a minimum of two up to a maximum of seven concentric circles obtained by incisions that develop around a central cup-mark.
descriptions.NUR6766: A short distance from the hypogeal tomb of Putzu, on the other side of the farm track that crosses the locality of Busola, two menhirs have been identified. One of the menhirs is still fixed in the ground in its original position. A second menhir, with a pointed lateral profile and an elliptical cross-section, flat on the longer side, is incorporated into the doorpost of the field entrance.
descriptions.NUR20295: The megalithic settlement, now completely destroyed, was located near Casa Manis. Only a menhir remains in the area later occupied by a Roman settlement.
descriptions.NUR6787: More similar to a stele than a menhir, having a parabolic arch shape. A dolmen is present in the vicinity.
descriptions.NUR6844: Isolated menhir, on its back bearing an alignment of cups.
descriptions.NUR6813: In this area, used for cultivation for many years, eight monoliths were found during ploughing; five of them still lie on the ground today. These menhirs, all made from a single block of local trachyte, have an average height of 180 cm and present one flat face and one convex face.
descriptions.NUR12081: It is a sacred area composed of seven menhirs, six of which are heaped nearby about ninety metres to the west, piled up during land-clearing work. This one, however, simply lies on the ground, unique in the area, finely shaped, 6.20 m long.
descriptions.NUR6826: The alignment of closely spaced stones at Serra Pillonadori stands on the south-western slopes of the Su Niu de is Crobus ridge and west of the Baccu Ungroneddus, in a position from which the valley of S. Barbara and the Rio Solanas can be taken in at a single glance and which is visible from practically every point of the inner ridges and valleys below. The five granite stones of which it consists are arranged on a north–south axis and face east.
descriptions.NUR6781: The three granite menhirs stand on the slope of the saddle: the first, aniconic (length 4.25 m; width 0.98 m; thickness 0.60 m) — pointed and split into two pieces — lies on the ground; the second — re-erected in the 1970s — is of proto-anthropomorphic type with an ogival shape and a plano-convex cross-section; the third, also proto-anthropomorphic, has an ogival shape and a flattened plano-convex cross-section. Two menhirs face each other frontally, almost as if marking a passage.
descriptions.NUR6823: A pre-Nuragic menhir about 5 metres high, still standing upright. The menhir was named after a giantess who often appears in Sardinian folk legends. The presence of many other menhirs in the area testifies to the widespread diffusion of religious practices linked to megalithism.
descriptions.NUR6840: Located within an area designated for sheep grazing, near the course of the river of the same name.
descriptions.NUR6812: The Pranu Muttedu park is one of the most evocative archaeological sites in inland Sardinia. The park area is divided into two parts, for a total extension of about 200,000 sq m. Excavations have brought to light numerous artefacts attributable to settled communities of the "Ozieri" culture dating to the Late Neolithic (3200–2800 BC). The archaeological complex has the highest concentration of menhirs known in Sardinia.
descriptions.NUR19753: About 250 m from the Nuraghe Noccus, on a rocky outcrop, there are: a very unusual tafone, now partly collapsed; three large monoliths (about 250 cm high), set a short distance apart, which could be menhirs; numerous boulders of various unusual shapes, in some cases next to the monoliths, in others scattered without a clear order but close to them. In the opinion of a (female) archaeologist, the menhirs do indeed seem to mark out the funerary space.
descriptions.NUR6845: The menhir, located within a flat field, is about 1.67 m high, with cup-shaped decorations.
descriptions.NUR6803: A very unusual menhir, pierced at multiple points, possibly artificially.
descriptions.NUR20404: It is located about 500 m east of the Is Perdas Croccadas menhir. In recent times it has been reconstructed and restored from three large fragments.
descriptions.NUR6774: The two menhirs are located about fifty metres apart.
descriptions.NUR6839: The menhir, known as Su Furconi de Luxia Arrabiosa, stands alone on a small plateau. It is quadrangular, tapering towards the top into an almost conical shape, and measures 3.60 m in height. On its main face, which faces east, twelve small cup-marks are carved.
descriptions.NUR6769: Located near the homonymous nuraghe, some giants' tombs are observed, concealed by dense vegetation that also partially hides the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR6796: At this site, within a distance of a couple of hundred metres, there are monuments dating from the Abealzu culture, 2700–2400 BC, the Early Bronze Age with the Nuragic wall, and the Bronze Age up to the Roman period, marked by the probable tombs.
descriptions.NUR3214: At this site, within a distance of a couple of hundred metres, there are monuments dating from the Abealzu culture, 2700–2400 BC, the Early Bronze Age with the Nuragic wall, and the Bronze Age up to the Roman period, marked by the probable tombs.
descriptions.NUR6811: Three or more granite menhirs placed near the homonymous nuraghe
descriptions.NUR6791:
There were two, but now only one can be seen intact, while the other lies overturned on the ground, broken into several pieces. They are located within the municipal territory of Sassari.

Nearby the remains of a dolmen should be found.
descriptions.NUR6836:
THE PISCINA'E SALI SITE. The archaeological area is reached by following an agricultural track that starts from Via Cimitero, continuing straight on at the junction at Gedilis and crossing the Pranu Corongiu plateau until the right-hand side road.

The area certainly played a prominent role in the past as regards religious manifestations; no fewer than ten menhirs have been found in the valley and are associated with the funerary contexts of Pranu Corongiu
descriptions.NUR6802: The menhir placed beside the ramp leading to the upper part of the altar was raised prior to the construction of the altar itself. It was the centre of a Neolithic village.
descriptions.NUR6810:
It is located near the campsite of the same name.

It consists of 25 menhirs, 22 of which are standing (but only five in their original position, as the others have been erected by the archaeological site's construction team).
descriptions.NUR6818: These two menhirs are attributable to the Ozieri Culture (4th millennium BC) and, for archaeologists, represent the Mother Goddess and the Bull God, characteristic symbols of other Sardinian prehistoric monuments such as the domus de janas, inside which they were depicted, and recurring also in Nuragic civilisation, especially in the bull-shaped form of the giants' tombs. Over time they have kept their original position and their function as votive monuments.
descriptions.NUR6777: The monolith, finely worked basalt, stands on a flat terrain less than 100 m from a domus de janas known as "Su forru'e su Taleri".
descriptions.NUR6814:
Probable location.

It consists of 4 menhirs.
descriptions.NUR19738: Menhir located about 40 m from the Nuraghe de Chirigu. The menhir has three faces: the two opposite ones are roughly semicircular with a flat surface, while the third, rear face is convex. Natural fissures and hollows can be seen, together with smooth areas that are probably not natural.
descriptions.NUR6776: Small menhir placed along the road facing the junction to Rocca Doria
descriptions.NUR19812: The menhir Sa Perda de s'Omini stands on a promontory at an altitude of about 230 m above sea level. It is a monolith whose shape is probably the work of weathering. It has the appearance of a human face. Some believe it was connected with the ancient cult of the Mother Goddess, especially given the presence of remains of ill-defined structures next to one of the two monoliths. In ancient times, and still today, it is regarded as the centre of the Island.
descriptions.NUR6779: It consists of two menhirs repositioned in the area.
descriptions.NUR6828: Series of menhirs in the area of Brentoni
descriptions.NUR10127: A small alignment of menhirs appears on the slope leading to Mamucada inside the plot of sa Figu on the border with the land of Padedda. On closer inspection they seem little worked and of a shape vaguely comparable to a pyramid prism with a polygonal base that is never the same. According to the old people most of them come from the steep part of Badde Saltara, which looks over the plain of S.M de Orria Pitzinna. mu
descriptions.NUR12951:
It is located in the territory of the comune of Tortolì (OG).

It consists of three menhirs laid on the ground, two broken into two parts and one small, resembling a baetyl.

They are undoubtedly the remains of a megalithic sanctuary.
descriptions.NUR6807:
The Perda Longa archaeological complex, situated in a hilly area a few kilometres from Tortolì, comprises fifteen menhirs, most of them fallen, two giants' tombs (these are not easy to locate) and three nuraghi on the surrounding hills.

Among the perdas fittas (the Sardinian name for menhirs), several blocks stand over 4 metres high. The archaeological site dates to the fourth millennium BC (pre-Nuragic), but continued to be frequented into the Roman period.
descriptions.NUR5469:
The Perda Longa archaeological complex, situated in a hilly area a few kilometres from Tortolì, comprises fifteen menhirs, most of them fallen, two giants' tombs (these are not easy to locate) and three nuraghi on the surrounding hills.

Among the perdas fittas (the Sardinian name for menhirs), several blocks stand over 4 metres high. The archaeological site dates to the fourth millennium BC (pre-Nuragic), but continued to be frequented into the Roman period.
descriptions.NUR5260:
The Perda Longa archaeological complex, situated in a hilly area a few kilometres from Tortolì, comprises fifteen menhirs, most of them fallen, two giants' tombs (these are not easy to locate) and three nuraghi on the surrounding hills.

Among the perdas fittas (the Sardinian name for menhirs), several blocks stand over 4 metres high. The archaeological site dates to the fourth millennium BC (pre-Nuragic), but continued to be frequented into the Roman period.
descriptions.NUR1321:
The Perda Longa archaeological complex, situated in a hilly area a few kilometres from Tortolì, comprises fifteen menhirs, most of them fallen, two giants' tombs (these are not easy to locate) and three nuraghi on the surrounding hills.

Among the perdas fittas (the Sardinian name for menhirs), several blocks stand over 4 metres high. The archaeological site dates to the fourth millennium BC (pre-Nuragic), but continued to be frequented into the Roman period.
descriptions.NUR6773: The concentration of menhirs in this area is considerable; they are in close continuity with those at Ovau, S'Aspiddarju, and Teularju. The menhir FIRULI in the vicinity and along a stretch of 6 metres and 60 cm.
descriptions.NUR11476:
Originally there were three, but only one remains standing.

Probable location.
descriptions.NUR6817: The Pranu Muttedu park is one of the most evocative archaeological sites in inland Sardinia. The park area is divided into two parts, for a total extension of about 200,000 sq m. Excavations have brought to light very numerous artefacts attributable to settled communities of the "Ozieri" culture dating to the Late Neolithic (3200–2800 BC). The archaeological complex has the highest concentration of menhirs known in Sardinia.
descriptions.NUR18506: It consists of several menhirs and fragments recovered during land reclamation.
descriptions.NUR12837: The Menhir Terra Coccoi is located on a hilltop at about 1 km north-east of Nuraxi Figus. It has a remaining height of about 2 metres.
descriptions.NUR11175: This is a monument that is probably Nuragic, in which the remains of a cistern can be identified, perhaps originally roofed with a tholos, and an adjoining building of elongated rectangular shape, built with rubble-core masonry.
descriptions.NUR14866: Pre-Nuragic and Nuragic village, of which only very few traces remain, already disappeared by the end of the Bronze Age.
descriptions.NUR7347: It is probably the door closure of a domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR842: Unlikely remains of a nuragic structure.
descriptions.NUR2395: Probable dismantled nuraghe located to the north-east; nearby there is a megalithic wall.
descriptions.NUR3662: A particular site with two different classifications. The first census defined the structure as "Nuraghe Crastu Ruju", the second as "Muraglia megalitica di Giusei", in the style of the more famous wall of Monte Baranta.
descriptions.NUR17375: It is uncertain whether the site dates to the Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR17231: Nuragic megalithic enclosure of probable defensive use, later repurposed in the Roman period, as evidenced by the presence of pottery fragments on the ground.
descriptions.NUR16396:
A particular structure is present, which appears to be nuragic and may have been used for surveillance.

Probable location.
descriptions.NUR14650: An object classifiable among the pre-Nuragic walls, of which there are various examples throughout the island.
descriptions.NUR20348: The high, lintelled entrance leads into what must have been a sheltered space built on the edge of a sheer drop. On the left as you enter there is a circular room; on the right of the corridor only the perimeter wall survives.
descriptions.NUR20092: It lies on the south slope of Monte Lerno. The structure is in a state of serious decay. Nevertheless, part of the wall is easily recognisable because one of the entrances is still in good condition. At first glance this could be mistaken for a dolmen because of its particular structure, with a massive flat stone resting on the walls. A short distance further downhill there is another building, resembling a hut.
descriptions.NUR19956: The megalithic wall is pre-Nuragic. It has a covered entrance with lintels on the south side. It ends at the bed of the stream to the west and, following an arcing course, at the eponymous proto-nuraghe on the north side.
descriptions.NUR5579: The perforated rock of Suttaterra stands on the limestone summit of Punta Su Nuraghe, where you can admire not only the natural arch but also a megalithic wall a short distance away, and get a sense of how far you are from the Codula di Ilune and the other beauties of the area.
descriptions.NUR11178: The Cala Ostina nuraghe is a low wall following a semicircular course, with a chord of 7.70 m, protected on three sides by sheer cliffs; the wall reaches a maximum height of 2 m in two or three courses of very large stones.
descriptions.NUR7206: A wall of clearly Nuragic workmanship, of undefinable function. In the centre of the site there is a singular structure consisting of a sort of silo cut into the rock, with straight walls except at the bottom (at 2.65 m) where it narrows; the rim, partially worked and squared on the outside with rebates, has some irregularly shaped cupmarks.
descriptions.NUR17278: Nuragic wall (200 m long, with double wall face). It enclosed a Nuragic village.
descriptions.NUR10186: A short stretch of slightly concave wall made of not very large stones is certainly worth observing, because whoever built it did so to meet a family need for a dwelling or for hunting. Assessed within the context of sa Mesana di sos Pianos and the nearby Cudinatos, contemporary with the Domus or the following period, it would take on a different identity. mu
descriptions.NUR10131: Apparently detached from the adjacent tomb, it must certainly have been built in relation to it, or vice versa. The site is also known as Culu de Muru. mu
descriptions.NUR10194: The area is heavily built up and rich in remains. The presence of this wall, built of medium-sized polygonal boulders, others only roughly shaped, does not seem to follow a pre-planned direction, but is by no means random. The surrounding territory is rich in features from which its importance can be inferred. The freely interpreted drawing is a partial ideal vision of the sites in that territory.
descriptions.NUR10187: It consists of about ten metres of megalithic wall made of large boulders placed on the ridge north of Monte Zennaru, facing Runaghe Paulusedda or Palusedda, in the centre of which the Rio Murrone flows as a winter torrent. The construction gives the impression of being intended, almost, to watch over that river crossing. On close examination there are no traces of any other building in the vicinity.
descriptions.NUR18930: Tomb I has an elongated, apsidal tomb body containing a burial chamber and a broad semicircular exedra in front of it. Tomb II, lying to the south-east and buried under collapse and earth, still shows the outline of its apsidal tomb body and exedra. Tomb III, perhaps a dolmenic burial, is in very poor condition.
descriptions.NUR13945: Of the monument, legible in the various components that make it up, the large trapezoidal stele is particularly present. It stands in the locality of the same name in the municipality of Aidomaggiore.
descriptions.NUR10258: It consists of several single-room units, some with an antechamber and two or three small internal rooms. It is reasonable to think that others exist, not yet evident in the womb of Mother Earth. Almost all of them stand on the ridge of the mountain and on the gentle slope of sa pala de s'Ozastru. On the plateau are the remains of the eponymous nuraghe, with a clear link between the two sites of different periods and reasonably an example of cultural and religious syncretism. mu
descriptions.NUR19991:
On the plain there are two massive rocky outcrops that emerge, more or less 200 metres long, 30 m wide, 6 m high.

I only saw Site I from a distance, but they are clearly visible and the landowner confirmed that there are several domus de janas.

Site II has about ten domus de janas all facing perfectly west, all very small except for two with several chambers. They are set at different heights in the rock, from 30 cm up to 4 metres above ground level.
descriptions.NUR19993:
On the plain there are two massive rocky outcrops that emerge, more or less 200 metres long, 30 m wide, 6 m high.

I only saw Site I from a distance, but they are clearly visible and the landowner confirmed that there are several domus de janas.

Site II has about ten domus de janas all facing perfectly west, all very small except for two with several chambers. They are set at different heights in the rock, from 30 cm up to 4 metres above ground level.
descriptions.NUR1060: It consists of at least three tombs.
descriptions.NUR8211: A domus de janas necropolis now incorporated into the urban fabric of the city of Carbonia, where 25 tombs of different sizes and types have been identified. Following a major restoration project in which the ancient Sulcitano medau, built in the 18th century, was restored, the site is currently managed by the Cooperativa Mediterranea, which allows free entry.
descriptions.NUR7762:
It is located within the municipal territory of Bosa (OR), inside an agriturismo.

The name might be incorrect.

It should include two hypogea, partly repurposed.
descriptions.NUR15768: The Preizza necropolis consists of three small domus de janas dug at the base of modest rocky outcrops.
descriptions.NUR16205: It is located within the municipal territory of Giave (SS) and includes 4 domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR11749: There are six domus de janas on site.
descriptions.NUR11750: The necropolis stands in the locality of "sa Serra", in a hilly area overlooking the stretch of the Tirso river near its confluence with the Taloro. The small necropolis consists of seven hypogea of the domus de janas type, cut into the trachyte that outcrops in individual beds or short rocky ridges.
descriptions.NUR19031: It is composed of at least four domus de janas, still under excavation.
descriptions.NUR6971: Complex consisting of 9 domus. Probable location.
descriptions.NUR12165: The find is located in the municipality of Orani and consists of five hypogea.
descriptions.NUR12358:
It is located within the territory of the comune of Buddusò (OT).

It includes at least 10 hypogea.
descriptions.NUR7138:
Domus de janas currently repurposed for other uses.

Should include 9 domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR19558: The necropolis lies about 4 km south-west of Alghero, on the northern side of the road to Olmedo. The site consists of domus de janas cut into the foot of the trachyte plateau dominated by the nuraghe Sant'Elmo, 150 metres away.
descriptions.NUR16222: It includes at least eight domus de janas, of which only three are detectable in plan.
descriptions.NUR16220: It includes at least seven hypogea, most of which are damaged by collapses and significant reuse.
descriptions.NUR17309:
The domus de janas of Silattari (Bosa – OR) are cut into the limestone slope that faces south towards the Modolo valley.

They are two hypogea with closely spaced entrances: one consists of 12 chambers and the second of two cells. Probable location
descriptions.NUR7218: The necropolis of S'Isterridolzu occupies a flat area, crowned to the east by a steep rock face. It contains ten hypogea cut into low limestone outcrops, one in an erratic boulder, and a last, unfinished one on a rocky spur: they appear distributed over a wide area (about 10,000 sq m); the distance between each hypogeum varies from 10 m to about 200 m.
descriptions.NUR17308:
For further details, see the publication "Archaeological Research in Marghine-Planargia" by Moravetti, pages 191–196.

Probable location.
descriptions.NUR15233: The Taulera domus de janas lies near the civil hospital of Alghero. In 1941–42 some soldiers encamped there found a skull showing a double trepanation. The individual to whom the skull belonged survived the first trepanation for at least a year, probably dying during the second.
descriptions.NUR16359: Three single-cell domus de janas with rectangular door.
descriptions.NUR7203: It is the archaeological site par excellence: beautiful, interesting, easily reached and therefore accessible to visitors. Unfortunately the latest restoration work has not had the desired effect, since the workforce and the site directors have not always been up to the task. The area that was meant to be equipped for groups leaves much to be desired. The interior spaces, on the other hand, are interesting (when they are not full of water), as are the engravings/drawings on the walls.
descriptions.NUR19243: There are the most important domus de janas in the Pozzomaggiore area. The cemetery consists of at least 20 tombs cut into the rock, some of which are incomplete and not finished, while others are buried or heavily damaged.
descriptions.NUR12831: The necropolis consists of two groups, of 7 and 31 units, of hypogean domus de janas; only one is single-chambered while the others have more complex plans and one of them contains as many as eleven chambers. They are of the "vertical and horizontal projection" type, that is, accessible through a vertical shaft or a descending dromos, almost always provided with steps leading into the vestibule.
descriptions.NUR12942: Hypogeic tomb consisting of two chambers. Restructured in a later period with the addition of a dolmenic corridor, it was reused in the Early Bronze Age during the Bonnanaro phase. Violated by looters.
descriptions.NUR7008: The necropolis is cut into a granite outcrop on the Buddusò plateau. It consists of 6 hypogea and is dated to 3200–2800 BC. Some domus de janas have single-chambered rooms while others have a multi-chambered plan. One of the domus de janas shows traces of red wall painting in parallel bands on raised bands.
descriptions.NUR17772: The site includes 17 domus de janas, two of which are incomplete and one almost entirely buried. The numbered positions of the domus are taken from the book Itinerario Archeologico nel territorio Orgolese.
descriptions.NUR6929: The Prunittu necropolis is in the Sorrana area. The complex consists of two clusters about a hundred metres apart and contains 27 domus de janas in total. Most of the hypogea are easily reached, but some, cut into the vertical face of a trachyte bench with their entrances set well above ground level (up to four metres), can only be accessed by lowering oneself from the plateau above.
descriptions.NUR11132: The necropolis consists of four domus de janas, of which the "tomba dell'architettura dipinta" is particularly well known, characterised by relief and painted decorations. The hypogeum, with a T-shaped ground plan, consists of a long dromos ending in a rectangular atrium, an antechamber, a central chamber and two side chambers.
descriptions.NUR7332: At the entrance to the village of Bari Sardo, on the hills of su Pranu, lies the necropolis of Funtana su Rettore, composed of three domus de janas. The domus, of the bicellular type, date to the Late Neolithic, 3500–2800 BC. The tombs, well preserved, are set at almost the same level on the rock face and retain the marks of the tool used to excavate them.
descriptions.NUR12164:
The domus de janas lie within the municipal territory of Nuoro, on the boundary with Orani.

The necropolis consists of at least three tombs cut into the granite, but the presence of a fourth tomb, hidden by bushes in the immediate vicinity, cannot be ruled out.
descriptions.NUR7190:
It consists of three small tombs. It is located in the territory of Montresta.

Probable location.
descriptions.NUR13357: The necropolis, dated to the second half of the 4th millennium BC and attributable to the Arzachena culture, consists of five stone cists, four of which are surrounded by circles of stones driven into the ground that originally marked the edge of the mound of earth and rubble raised over the burial.
descriptions.NUR6960: In the middle of the forest, dug into trachyte and decorated on the portal with probable bull's-head protomes.
descriptions.NUR11172:
The tomb has three rooms, rectangular in plan, cut into the rock and interconnected.

It dates to the time of the Bonnanaro culture (1500–1300 BC).
descriptions.NUR6993:
The complex currently consists of 15 domus de janas.

The hypogea, set at a considerable height above the surrounding ground (from a minimum of 0.60 m to a maximum of 4.00 m), were originally reached by footholds cut in the rock; collapses and fractures in the rock face now make access particularly difficult.
descriptions.NUR14186: The site includes the remains of a Carthaginian necropolis (about 120 tombs) built by the inhabitants of the Phoenician settlement located near the altitude of Santu Teru, which emerged at the end of the 6th century BCE.
descriptions.NUR12142: Subterranean complex consisting of six domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR12880: Monte Claro culture underground. The site was used during the Nuragic, Roman, and medieval periods.
descriptions.NUR3472: See Giuseppa Tanda's book “L'arte delle domus de janas”, page 97.
descriptions.NUR12072: It is located in the municipality of Orani and consists of 8 domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR1329: In a fairly large area there are numerous sarcophagi obtained from large parallelepiped-shaped blocks of trachyte and basalt of considerable size (2.50 x 0.90 x 0.90). Since they are positioned here and there without any defined or reasonable order, one is led to deduce that this was a place where they were made.
descriptions.NUR8149: The nuraghe is composed of a seven-sided curtain wall, with a tower at each corner (partially visible), and a multi-lobed bastion of difficult interpretation, with an opening facing towards N.ghe Melas, or Fumiu.
descriptions.NUR574: The nuraghe is completely ruined and overgrown with shrubs. Like the very nearby Zianeddu (B) it is classed as a “tancato” nuraghe: on the front of the main tower a wall mass encloses a smaller tower and a courtyard set between the two towers.
descriptions.NUR1884: Single-tower nuraghe in blocks of sandy limestone. Nuragic settlement with finds of Middle Bronze Age pottery. The site is currently neither accessible nor easily understood; a study for its philological reconstruction would be appropriate.
descriptions.NUR18117: A few metres from the S.Giagu Nuraghe, the remains of a nuraghe completely covered by Mediterranean vegetation and brambles can be seen.
descriptions.NUR925: The nuraghe is in a state of complete abandonment. Partly buried and completely overgrown by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR1615: Destroyed nuraghe. The interior of the nuraghe can be seen only from the top of the tholos. An architrave of access is visible.
descriptions.NUR15264: Nuraghe reported on Wikimapia, no name in the locality Punta Sa Cresia
descriptions.NUR15945: Lapidary circle. It could be a nuraghe left incomplete.
descriptions.NUR3346:
Nuraghe immersed in vegetation. Nearby is the eponymous Nuragic burial.

On the west side of the monument a short stretch of wall tangent to the central tower is still partly visible, while the plan shows the course of the outer perimeter.

The entrance to the tower is lintelled, with a trapezoidal cross-section, and leads into a corridor with a flat ceiling.
descriptions.NUR6202: Nuraghe Abbaia (Acquaviva); it stands halfway up the mountain of the same name, near two abundant springs. This nuraghe, of which only scant remains survive, also served to watch the coastline in visual contact with Nuraghe Ottiolo.
descriptions.NUR6036: The area where the nuraghe stands is rich in archaeology. Situated on the highest part of the Sa Sèa plateau, it dominates the whole Valley of the Nuraghes of Torralba and has a view (albeit distant) of Santu Antine. About 50 metres to the north there is a strange construction: an enclosure bounded by a wall about 2 metres high, with an elongated shape measuring roughly 10 x 30 metres.
descriptions.NUR5932:
The Accas nuraghe is in a fair state of preservation. The monument has not been excavated, and both the entrance and the interior are partly buried, probably to a depth of about 2 m relative to the nuraghe's original floor level.

The chamber is nevertheless accessible. Inside, on the left, the stairwell is completely buried and inaccessible.

Inside the chamber, along the walls, the three niches are only just distinguishable because they too are filled with earth.
descriptions.NUR5613: Nuraghe in good condition. The interior is almost complete. The tholos is open because the closure ashlar is missing.
descriptions.NUR3950: The Acchettas nuraghe appears completely destroyed at first sight; a stretch of the polygonal walls is still visible on the west side. During land-clearing work large quantities of rubble were dumped on the monument.
descriptions.NUR3035: It now appears as a single-tower nuraghe, surrounded by well-cultivated fields; it is imposing, with free-standing walls about seven metres high. To the right a steep helical staircase leads up to the top of the nuraghe; to the left a niche overlooks the entrance area. Inside the circular chamber three further niches can be seen, clearly defined. The view from the terrace takes in the woods and the well-tended lands of the industrious people of Samugheo. It deserves to be visited and enhanced.
descriptions.NUR2161: Tholos nuraghe of single-tower type. Despite its poor state of preservation the circular plan that characterises a fairly small nuraghe can still be made out, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt of which a maximum height of about 2 m of the outer wall face survives.
descriptions.NUR2271: A circle of large boulders but without a foundation, so it must be considered doubtful. For the time being this structure has been classified as a "Nuraghe" and assigned the function of a "Meda" for the entrance to the cove.
descriptions.NUR4828:
A Nuragic complex consisting of a central body with a bastion and four lateral towers. Bronze Age, 2nd millennium BC.

A large nuraghe on the hilltop overlooking the Colostrai lagoon, in an area that was heavily settled in the Nuragic period. A landing place and two river mouths, partly navigable, completely controlled.
descriptions.NUR5417: The Adoni nuraghe is a complex nuraghe dating to the Bronze Age, located in the municipality of Villanovatulo in the province of Cagliari. The site stands on a rise about 800 m high in the centre of the historic Sarcidano region. The first excavations date back to the mid-nineteenth century. The whole complex consists of a central tower and a four-lobed bastion, surrounded by a village. Various finds have been recovered at the site, including pottery and a fragment of a bronze handle.
descriptions.NUR3395: It is a completely collapsed nuraghe that retains a maximum height of 1.90 m.
descriptions.NUR5539: The Aeddos nuraghe stands at 368 metres above sea level on the Sa Serra plateau of Orotelli. The first phase dates to the Bronze Age (1300–900 BC). The nuraghe has a trilobate structure, composed of a central tower and three concentric towers. It is built of large polyhedral ashlars of local granite laid in irregular courses. The height of the visible masonry from the central tower reaches 8.30 metres.
descriptions.NUR965: It is a complex nuraghe that is not easy to interpret, consisting of a main tower and the remains of two other probable towers. The nuraghe is built of roughly worked sandstone and schist blocks laid in polygonal masonry. On the west/south-west side the walling incorporates a rocky spur.
descriptions.NUR3848: The Nuraghe Agnu is built of granite, with a horseshoe plan because it is partly set against the rock face. It has a monumental entrance, oriented to the east and fitted with a lintel, leading into a corridor that was once fitted with a wooden sliding door descending from above. On the sides two corridors open; one leads to a domed cell, the other passes through the wall and out through the natural rock.
descriptions.NUR2612:
It is one of the many prehistoric monuments that make Seneghe one of the Sardinian municipalities with the highest density of material evidence of that remote civilisation.

Single-tower nuraghe, partially collapsed and covered in vegetation
descriptions.NUR5857:
It is one of the many prehistoric monuments that make Seneghe one of the Sardinian municipalities with the highest density of material evidence of that remote civilisation.

Single-tower nuraghe, partially collapsed and covered in vegetation
descriptions.NUR5680: With the presence of two nuraghi, the remains of a village and a giants' tomb, it forms a significant complex for reconstructing the historical events of the territory. The single-tower Nuraghe Corru 'e Oe stands on a small plateau visually linked with the four-lobed Aidu and with three others that appear to have belonged to a single defensive and territorial surveillance system. Near the nuraghe the remains of a village have been found, consisting of circular huts;
descriptions.NUR2808: With the presence of two nuraghi, the remains of a village and a giants' tomb, it forms a significant complex for reconstructing the historical events of the territory. The single-tower Nuraghe Corru 'e Oe stands on a small plateau visually linked with the four-lobed Aidu and with three others that appear to have belonged to a single defensive and territorial surveillance system. Near the nuraghe the remains of a village have been found, consisting of circular huts;
descriptions.NUR6149: With the presence of two nuraghi, the remains of a village and a giants' tomb, it forms a significant complex for reconstructing the historical events of the territory. The single-tower Nuraghe Corru 'e Oe stands on a small plateau visually linked with the four-lobed Aidu and with three others that appear to have belonged to a single defensive and territorial surveillance system. Near the nuraghe the remains of a village have been found, consisting of circular huts;
descriptions.NUR2544: With the presence of two nuraghi, the remains of a village and a giants' tomb, it forms a significant complex for reconstructing the historical events of the territory. The single-tower Nuraghe Corru 'e Oe stands on a small plateau visually linked with the four-lobed Aidu and with three others that appear to have belonged to a single defensive and territorial surveillance system. Near the nuraghe the remains of a village have been found, consisting of circular huts;
descriptions.NUR3462:
A nuraghe bearing an inscription carved on an ashlar that marks the boundary between the territory of the Ilienses and the Balari.

The inscription reads "ILI IVR IN NVRAC SESSAR M C", i.e. the rights of the Ilienses of Nurac Sessar. Its importance also lies in being one of the earliest attestations of the name given to Sardinian towers.
descriptions.NUR6474: It consists of a central tower and three auxiliary towers linked by stairs and corridors that are now partly impassable.
