A stair on the right gives access to the ground floor and the upper floor, which now lacks a roof. The ground-floor chamber, of considerable size, is distinguished by three other large niches reaching 4 metres in height.
descriptions.NUR5538: Here also a mezzanino and a subsidiary staircase, elevated within the right niche of the chamber. A nuraghe that reminded me, in layout, of the Crabia at Bauladu.
descriptions.NUR3020: Single-tower with its top missing and a tholos partially collapsed, accessible from the inside
descriptions.NUR3222: Single-tower with its top missing and a tholos partially collapsed, accessible from the inside
descriptions.NUR13362:
Situated just outside the town of Arzachena, it appears as an imposing structure, although the upper floor has partly collapsed.

It is built of large blocks of granite and dates to around the Middle Bronze Age (about 1600 BC) on the basis of the numerous finds recovered during the excavations.

The walls of the nuraghe lean against a large granite boulder; for this reason the nuraghe has an irregular plan that gives it a "pseudo-nuraghe" appearance. (MIBACT)
descriptions.NUR4172: The nuraghe, in a good state of preservation, consists of a main tholos to which other masonry parts were added later. A long corridor and a staircase lead off from the entrance. In the main chamber, where the roof has collapsed, there are several niches. The nuraghe, datable to 1500–1200 BC, stands on a hill whose slopes show the remains of circular and oval walls, probably belonging to a village.
descriptions.NUR869: The single-tower nuraghe, in a fair-to-poor state of preservation (six courses above ground), stands on top of a promontory overlooking a rocky ridge, built against the bedrock.
descriptions.NUR5640: Wikipedia identifies this nuraghe as one of the last to be built, with progressively less pronounced external wall slopes. It retains the tholos almost intact, except for some courses.
descriptions.NUR5698: Four-lobed nuraghe Alvu, built of squared white stones, with numerous hut bases around it. It shows constructional details in the interlocking of the corner masonry not found in other nuraghi.
descriptions.NUR2993: The central tower survives on the outside to a height of 6.40 m; on the left of the corridor the stairwell opens, with a trapezoidal opening, completely filled with collapse; the entrance to the chamber also has a trapezoidal opening; the inner chamber, essentially circular in plan, has a maximum diameter of 4.76 m and a maximum height of 5.60 m; the tholos survives almost entirely, except for the last two courses.
descriptions.NUR6238: Nuraghe Alvu di Nulvi: "alvu" = white. A four-lobed nuraghe, very beautiful, although in a fairly degraded state of preservation. Human and institutional neglect, together with the harshness of the elements, contribute to its deterioration. Let us remember that present-day municipal boundaries make no sense when referred to the Nuragic period, and future generations will have one piece fewer with which to reconstruct the historical and cultural period of our forebears.
descriptions.NUR3357: The structure still retains 12 corbels. Complex nuraghe with an outer wall and a surrounding village in basalt blocks. Noteworthy for the presence of large corbels still in situ. Entrance to the west (rare). Unfortunately covered by dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR6242: A circular single-tower nuraghe with three niches. It stands on an island in the middle of Lake Cuga, which was spared when the dam of the same name was built. It cannot be reached by land; the only access is by boat or canoe after a journey of 20–25 minutes. Each time one lands there after the winter season, the rebirth of the flora and fauna is revealed anew, forming a natural frame for the archaic shapes of the nuraghe. The quantity of incisions and cupmarks is striking.
descriptions.NUR3339: Complex nuraghe: due to the state of degradation and the significant burial of the structures, it cannot be securely assigned to any defined type.
descriptions.NUR4727:
A complex consisting of five towers linked by curtain walls often resting on the natural rock.

The site is internationally known because, for the first time in Sardinia, Mycenaean pottery was found here.
descriptions.NUR14967: Disappeared nuraghe but of which traces remain in local memory and the basal circle
descriptions.NUR2494: Practically the nuraghe no longer exists; only some piles of large stones remain, which still allow one to perceive its original location.
descriptions.NUR2075: Nuraghe completely collapsed, only some courses remain among the dense Mediterranean scrub.
descriptions.NUR2118: Complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and a bastion with three towers. The original tower survives, filled with earth and collapse. To the south-east stands a tower of which part of the wall structures can be seen; the inner wall face is barely visible because of collapse and vegetation. A curtain wall links this tower with another oriented to the north-east, of which almost the entire wall outline survives. A third tower oriented to the south-west preserves its external perimeter almost intact.
descriptions.NUR19653: Complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and four towers. The outline of the walls of the original tower survives almost entirely; its interior is filled with earth, collapse debris and vegetation. Three towers added laterally stand to the south-east, north-west and north-east, all overgrown with vegetation that makes their structure hard to see. The fourth tower lies to the south-west, detached from the main body. Traces left by illegal excavators are clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR4465: Complex nuraghe completely collapsed. It projects towards the "Seven Brothers" and towards the Geremeas Sea.
descriptions.NUR1817: Location of the remains of the Antoi Letze nuraghe
descriptions.NUR3022: Basically a pile of stones; at the top a circular opening is visible, forming a 2 m deep shaft, which I assume was the flat lintel of the staircase that ran along the inner wall.
descriptions.NUR4327: The Nuraghe Anulù belongs to the settlement of the same name, a large village dating to the late Nuragic period, composed of about thirty circular huts of medium and small size, interspersed with several walls.
descriptions.NUR21014: Located on a hilltop. It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe with evidence of huts in the surrounding areas.
descriptions.NUR8526: The archaeological area includes a complex nuraghe, Nuraghe Appiu, at the foot of Monte Cuccu, facing the sea, three-lobed, collapsed on the outside but with three large rooms still intact inside; a village attached to the nuraghe, of about 200 huts; another nuraghe, single-tower; a giants' tomb and two small dolmens. Nearby there are also a megalithic circle and a "megaron" temple.
descriptions.NUR5553:
The four-lobed bastion has a rather disordered structure of large polyhedral blocks; all the chambers have collapsed vaults, while the courtyard is partly filled with rubble; the main entrance is visible on the eastern side.

A stretch of enclosure wall can be seen to the west of the bastion, but it is not clear whether it extends around the other sides as well. All the ground around the bastion has been completely cleared of stones and is cultivated, with abundant Roman pottery on the surface.
descriptions.NUR4561: The monument, although very well preserved, is hard to read in plan because of the dense vegetation that also makes it difficult to locate. Two towers, an internal courtyard and parts of the connecting walls between the structures can be recognised. The central body, which survives to a height of 10 courses of medium and large blocks of volcanic stone in polygonal masonry. It is characterised by steeply sloping walls and an elliptical plan.
descriptions.NUR5979: Structures belonging to a single-tower tholos nuraghe. The nuraghe, built of local polygonal basalt blocks, survives in its outer wall face to a maximum height of just over 4 m. The inner chamber has collapsed and the remaining part is filled with the same collapse material. The entrance, identifiable to the south, is lintelled with a height of 1.20 m. The workmanship of the lintel and jambs is fairly rough, with barely dressed blocks.
descriptions.NUR6274: The structures of the nuraghe, of the simple tholos type, are buried and covered by dense vegetation. Some courses of local basalt blocks emerge partially on the summit of the small rise formed by the structures and the earth covering them.
descriptions.NUR4652: No official records exist, but locally it is said that a complex nuraghe and a very large village lie buried beneath the hill, as suggested by the traces left by tomb robbers.
descriptions.NUR5385: Complex nuraghe with a village and sacred well in the vicinity
descriptions.NUR2609:
Complex nuraghe, in which several building units, visible only in part, lean against the central body, a tower of trachyte blocks with a circular plan. In the surrounding area, especially to the south-east, there are numerous Roman-period potsherds.

The Sassari urban plan (11 Dec. 2014) defines it as "Nuraghe Arcone II".
descriptions.NUR6326: It seems to belong to the category of "uncompleted" nuraghes, yet the dense vegetation cover prevents a precise definition.
descriptions.NUR5464: From a period subsequent to the adjacent Monti Pintau II, about seven courses of ashlars strongly densified remain.
descriptions.NUR4892: Five courses remain, their irregularity suggesting a proto-nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5146: The nuraghe consists of a central tower surrounded by a wall, against which several secondary towers are built. The central tower, which originally had several superimposed floors, now preserves only the lower floor and the staircase that led to the upper ones, partially blocked by collapse debris.
descriptions.NUR966: The archaeological park contains a hypogeal necropolis made up of about fifteen domus de janas (the fairy houses), the prehistoric tombs cut into the rock faces of Sa Carona Arrubia (red rock face) and into the large basalt erratic boulders, and a few single-tower nuraghi.
descriptions.NUR2180: The archaeological park contains a hypogeal necropolis made up of about fifteen domus de janas (the fairy houses), the prehistoric tombs cut into the rock faces of Sa Carona Arrubia (red rock face) and into the large basalt erratic boulders, and a few single-tower nuraghi.
descriptions.NUR5113: The archaeological park contains a hypogeal necropolis made up of about fifteen domus de janas (the fairy houses), the prehistoric tombs cut into the rock faces of Sa Carona Arrubia (red rock face) and into the large basalt erratic boulders, and a few single-tower nuraghi.
descriptions.NUR7014: The archaeological park contains a hypogeal necropolis made up of about fifteen domus de janas (the fairy houses), the prehistoric tombs cut into the rock faces of Sa Carona Arrubia (red rock face) and into the large basalt erratic boulders, and a few single-tower nuraghi.
descriptions.NUR7028: The archaeological park contains a hypogeal necropolis made up of about fifteen domus de janas (the fairy houses), the prehistoric tombs cut into the rock faces of Sa Carona Arrubia (red rock face) and into the large basalt erratic boulders, and a few single-tower nuraghi.
descriptions.NUR7011: The archaeological park contains a hypogeal necropolis made up of about fifteen domus de janas (the fairy houses), the prehistoric tombs cut into the rock faces of Sa Carona Arrubia (red rock face) and into the large basalt erratic boulders, and a few single-tower nuraghi.
descriptions.NUR5090:
It is located to the south, near the border with the territory of Usellus.

It is a simple type and is very damaged.
descriptions.NUR5752: The Nuraghe Aresti lies on the boundary between the municipal territories of Narbolia and Seneghe, about 1 km north-east of Narbolia, a short distance from the SP 11. It is a complex nuraghe in a fair state of preservation. The central tower is accessible and has a fine entrance with a corbelled corridor and an intact tholos over the inner chamber.
descriptions.NUR3236: It is a corridor proto-nuraghe built of basalt.
descriptions.NUR4005:
Hidden by dense vegetation, we find the nuraghe Arigau. Completely covered in earth and vegetation, with only a few courses of the base visible.

The nuraghe lies at Santa Maria Acquas, on a hill behind the amphitheatre. Apparently a single-tower nuraghe. Never studied and completely covered in earth and vegetation.
descriptions.NUR2741:
It lies within the municipal territory of Nule (SS).

The nuraghe is a single-tower nuraghe with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a central chamber flanked by three niches arranged in a cross.

The tower has a circular plan, while the roof has collapsed.
descriptions.NUR4499: The nuraghe, datable to the Middle Bronze Age (15th–14th century BC), has a single-tower structure and a truncated-conical shape with a diameter of twelve metres and a surviving height of ten metres. It is built of well-worked limestone-schist blocks laid to form the tholos, which has lost its top courses. The entrance leads into a corridor four metres long, equal to the wall thickness, which opens into the main chamber, circular and over five metres in diameter.
descriptions.NUR2667:
The building, set in a commanding position at the eastern end of the hill of the same name, is a three-lobed complex nuraghe with a village around it.

Here too there must have been a king who ruled the whole plain.

The finds suggest that the Romans arrived later as well.
descriptions.NUR4986: (From Mitz'arramini, the locality where it stands), it is a complex multi-tower nuraghe near which a village is also present. The vaulted building, with a toponym recalling copper, where the central tower and a secondary tower are clearly identifiable but unfortunately still sealed by aeolian and agricultural deposits for lack of thorough investigations.
descriptions.NUR5178: Up to five courses of enormous, irregularly shaped cyclopean basalt blocks survive, reaching a height of up to two and a half metres. The central tower is incomplete, forming an angle of 270 degrees. From it a wall runs east and another runs north. What structure these walls enclosed is not at all clear because of brambles and various later alterations.
descriptions.NUR2823: It lies within the municipal territory of Seneghe (OR). Single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The vault has collapsed and the chamber is filled with the collapse debris. The surviving height of the building is about 3.50 m. The trapezoidal entrance is clearly visible, fitted with a monolithic lintel and faces east (1.70 m high x 0.80 m wide at the base).
descriptions.NUR5472: Nuraghe of the tancato type with a main tower and an additional structural body (second tower and courtyard). The monument is located adjacent to the parish church.
descriptions.NUR3843: The structures of the nuraghe, of the simple tholos type, are buried under a considerable depth of soil and covered by dense vegetation. Some courses of local basalt blocks emerge partially on the summit of the small rise formed by the structures and the earth covering them.
descriptions.NUR4277: Four-lobed nuraghe. A nuraghe with the addition of two lateral towers connected to the original tower by a semi-circular corridor.
descriptions.NUR5308: It dates to about 1500 BC; the collapse is dated to the 9th century BC, and it remained uninhabited until 100 BC when the Romans arrived. It consists of a central tower surrounded by five other towers and an outer wall (outer enclosure), with a further seven towers forming another defensive curtain wall enclosing several courtyards. A second outer curtain wall and a third with three more towers are also present. The total number of towers is twenty-one. The area exceeds 5000 m².
descriptions.NUR5304: The nuraghe is a single-tower type, with a curtain wall about 80 cm thick; it rises from the surrounding vegetation to a height of 4 metres. Its position is strategic, lying halfway between the Fenu nuraghe and the nearby spa area where three other nuraghi stand, one of them part of the same spa complex. It is the best-preserved nuraghe in the municipal territory of Sardara. The size of the lintel is striking
descriptions.NUR15038: Single-tower nuraghe with a ruined and buried village
descriptions.NUR10755: Nuraghe Artòra dominates the Capo Comino spur from 120 m above the sea and performed the watchful function of the present-day semaphore. Situated a short distance from the lighthouse that dominates Capo Comino, it is described by Relli as a complex nuraghe on the summit of the same name, but is barely distinguishable because it is covered by a concrete platform built for military purposes during the Second World War.
descriptions.NUR2755:
It is a single-tower nuraghe roofed with a tholos, still in good condition: it survives on the N-NE and N-W sides to a height of 10.50 metres, while the SE side, corresponding to the entrance, has collapsed.

The external wall face, of 26 courses of stone, is formed by large polygonal blocks in the base, which has a diameter of 14 metres, while in the upper part the blocks are sub-square and of modest size, becoming more regular as the height increases.
descriptions.NUR6337: Here too the situation is critical because the remains of the nuraghe are a shapeless heap of stones, yet they still reveal some of the monument's constructional features. As is typical of most Chiaramonti nuraghi, the entrance — with both jambs and the lintel still visible — faces east-south-east.
descriptions.NUR2776: Complex nuraghe with the tholos intact. Part of the external wall face has collapsed.
descriptions.NUR1805:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a chamber flanked by two opposing niches.

The tower cannot be fully defined in its outer perimeter because of collapses and dense shrub vegetation, but a circular ground plan about 10 metres in diameter at the base is to be assumed. The surviving height is 6.50 m on the south-east side and 4.80 m on the north-west side. The masonry consists of medium and large basalt blocks laid in horizontal courses that are not always regular.
descriptions.NUR2756: It is a single-tower nuraghe and is in an advanced state of decay. Some elements of the construction are still visible, however. For the moment it shelters a few domestic animals right on the main entrance. I want to exorcise the situation by thinking of the great people of the nuraghi… "from the stars… to the stables" if institutions and civil conscience linger and persist in abandoning our monuments. mu
descriptions.NUR3393: Single-tower, it is a newly identified feature because the central chamber has imploded and the wall face has collapsed to the west. Some characteristics of the Nuragic masonry can be observed. Nuraghe of San Pietro. Local tradition does not recall a church dedicated to San Pietro in this place. It probably refers to a property linked to the church of San Pietro that stood in the village located at Elva nàna, the name of which has not survived. Mu
descriptions.NUR11143: Single-tower nuraghe submerged beneath the waters of Lake Cuga. It was recorded by the archaeologist Ercole Contu in the period before the dam on the Cuga was built. It belongs to the complex of nuraghi in the Chessedu–Cuga valley.
descriptions.NUR5024: The Asusa nuraghe, built around 1300 BC, consists of two towers looking onto a courtyard and has its main entrance to the east. In one of the interior rooms archaeologists uncovered a circular ring belonging to a well or cistern that has yet to be explored.
descriptions.NUR3625: The name comes from the place name Monte Atarzu. In the Chiaramonti dialect of Sardinian we say de sa pedra atarzina, of which the mountain is very rich. The name could not be more appropriate, because several flint-working sites have been identified for making tools for everyday use or for hunting, such as knives and arrowheads. There are a few large megaliths hidden by a big thicket of mastic.
descriptions.NUR6438: A bronze "antenna" sword found at Ploaghe near the nuraghe "Attentu" (in 1874 the nuraghe was studied by the archaeologist Giovanni Spano, a native of Ploaghe, who carried out the first stratigraphic excavation in Sardinia there)
descriptions.NUR6100: Multi-lobed nuraghe, consisting of a main tower plus three smaller towers. The diameter is about 11 metres. The central tower is built of large boulders, while the front addition uses smaller stones.
descriptions.NUR5622: Preserves the tholos intact. There is a Nuragic settlement around the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5609: The Atzara nuraghe is a three-lobed complex nuraghe with a tall central tower distinguished by a broad base. The walls linking the three outer towers are still in good condition, while the reinforcement structures were built in Punic and Roman times. It has recently been cleared but awaits a more thorough excavation to understand its structure better.
descriptions.NUR6333: The surviving buried structure, for at least two metres below the present ground level, because the core has spilled out from inside the wall face, making it impossible to enter the internal chambers of the nuraghe, which is classified as a corridor nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR3077: Archaic corridor nuraghe. The nuraghe stands on a hillside and is laid out on two different levels, adapting to the lie and slope of the ground. The structures are largely covered by vegetation, but the north-west and west parts can be seen in particular. The north-west part follows a semi-circular course, while the west part consists of a massive wall that extends in a straight line towards the south.
descriptions.NUR1994: A single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal basalt blocks. Four to five courses of large blocks laid in a circle remain, forming a structure of fair size, very similar to other nuraghi in the area. The maximum surviving height is about 3 m. The inner chamber has collapsed and is filled with collapse debris. The entrance cannot be identified.
descriptions.NUR5948: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a large circular chamber whose walls corbel particularly steeply. A distinctive feature of the nuraghe is the absence of the corridor niche and the staircase. Outside, in the area around the tower, several worked blocks of varying size are visible.
descriptions.NUR4669: It is a complex nuraghe, whose ground plan cannot be deduced because it is largely buried. A tower to the west is faintly visible, showing up to five courses. Elsewhere various circular courses emerge here and there.
descriptions.NUR570: Complex nuraghe of difficult definition due to its state of degradation and the significant burial of its structures. Located on the summit of Capo San Marco, with panoramic views in all directions.
descriptions.NUR5831: Damaged nuraghe of which no description is available
descriptions.NUR6370: Damaged nuraghe of which no description is available
descriptions.NUR6410:
It is completely covered with earth and vegetation; one would not even notice that it is a nuraghe were it not for a few limestone blocks laid one on top of another visible on top of the hillock.

On the side away from the sea, a few metres from the summit where the central tower stands, inside a hollow one of the towers of the nuraghe can be seen, in which its tholos, sectioned in half, is visible, built of sandstone and limestone blocks.
descriptions.NUR8248: Single-tower nuraghe built on a rocky outcrop. Only a few courses remain visible, intersected by the rock, together with some lower wall structures, though still connected to the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR20071: A complex nuraghe, but heavily ruined and never studied. It is completely overgrown with vegetation and not easy to interpret. It shows a probable internal staircase and remains of external masonry belonging to secondary rooms.
descriptions.NUR4223: The site is hard to locate. It appears to the visitor as a heap of buried ashlars, only very partially exposed. It is reached via the mid-slope path behind the settlement of Capoterra,
descriptions.NUR6157: From its position on the Badde ridge it commands the right-hand course of the Rio Giunturas and joins the cliff edge superbly, almost as if to declare its dominating position. The inner chamber with its characteristic orthogonal cells can be made out, and the chamber is covered on the sides by organic debris.
descriptions.NUR5933: From the top of a small hill it overlooks the surrounding territory, where two water mills once stood on a small drop in the Rio Iscanneddu. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a few basal courses of medium-sized stones, only partly dressed. Its name undoubtedly dates from the medieval period when monastic orders settled in the area (10th–11th centuries).
descriptions.NUR1059: Remains of a nuraghe tower built from basalt blocks.
descriptions.NUR1815: In very poor condition, the outer megalithic circle destroyed to make room for pasture; in this nuraghe a bronze model boat was found and stolen, the largest ever discovered in Sardinia, as much as 38 cm long, called the Sun King's boat, now kept in the Sanna Archaeological Museum in Sassari.
descriptions.NUR2920: The monument, made of trachyte, has a rectangular plan (12 m x 7 m) and includes an 'elbow'-shaped corridor inside. It shows significant collapse along both the western wall and the southern side.
descriptions.NUR1583: Single-tower nuraghe in good condition, partly covered by vegetation. In the field, a scatter of Roman pottery.
descriptions.NUR3354: This site, too, loudly proclaims its increasingly incipient state of ruin. Abandonment and neglect make a programme of recovery and consolidation ever more urgent. At the very least a systematic campaign of survey and assessment of the extensive archaeological heritage in the territory of Chiaramonti should be launched.
descriptions.NUR3874: Reduced to a ruin like most of the other sites in the municipality of Chiaramonti. It does, however, show a few basal circles of cyclopean boulders, among which the main entrance stands out with its massive lintel facing south-south-east.
descriptions.NUR6377: It is a circle of polygonal cyclopean boulders improperly known as a nuraghe. Lacking a specific title for its definition, I therefore continue to consider it as such, but on the evidence I lean towards a ceremonial circle. Nuraghe del guado della moglie. See Badu muzère. mu
descriptions.NUR1656: Single-tower nuraghe composed of trachyte and andesite blocks. It remains about 3 metres high above the current campagna level.
descriptions.NUR2874:
Today, unfortunately, it appears to be considerably damaged.

It also had a bilobate bastion added at a later date.
descriptions.NUR14359: Single-tower nuraghe near a small hotel. Ruined
descriptions.NUR1992: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. It stands on a rocky spur overlooking the whole western slope of Montiferru down to the sea, and is almost completely hidden by tree vegetation. It is built of polygonal blocks of local basalt and survives to a height of about 2.60 m. The inner chamber has collapsed and the remaining part is filled with its collapse debris.
descriptions.NUR3873: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The nuraghe has been almost completely dismantled and the remains consist of the first two basal courses, built of roughly dressed blocks of local basalt. The maximum surviving height is about 1 m, while the diameter of the nuraghe is about 12 m. The entrance must have been to the south-east, where a hut has been built.
descriptions.NUR5707: It belongs to the group of nuraghi with a basement level, I say this with the benefit of inventory because survey is prevented by sturdy thorny plants that have colonised the structure. The basal circle is composed of vaguely squared boulders that interlock well, creating a regular wall face together with some natural rock outcrops. It has a raised entrance above ground level that highlights the sacred character of the construction.
descriptions.NUR6243: In a precarious state of conservation, it is surrounded by patches of rowan and shrubs that may compromise its stability.
descriptions.NUR3869: Single-tower nuraghe with a cylindrical shape, neither niches nor stairs are present.
descriptions.NUR3788: Nuraghe covered with ficus indica plants and disturbed by a structure that has developed beside it.
descriptions.NUR1535: At Baratè, on a low rise in an area used as an olive grove and partly as a vineyard. On the north side four courses survive (height 1.80 m) of trachyte blocks; on the south side the remains of the elevation are covered by vegetation. Boundary walls lean against the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR8233: Nuraghe probably a single-tower, covered by collapse and vegetation. Only a single course emerges.
descriptions.NUR913:
The monument, of simple type, stands in an area currently used for pasture; the entrance has a lintel surmounted by a relieving window, while the jambs consist of well-shaped granite blocks laid in decreasing size towards the top.

The entrance leads into a passage towards the chamber, built of very well-worked granite ashlars and covered by an ogival-section roof.
descriptions.NUR5721: The proto-nuraghe Bardalatzu stands on the western end of a basalt plateau, in a rugged and hard-to-reach area, overlooking a narrow, deep valley where the Riu Murtazzolu and the Riu Cuguttu meet. The monument is of considerable size, with an irregular ground plan that adapts to the triangular profile of the hill on which it was built.
descriptions.NUR4273: Well-preserved nuraghe, part of a larger settlement. The central tower still has its roof and a lower level below which entry has not yet been achieved.
descriptions.NUR2926: Complex nuraghe, cannot be definitively classified by its state of degradation or by the significant burial of its structures; in the vicinity, traces of an inhabited settlement, village.
descriptions.NUR10449: The central tower is elliptical, typical of a proto-nuraghe. The towers are more regular in shape, suggesting they were built in later phases, as was the curtain wall of the courtyard, which encloses a system of stairs and silos (presumably for storing agricultural produce). Some parts of the towers show a smaller-scale fabric in the curtain wall, with flatter, more regular stones.
descriptions.NUR4338: It stands on a rocky spur along the Pardu River. This is a nuraghe of at least four towers surrounded by a defensive curtain wall. Of the four towers, three are still in good condition, while only the base of the fourth can be made out. The site today appears split in two. The east side, which does not face the river and stands on the rock, is still intact. The west side, which faces the river, has almost completely collapsed, with an enormous quantity of boulders scattered down the slope.
descriptions.NUR1448: It consists of only a few meagre remains and some stones of the nuraghe, which is completely overgrown by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR5340: Single-tower nuraghe completely collapsed, with only a few courses emerging from the low scrub.
descriptions.NUR5623: It is a single-tower nuraghe built of large, well-worked basalt blocks. The entrance, oriented SSW, is topped by a rectangular relieving window and leads into a corridor with an ogival roof; on the left of the corridor is a niche. The chamber, completely filled with collapse, survives to almost 5 metres (9 courses). On the right side of the chamber a niche cut into the wall thickness is visible.
descriptions.NUR4101:
A short distance before Muravera, at km 51, next to the SS 125, the monument is well signposted and easy to reach. The building consists of a central tower to which a three-lobed bastion with a concave-convex outline was added later, enclosing a small courtyard. The whole complex measures 24 m on the N-S axis and 16 m on the E-W axis.

The central tower, circular in plan (9 m external diameter), survives to a maximum height of about 10 m.
descriptions.NUR811: The nuraghe stands near the coast of Trinità d'Agultu, south of Isola Rossa. It has an almost elliptical plan and can be reached from the hamlet of Paduledda by taking the road to “La Scalitta”.
descriptions.NUR4010: Single-tower nuraghe that re-emerges from the lake only during periods of drought
descriptions.NUR5595: The Battizzone nuraghe is a three-lobed type, with towers joined by an outer wall that forms an internal courtyard at the front. At present the courtyard and the lateral towers are completely filled with collapse debris, making access to the central tower impossible; the entrance lintel is partly visible. A corridor is also visible in the courtyard area, which probably served as the entrance to one of the lateral towers and is notable for its considerable height.
descriptions.NUR2304:
Traces of a nuraghe built of basalt. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

PUC Arbus Historical and Cultural Report p. 13 Table 12C No. 3360
descriptions.NUR12990: The Bau 'e Tanca nuraghe at Talana stands at an altitude of 1122 metres above sea level and is surrounded by a village, of which the courses of some huts and the piles of stones used to build them are still visible. Interesting for the unusual symmetry of the clusters that make up the village.
descriptions.NUR502: Completely embedded in the scrub, it is difficult to identify.
descriptions.NUR3228:
The complex consists of a nuraghe, an outer wall and a village.

The nuraghe comprises a central tower to which at least two lateral towers were added, now not fully detectable.

A large outer wall, incorporating at least four towers, with an irregular curvilinear course, surrounds the complex.

In the area in front, the remains of numerous huts and rectangular apsidal dwellings leaning against the inner profile of the outer wall.
descriptions.NUR14990: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure is difficult to define
descriptions.NUR8833:
It lies to the north-east of the village, a short distance from the nuraghe Luas and the proto-nuraghe Friarosu, and is visible from the provincial road that leads to Ruinas after the turn-off for Villa Sant'Antonio.

The plan of the nuraghe is decidedly unusual in that it has two circular structures joined by a corridor.

What makes the site even more interesting is the presence of a large granite boulder, oriented to the east, placed there presumably in the pre-Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR5664: The monument, considered a proto-nuraghe, is in fact a transitional structure between the corridor nuraghe and the tholos nuraghe. The complex consists of a central tower with a terrace, a bastion, and various huts both inside and outside an outer wall. It now lies beneath a viaduct; indeed, only a few centimetres separate the last surviving stone courses of the monument from the concrete beams that support the road.
descriptions.NUR5555: The Benas nuraghe stands on a small hill at the locality 'Tanca sa cresia', north-west of the Jana nuraghe, in the territory of Solarussa, 200 m from the border with Zerfaliu. It is a complex nuraghe, with a courtyard and three secondary towers. The central tower is particularly interesting, preserving the intact tholos roof of the ground floor. Inside there are three niches and a curious staircase on the right-hand side of the entrance corridor.
descriptions.NUR9878: The nuraghe is completely collapsed, probably known also by the name Tostoinus.
descriptions.NUR4182: Complex nuraghe partially dismantled, with only the low courses remaining
descriptions.NUR2273:
Remains of a nuraghe and traces of a Nuragic village.

Built on a granite rise, this nuraghe is not currently recognisable among the remains of an extensive village that lasted into the Roman and early medieval periods, as attested by fragments of pottery, roof tiles and jars.
descriptions.NUR3977: The Bia nuraghe now appears as a ruin. It is not a single-tower nuraghe (although the most visible tower is very probably the central tower), since other walling can be made out to the south.
descriptions.NUR1004: The nuraghe lies inside the Fertilia Military Airport, in an area skirted by one of the internal connecting roads. The construction of the military structures and the subsequent underground services installed nearby must have erased every possible surface trace of the site's occupation in historical times, to the extent that no scatter of ceramic material relating to the nuraghe's phases of use could be identified.
descriptions.NUR5128: The nuraghe is named after the light colour of the lithic material used in its construction.
descriptions.NUR5373: Some wall courses remain, probably belonging to the outer wall.
descriptions.NUR3498: The nuraghe is not marked on IGM maps and its type is undetermined.
descriptions.NUR10885: Towards the road that leads from Samatzai onto the SS 128. On the right you reach the locality of Bidda Mendula. On a low sandstone promontory (altitude 150 m) the ruins of a nuraghe built of large sandstone marl blocks can be seen, belonging to a Nuragic settlement. On the surface a circular building is visible, probably a single-tower nuraghe, 14 m in diameter, which on the west side shows the remains of a facing wall 2.30 m thick, visible for several metres.
descriptions.NUR5283: The nuraghe is very badly degraded, certainly repurposed over time for various uses.
descriptions.NUR1180: Damaged nuraghe, of which only a few courses remain standing, embedded in natural rock masses.
descriptions.NUR4689: Complex nuraghe, eroded and enveloped by vegetation, of difficult definition
descriptions.NUR3325: The nuraghe Bidighinzu or Su Idighinzu, which in Sardinian means "dry vine shoot", is a single-tower monument that still preserves its intact tholos, located in the territory of Ploaghe.
descriptions.NUR5321: It lies in the municipality of Mandas (CA). What remains of the nuraghe is visible on the north and north-west sides, where three courses of limestone ashlars emerge; the rest of the boulders are scattered around the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5801: Very complex nuraghe. It has a trilobate outer wall and an internal central tower. Traces of a village outside. The state of conservation is very poor.
descriptions.NUR3541:
The nuraghe has a sub-elliptical plan, with its long sides aligned east–west. The masonry is roughly polygonal.

The entrance faces north and has a lintel resting on a few large blocks that form the jambs; it is surmounted by a smaller ashlar, which in turn is set within a semicircular ring of blocks that diverts the weight of the superstructure onto the jambs.
descriptions.NUR1803:
The nuraghe is a complex type, consisting of a central tower enclosed by a four-lobed bastion with four corner towers linked by curtain walls with a concave–convex profile.

The bastion (NS axis 17 m) is fairly well preserved on the western side and only partially on the north-western side, while the remaining perimeter appears completely collapsed and covered with rubble.
descriptions.NUR6069:
The monument is now known as Nuraghe Urpes, but it is actually Nuraghe Bighinzone, while Nuraghe Urpes, which stood nearby, has been completely destroyed.

The nuraghe looks at first sight like a single-tower nuraghe, but a closer analysis of the structures shows it to be a four-lobed nuraghe with curtain walls of concave-convex profile, itself enclosed by an outer wall with towers of which a few significant traces still remain.
descriptions.NUR3185:
The nuraghe, almost completely demolished, is traceable in its entire ground-plan profile (diameter 11 m, surviving height about 2 m).

Near the nuraghe, scattered over an extensive area (about 12 hectares), the remains of a great many circular structures (generally more than 7 m in diameter) and rectilinear ones can be seen, attributable to the ancient settlement and probably also belonging to a sacred area.
descriptions.NUR6303: The monument, built of granite boulders and preserved to a maximum height of 3 m, has a lintelled entrance leading to a corridor with a flat-lintelled roof, passable only for a short stretch because of a collapse.
descriptions.NUR5567: Complex nuraghe belonging to the nuraghi of the Cuga valley. The associated village and the outer structure are heavily altered. It allows access inside as far as the tholos, which is still perfectly intact.
descriptions.NUR18916: Proto-nuraghe with a central corridor leading to two rooms.
descriptions.NUR4462: The nuraghe is not far from an unrecognisable and now destroyed domus de janas, on top of a hill overlooking the Giara di Collinas. Its condition is practically neglected, left to itself, but one can see how extensive it was because the surrounding ground is strewn with boulders.
descriptions.NUR5510: From the aerial photograph it appears to be a complex nuraghe with a village.
descriptions.NUR3001:
The nuraghe is heavily eroded.

In the vicinity lies a pre-Nuragic settlement dating to the Neolithic period.
descriptions.NUR5511:
The Nuraghe Biriola lies at Dualchi, about four hundred metres from the Nuraghe Piddio. It is a complex nuraghe that looks like a veritable fortress of considerable size (about 38 by 22 metres). The central tower contains a large circular chamber with a corbelled roof; niches, partly accessible, are set in the central part of the structure.

A village once stood around the nuraghe, and traces of it are still visible.
descriptions.NUR4947: The Nuraghe Dom'e Biriu lies about 1.5 km north of Genoni. Largely ruined, a tower of roughly square plan can still be made out, built with horizontal courses and almost squared blocks.
descriptions.NUR21006: Granite nuraghe, of large and medium blocks. It appears to be a tancato nuraghe with two towers, which can be documented: a stretch of the central tower wall on the north side, three courses high, and the interior of the upper part of the secondary tower.
descriptions.NUR6335:
The monument, of the tholos type, cannot be entered because of collapse, but it has a circular plan about 9 metres in diameter and preserves, on the outside, a stretch of wall up to 2.20 metres high, formed by five courses of large trachyte boulders.

A short distance from the nuraghe are the remains of a wall, probably a surviving stretch of outer wall.
descriptions.NUR18893: The corridor nuraghe, rectangular in plan and built of large granite boulders, survives to a maximum height of 4 m; it has an entrance topped by a lintel leading to a flat-roofed corridor, off which open a semicircular niche and an elongated chamber.
descriptions.NUR14322:
It should preserve an intact tholos.

An imposing complex nuraghe, today it appears as a wooded hill.

On the summit a staircase allows access to the interior chambers, probably the central tower.

I advise against an internal visit; because of the large roots of the vegetation it hosts, the nuraghe is very unstable!
descriptions.NUR17914: The site is located in the area of Boe and is completely destroyed; only some courses of the foundation remain visible.
descriptions.NUR6049: Complex nuraghe with only a few courses remaining, partially collapsed and overgrown by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR18264: It is located within the territory of the comune of Furtei. It is mentioned by Vittorio Angiu in the Geographical-Historical-Statistical-Commercial Dictionary of the States of S.M. under the entry Furtei as Nuragi-Ais.
descriptions.NUR5860: Corridor nuraghe in good state of conservation
descriptions.NUR2862: Partially eroded, invaded by vegetation, and difficult to explore. The central chamber, the entrance, and the circular corridor remain clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR2425: The monument stands in a commanding position; the extensive collapse of the outer wall face prevents an accurate reading, but it appears to be a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan and two storeys, with a spaced outer wall.
descriptions.NUR5031: Damaged and collapsed nuraghe, of which only the entrance portal and the interior remain.
descriptions.NUR863: Single-tower nuraghe hardly accessible due to vegetation.
descriptions.NUR4106:
A. Sanguinetti, who in 1970 complained that, among other things, it was partly buried under stone dumps caused by the reclamation of the surrounding farmland.

The author nevertheless described a single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical plan and an entrance facing north-east, and hypothesised a straight access corridor.
descriptions.NUR4624: Nuraghe situated on the mountain called Punta Breigara. Locals call the site "nuraghe de s'omu e is abisi"; the base of a tholos about 1.50 m high is present. Vegetation has completely covered the site and makes further identification impossible. Difficult access; the roads are on private land.
descriptions.NUR6130: A small single-tower nuraghe; around it is a small domus de janas necropolis, in which there are decorations of carved bull's-head protomes.
descriptions.NUR2893: Complex tholos nuraghe. Completely enveloped by vegetation, it is a large nuraghe whose features can only be vaguely guessed. It appears to consist of a central tower and two added towers, with an internal courtyard now filled with collapse blocks. Built of large blocks of local basalt, it survives in good condition, although it is hard to observe because of the bushes that envelop it.
descriptions.NUR4146: Complex nuraghe completely collapsed and buried.
descriptions.NUR14923:
Nuraghe. Located on top of a hill, with views over the area of Sa Gruttixedda (Pozzo/Village Nuragic)

Covered with large stones and vegetation.
descriptions.NUR4584: Situated on the boundary with the territory of Guasila, at the foot of the basalt plateau of Lasìna, on the western side that slopes down towards the territory of Samatzai. The building consists of a single tower with an external diameter of 12 m and preserves the basal course intact around its entire circumference. The materials used are sandstone.
descriptions.NUR4290: The complex includes a nuraghe, consisting of a central tower on the summit of a basalt hillock and various added structures positioned along the slopes of the same rise, investigated archaeologically in 2003, and an important village of huts, located on the south-eastern slopes of the hill.
descriptions.NUR4616: Complex nuraghe, collapsed and with only a few buried courses remaining, where a frontal addition followed the original tower.
descriptions.NUR4309: Complex nuraghe, collapsed and with only a few buried courses remaining, where a frontal addition followed the original tower.
descriptions.NUR4311:
A. Sanguinetti, who around 1970 described an elliptical-plan tower with a rather irregular outer circuit and wide gaps, especially to the south-south-west, where he hypothesised an entrance opening.

The maximum diameter of the monument has been calculated at about 11.10 m, while no observation on the construction technique employed is possible because no wall faces still in place can be distinguished.
descriptions.NUR15059: Complex nuraghe, quadrilobate, of which only a small amount remains
descriptions.NUR5454:
It stands on the summit of a conical hill at 275 m above sea level.

Ruins of a very important settlement. Complex nuraghe with a probable surrounding village. The ground plan consists of a central tower surrounded by four lateral towers joined by curtain walls. The materials used are large roughly hewn blocks of calcareous marl. A large circular livestock enclosure, still visible, was built on the north-west side with the collapsed material from the settlement.
descriptions.NUR4869: Multi-lobed, with a central tower of which only the basal course survives; this breaks off to the south and south-west for a length of 8 m, where the foundations of four peripheral towers appear, originally joined by straight curtain walls, forming a basal platform supporting the main tower, which has a diameter of 9.60 m. About 11 m from the central tower the basal walling of a circular hut 8.40 m in diameter is almost entirely visible. The structures of the complex are composed of sandstone blocks.
descriptions.NUR15062: Complex nuraghe with a dismantled and buried village
descriptions.NUR4302:
Single-tower nuraghe of which only the ground-level courses remain.

Twenty-two Nuragic villages, large and small, are known in the municipal area, not all occupied at the same time. They are often found near a nuraghe, as in the case of the Bruncu Pubusa site.
descriptions.NUR4511: Settlement in considerable decay. Situated at 256 m above sea level. On the summit a crown of limestone rocks surrounded by shrubby scrub is visible, including s'arrùda (Ruta d'Aleppo). The remains of the Nuragic construction have an internal diameter of 4.05 m. It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe but the dense expanse of scrub could hide other structures. The position is strategically elevated, with a very wide visual basin.
descriptions.NUR14998: Complex nuraghe with a dismantled and buried village, the structure of which cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR5362: A ruined nuraghe on the so-called crown, of basalt, of the Giara di Gonnosnò/Genoni. Covered in vegetation, it is not easily accessible.
descriptions.NUR18225: Nuraghe known from ancient writings (Taramelli) and in the toponym recognized by the elders of the village. Noted by Costantino Corongiu.
descriptions.NUR11568: It is a proto-nuraghe or early nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR12748: Near the settlement, never subjected to excavations or studies. Particularly eroded, it shows traces of huts in the vicinity.
descriptions.NUR4658: On the summit of the nuraghe ruins, during the post-war period a watchroom was built for the sentinels of the powder magazine. Single-tower, rock-cut, collapsed and buried.
descriptions.NUR5673:
Complex nuraghe.

Although listed as Brundette Nuraghe, it is instead known (even by the local elders) as Chentucheddas Nuraghe, and it is situated on the edge of the named rock.
descriptions.NUR1218: This nuraghe, on the boundary between the municipalities of Olmedo (SS) and Sassari, appears in Filippo Nissardi's Nuragic Map of the Nurra (published by G. Pinza in 1901) as "Nuraghe Grascioleddu" and is assigned to Olmedo.
descriptions.NUR6402: In a dominant position above the Riu Liscoi, on a spur of granite rock, a corridor nuraghe is visible, elliptical in plan and built of pink granite and trachyte; the interior cannot be visited because of collapses, and it is flanked by the remains of several circular huts.
descriptions.NUR3016: Bocca d'Irghiriai is a narrow, rugged rocky saddle that separates the cliff face of Monte Bàrdia from the massive stronghold of Monte Irveri. It must have been a pass used in antiquity as well: near the rocky spur that overlooks the saddle to the east lie the scant remains of a single-tower nuraghe built of limestone.
descriptions.NUR3174: It is located on the shores of Lago del Cuga and spends most of the year submerged under water. It also belongs to the nuraghes of the Cuga valley.
descriptions.NUR6393: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The building is in a fair state of preservation despite the considerable alterations it has undergone. It has a surviving height of about 5 m. The outer wall face is clearly visible and better preserved on the north-east side, while on the southern side it is heavily altered and covered with vegetation. (Pruna on the I.G.M. map)
descriptions.NUR3180:
It has a vaguely trapezoidal plan (10.50 x 10.20 x 11.10 x 4.50 m) with rounded corners and a raised entrance (0.75 m above ground level), with a rectangular opening (width 1.47 m – height 1.98 m), lintelled and facing north-east.

The interior of the monument is not visible because of the collapse.

The masonry consists of roughly dressed polygonal blocks of medium and large size laid in irregular horizontal courses.
descriptions.NUR814: Three-lobed nuraghe, reused in the Roman and medieval periods. The village surrounding the tower, now almost entirely vanished due to agricultural mechanization, is one of the largest in the Uri region.
descriptions.NUR6354: The monument, of complex type (four-lobed), comprises a main tower to which four secondary towers have been added, linked to the north and east by straight curtain walls, while the connecting wall structure to the west is curved.
descriptions.NUR2106: The monument, located near the Borore cemetery and a short distance from the Nuraghe Pischedda, is reduced to a few courses of the elevation, which nevertheless allow it to be identified as a complex nuraghe of the “a tancato” type, consisting of the central tower to the north-west, joined to a smaller opposing tower to the south-east by two straight wall wings that enclose a trapezoidal space; the whole is bounded by an outer wall. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR6010: Nuraghe Busoro lies in the municipality of Sedilo, about 1.5 km north of the village. It is a single-tower nuraghe, built of basalt; the internal tholos lacks its uppermost courses.
descriptions.NUR3202: The Nuraghe of Busurtei stands on top of the hill of the same name, from which there is a breathtaking view. Near the nuraghe, in the medieval period, stood the small village called Busurtei, Busateri or Buzarcheri, which belonged to the diocese of Santa Giusta in 1224. About a hundred metres north of the nuraghe there is a spring whose water is said to be the best of all the springs in the territory of Sedilo.
descriptions.NUR5101: Complex nuraghe or nuragic fortress, apparently earthen and completely levelled to the ground, with only the low courses partially buried remaining. From it, a large part of the Marmilla could be seen.
descriptions.NUR3591: It lies a few dozen metres from the building. It is a fine example of a single-tower nuraghe in a fairly advanced state of decay. Some features can be seen, but they appear to be relatively recent additions and therefore not attributable to the Nuragic construction, which would seem to be a sacrificial altar. Nuraghe of the sprouted site. See Càcchile. mu
descriptions.NUR10095: Complex nuraghe with frontal addition and lateral extension, featuring a central tower and two additional towers with bastions, and in the middle lies the courtyard as an integration space.
descriptions.NUR6002: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a niche, a corridor staircase, and a chamber flanked by three niches arranged in a cross. The monument was bounded by an outer wall running about 10 metres from the tower, perhaps for 380°; it lies on the boundary between the territories of Dualchi and Sedilo.
descriptions.NUR5554: The Nuraghe Cae is a complex nuraghe, with a central tower and at least two towers joined by a bastion; the presence of another two towers on the south-east side is probable, and a semi-underground gallery is also mentioned. A small village and signs of the area's reuse in Roman times are also present.
descriptions.NUR6467: It lies to the south-east of the village, not far from the Tirso River. Its state of preservation is very poor, being almost completely destroyed, like the Jana nuraghe. However, the extent of the rubble, about 25 x 18 metres (1), suggests a complex of considerable size. Nor can one overlook the fact that the very long fence enclosing the field in which it stands is built entirely from the stones of the nuraghe itself.
descriptions.NUR6321: It is a single-tower nuraghe, with a stair and a corridor niche, a ground-floor chamber flanked by two subsidiary rooms, and a further room above the corridor. It probably had an added structure (a courtyard?) and an outer wall enclosing various related structures of the adjoining settlement. The nuraghe is easily reached from the road called Valle dei Nuraghi, following an unsurfaced track that lies on private property, so access is not guaranteed.
descriptions.NUR4047: The Caìu nuraghe is certainly the remains of a tancato nuraghe, that is, two towers enclosing a small internal courtyard, probably datable to the end of the Recent Bronze Age. It lies near the Genna Salixi Necropolis.
descriptions.NUR15254: Ruined nuraghe enveloped in the maquis. Presumably complex. Several courses of the masonry are clearly visible. The outline of the central tower and some secondary chambers connected to it can be made out.
descriptions.NUR3447: The monument stands on a natural terrace in a hilly area used for pasture. About 300 m to the north-west lies the giants' tomb of Funtana Morta. The nuraghe is almost completely destroyed and only the external ground plan, vaguely circular, can be made out.
descriptions.NUR3074: On a plateau used for crops and pasture, only the basal course has been identified, made of large, roughly dressed blocks, of what is thought to have been a nuraghe. Its sub-circular ground plan, which incorporates a large natural granite boulder, is still legible. Because of stone-clearing work and the reuse of the ashlars for dry-stone walls, not even traces of the collapse survive.
descriptions.NUR5744: Possible remains of a proto-nuraghe on which later Roman activity also took place, constructing part of a military outpost.
descriptions.NUR6289: Very ruined, so its structure is hard to make out. A lintelled corridor is visible to the north of the chamber. To the south an ogival chamber. Around it the remains of the village huts can be recognised.
descriptions.NUR4194: The central tower, which at its top has a diameter of about 8 m, is clearly legible. It survives for nine courses of regular sub-squared masonry with medium-sized blocks wedged with stone chips. The upper interior is completely blocked by collapse. Added structures can be made out, though with difficulty, hidden by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR2694:
It stands on a ridge from which it is possible to control the valley where the Nurritani people were settled, bounded by the Roman boundary stone found in that area by Prof. Mastino.

The region lying south of the Tirso extended between Orotelli and the sources of the Tirso east of Benetutti, and bordered the Goceano to the north and the Barbaria to the south.
descriptions.NUR1923:
It is a complex nuraghe of which the central tower and three other perimeter towers are visible (the presence of a fourth on the WSW side is not ruled out), joined together by a wall following a straight and curvilinear course.

The last excavation campaign ended in 2009.

The masonry is built of cyclopean basaltic andesite boulders, averaging 3 quintals each, with small stones and mud mortar also used in the interstices.
descriptions.NUR2787:
The nuraghe still has an accessible tholos, although its top is missing. The entrance lacks its original material all the way up to the top of the tower, perhaps because of a collapse that affected the load-bearing structures of the wall in the past. The masonry has been rebuilt.

The nuraghe was almost certainly used both as a shelter and as an animal pen, and this has allowed it to be preserved in good condition.

The monument has the stairway on the left, with 13 steps still in place.
descriptions.NUR3605: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. In very poor condition, a few boulders of the entrance jamb and part of a basal course are visible. The entrance faces west. The nuraghe has suffered repeated robbing, as shown by several heaps of basalt boulders a short distance away. Even so, it cannot be ruled out that the nuraghe was never finished, as is documented elsewhere in the area.
descriptions.NUR2296:
Small single-tower nuraghe completely destroyed.

The nuraghe was listed under the name Pirastu Fattu, but the owner, Mr G. Raspa, who was born and has lived in those places, states that the real name is Campo Maggiore.
descriptions.NUR2687: Single-tower built on the summit of a cliff, almost completely collapsed, walls about two metres thick, previously used as a shelter for animals.
descriptions.NUR2717: Complex nuraghe of the type with lateral addition. Built of local basalt. It has a partially collapsed and recently restored vault, in relation to the last use as a sheepfold.
descriptions.NUR10798: It is a proto-nuraghe or early nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR3710: It appears to be a corridor nuraghe, partially collapsed and immersed in vegetation.
descriptions.NUR2140: A single-tower tholos nuraghe, built of large polygonal blocks of local basalt. It survives to a height of 4–5 courses and the inner chamber has collapsed in on itself, leaving it filled with collapse debris. The diameter is about 12 m. The entrance faces south-east, although it is hidden by the structures of a later hut built against it.
descriptions.NUR3921: Structures belonging to a simple single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The remains of the nuraghe are very scanty and lie among several contemporary structures. It must have been a small nuraghe; a few basal courses can be seen, overlain by a mass of displaced blocks, to a maximum surviving height of 1.50 m. The chamber has collapsed completely. The entrance cannot be identified.
descriptions.NUR5858: Single-tower with a circular plan and a chamber completely missing its top; three niches arranged in a cross can be seen. The external wall face remains with five courses. The entrance, located in the south-east, has collapsed.
descriptions.NUR2138: Probably a single-tower tholos nuraghe. Almost completely hidden by dense vegetation, it appears as a heap of polygonal basalt blocks lying in disorder. A few courses can be made out inside a thicket of mastic on the west side.
descriptions.NUR6363: Near one of the 5 corridor nuraghe present in the territory of the comune of Ghilarza
descriptions.NUR5010: It is a massive andesite nuraghe with a three-lobed plan, the result of adding two secondary towers in front of the central tower, linked by walls that enclose a central courtyard. Not far from the nuraghe stands a hut of considerable size; nearby there is also a well carefully lined inside, also probably dating to the Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR5391: In the territory of Sanluri there are remains of as many as 15 nuraghe, three of which are complex nuraghe with multiple towers: Corti Sa Perda, Geni, Nuraxi Candelas.
descriptions.NUR1905: Nuraghe no longer existing. The nuraghe is mentioned in Spanish documents of the Episcopal Curia (12 October 1720) as a landmark, under the name “Nuraxy de Condiazzus/Candiazus”. It also appears in Angius as “Nuargi de Candiazzus” (1840), on the IGM maps (1897), in Taramelli (1910?), and from my fellow citizen Pinuccio Orlando as Nuarxi de su candiacciu (Toponimi dell'Isola).
descriptions.NUR2794: It is also known as Su Canarzu and is recognised as Su Aijanu, which is the name of the plot of land on which it is built. Only the large closure stone and the two jambs are visible. In the surrounding area there are stones worked by man that were used to mark boundaries, and also wild olive or mastic trees.
descriptions.NUR12967: Remains of a single-tower nuraghe and village.
descriptions.NUR3152: Unusual rectangular plan with a probable entrance on the south side, which has collapsed completely. The north, west and east sides remain visible. Built on the edge of a steep slope, it is probably a temple dedicated to the water cult, as suggested by two springs (long dry) at the foot of the structure on the south side. One spring is covered by an almost intact tholos with its entrance partly blocked by a collapse, while the other, triangular in plan, shows clear traces of a spring at its apex.
descriptions.NUR4040: Complex nuraghe, collapsed and with only a few buried courses remaining, where a transverse addition followed the original tower.
descriptions.NUR6094: Nuraghe “a tancato” has on the front face of the main tower a wall of irregular shape that encloses a smaller tower and a courtyard situated between the two towers.
descriptions.NUR4787: Complex nuraghe still entirely to be discovered and described
descriptions.NUR1424: Provided with a corresponding Nuragic settlement.
descriptions.NUR3465: Nuraghe surrounded by vegetation. at the edge of the village, single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical plan, still in good conservation.
descriptions.NUR576: Complex nuraghe, it cannot be confidently assigned to any defined type due to the state of degradation or the significant burial of the structures.
descriptions.NUR16406: Of the nuraghe (later converted into an anti-aircraft post during World War II) no traces remain as it was erased by the construction of the restaurant, which was subsequently abandoned.
descriptions.NUR19410: The nuraghe, of which no trace remains, stood on the headland now called Torre Canai – Turri. The map of Sant'Antioco drawn by the geographer Major Besson in 1744 suggests that the tower, built by order of the King of Sardinia, Charles Emmanuel III, in 1757 on the headland “su moru”, was constructed using the Nuragic structures.
descriptions.NUR5923: Nuraghe in very poor condition of conservation
descriptions.NUR6031: Single-tower with a tholos in polygonal basalt ashlar. Broken lintel. Stairwell on the left side from the entrance corridor. Two niches visible inside the chamber. Traces of huts in the vicinity.
descriptions.NUR4888: Nuraghe Carcina stands in the countryside of Orroli, about 1.5 km south-east of the village. It is abandoned but in fair condition. It appears as a complex nuraghe with two towers clearly visible. The main tower has a surviving height of over 3 metres and is entered through a doorway topped by a fine sloping lintel. This doorway is largely buried and gives access to a chamber with a tholos that is missing its top courses.
descriptions.NUR5212: On an isolated hilltop located about 40 metres south-southwest of the Su Sonadori nuraghe, the remains of a complex nuraghe were observed; currently it is concealed by heaps of rubble stones.
descriptions.NUR5256: At the western end of the elongated Carronca Simoi ridge, beneath the ruin of a small rectangular building, scant remains of a probable nuraghe can be seen; about 20 metres to the east of it, some stone blocks appear to belong to a round Nuragic hut.
descriptions.NUR674: Nuraghe with extensive collapse on the eastern side, difficult to read in plan. Adjacent huts belonging to a probable village.
descriptions.NUR4908: Probably four-lobed, and one of the most imposing in the area. It consists of a central tower enclosed in a bastion with three transverse front towers. The lintel is currently visible at the level of the collapse that fills the courtyard. From inside the chamber the entrance corridor is visible. The stair leading to the upper part of the tower, which very probably had two storeys given the extent of the collapse on the north side, must have started from it.
descriptions.NUR4397: Single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, of which only the base survives, controlling the valley of the Rio Gutturu Mannu to the east. Taken from the archaeological map of Sant'Andrea Frius drawn up by Roberta Relli and Antonio Forci.
descriptions.NUR995: In very poor condition, only scant elements of the structure survive amid the vegetation. The location is uncertain, on the left bank of the Canale Orune, next to the water tank built during the Second World War.
descriptions.NUR11483: Complex nuraghe with settlement. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR11531: Complex nuraghe, a main tower with a frontal addition of a second tower. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR994: Single-tower built of large white limestone blocks, situated in a cleared area within an olive grove, with a direct drop to the Orune Channel to the north-northeast. Only three courses remain, with a maximum height of about 3 m.
descriptions.NUR3531: On the map provided by the Forests Agency, it appears as such, and shares the same toponym as the nuraghe located a few km to the north-east.
descriptions.NUR1086:
Nuraghe "CASTEDDU" located in the hamlet of Pozzo S. Nicola (municipality of Stintino).

It could be a three-lobed or four-lobed nuraghe, currently buried.

L.L.
descriptions.NUR17933: The eastern part, which enjoys an excellent view over the whole inner gulf of Olbia, is the best preserved. It rises about four metres from the ground. The lintel is barely visible (see photo) while the entrance is almost completely buried. Traces of the megalithic enclosure are barely visible, but the multitude of remains and collapsed blocks suggest the monument's importance.
descriptions.NUR15002: A ruined and buried single-tower nuraghe whose structure cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR5132: It is a complex nuraghe consisting of two towers. The original second floor has collapsed, blocking part of the first level.
descriptions.NUR6017: Only a few courses of porphyritic material are visible.
descriptions.NUR5900: Single-tower with its top missing and a collapsed vault inside. The best-preserved section is four metres high and has eight courses. To the south-east the entrance is preserved with an architrave and a window for drainage.
descriptions.NUR3347: Nuraghe with a large village and giants' tomb of attachment. Damaged and overgrown with vegetation. The shape is difficult to identify.
descriptions.NUR1579: It is located within the territory of the comune of Sassari. It is heavily eroded and surrounded by dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR3473: Diroccato, only the first courses are visible. It must have been of considerable size, having a base diameter of about 15 metres.
descriptions.NUR2736:
The nuraghe lies near the village of Birori and consists of a low hill that has formed over time on the ruins of the monument.

From what can be seen it is a four-lobed nuraghe with a central tower enclosed by a bastion with four corner towers. Around the fortress the traces of an outer wall and the circular outlines of numerous huts are clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR2803: The nuraghe, as shown on the maps of the former cadastral survey, is listed under the name "Chessalzu". Only a few buried courses remain.
descriptions.NUR11141: Nuraghe with frontal bilobate addition. Today completely submerged by the waters of the Cuga basin. It belongs to the complex of nuraghes surrounding the Chessedu Cuga valley.
descriptions.NUR4867: An imposing Nuragic site. Various hypotheses and recent analyses suggest the remains of a four-lobed (or five-lobed) complex nuraghe. Currently open to the public; the north tower can be visited. A central opening leads to internal chambers and continues into precarious passages that suggest a complex, articulated structure.
descriptions.NUR2715: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. It is almost completely covered by climbing vegetation, especially on the side facing N–NE. The western side is the most legible, with structural remains standing just over 4 m high, while the tower as a whole is about 7 m high.
descriptions.NUR737: Always within a private plot of land lies the base of this nuraghe. A probable presence of a village in the immediate vicinity.
descriptions.NUR3423: Reduced to the extreme act of ruin. Only some basally arranged stones, variously shaped, remain, all set within a large mass of mastic wood.
descriptions.NUR5369: Nuraghe and structure of uncertain definition
descriptions.NUR2269: In its present condition no scatter of lithic or ceramic material is visible on the ground; however, the presence of structures belonging to a possible village cannot be ruled out, their remains may have been obliterated at the surface by changes in land use.
descriptions.NUR3897: Only a few traces of the structure remain; the site is neither accessible nor easily legible at present. Following the penetration of the Greek Church, Greek Orthodox monks and hermits taught the inhabitants the production of sun-dried bricks in the eastern manner, made of mud and straw (ladrini), which were used for building houses, using the stone taken from the nuraghe Zira as a foundation.
descriptions.NUR19888: It stands on Cuccuru Cireddu at 130 m above sea level. It is not in good condition and is almost completely covered by mastic. It is in visual contact with the Nuraghe Monte Eghedda about 1 km away and the Nuraghe S'Omu e S'Orku about 2 km away as the crow flies. Documents from the Municipality of Maracalagonis also report a necropolis, perhaps "Roman"; indeed, a large amount of material is present all around the nuraghe over a wide radius.
descriptions.NUR5769:
More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe or corridor nuraghe.

It appears in the maps of the former cadastral survey and is listed as Nuraghe Piraruja.
descriptions.NUR5228:
The nuraghe was built directly on the bedrock, and its plan appears to have been adapted to the irregularities of the rock, since walling can be seen on several levels along the slopes of the outcrop.

On the summit the monument, now almost completely destroyed, seems to have an elongated plan, but its very poor state of preservation and an illicit excavation make the whole difficult to interpret.
descriptions.NUR4387:
In its present state of preservation it is only possible to hypothesise, on the basis of the few identifiable wall stretches, that the monument developed on several levels following the different levels of the rocky peak on which it was built.

Perhaps its major axis was oriented north–south, but the position of the entrance and the plan layout of the chamber remain undefinable.
descriptions.NUR5576: It consists of a central nucleus attributable to the type of the so-called “corridor nuraghi”, which are older and structurally different from the “tholos nuraghi” (because the roof is not a false dome but flat-arched), in which two chambers can be identified: one is circular, with a diameter of about 7 metres, the other oval, with a diameter of about 8 metres, connected to each other by a “flat-arched covered corridor”.
descriptions.NUR3114:
It is in very poor condition.

It is a circular single-tower nuraghe (diameter 11.50 m), built with massive limestone blocks. At present the wall face survives to a maximum height of 1.80 m over three courses of stones on the south side and 0.80 m over a single course on the north side.
descriptions.NUR6268: Name and/or location might not be accurate.
descriptions.NUR658: Name and/or location might not be accurate.
descriptions.NUR4670: Proto-nuraghe of elliptical or sub-elliptical profile
descriptions.NUR6294: DIRROCCATO NURAGHE WITH ABOUT SIX COURSES EXTERIOR TO GROUND LEVEL
descriptions.NUR6188:
The monument stands on the edge of a steep rock face that drops sheer to the south, in an area of particular interest for the presence of numerous archaeological monuments, both prehistoric and Nuragic.

The building has a roughly quadrangular plan and is crossed by a through corridor flanked by opposing pairs of large niches; the corners are rounded, the walls where the entrances open are straight in profile to the ESE and slightly concave to the ENE.
descriptions.NUR20354: It is a quadrilobate rectangular structure very similar to Santa Barbara in Macomer. It has a ground area of about 400 m².
descriptions.NUR5924: The Nuragic site lies in the locality “Su cuccuru de i Zannas”, on the edge of the village. It is a five-lobed nuraghe with an internal courtyard, whose first phase belongs to the Final Bronze Age, overlaid by several phases of reuse ranging from the Late Punic period to the Roman Republican period. A Late Antique – Early Medieval settlement stands against the monument and was occupied at least until the 7th century AD.
descriptions.NUR3390: The Nuraghe Codas is a single-tower nuraghe built of basalt blocks, situated about 7 km south of Paulilatino. Together with the Nuraghi Forreddos, De Mesu and Su Guzzu it forms a quadrilateral between the territories of Zerfaliu and Paulilatino. Despite several collapses it has kept its majesty intact.
descriptions.NUR5507:
Very deeply buried four-lobed nuraghe, probably still preserving intact environments.

Access to it is currently impossible.
descriptions.NUR6352:
A single-tower tholos nuraghe standing in the middle of the dense holm-oak and downy-oak woodland of the Sos Paris area, Codinazza locality. Four basal courses built of large polygonal blocks of local basalt are visible, reaching a maximum surviving height of about 2.50 m. The base diameter of the nuraghe is about 13 m.

The inner chamber has collapsed in its upper part and the surviving portion is covered by a substantial fill of collapse debris.
descriptions.NUR777: It is a single-tower nuraghe; currently two courses of the base remain standing; the stones that made it up lie both inside and outside. The entrance is perfectly clear, but the lintel cannot be identified with certainty. Built of basalt, it dominates the whole Gulf of Gonone to the south. From the top the nuraghe Buca d'Irghiriai can also be seen, on the pass of the same name.
descriptions.NUR2693: The nuraghe, collapsed internally, shows a fairly irregular plan, typical more of proto-nuraghe than of true tholos nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR3686:
This nuraghe stands on a hillock opposite the village of Mara.

It is signposted yet completely neglected. To reach the monument one has to pick through tall scrub that makes it almost invisible. For this reason it is hard to describe, especially for a layperson.

It appears to be of the corridor type.
descriptions.NUR2753: Nuraghe built of calcare ashlar. On top of it a shelter was constructed with the erection of new walls made of small calcare ashlar. To the north, at the entrance, there is a concio with a carved recess.
descriptions.NUR6318: It is one of many nuraghes in the Thiesino area, of which today only a few remains can be identified.
descriptions.NUR3119: Single-tower nuraghe in excellent condition. Corbelled entrance corridor with a left-hand intramural staircase.
descriptions.NUR3047: The monument, about 300 metres north-west of the Nuraghe Su Figu, is now almost completely buried under rubble from the clearance of the surrounding fields, a fact that makes the plan of the nuraghe extremely difficult to read. It appears to be a circular single-tower nuraghe, with a stair and a corridor niche, visible where the top is missing.
descriptions.NUR6230: Single-tower nuraghe, in basalt, with its tholos collapsed.
descriptions.NUR5781: Complex nuraghe with remains of a village; in 2016 it was surrounded by dense vegetation, making it impossible to visit.
descriptions.NUR6439: It is a fine example of a nuraghe built with a subsidiary staircase and a sub-floor chamber. It can be entered to reveal its structure, which rises with blocks of friable white limestone inside a grove of oaks, ashes and yews that make the setting pleasant and evocative. It is almost entirely covered by fill earth that has fallen from the slope, so that it is nearly completely buried. Nuraghe of the valley of the judge, of the king of Torres.
descriptions.NUR3764: Eroded by the force of water
descriptions.NUR6050: Conca e Bentu (Porta del vento). Single-tower nuraghe built with cyclopean technique; it has a central chamber with three niches arranged in a cross, only the right-hand and left-hand ones being visible, the central one having collapsed. The chamber is reached from a lintelled corridor with a flat roof, which has a storage cell on the right and the start of the staircase that led to the upper floor or the terrace on the left.
descriptions.NUR2799: Simple single-tower nuraghe, in very poor condition, with traces of a possible settlement.
