descriptions.NUR552: On the north-western tip a few alignments of small blocks can be made out, suggesting the remains of a nuraghe tower; on the south-eastern tip a short stretch of curvilinear walling; in the hollow to the north a closing wall between the two tips.
descriptions.NUR944: Single-tower nuraghe stands on a cliff face with a sheer drop, along which the structure has collapsed, rendering it inaccessible but with a base at least 12 m in diameter. Around it, the remains of a megalithic wall, intended for site defence, are present.
descriptions.NUR4241: The tower of Conca Santinta must have had a significance that went beyond the purely strategic, since large quantities of metalworking slag have been found on the site, and the minerals that make up the hill have properties particularly suited to the working and production of ceramics.
descriptions.NUR3919: Situated at the base of a tafone on the south side of the Berchida valley, a small village stands composed of a few huts built with dry-stone masonry. Initially identified as a nuraghe, it does not in fact have the characteristics of one.
descriptions.NUR2587: Nuraghe completely immersed in vegetation and partially eroded due to this. Structure not easily legible
descriptions.NUR1026: The poor state of preservation does not allow a clear reading of the structure, which nevertheless appears to be a single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical shape.
descriptions.NUR6465: Only faint traces of the nuraghe remain.
descriptions.NUR5967: Corridor nuraghe with a tholos and relatively intact. It has the peculiarity of a double symmetric entrance, as seen in corridor nuraghe, although it features a tholos. In excellent condition and carefully maintained by the community of S'Aspru.
descriptions.NUR6257: Nuraghe with buried entrance. Access to the interior is possible through a passage leading to a staircase chamber. The chamber features three niches, with the tholos intact. In the area, several baetyls and cremation urns are also present.
descriptions.NUR4930: The nuraghe is in a state of considerable degradation, and there are artificial structures also inside the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR4492: The nuraghe is in very poor condition, reduced merely to some courses.
descriptions.NUR15939: In the current census this monument is listed as "Nuraghe su Nidu su Cojvu".
descriptions.NUR4716:
A corridor nuraghe, affected by a conspicuous collapse, built with polygonal blocks of local stone. Among the collapse of the imposing wall face, the perimeters of the upper portions of some oval chambers can be made out.

To the north-west, traces of occupation from the protohistoric and historic periods are visible, consisting of short, semi-hidden stretches of walling.

Santoni mentions it under the name nuraghe Moru Nieddu B.
descriptions.NUR8274: Complex nuraghe almost completely devastated by the construction of a aqueduct with a cistern directly situated upon the nuraghe itself.
descriptions.NUR3149: The nuraghe is a complex type, probably with a frontal addition, although its poor state of preservation and the abundant spontaneous vegetation on the ruins do not allow an optimal reading. The building is constructed of local basalt blocks laid in polygonal masonry. The central tower survives, with its chamber collapsed, and an enveloping bastion with two probable towers on the front.
descriptions.NUR15047: Complex nuraghe, partially eroded and buried, for which it is not possible to define the structure.
descriptions.NUR704: The remains of the Corongiu nuraghe lie in the municipality of Ollastra, in the Serra Laccus area. Unfortunately the monument has been almost completely dismantled. It must have been a tholos nuraghe, but its ground-plan module is not clear.
descriptions.NUR4764:
It is a proto-nuraghe in a dominant position on the edge of Pranu e Muru, the basalt lava flow in the territory of Nurri, east of the Flumendosa river. From the red crown one commands the Santa Vittoria mountains as far as the Gennargentu and, below, the canyon in which the roughly 17 kilometres of the Medio Flumendosa lake have been formed.

The corridor nuraghe joins its austere bareness to the majesty of the landscape that can be admired from there in a full 360 degrees.
descriptions.NUR2116: Complex nuraghe of which a circular chamber in a central position survives. It may be the central tower, of which the entire perimeter outline survives, though only for a single course. The inner wall face of the central tower is visible on the sides oriented from north to south-east. The tower abuts the edge of a rocky ridge, with a sheer drop to the north. A built structure is abutted against the original tower, of which the points of contact oriented to the west and north-west survive.
descriptions.NUR3720: What remains of the probable nuraghe rests on a granite outcrop, of which some stretches were very likely incorporated into the wall face. At present only half a circuit of roughly dressed, medium- and large-sized granite blocks survives in plan. At the base of the outcrop, at a slightly lower level, two short wall stretches survive, whose function cannot be determined because of the monument's state of preservation.
descriptions.NUR3834: It is in a very ruinous state and the outer wall face is bulging out towards the north-east. Unfortunately its hours are numbered too. Too ancient and forgotten, targeted by treasure hunters, it is subjected to every kind of criminal damage. Against its will it played a leading part in the national Rai Tre programme "All'ultimo minuto". It belongs to that large group of nuraghi with a sub-floor chamber. A visit is strongly discouraged.
descriptions.NUR4395: More likely it is an ancient nuragic hut.
descriptions.NUR15043:
A ruined, buried nuraghe of unidentifiable structure.

Traditionally the locals place it near the river. Visually only a circle of stones at ground level can be seen.
descriptions.NUR4001: The Nuraghe Corrulia or Currulia stands near the Flumendosa valley in the municipality of Villasalto. To reach it you cross a small bridge leading to a farmstead beside which the nuraghe stands. It is a single-tower nuraghe, now with its top missing, lying in a state of abandonment.
descriptions.NUR21100: Nuraghe heavily collapsed, located in the heart of the city
descriptions.NUR5568:
Practically in the town, on a ridge overlooking Tossilo, this completely derelict single-tower nuraghe stands out. Its layout is the most classic one, with a niche to the left of the entrance to the south-south-east, and the staircase to the upper floor on the left. Inside the tholos, though completely covered in brambles, the three typical niches can be made out.

A splendid spot for sunsets of nostalgic meditation.
descriptions.NUR4980: Nuraghe in very poor condition, only a few external points are visible, many stones are scattered in the adjacent ground, and almost the entire structure is enveloped by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR5685: Single-tower nuraghe in good state of conservation, missing the lintel and access to the staircase leading to the upper floor. Maximum height five metres.
descriptions.NUR12149: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a settlement that has now been completely destroyed.
descriptions.NUR976: Remains of a small single-tower nuraghe built of limestone.
descriptions.NUR5077: Complex nuraghe with a main tower and an additional tower on the eastern side.
descriptions.NUR5318: Remains of a single-tower nuraghe built of basalt.
descriptions.NUR3355:
Il Corvos, apparently a single-tower nuraghe, is in fact a complex nuraghe whose central two-coloured tower still survives in excellent condition, with the first level in limestone and the second in trachyte.

Once through the entrance threshold, the unusual anticlockwise staircase is immediately noticeable, starting on the left side of the corridor; the chamber, which has three niches and is largely buried, preserves its intact tholos, about 5 metres high. The upper floor, however, has collapsed.
descriptions.NUR3305: Single-tower nuraghe probably. Completely covered by vegetation, making its structure difficult to interpret.
descriptions.NUR3850: The nuraghe is located on the summit of a steep rise, characterised by dense woodland, and stands on a rocky granite outcrop that commands an excellent view of the surrounding territory. The monument, in a serious state of decay, is a simple nuraghe with a roughly circular plan, barely recognisable because of the extent of the collapse.
descriptions.NUR16859: Sparingly visible and identifiable, completely engulfed by mastic and cisto. Presence of numerous large trachyte boulders.
descriptions.NUR5019: A single-tower nuraghe now destroyed, near which dense material is found ranging from the Abealzu facies to the Imperial Roman period. The site lies in a locality reachable only by a hike near one of the Forestry Corps lookout towers on the slopes of Monte Arci. The nuraghe, hidden by thick vegetation, is in very poor condition.
descriptions.NUR3830: Single-tower nuraghe with its top missing; the position of the nuraghe is uncertain, and it does not appear marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR1055:
This is an archaeological area that cannot be defined because of the collapses and the vegetation. However, the data collected lead me to determine that it is a complex nuraghe, consisting of an ancient tower surrounded by a massive wall (bastion) with a continuous, concave-convex profile that probably encloses a courtyard, and some minor towers.

All around, the remains of walls (outer wall?) built with blocks of considerable size are visible.
descriptions.NUR2565:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a niche, a corridor staircase, and a chamber flanked by two niches.

The tower, circular in plan (diam. 11.60 m), survives to a maximum height of 6.00 m with 14 courses to the north-west, while at the entrance the elevation reaches 5.20 m over 11 courses: the south-west wall, by contrast, has largely collapsed.
descriptions.NUR2063: A single-tower nuraghe that has collapsed inwards, of which the doorway and about five courses of the tower survive.
descriptions.NUR2747: Complex nuraghe with lateral addition, with two secondary towers added to the main tower. Built of local basalt blocks laid in fairly regular courses. The entrance to the main tower is on the east side; it is trapezoidal with a lintel formed by three irregular blocks and surmounted by an irregular relieving window.
descriptions.NUR3369: The Crabia nuraghe is a single-tower type, built on two superimposed storeys that are still intact, each with a circular central chamber roofed with a tholos. Its distinctive feature is the presence of two staircases: one to the left of the entrance corridor, leading to the first floor and perfectly preserved, while the other, running in the opposite direction to the first, is concealed in a niche inside the tower on the right and leads to a hidden niche on the first floor.
descriptions.NUR1434: The nuraghe has about eight surviving wall courses. The entrance lacks the outer lintel. The stair is visible on the left side and the entrance niche on the opposite side. The tholos chamber has its top missing and is almost completely filled with vegetation, collapse debris and sediments up to a height, against the walls, that exceeds the lintels of the niches, except for the one on the left, whose far end can be glimpsed.
descriptions.NUR4725: This nuraghe is only one of the countless examples found within the territory. Its condition is appreciable, but a maintenance intervention by the municipality was necessary because of some landslides.
descriptions.NUR5066: It is built of cyclopean andesite blocks and consists of a large central tower joined to three towers. Of these, two show their entire interior structure: precisely the east and the west towers. It would be possible to enter the west one to explore the inside of the nuraghe, but I had neither the time nor the wish to risk it. Up to seven courses of the central tower are visible, reaching a height of almost three metres, while up to six courses of the west tower are visible, reaching a height of two and a half metres.
descriptions.NUR5584:
The unpublished proto-nuraghe Crapianu appears to be a decidedly original example among the archaic Nuragic buildings known as proto-nuraghi.

Its most significant peculiarity is that it preserves, inside a large rectangular chamber, unmistakable traces of a supporting ledge (offset) that held up the upper chamber, at a height of two and a half metres.
descriptions.NUR6252: It is almost certainly a single-tower nuraghe standing on a cliff, as if to emphasise its impregnability against a probable enemy attack. About twenty courses of ordered stones are visible in the circles. The inaccessible tholos is probably intact.
descriptions.NUR4653: A few surviving courses of the Crastu nuraghe, located within the village of the same name
descriptions.NUR6284: Of the corridor nuraghe, possibly with a sub-elliptical plan, only some fragments of granite walling from the first course of the base remain.
descriptions.NUR6156: Probable proto-nuraghe, of semicircular plan attached to a rocky mass. Presence of two menhirs
descriptions.NUR5946: It has an elliptical plan and is built on a bed of granite rock. The interior has completely collapsed, suggesting the existence of a chamber to the north with a curvilinear layout. The entrance is not currently visible, but it was probably on the north side, as that is the most accessible. During clearance work, several early medieval ceramic finds decorated with "stampiglia" were recovered.
descriptions.NUR918: The nuraghe, a simple type, retains three quarters of its outer perimeter, while on the south side, where the entrance presumably was, it has collapsed. It has a roughly circular ground plan and is built of roughly dressed granite blocks laid in irregular courses. The interior cannot be seen because it is filled with collapse debris, but from the top of the surviving wall the circular course of the chamber can still be made out.
descriptions.NUR5716: Four-lobed nuraghe, with four towers at the corners of the quadrangular bastion and an internal courtyard facing the central tower's entrance.
descriptions.NUR15177: The oval perimeter outline survives intact. The outer wall face reaches its greatest height on the west-facing side, where eight courses of polyhedral blocks can be counted. Unfortunately the interior is covered with vegetation and collapse, which prevents the contents from being seen.
descriptions.NUR19543: The nuraghe, probably of complex structure, was built on the same rocky ridge as the corridor nuraghe, to the north of it. It shows a very extensive collapse. The central tower can be identified thanks to the presence of two courses of boulders that survive in their original position. On the rocky ridge there is a curvilinear wall running from the west side round to the south-south-east side. On the south side stretches of walling, not well defined because of the collapses, appear to link the two nuraghi.
descriptions.NUR4418: The central tower is visible for four courses of cyclopean blocks. It is likely that at least four more courses lie underground. To the east and north are the remains of two secondary towers, of which little can be seen. Some wall connections are visible on the surface.
descriptions.NUR11023: On the remains of the nuraghe Crixionis a fortified concrete position protected against small-calibre fire, i.e. an observation post serving the coastal defence batteries of the sector, was built during the Second World War.
descriptions.NUR18441: Likely three-lobed, with only the base courses remaining.
descriptions.NUR3570: A mixed-type complex nuraghe, consisting of a main tower with a partially collapsed inner chamber, a second tower on the SW side, and an imposing structure crossed by a corridor that appears to end in a small courtyard containing a further small tower. The monument is very difficult to interpret, both because of the vegetation cover and the deep deposits, as well as the unusual nature of the building itself.
descriptions.NUR17081: Single-tower nuraghe built of basalt. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR2166: Single-tower nuraghe built of basalt. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR14798: It lies in the area of the great Nurra land-reclamation scheme and is one of the nuraghi in the zone that has a mezzanine floor. A complex nuraghe of roughly dressed sandstone blocks, well preserved, it stands inside a private farm used for fruit and vegetable growing. It was reused during the Second World War by the construction of bunkers. In 1940–43 Nuraghe Cubalciada was incorporated into the defensive system of the 204th Coastal Division.
descriptions.NUR5993:
It is a proto-nuraghe; the tower survives to a maximum height of 5.50 m.

Within a radius of 400 m there are 3 giants' tombs, one nuragic spring, and 5 baetyls.
descriptions.NUR4700: The Cuccurada archaeological complex stands on the southern tip of the Mogoro basalt plateau of “Sa Struvina”, in a position commanding a wide view over the Campidano plain and the Rio Mogoro valley. Excavations carried out from 1994 to the present have revealed the presence of monumental structures attributable to different periods: a megalithic wall and a cyclopean structure with an elliptical plan (Cuccurada A), attributable to the developed Eneolithic (Monte Claro Culture, 2700–2200 BC).
descriptions.NUR4083: The actual nuraghe no longer exists, though a section of the perimeter walls is still visible at the summit of the hill. The hill's shape suggests it may conceal more than what is presently apparent.
descriptions.NUR3879: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The structures are completely enveloped in vegetation, so that they look like a small natural rise covered in brambles, bushes and scrub. Although the monument's type can only be guessed at with difficulty from observation, it is likely that if cleared of vegetation it would prove to be in fair condition.
descriptions.NUR10527:
Nuragic settlement with Middle and Late Bronze Age pottery. Following deep excavations for industrial purposes, the site has recently undergone profound changes.

The single-tower nuraghe has been demolished and the building stones have been set aside; the materials are still visible.
descriptions.NUR14959: Damaged nuraghe of which it is not possible to define shape and dimensions
descriptions.NUR4579: The upper part of the structure is visible because it is buried. It consists of a larger tower joined by walls to a smaller tower. The best preserved and most documentable details are on the north side, where two or three courses of the towers and the wall joining them emerge. The stone used is limestone.
descriptions.NUR4257:
The monument has a complex plan in which at least two bodies can be distinguished, one leaning against the other, developing along a north-east–south-west axis 16.50 m long.

The perimeter of the north-eastern body, which has almost completely collapsed and is partly buried, can be traced only at the point where it joins the other tower and in part on the western side.

It may have been an elliptical element whose major diameter measures about 7 m.
descriptions.NUR4806: The nuraghe is completely hidden by earth and vegetation, which give it the appearance of a modest hillock (in Sardinian “cuccuru”) several metres high rising above the waters of the State saltworks; the material conceals the millennia-old structure.
descriptions.NUR3163: Nuraghe belonging to the category of "uncompleted"
descriptions.NUR2678: Nuraghe belonging to the category of "uncompleted"
descriptions.NUR15639: Nuraghe belonging to the category of "uncompleted"
descriptions.NUR15011: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR15013: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR15016: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR14996: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR15045: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR15049: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR15034: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR4666: The basal courses of the single-tower nuraghe are visible among the bushes.
descriptions.NUR4502: The structure recorded here is of unclear form; it may be a small complex nuraghe built over an earlier proto-nuraghe. Ceramic fragments of the Nur I-IIA/B phases are visible around it. It could also be a small mixed nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR11039:
It is located in the territory of the comune of Marrubiu (OR).

More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe or corridor nuraghe with an elliptical plan, accompanied by a large settlement of circular huts.
descriptions.NUR4594: Single-tower nuraghe, of which a few ashlars survive, not easily distinguishable. Nuraghe inhabited up to the Iron Age.
descriptions.NUR3140: It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe, unfortunately also reduced to ruin. Few features are visible because fill soil and a haphazard pile of boulders resulting from land improvements, but of historical and cultural deterioration, have destroyed its essence. mu
descriptions.NUR19453: It is very ruined and overgrown with dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR1577: It is very ruined and overgrown with dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR11019: It is buried on a hillock, in Sardinian cucuru. The upper part, certainly the top of the main tower, can be visited. We see concentric courses of large stones. At the top there are small openings which, if excavated, would lead inside the structure.
descriptions.NUR5815: Single-tower nuraghe belonging to the complex of nuraghes in the Cuga valley. Currently almost invisible and impenetrable due to the thick vegetation.
descriptions.NUR4425: One of the most important historical testimonies near the municipality of Arbus is the nuraghe of Cugui, one of the most original in Sardinia. Set on the summit of a hill in the direction of Fluminimaggiore, the nuraghe of Cugui is easily reached from the Canau area, known for its spring. The nuraghe has three towers, one of which is accessible, although taller people may have considerable difficulty getting inside.
descriptions.NUR3904: The structures, most likely to be interpreted as the remains of a single-tower tholos nuraghe, are literally hidden by a thicket of mastic. A few basal courses, made of polygonal blocks of local basalt, can be glimpsed on the south side. The nuraghe is practically destroyed.
descriptions.NUR19636: It is a small single-tower nuraghe. The ruin stands at most about 2 metres high and consists of a few superimposed courses of medium-sized, roughly worked stones. The external diameter of the nuraghe is about 11 metres. It is built of mixed basalt, limestone and schist stones. The monument is in a precarious state of preservation.
descriptions.NUR1085: Probable single-tower nuraghe, built of limestone.
descriptions.NUR5436: The ruins of the Lepuri nuraghe are not easy to locate. Of the nuraghe, perhaps placed to guard the stream that once flowed a short distance to the south, only a few non-contiguous wall segments survive, suggesting an elongated plan and construction with large, completely unworked or at most roughly dressed boulders.
descriptions.NUR5424: Complex nuraghe with a central tower, with a facade featuring two additional towers. Surrounding it are the remains of what must have been the village.
descriptions.NUR3847: Extensive ruin remains only a small portion of masonry, composed of medium-sized stones arranged on two or three circles.
descriptions.NUR3294: The remains of the nuraghe "CULZU" lie in the municipality of Torralba (SS) in the Su Segadu area, a few dozen metres from the nuraghe Longu, in the so-called Valley of the Nuraghi; it is a single-tower nuraghe built of basalt with a chamber flanked by three niches. It has the entrance and the entrance corridor to the chamber; the tholos is missing its top and various trees growing inside the central chamber protrude from it.
descriptions.NUR4560: Four-lobed nuraghe in which a bronze figurine and the hull of a boat, also bronze, shaped like a four-tower nuraghe, were found.
descriptions.NUR6215: The building has collapsed on the south side and dense vegetation conceals its full extent. The central tower measures about 12 m in diameter and its present height is 7.30 m. At present a short stretch of the stairwell is visible on the north side, where the facing survives and may be the remains of the bastion of a complex building. The nuraghe stands on natural outcrops of trachyte. Around the nuraghe lies an extensive settlement that was also occupied in Roman times.
descriptions.NUR3819: Remains of a nuraghe, of which only the bases remain.
descriptions.NUR5328: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and a bastion with two additional towers. On the north side there are two more towers with a wall, at the narrowest point of the Taccu Ara plateau. Built of basalt.
descriptions.NUR8045: THE NURAGHE THE FOREST HIDES - Nuragic foundation, probably under construction and never finished because there are no collapses and the built structure stands about 1.8 m above ground level.
descriptions.NUR3511: It is located within the territory of the comune of Nuoro. Only a small remains, but nearby there is a giants' tomb.
descriptions.NUR4733: Between Tratalias and S. Giovanni Suergiu, near Is Loccis. In very poor condition.
descriptions.NUR5819: The Nuragic structure of Donna Ciccia is of interest; its name comes from the place-name of one of the plots of land on which it stands; locally it is better known as "sa traversa" because the roads to Sassari and Ozieri cross there. The colour of the stones used in its construction immediately catches the eye. It is still partly visitable despite being in an advanced state of decay. I would invite any reporters to do so with good reason "and not by hearsay".
descriptions.NUR3525: The nuraghe, near an agricultural farm, features a small tower added.
descriptions.NUR4396: Ruined nuraghe. The central tower is clearly visible for 10 courses. A possible trace of an outer wall preceding the north tholos is present. The south-east turret has completely collapsed. The nuraghe appears to have imploded on itself in non-recent times. A short distance away a structure can be identified that suggests it may be a dolmen.
descriptions.NUR5461: It is located within the territory of the comune of Guasila, inside a private plot planted with Mediterranean scrub.
descriptions.NUR4399:
Nuraghe, probably complex, with a village.

Later occupation after the Nuragic age is also evident in the area, shown by the scatter of historic-period pottery fragments on the ground.

The complex, which is difficult to reach, is currently covered by dense vegetation that hides the hut structures, making a correct reading of the plan and its layout difficult.
descriptions.NUR4589: Only a few traces of the completely collapsed settlement remain to the south. Excavated by illegal diggers. Remains of the wall faces are visible.
descriptions.NUR2584:
The nuraghe lies on the outskirts of Sassari, on the SS 127 towards Osilo, behind a sheepfold, on the edge of a precipice in a commanding position over the valley below. Besides being on the brink of the cliff, it is built on a natural bastion, standing on top of a limestone block detached from the ravine itself.

Several structures of uncertain date lean against the main tower.
descriptions.NUR5544: It is a complex nuraghe, partially eroded, located at the centre (mesu) of a wide valley bordering the Alto Oristanese plateau.
descriptions.NUR3795: Among the Florinas nuraghes of simple tholos type, the De Mesu nuraghe (a single-tower, circular structure fairly well preserved) is particularly significant, featuring three deep niches arranged in a cross pattern within the chamber.
descriptions.NUR10185: At the level of a large ruin, a few polygonal blocks from the basal circles are present, sometimes vaguely dressed. The presence of the main entrance facing south-east is evident. The surrounding area is rich in ancient traces and finds. An interesting sheepfold that may date back a few centuries.
descriptions.NUR1892: Nuraghe of which only a small amount remains due to construction in immediately adjacent areas
descriptions.NUR11529: Small nuraghe facing the Giants' Tomb of Coddu Vecchju. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR3666: The Orizanne nuraghe is located alongside the road from Nuoro to Bitti. Like other nuraghes, it has a large oak tree inside the collapsed tholos.
descriptions.NUR10070: In total ruin, only a few large roughly squared boulders remain. The oldest villagers remember its existence, even if only a few basal circles were left. When the Sassari–Tempio dual carriageway was built, the earthworks for it affected more than one site, in total disregard for the enormous historical value they represented, to be used as sub-base for the road network.
descriptions.NUR4011: These are the ruins of a site and a settlement that must originally have been of medium-to-large size. One can indeed make out what must have been the imposing central tower (only the base, the side walls and the entrance lintel remain), at least three other towers, and extensive fortifications running all round the perimeter of the low hill on which the site stands.
descriptions.NUR4117: Tholos nuraghe. There were two towers; one has been completely dismantled to build the drystone wall that runs along the mountain. On the south-east side the tower stands over 4 m high, while the interior is blocked by a layer of earth and debris that makes it inaccessible. Beside it is a cave recently explored by the Uras caving group.
descriptions.NUR1861: Complex nuraghe of which the refaced central tower and wall stretches of three probable lateral towers survive. Three courses of masonry are preserved of the central tower; unfortunately vegetation and accumulated collapse boulders conceal its inner wall face. The refaced central tower [is surrounded] by remains of a bastion of which stretches of curtain walls coordinating the remains of three probable towers survive.
descriptions.NUR2641: It is a single-tower nuraghe with its tholos collapsed. About ten courses and part of the internal niches still survive, unfortunately used by the local herdsman as a place to store produce and also various plastic waste.
descriptions.NUR10489: Another nuraghe completely destroyed, but partially visible on the maps of Sardinia from 1954 and 1977.
descriptions.NUR3135: The name is the one given in: Archaeological Maps of Sardinia by Antonio Taramelli.
descriptions.NUR4814: Nuraghe of the final phase of the Nuragic period, built on the cliff that dominates the valley of the San Pietro Paradiso waterfall, also known locally as "Cascata de s'ascedu".
descriptions.NUR10126:
Seen from a short distance it looks like a rubble hill that hardly suggests a prehistoric monument. We are facing a colossus that offers several readings and which I personally classify among the infrapiano type.

Nuraghe del (terreno) chiuso del re. The presence of the term re almost certainly indicates that in the giudicale period the site belonged to the personal or family estate of one of the judges or kings of Torres or of Logudoro. See Tanca de su re. mu
descriptions.NUR5386: Up to six courses survive for over two metres in height, in large worked sandstone blocks laid and fitted to give the tower perfect circularity. The perfection of the shape is not only horizontal but also vertical. What is visible is the central tower, and it was probably a single-tower nuraghe, but since there is a high mound to the south-east of the visible tower, the presence of something else there cannot be ruled out. The visible tower must have at least four or five courses below ground, judging by the height of the mound of ashlars and earth surrounding the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR12244: Single-tower nuraghe in the territory of Oniferi, located just tens of metres from the necropolis of Sas Concas, is situated in the valley below near the river. Only some blocks remain visible.
descriptions.NUR3271: In a total state of ruin, the few remains are incorporated into a wall of the perimeter tancato. Only the historical memory of the owners of the adjacent properties recalls its existence. A few medium and large boulders are modestly visible.mu
descriptions.NUR1903: The structures suggest the remains of a probable proto-nuraghe. Viewed from a raised position at least two rectangular rooms can be distinguished, while the rest is hidden by vegetation. Unfortunately, various field-clearance operations, with the subsequent piling of stones on top of the ancient structures, cast doubt on the true nature of any other buildings.
descriptions.NUR4660: Corridor nuraghe, a hypothesis supported by the shape of the entrance (lintelled). The site is easily accessible and visitable. Traces of pottery on the outside suggest unauthorised excavations. About 200 m away there is an allée couverte giants' tomb, which some scholars describe as an unfinished work.
descriptions.NUR5794: It had a very complex plan.
descriptions.NUR4168: A double curtain wall of large stones appears along the edge of the hilltop, enclosing a previous Nuragic structure, the nuraghe Diana.
descriptions.NUR4914: The complex nuraghe Diana consists of a tholos and two minor towers linked by a curtain wall to form an overall triangular shape. In the centre is an open-air quadrangular courtyard giving access to the various rooms.
descriptions.NUR10236: If one favours a defensive function for nuraghi, this one at Elighia I is the clearest example. From an altitude of over 600 m a.s.l. it commands the surrounding countryside for 360° and, like a sentinel, keeps watch over anyone rash enough to venture into these lands. Unfortunately it too is in a ruinous state.
descriptions.NUR5594: A site that is difficult to interpret. The nuraghe is certain, but the presence of a giants' tomb also seems certain; it disappeared after land-reclamation works. The term cantòne refers to squared stone blocks, often of limestone or trachyte tuff (pèdra contonina). This surname, no longer in use, probably originated from the quarryman's trade that the unknown brothers from whom the place-name derives must have practised.
descriptions.NUR9817: The near-total absence of building stones has left just enough to understand the nuraghe's ground plan. There is practically an X-ray of the layout: it is as if someone had razed it to the ground, for a massive entrance with its lintel still in situ is detectable, and another, megalithic lintel lying on the ground. The basal circle is composed of ordered stones with a corridor and orthogonal cells. Formidable for specialist study.
descriptions.NUR12917: Nuragic hut or nuraghe base, not marked on IGM map, currently reduced to a rubble heap
descriptions.NUR20260: Probable nuraghe (Ugas 2022), situated beneath the remains of an eighteenth-century fort later used as an anti-aircraft position. Some archaeologists believe it was a four-lobed nuragic palace; others consider this unlikely. Further studies are awaited.
descriptions.NUR9870: The state of abandonment and decay before us is serious. Unfortunately, the indifference of the institutions, which still fail to act despite repeated calls to do so, provokes indignation. The structure is interesting and some parts can still be visited despite the collapses. The corridor remains clearly visible, opening through a dolmenic doorway onto the nearby cliff.
descriptions.NUR11453:
Proto-nuraghe Mura Barbaros. The monument consists of an outer wall that encloses, for at least three-fifths, a building of rather irregular shape. On the level of the collapsed top a short stretch of corridor to the south-east can be made out, partially closed by four lintelled slabs, while to the south-west the lintelled entrance of a second corridor is visible.

Almost a continuation of the previous one.
descriptions.NUR10198: The name of the nuraghe almost certainly comes from the place name. It is a very unusual nuraghe for its construction technique. Unfortunately it has suffered a conspicuous collapse on the west side that limits the survey. Nuraghe of the elongated height of Pantaleo or "of Pantaleo Serra", proper name. It is the first of three nuraghi that stand on the edge of an elongated height. See Sèrra Pantalèo. mu
descriptions.NUR14918: Situated at 140 m above sea level, a Nuragic complex partially damaged by the construction of the Ussana–Donori provincial road. Barrali. The ground plans of the structures belonging to the Nuragic complex were to be brought to light in order to define their structural characteristics and assign a precise chronological date; although the owners granted permission, the excavation campaign was not carried out.
descriptions.NUR11966:
The monument stands on the summit of a rocky granite spur and commands the whole surrounding area; it is bounded on one side by an outer wall and on the other by the natural rock.

It is not clearly legible, because only a few stones of the first course remain; it suggests a small nuraghe or a Nuragic lookout point.
descriptions.NUR10488: The nuraghe has been completely destroyed. It is mentioned in a zone characterized by a Nuragic settlement encompassing an extremely large area.
descriptions.NUR3248: It is a single-tower nuraghe built of basalt blocks, situated in an area where a large number of nuraghi are found, perhaps functionally linked and all close to the course of the Rio sa Mela, a right-hand tributary of the Tirso.
descriptions.NUR5954: Both the nuraghe and the giants' tomb are in very poor condition of conservation and are surrounded by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR4918: Damaged nuraghe of which only 5 or 6 courses remain.
descriptions.NUR4970:
A tancato-type nuraghe, it consists of two towers linked by an internal courtyard entered through the entrance.

The oldest part of the nuraghe is the tower on the right as you enter, while the tower on the left and the connecting walls were added later.
descriptions.NUR4478: Remains of the nuraghe and the Nuragic and Neolithic village.
descriptions.NUR3407: The De Planu or Don Micheli nuraghe has a diameter of 12.50 m and a wall thickness of four metres. The circular chamber, 3.80 m in diameter, is reached through a corridor 4.50 m long, blocked for two metres. At a depth of two metres fragments of vessels with handles of different shapes and a mould hollowed out in the centre came to light; at a depth of one metre fragments of tableware, human bones and a cremation burial were found.
descriptions.NUR861: Single-tower nuraghe built from roughly hewn limestone blocks. It is hidden beneath an impenetrable layer of vegetation.
descriptions.NUR2843:
It is of mixed type, built of large granite blocks, with a central tower reaching 12 metres in height, with corridors and surrounded by three secondary towers. The lintelled entrance gives access to a corridor with a side chamber containing a well just under 2 metres deep. In the central chamber there is another corridor where the helical staircase leading to the upper floor is located.

The other three towers are partially collapsed and difficult to access;
descriptions.NUR6123: It consists of a central tower about 7 metres high and two lateral towers linked by a bastion that wraps around and protects the whole structure. The central tower still has its intact corbelled dome (tholos), while the lateral towers have collapsed. Access is from the south-east, through a small triangular courtyard that leads straight into the entrance of the structure. On the left, after a short corridor, a staircase opens that leads to the top.
descriptions.NUR7162: Multicellular and with an unusual plan.
descriptions.NUR492: Single-cell domus de janas with a carved stele above the door.
descriptions.NUR3419: Collapsed and heavily altered single-tower nuraghe, even repaired with masonry of small concrete blocks
descriptions.NUR5715: Around the area there are numerous traces of very ancient presences, such as votive menhirs and ashlars of various shapes. Other constructions enrich the territory, such as the namesake spring Nuraghe. Polilobato, situated on the summit of the mountain of the same name, and, a little further on, one of the most important Nuragic sacred wells: Su Tempiesu.
descriptions.NUR4401: South-east of Siurgus-Donigala, near the boundary with the territory of Goni. Built on a rise at 494 m above sea level, well-worked limestone blocks were used that survive today to a height of about 5 m. The inner chamber has its top missing, is filled with collapse debris, and shows an ogival entrance. Around the nuraghe the basal courses of the huts of a village can be seen, and slabs driven into the ground that may indicate burials.
descriptions.NUR6084:
His Majesty ERGULIS, the largest of the nuraghi in the Cuglieri area, is a single-tower nuraghe at 106 m above sea level and survives intact in both its masonry and its vault.

It has two opposite niches just beyond the entrance lintel and two inside the chamber, while the niche that would face the entrance is missing.

The lintel has a relieving window facing south.
descriptions.NUR5545: Proto-nuraghe partially collapsed and covered by a dense vegetation layer
descriptions.NUR3261: Single-tower nuraghe standing next to an agritourism farm, of which only three courses survive
descriptions.NUR2677: Single-tower nuraghe standing next to an agritourism farm, of which only three courses survive
descriptions.NUR5913:
It lies in the municipality of Santu Lussurgiu (OR), a few kilometres from the hamlet of San Leonardo de Siete Fuentes.

It is a three-lobed nuraghe with a central tower and two minor towers, one to the south-west and the other to the north-east. Traces of a curtain wall a few metres from the entrance of the first tower, which enclosed the complex, also survive.
descriptions.NUR5812: It is in a very poor state of preservation. Enough remains, however, to allow a basic assessment. From the hill at about 600 m above sea level it overlooks the basalt plateau below, serving well as a lookout. A short distance away, almost next to the nuraghe, some stones are visible that could be baetyls or belong to a giants' tomb.
descriptions.NUR3023: Single-tower nuraghe partially buried in vegetation, with only the large lintel remaining, resting on the lateral walls and free above.
descriptions.NUR5551: Complex nuraghe with a village, very close to the better-known Nuraghe Majore. A turreted bastion (two towers) with a transverse-frontal layout and an intermediate courtyard was built against the central tower, which still has an intact tholos chamber. A third tower, set back from the two frontal ones, with an entrance corridor and an intact tholos, can also be clearly identified.
descriptions.NUR4989:
A complex nuraghe hidden by a conspicuous collapse. A large village of huts to the south-south-west is entirely covered by scrub. On the southern edge of the village a building with curvilinear walls of squared blocks may date to the Nuragic period.

On the hill to the west of the main rise, a Nuragic building, previously thought to be a giants' tomb, appears in fact to be a circular structure ("tower-hut?").
descriptions.NUR5995:
The monument, four-lobed and sub-rectangular in plan, has a central tower of trachyte with a circular plan about 10 m in diameter, and lateral towers linked by a curtain wall built in polygonal technique with roughly dressed boulders.

Near the south-east and north-west sides the remains of several structures with circular-plan rooms are visible.
descriptions.NUR2965: Near the nuraghe there is a Nuragic spring. It is located in the Pedruitta plain. It is immediately evident that it represents an extremely ancient Nuragic feature.
descriptions.NUR2975: (16th–13th century BC), it is built of trachyte. It has a corridor with a spiral staircase on the left and a guard niche on the right, and a vaulted chamber, perfectly preserved, with three niches arranged in a cross. The entrance jambs of the nuraghe are 1.52 m and 1.24 m high respectively. The tower reaches a maximum height of 8 m and consists of seventeen courses of stone. The entrance faces east; its perfectly worked lintel is 1.60 m long, 0.70 m high and 0.80 m wide.
descriptions.NUR6211: Complex three-lobed nuraghe. The central tower has a chamber with three niches set around it. Built of granite.
descriptions.NUR1576: The Ertas nuraghe is the largest Nuragic monument in the Sassari area. It is a four-lobed structure, completely buried and covered by impenetrable vegetation. From the entrance on the south-east it is possible, by crawling, to reach the main tholos, which is still intact.
descriptions.NUR8683: Single-tower with a large diameter, of which only the courses remain up to about 2.50 m in height, with the entrance and lintel.
descriptions.NUR881:
Small observation tower.

Nearby is a hut with a "rotonda" equipped with a bacile.
descriptions.NUR4473: The ceramic finds recovered date to the Monte Claro phase and correspond to those from the nearby nuraghe Trobas. This stands on a rise flanking the prehistoric track to Villanovaforru and has an unusual layout with a large semi-underground chamber and four adjoining rooms.
descriptions.NUR865: The nuraghe is located in the middle of a field cultivated with grain, with very poor visibility. The nuraghe's structure is visible in the field, but not the extent of the village area.
descriptions.NUR2646:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a refacing and an outer wall that recalls the Nuraghe Aidu Olostru of Bortigali in some respects. To the WNW the remains of a massive outer wall (thickness 2.30 m; height 3.00 m) are visible for about thirty metres; it probably enclosed the nuragic tower but now survives only partially, with three or four courses, at a distance of 12–20 metres from the nuraghe.

An extensive village, of which the remains are visible, extended around the inside of the outer wall.
descriptions.NUR8570: This site lies in an olive grove and was studied in the past. It is now completely destroyed and it is unclear whether any village remains survive underground. Some hut or nuraghe shapes can still be made out. The farmland is covered with squared stones and stone fragments. Most of the stones of various sizes have ended up in the many dry-stone walls that surround the site.
descriptions.NUR5488: The Nuragic village lies at 1200 metres above sea level and is one of the highest in Sardinia. Part of the village is fenced, but the gate is open. The three-lobed nuraghe is surrounded by springs and mountains and set in an unspoilt landscape. Inside the nuraghe a staircase leads to the upper floor and the central tower, whose tholos is intact. The remains of the circular huts that made up the village and the nuraghe are of granite.
descriptions.NUR5783: On the site, especially on the steeper side facing Via Aldo Moro, the remains of numerous huts are visible, together with worked stone and ceramic material of various types. The ceramic material is also present in large quantities on the opposite, flat side, to the south of the nuraghe. Some glazed fragments with fewer inclusions appear to indicate occupation later than the Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR1264: Area where ancient maps indicated the location of the nuraghe Evrassu, in the countryside of the commune of Pozzomaggiore (SS); what remains of the nuraghe Frassu (in the countryside of Pozzomaggiore)
descriptions.NUR4064: Complex nuraghe, four towers arranged in a cross around a large courtyard. It consists of a central tower, about 3 m high, linked to two secondary towers by a curtain wall. Some studies describe the complex as a four-lobed structure with concentric additions.
descriptions.NUR4470: A Nuragic village never studied or excavated, lying inside the Gutturu Mannu park, in the Assemini administrative enclave, on the left bank, opposite the springs of the same name. It is completely enveloped by holm-oak woodland, making it almost invisible from the outside.
descriptions.NUR4844: Nuraxi Fenu, inside which, during the excavations, remains of a hearth and animal bones, fragments of Roman pottery and a coin datable to the 3rd century AD were found, allowing a sporadic occupation of the site between the 2nd and 3rd centuries AD to be hypothesised. A violent fire marked the end of the Nuragic occupation, although it was sporadically frequented in the Punic and Roman periods.
descriptions.NUR5877: It is impossible to enter due to the conspicuous collapse affecting the entrance area.
descriptions.NUR4685: It lies to the south, near the boundary with the territory of Usellus. It was presumably a simple single-tower type. It is in very poor condition, although it cannot be ruled out that part of it has been buried over the centuries by natural or human action.
descriptions.NUR1246: At present it is completely buried and covered by shrub vegetation. Because of this its ground plan cannot be read, except for a single course of blocks emerging from the hillock; judging by the extent of the remains it is likely to be a complex type. In the surrounding ground outcrops of roughly dressed limestone ashlars can be seen, suggesting the existence of a village, traces of which are also detectable through photogrammetric analysis.
descriptions.NUR8207: The nuraghe cannot be detected on the ground because of dense scrub covering a possible destruction layer. The presence of abundant pottery nevertheless indicates the Nuragic origin of the site's occupation.
descriptions.NUR14937: The monument lies at 191 metres above sea level in the locality of Fidrigu. The nuraghe is completely destroyed; the few remaining boulders are scattered and it is impossible to reconstruct the original structure. The situation was made worse by the work carried out to install an Enel pylon. As stated above, the nuraghe was abandoned and consequently completely destroyed, and now not even all the boulders that made up the nuraghe remain. The site is on private property.
descriptions.NUR2813: Damaged nuraghe but with the interior accessible. The portal and about five courses of the wall masonry remain.
descriptions.NUR3642: A ruined nuraghe of which it is difficult to say whether it belonged to the category of unfinished nuraghi or single-tower nuraghi
descriptions.NUR3391: Single-tower nuraghe with its top missing but free from the ashlar fragments of the collapsed tholos. Used as a sheepfold.
descriptions.NUR17371: It is heavily eroded and surrounded by dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR992: Now fully incorporated into a mass of rubble, it is in very poor condition with stones scattered throughout.
descriptions.NUR5904: The complex comprises a corridor nuraghe with an attached settlement and a giants' tomb. The proto-nuraghe was entered through an opening at the north-western corner. A short distance from the nuraghe the remains of several huts from the ancient village can be identified.
descriptions.NUR10518: Nuragic settlement with a single-tower nuraghe built of sandy limestone blocks. Middle Bronze Age pottery. The landscape setting of the nuraghe has been radically altered since the site was recorded; nevertheless, traces worthy of protection remain.
descriptions.NUR3863: The nuraghe, located in an area used for pasture, is completely covered by vegetation. Because of the condition the nuraghe is in, it was impossible for us to determine its type, or the possible presence of an entrance or a lintel.
descriptions.NUR3716: The monument, situated in a predominantly hilly area currently used as pasture, is irreparably destroyed. The base of the outer perimeter can still be seen because outcrops of granite emerge from the ground forming a circle.
descriptions.NUR529: Single-tower nuraghe with probably a settlement.
descriptions.NUR795: Masonry of barely rough-hewn blocks alongside others that are well shaped, of various sizes. The side towers: the one on the left is better preserved than the others, rising from the ground for four courses of blocks of considerable size; the tower on the right is barely visible on the surface, with two courses partly buried; the third tower, its footprint covered by collapse, stands opposite the entrance.
descriptions.NUR5678: Situated on the boundary between Sindia and Macomer, this nuraghe lies about 1000 m from the important and well-known archaeological area of Tamuli (Macomer). It is a complex nuraghe with a central tower and two partially preserved secondary towers. The main chamber is circular and has three niches arranged in a cross; the tholos survives intact. At present it appears to the visitor 'protected' by dense vegetation that almost completely covers it.
descriptions.NUR21004: Nuraghe reported whose category cannot be defined
descriptions.NUR15238: The Flumenlongu nuraghe is a single-tower structure with at least two superimposed floors, to which are attached, besides an open courtyard space, a secondary tower and several accessory rooms. A village of circular huts extends around its margins; its extent has not been defined. An important hoard came from one of them, yielding ingots, axes, an adze and several bracelets.
descriptions.NUR2729: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, 11 m in diameter, preserved to a height of about 2.5 m over three courses. Cyclopean walling of barely dressed boulders. The entrance, to the south-east, lacks a lintel and leads into a corridor about 2 m long.
descriptions.NUR15020: Single-tower nuraghe, it faces the Nuraghe Su Nuraxi on the other side of the Rio su Gaffu.
descriptions.NUR3380:
It lies in the municipality of Florinas (SS).

A badly ruined nuraghe; only a few courses of limestone ashlars remain at the base.

An old cart track used to pass nearby, branching off the Florinas–S. Maria di Sea municipal road, but its course has been almost completely erased by pastures.
descriptions.NUR15951: The nuraghe retains a few surviving courses of masonry, more visible on one side. The original position of the doorway can be made out; inside, the base of the chamber is also detectable, but no details of interest can be recorded because it is filled with rubble of varying sizes.
descriptions.NUR3995: another nuraghe in the Segariu area, though neglected and eroded
descriptions.NUR17650:
Completely buried externally, it retains internally a small tholos that extends into a dead-end corridor.

More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe or corridor nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5835: It has a vaguely circular, ellipsoid shape, with two entrances and a central chamber with a niche. Maximum height 4.50 m. The corridor section is ogival-truncated and the roof consists of four large slabs laid flat. On the level of the collapsed top, between the two corridors and the chamber, a stretch of corridor (length 4 m; width 1.25/1.50 m) is visible, whose course and function are difficult to determine in its present state.
descriptions.NUR3209: The nuraghe Franzesu stands in a commanding position on the Spiritu Santu plateau, with a wide view ranging from the Gulf of Asinara to Corsica, controlling important access routes. The nuraghe consists of a central tower and a bilobed frontal bastion without a facing. The bastion is built of large trachyte blocks; it is thought that some of these may be reused menhirs, and at least one certainly was.
descriptions.NUR4563:
The nuraghe is situated practically at ground level.

The poor quality of the rock has likely contributed to the poor condition in which the monument now exists.
descriptions.NUR3572: The nuraghe was almost completely destroyed in the 1960s to obtain building stone for houses. Near the nuraghe there is a well of the same period, which presumably belonged to the building.
descriptions.NUR5758: easily visible, adjacent to the municipal road, almost destroyed at the top of the tower, there is a covered entrance surrounded by bushes.
descriptions.NUR5929:
It lies on the boundary between the municipal territories of Bortigali (NU) and Dualchi (NU), but belongs to the municipality of Dualchi.

More precisely it is a proto-nuraghe. Several cinerary urns are found around it. It consists of two megalithic walls still partly intact.
descriptions.NUR5164: The proto-nuraghe Friarosu of Mogorella has a sub-rectangular plan with convex short sides, because at the base of the wall mass it incorporates three chambers, two sub-oval and one ellipsoidal, with a corbelled ogival roof.
descriptions.NUR5607:
The Fronte Mola is an interesting corridor nuraghe, the only one known so far with a rectangular plan (length 16.20 m; width 12.00 m; surviving height 8.00 m).

Its long side is oriented along a north-south axis and the entrance faces south.

It is built at the base with large, roughly dressed limestone blocks, and in the upper parts with smaller boulders laid one on another and wedged with chocks.
descriptions.NUR15847: Stunning single-tower nuraghe, partially collapsed. It features an intact tholos and an anti-clockwise staircase.
descriptions.NUR6186: A ruined nuraghe, buried and covered in vegetation. It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR3269:
The single-tower nuraghe stands right next to the SS131, beside a sheepfold. It is used as a shelter for sheep. The tholos is almost intact except for the top courses.

Little or nothing remains of the huts that presumably stood beside the tower.
descriptions.NUR6046: A single-tower tholos nuraghe, visible beneath a dense thicket of wild olive and mastic. Apart from a concentration of scattered blocks, a few basal courses of the building remain, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The surviving structures are filled with collapse debris.
descriptions.NUR3701:
A single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. Several courses are still visible in elevation, and the entrance, facing south, can be seen with its monolithic lintel still in situ.

The interior of the chamber is filled with collapse debris from the structure itself. Blocks from the collapse are found around the standing remains, mainly to the north, west and south.
descriptions.NUR2839:
This nuraghe has a trilobate plan, that is, it consists of three towers, a central one and two lateral ones that are half destroyed.

In the central tower we find the main chamber, a circular room in which the wall, narrowing as it rises, forms a true vault ending in an opening that was probably closed in the past by two smaller stones. Near the entrance, on the left-hand side, a spiral staircase with rough steps begins.
descriptions.NUR5982: A tholos nuraghe, presumably of the single-tower type. Vegetation currently covers almost the entire nuraghe, except for a short stretch of the west side where a few courses of the outer wall face, made of polygonal basalt blocks, can be glimpsed.
descriptions.NUR916: Remains of a small granite nuraghe
descriptions.NUR4556: The single-tower nuraghe stood on a rise near a spring where a protected fountain, built of masonry, was made and still exists today. A comparison of the 2017 and 2019 aerial photographs shows that buildings have been erected on the little that remained of the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR3308: "Tancato" nuraghe Funtana Mela, Macomer. The plan is taken from Moravetti, Archaeological research in the Marghine-Planargia.
descriptions.NUR18842: Unfortunately, almost entirely destroyed by erosion. Only a few blocks remain in their original position.
descriptions.NUR3337: It stands on a basalt spur accessible from only one side, west of the village of Sagama. It has a polygonal plan with a straight, slightly convex façade to the north-west where the entrance opens. In the centre of the main wall the main entrance opens with a rectangular opening and lintel. On entering there is a straight corridor; in the right-hand side of the first stretch two niches open side by side.
descriptions.NUR5476: The Furcadizzo nuraghe stands on the small promontory. The monument has suffered heavy collapses. Around the area, wall structures of mixed curvilinear and rectilinear plan can be identified.
descriptions.NUR2653: It is a very beautiful and harmonious trilobate nuraghe in its structure. It is only partly accessible because of obvious and widespread collapses. Construction methods and details of the highest order can be appreciated. The name, which derives from the place-name of the land, nevertheless indicates intense smelting activity. Numerous finds of bronze semi-finished products in the characteristic ox-hide shape.
descriptions.NUR3103:
In a dominant and strategically privileged position.

It is a single-tower nuraghe with an added structure, a circular chamber with three niches arranged in a cross.

Because of the collapse, the entrance to the south-east is not currently detectable, nor are the corridor and any subsidiary spaces (niche and/or staircase), although their presence can be considered certain given the evolved type of the chamber.
descriptions.NUR2714:
Despite the very dense vegetation and the collapses the monument has suffered, the ruins of a central body flanked by two towers, built of pink trachyte boulders, can be made out.

A short distance away, to the south-west, traces of several circular stone structures are visible.
descriptions.NUR6128: The collapses and dense vegetation do not allow the structure to be defined perfectly, but it appears to have an elliptical plan and to be of mixed type: a corridor nuraghe, probably flanked by a tower built at a later date, to which a further circular tholos structure may have corresponded.
descriptions.NUR4264: The nuraghe, the best-visible side of which is from the vineyard in front of the pigsty, appears in any case to have been a single-tower nuraghe, built with roughly dressed blocks of fairly regular parallelepiped shape and medium-to-large size.
descriptions.NUR19954: Bilobate nuraghe, fairly well preserved. Tower A appears older and more imposing. Around the nuraghe lie the remains of the village of the same name. Some maintain that the five small windows were related to astronomical events.
descriptions.NUR4810: A hill covered with vegetation hiding a nuraghe among the largest in the area. It extends over at least two hectares of land to the lacaras.
descriptions.NUR4798:
The Nuragic people decided to wall up the tafoni and erect a single, distinctive tower that probably had an additional room above the surface of the rocky outcrop.

Inside these walls fitted into the granites there are very steep stairways.

Not much remains of the large central communal building, perhaps also because of the choices made by La Marmora and Spano who, in their search for the "floor level", had part of the original superstructure moved and pushed down below.
descriptions.NUR5254: The nuraghe is a complex type, consisting of a five-lobed bastion enclosing the original tower and a courtyard. The central tower, circular in plan (13 m external diameter), survives to a maximum height of over 12 metres. The wall face is built of blocks laid in horizontal courses. The lower chamber is filled with rubble, laid transversely to the helical staircase — also blocked — that started from the ground floor.
descriptions.NUR4048:
It stands on the summit of a hill in the Marmilla. The structure is a complex type, formed by an original central tower built in the Middle Bronze Age, to which four more towers and a bastion were later added. One of the four towers was subsequently sacrificed during a further building phase that presumably also saw the construction of the massive hexagonal outer wall.

In the Early Iron Age a new village developed on the site.
descriptions.NUR11567: Single-tower nuraghe, it marks the boundary between the municipal territories of Villamar and Pauli Arbarei.
descriptions.NUR20319: Single-tower nuraghe with only the two base courses apparently remaining. It is very likely that there was an entire village nearby, given its strategic location and the traces that are still visible.
descriptions.NUR4852: One of the nuraghi in the municipal territory of Villa Sant'Antonio is the nuraghe of 'Genna sa Pira', datable to the full Middle Bronze Age (1500–1200 BC), although its construction saw numerous later additions over the centuries.
descriptions.NUR4626: Single-tower nuraghe of which only a very small, or no, remains. Inhabited until the Recent Bronze Age. Afterward, life ceases at many nuraghes, which have lost their original function.
descriptions.NUR4601: A proto-nuraghe later transformed into a single-tower nuraghe,
descriptions.NUR3969:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan that reaches 29 m in length including the collapse debris closest to the monument.

Its state of preservation allows the structure to be followed in general around its entire outer perimeter, which was not affected by any refacing of the masonry. It is difficult to identify where the entrance opened, probably to be located in the southern quadrant.
descriptions.NUR15133:
A pre- and proto-historic complex comprising a modest Early Neolithic village, a complex nuraghe enclosed by an outer wall, and its village of huts. Inside the village a well for water supply has been dug, of uncertain date.

The buildings are constructed of blocks of local andesite.

Above the Nuragic hut village a fine sheepfold has been built, bounded by dry-stone walls.
descriptions.NUR1916:
Trilobate nuraghe (?) on the summit of the Ghilotta hill, built with polygonal blocks of the local volcanic rock.

The towered monument is surrounded by a village of circular huts whose perimeter walls survive to a fair height. Collapses and vegetation make the complex hard to read.

At the south-east edge of the complex the Case Lenzu, an agro-pastoral farm of the medau type, have been extensively altered in recent times.
descriptions.NUR19705: Nuraghe partially destroyed by quarry work. The site is of particular interest because of the discovery in the area of three swords, with pistil-shaped blades and a central rib, and a tang to which two wings with holes for fixing the handle are attached, recovered during the 1950s. This typically Iberian type finds comparisons with specimens from the territory of Baunei, and with the sword resting on the shoulder of the “Warrior” of Uta.
descriptions.NUR18177: The nuraghe has suffered significant collapses and is surrounded by dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR3820: It is reduced to ruins but very interesting for its star-shaped layout. A Megaron-type temple is present. For clarity I will use the number I to indicate the first of the three found in a very small area with the place-name Giaganu Dominigu. I do not have the systematic survey carried out by the Sassari Superintendency; on my part I propose an ideal reconstruction that comes as close as possible to the real one, considering that we are "on home ground".
descriptions.NUR5029: Nuraghe almost entirely destroyed, with only a semicircular stretch of masonry remaining.
descriptions.NUR2115: Nuargi Ega de is gruttas (V. Angius 1840). Devastated complex nuraghe. The wall faces delimiting the central tower are visible, and inside it the damage caused by clandestine diggers is clear. The outer wall face, though largely covered by vegetation, survives along almost its entire circuit. To the south-east a small break in the wall face can be seen, where the entrance was probably located.
descriptions.NUR5231: Built mainly of boulders like those of the Arresi nuraghe, four towers are visible, plus one almost completely destroyed. Some elders still remember the north-west tower intact. They say it had a well so deep that you could not hear the stones they dropped hit the bottom.
descriptions.NUR20106: Located in the area of Tidula, it features a corridor niche and one in the tholos, still intact.
descriptions.NUR3561: Built of granite blocks quarried on the spot, the nuraghe consists of a circular tower about 4.5 m in diameter and an added pseudo-elliptical body (with a major axis of about 12 m and a minor axis of about 8 m). No traces of huts are currently visible, but it is likely that some structures were built against the site's perimeter and that the natural tafoni were exploited for various uses.
descriptions.NUR5957:
It is built of medium and large boulders laid in rather rough courses; the plan is oval, and it has two entrances and two stairways leading to the upper floor.

The roof is formed of large slabs set side by side.

The east entrance has partly collapsed and was probably connected to the stairways, while the west entrance leads to the central corridor off which open a deep niche and a stairway that has almost completely collapsed. Probable proto-nuraghe
descriptions.NUR3130: Traces of the Nuragic village are also present.
descriptions.NUR3132:
It is located at the highest point of Florinas. (517 m a.s.l.)  

Today, unfortunately, it has collapsed inward.  

It features a main tower and two additional towers.
descriptions.NUR3329: The nuraghe, situated inside the equipped area of Girgini, is irreparably destroyed; all that is still visible is the single basal course, while various parts of the nuraghe have been used to build a wall nearby.
descriptions.NUR3069: Bitorre nuraghe, collapsed and inaccessible, faces north and dominates the entire northern coast from Stintino to Isola Rossa.
descriptions.NUR14927: Complex nuraghe with village. It lies on the border with the municipality of Sinnai in the Campidano State Forest. A mountainside is completely covered with stones and it is very difficult to make out structures. In some places wall structures are visible.
descriptions.NUR2492: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and three additional towers with bastions (four-lobed). Around the nuraghe, traces of a settlement.
descriptions.NUR3467: The Golunie nuraghe stands on land owned by the Guiso family (former Barons) exactly on the boundary between the territories of Orosei and Dorgali, in the Cala Osalla area, and looks out both towards the Marina beach in the area of the second pier of Osalla (Orosei) and towards the beach of the same name (Dorgali).
descriptions.NUR4925: The building, a circular single-tower nuraghe about 10 metres in diameter, adapts to the plateau, incorporating rock outcrops into its basal structures. The external wall face, made of roughly dressed limestone blocks laid in regular courses, survives to a maximum height of 8.10 metres. On the west and south-east sides, at a height of 3 to 3.5 metres from the ground, a restoration carried out in antiquity is clearly visible, made necessary by the subsidence of the masonry.
descriptions.NUR3792: It is in a state of total abandonment. The structure is built of limestone and schist. Part of the tholos wall face is visible, along with some added structures that suggest a complex monument. Around the structure there is a heavy scatter of material surfacing, almost certainly belonging to a village leaning against the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR8972: The Nuraghe Gorroppu, or 'Presethu Tortu', stands on a rocky spur south-west of the gorge of the same name. The settlement is naturally fortified on the south side, while on the opposite side it is protected by a substantial megalithic wall, very well preserved, reaching a height of over 3 metres. Inside the settlement there are numerous quadrangular buildings, some in a fair state of preservation.
descriptions.NUR544: It is a four-lobed nuraghe destroyed to build the Navy base on the same site. Lamarmora and Cugia mentioned it in the nineteenth century. Lamarmora surveyed the nuraghe and produced monographs in which the partitions of the Roman aqueduct, which ran exactly over the nuraghe, are also clearly visible. At least two Nuragic wells were present in the surrounding area.
descriptions.NUR5477: Illegal diggers have exposed some courses of the wall of a small elliptical structure.
descriptions.NUR4797: Single-tower nuraghe situated on the plain, enclosed by a wire fence. Four courses of the external wall face on the north-east side are currently visible, in medium-sized blocks. The presence of other archaeological remains around it cannot be ruled out.
descriptions.NUR2047: Only the lower part of the nuraghe remains, used also as a sheepfold. Likely elliptical in shape or at least non-circular. Diameter at the top is about 10 m.
descriptions.NUR19553: A few remains of a single-tower nuraghe built of limestone. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR10636: What remains of a small nuraghe near Santu Sciori. A church has been built upon it. Mentioned in the writings of Vittorio Angius for the discovery of some giant bones.
descriptions.NUR4464: The nuraghe is now in a poor state of preservation, with several collapses that prevent a precise reading. Only two towers can be clearly distinguished, between which a small courtyard probably opened, as is typical of complex nuraghi. The main tower (central tower) contains niches and a stair in the corridor that led to the upper levels, which have now collapsed.
descriptions.NUR4440: The tower remains as a mound of earth on which the filars of the nuraghe emerge, probably part of a complex.
descriptions.NUR4070:
The nuraghe is inaccessible due to the presence of a high metal mesh.

Nearby is a menhir, always within the fenced area.
descriptions.NUR3158: Situated about a hundred metres east of the well-known giants' tomb of Imbertighe, with which it had an obvious cultural connection, the nuraghe now lies inside a farm. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a slightly elliptical plan (14.10 x 15.25 m), an entrance to the south-east, and a surviving height of 2.75 m to the north-west and 1.70 m to the south-west, with five and four courses respectively.
descriptions.NUR2268: Located near the quarry of Monte Ladu, on the banks of an artificial pond. Part of the base is still visible.
descriptions.NUR6299: Among the heaps of stones the main tower emerges at the highest point, where the entrance is topped by a bare lintel. The open-air entrance has the niche on the right intact and on the left the collapsed stairwell, passable up to the upper floor from which the interior of the tholos with its two side niches can be seen. On the north-west side a double chamber, partly underground, is entered; it probably connected with the central tower in the lower part, which is now below ground.
descriptions.NUR4741: The monument, also known in the literature as “Pranu Nuracci”, is a complex polylobed nuraghe. Two lateral towers, the perimeter walls and the central tower survive. The south-western lateral tower and the northern one survive to a height of about 4–5 courses. The central tower, in good condition, has 12 courses of polygonal masonry with large, barely dressed blocks, a south-east entrance with a monolithic lintel.
descriptions.NUR3805: Perhaps it is the same nuraghe referred to as Thorcodossile in some books, located about 500 metres further west. Only a few ruins remain at the top of the hill.
descriptions.NUR1163: Visitable, collapsed in on itself, central tower with a tree inside, large walls of limestone tuff. Used in the Roman period, as shown by the presence of roof-tile sherds. In the rocky outcrops nearby there are laccus. Traces of a village around it.
descriptions.NUR5491: Complex nuraghe, known to many elders by the name "Sa Reggia", was probably a three-lobed structure with a village. Today it is a heap of ruins and undergrowth more than 10 metres high.
descriptions.NUR10184:
Proto-nuraghe of sub-circular shape (D. Carta 2010)

The single-tower nuraghe dates to the Middle Nuragic period. The building is unusual; its chamber is partly cut into the rock.

Investigations by G. Ugas led to the identification in 1981 of a Punic settlement at Is Argiddas, on the border with the municipality of Sanluri.

The Punic centre, of which stretches of walling in small stones bonded with mud have been identified, overlies a prehistoric and protohistoric settlement.
descriptions.NUR4336: The monument has collapsed in several places and is not altogether easy to interpret: it appears to have been a single-tower nuraghe, yet curvilinear wall outlines are visible around the main building. These could be dwelling units (huts?) or additional structures attached to the main body, in which case it would be a complex nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR1880: "Massive and of irregular plan, in which the dimensions of the walls prevail over the internal spaces, marking an imperfect mastery of the building techniques proper to later tholos nuraghi." Following the traditional classification, the megalithic construction of Is Bangius can be ascribed to the type of monuments of the archaic phase, such as corridor nuraghi.
descriptions.NUR4946: Complex nuraghe consisting of two towers joined by a corridor, built in basalt.
descriptions.NUR5722: It is a simple nuraghe, judging from the few remains highlighted by the stones scattered here and there inside and outside a centuries-old thicket of mastic. The boulders are of medium size and some appear vaguely dressed. Few are the surviving courses, which do not yield sufficient results for a survey.
descriptions.NUR812: Nuraghe destroyed by agricultural mechanization, now no longer visible
descriptions.NUR6131: Only a few medium-sized boulders of the basal circle survive in a ruined state; inside them the entrance facing south-east can be seen. With the main structures of the nuraghe missing, it is likely to be classified as a tomb.
descriptions.NUR5163: From the nuraghe one enjoys a breathtaking view of the underlying Lake Flumendosa.
descriptions.NUR18385: Complex nuraghe of an evolved type, definable in plan as consisting of only the central tower.
descriptions.NUR19125: It is located in the middle of a large cultivated area; no road or path passes near it.
descriptions.NUR3083:
The Iscobalzu nuraghe consists of a nuragic tower standing about 5 metres high. The doorway is half-buried and does not allow access to the interior because of the fallen stones from the dome.

Its size and state of preservation are the best among the nuraghi in the area.
descriptions.NUR3622: It is a fine example of a single-tower nuraghe with a collapsed but easily accessible tholos chamber. The nuraghe displays a variety of constructional and architectural features. Facing north is an entrance that was clumsily walled up in recent times; it lies about 2.00 metres above the present ground level.
descriptions.NUR3714:
Not easily accessible, it is reached after a steep climb through arid, rocky pastures, among protruding stones that hint at the ancient existence of a large village.

Nothing of this monument appears to have been excavated, and only the tholos of the second level alone is accessible.

The courtyard in front of the main tower appears completely buried under ashlars and brambles.
descriptions.NUR14202:
There are nuraghi that are not only grandiose in themselves but also for the landscape in which they stand.

The nuraghe Iscolca is one of these: it dominates the Semestene valley and those of the surrounding villages. Not easily reached, it is accessed after a steep climb through dry, rocky pastures, among protruding stones that hint at the ancient existence of a large village.
