Nothing of this monument appears to have been excavated, and only the tholos of the second level is accessible.
descriptions.NUR20230: Nuraghe of which only a small portion remains at the centre of the settlement of Is Collus. Following a report to the supervisor, archaeological investigations were carried out, but the results are unknown.
descriptions.NUR21162: Nuraghe that was demolished to build a radar base at the tip of Is Ebbas in the 1960s, known as Nuraghe Is Ebbas or Nuraghe Su Brecconi. Information provided by local elders
descriptions.NUR4271: It is a complex nuraghe, with at least the upper courses of the walls skillfully dressed in arenaria. Unfortunately, it is difficult to visit and document due to the vegetation.
descriptions.NUR12905: Nuraghe almost completely dismantled, only a few courses of stones remain.
descriptions.NUR3966: Military outpost of the war 1940/45 built on the remains of the Nuraghe Is Meris.
descriptions.NUR4717: It consists of a nuraghe of an unusual type, built of roughly squared megalithic blocks laid in fairly regular courses. To the north-east an extensive village spreads out, mostly reduced to a scatter of stones; from the general collapse a few megalithic structures and some huts uncovered by unauthorised diggers emerge. The nuraghe, on the other hand, retains its original elevation to a certain height, but its ground plan is not immediately legible.
descriptions.NUR10096: Complex tancato nuraghe, with a central tower and a secondary tower joined by walls, and a courtyard between the two towers. Remains of walls, embankments and wells used for collecting water are also present.
descriptions.NUR4065: Among the few remaining elements of the nuraghe, the lintel deserves special mention, appearing almost suspended in the air.
descriptions.NUR18739: Nuraghe completely destroyed by agricultural improvement works. Possible location.
descriptions.NUR4805:
Multi-lobed nuraghe built of white limestone.

It preserves a magnificent, intact tholos. Is Paras is one of the most elegant constructions of Nuragic Sardinia. It consists of a central tower partly enclosed by a three-lobed bastion that includes a large courtyard. The main tower, circular in plan (diameter 12.50 x 12.70 m), built of white limestone blocks, 12.70 m high, was formed by two superimposed storeys, of which the lower one survives today.
descriptions.NUR5405: Small complex nuraghe to which a lateral transverse addition was later added
descriptions.NUR5917: Ispiene was part of the territory of Chiaramonti. About fifteen years ago we ceded two thousand hectares to the new municipality of Erula, and with it a number of nuraghi including Ispiene. That is why "I still feel it is mine", and if you want to find the character of a fortress you must come here, but even more so the imperishable sacred character that pervades the nuraghe with its cells and the sun that at the zenith on the summer solstice penetrates them to join with Mother Earth. mu
descriptions.NUR16201: The probable nuraghe stands halfway up Monte Sa Corona Arrubia. Its structure cannot be determined: a large quantity of collapse boulders lies in disorder, and dense vegetation prevents an overall view. A few courses with a circular alignment are still visible in their original position, probably belonging to the central tower. Numerous potsherds lie on the surface in the area.
descriptions.NUR526: The nuraghe is located in the territory of Riola Sardo, adjacent to the marsh; the nuraghe was not recorded and appears even less in the maps.
descriptions.NUR20255:
What is visible is only a small portion. The rest is completely buried and covered by vegetation. A circular structure on several levels.

A little lower down an ancient wall, cut into the rock and formed of very large stone blocks.
descriptions.NUR5697: The structure of the nuraghe is clearly complex; the compact mass of the monument is immediately apparent, dominated by the central tower. To the north-west of the nuraghe, about ten metres away inside the enclosure, stands a large stone which, because of its shape, is thought to be a stele; its presence gives the site its name, and also the name of the Nuraghe Istelai, or "place of the steles". All around, traces of the ancient human settlement are evident, ranging from the pre-Nuragic period back to the Neolithic.
descriptions.NUR4949: The Nuraghe Su Nuraxi of Loceri was built incorporating a rocky ledge. The main tower is well preserved and was built with blocks of local granite, partly rough-hewn and laid in regular courses. Its entrance is raised above ground level by at least three courses.
descriptions.NUR5097: The Nuraghe Su Nuraxi of Loceri was built incorporating a rocky ledge. The main tower is well preserved and was built with blocks of local granite, partly rough-hewn and laid in regular courses. Its entrance is raised above ground level by at least three courses.
descriptions.NUR11485: Single-tower nuraghe. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR2744: Single-tower nuraghe. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR11486: Single-tower nuraghe. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR6484: Built of local granite boulders, it has a roughly triangular plan and shows mixed features of corridor nuraghi (the most archaic type of nuraghe) and tholos nuraghi (an evolution of the former). The central chamber with its tholos roof is still intact, while the side chambers have partially collapsed. The building has two entrances, one to the south-west (the main entrance) and another to the south-east.
descriptions.NUR1347: The nuraghe, of which only a few remains are left, is at an elevation of 599 metres.
descriptions.NUR6436: Situated near the municipal pinewood, four kilometres north of the village, the nuraghe Jana is in a poor state of preservation. Not only has the nuraghe collapsed internally, but it was also used in the past as a shepherds' shelter, so that many of its stones have been laid out radially as a boundary wall.
descriptions.NUR4485: Single-tower nuraghe near Nuraghe Arrubiu. It is hidden by vegetation and a small nuraghe, Nuraghe Jana II, stands nearby on the steep slope of the hill.
descriptions.NUR12592: Single-tower nuraghe near Nuraghe Arrubiu. It is hidden by vegetation and another nuraghe, Nuraghe Jana, stands nearby on the steep slope of the hill.
descriptions.NUR6065: "Nuraghe Ianna Bassa, below Monte Sedda Sos Campos, near good springs are the remains of the nuraghe, part of the base and above it a heap of stones. On land belonging to Antioco Sanna." Taramelli's description, seventy years on, still substantially matches the present state of the ruins.
descriptions.NUR1709: The sacred area, dominated to the east by the striking granite crests of Monte Senes (about 862 m above sea level), was built in the Nuragic period at the Janna 'e Pruna pass, now crossed by the Irgoli–Norghio road and a crossing point (about 590 m above sea level) that has been used since very ancient times along a mountain route linking the Riu Siniscola valley with the Cedrino valley, important corridors from the coast into the interior of the island.
descriptions.NUR8044: Uncertain structure, appears to be a Nuragic foundation.
descriptions.NUR3715: Small nuraghe reduced to a heap of ruins.
descriptions.NUR5619: Monument in poor condition of disintegration. It is located on a secondary summit of the Monte Nibbarone (237 m) at an elevation of 168 m a.s.l., from where it dominates the entire valley below.
descriptions.NUR11527: The complex consists of a nuraghe and a village of about 90–100 huts spread over 5 hectares. Because of its great extent and the number of buildings, the site is considered unique in the Gallurese Nuragic context.
descriptions.NUR3749: The boulder of “La Serra” takes its name from the nearby Nuraghe, a monument thousands of years old, shaped like a truncated cone and now reduced to a ruin. The massive multi-cupmarked find is assigned to the Late Neolithic, although there are no certain dates; what is certain is that the monolith belongs to a period much earlier than the Nuraghe. (Pieragica)
descriptions.NUR1447: Single-tower nuraghe in very poor condition, only two courses remain.
descriptions.NUR1536: Single-tower nuraghe. Destroyed by a bulldozer to build a restaurant in the 1980s–85. A pot and a bronze dagger were found during the excavation. Built in the Recent Bronze Age (1300–1150 BC).
descriptions.NUR19547: Single-tower nuraghe of white limestone inside an olive grove; the property fence runs tangent to the structure. Three courses survive on the east and west sides. Covered in vegetation, a tree growing in the centre of the nuraghe threatens its stability.
descriptions.NUR2911:
From the structure a large part of the Irgoli plain is clearly visible; to the north-east Monte Oddie can be seen.

In the surrounding area there are several collapses, and many ashlars from the structure have been used to build the dry-stone walls.

This is a tholos nuraghe partly leaning against the natural rock to the west; it has an inner and an outer wall face, and between them the spiral staircase can be made out; a guard chamber to the east is plausible, and a possible access ramp starting from the west.
descriptions.NUR5907: A careful survey found no trace of the nuraghe Lavrone, although some old people said it must have been there. The site has certainly been modified by humans, as shown by the presence of some man-made objects. The curious anecdote is that Uncle Giacomino, who is no longer with us, built more than "one nuraghe", meaning the heaps of stones gathered when clearing the fields. "Nuraghe dell'alloro grande". mu
descriptions.NUR3699: The nuraghe stands on land used for grazing and partly for vineyards. It has been irreparably destroyed by illicit excavations in the area. Only a short stretch of wall can be seen, which does not allow its dimensions or construction type to be determined any further.
descriptions.NUR528: The quadrilobate complex nuraghe is reduced to a heap of large stones covered by dense vegetation, yet its massive presence can still be perceived.
descriptions.NUR5696: The site consists of the nuraghe, formed by the central tower and two towers, various buildings all around that would suggest the presence of an important village in antiquity, and finally a building that appears to be an ancient sanctuary.
descriptions.NUR17377: It is more likely that this structure belongs to the nuraghe "Tanca di Monsignori", mentioned in the nuragographic map by F. Nissardi (published by G. Pinza in 1901).
descriptions.NUR3537: A few hundred metres from the nuraghe Paddaggiu lies the nuraghe Li Colti. It may be a four-lobed nuraghe. The central tower survives to a height of 6 m, while the bastion appears as high mounds of rubble and only one tower is discernible.
descriptions.NUR1486: The little that remains of the nuraghe Li Espi near the Liscia dam
descriptions.NUR8734: Probable proto-nuraghe consisting of a tower sector leaning against a tafone. Probable entrance to the south-east. From the top of the rock it leans against there is a view of the archipelago to the north-east and of Rena Majori to the north-west.
descriptions.NUR3105: Nuraghe about 9 m high, built with large basalt ashlar blocks. Corridor entrance about 5 m long with stairs on the left and a niche on the right. Intact tholos, diameter 5.30 m.
descriptions.NUR5906:
The monument stands on the summit of a low hillock, in an area currently used as pasture.

Of the simple nuraghe, which rises on a granite outcrop, only the outer wall face is visible, for 1.50 metres.

The chamber plan is sub-circular and rather irregular because a roughly trapezoidal rocky spur, projecting slightly into the chamber, has been incorporated into the wall face.
descriptions.NUR5564:
Complex nuraghe. A bastion formed by at least three towers was added to the main tower, but a fourth tower probably existed as well, though it is not visible today because dense scrub covers the whole nuraghe.

The tholos survives intact.
descriptions.NUR6420: One of the best-preserved single-tower nuraghi in the territory of Seneghe
descriptions.NUR3431: Nuraghe built with calcareous white ashlar laid upon a rocky massif emerging from the dense forest. The walls remain to human height.
descriptions.NUR2825: Complex nuraghe of the lateral-addition type. A main tower is visible with a secondary tower alongside it on the east side. The entrance to the main tower, facing south, is lintelled and buried for more than half its original height. The entrance corridor, with the typical ogival section, is about 4 m long and built of perfectly worked basalt ashlars, showing a level of construction skill rarely found in other nuraghi in the area.
descriptions.NUR6248: Single-tower nuraghe enveloped in vegetation, partly collapsed
descriptions.NUR3474:
The peculiarity of this nuraghe lies in the fact that the chamber wall opposite the entrance has a short passage leading to a large lintelled window, topped by a relieving window.

The nuraghe is a single-tower nuraghe and shows no trace of any kind of staircase. The entrance, set to the north-west, has a lintel surmounted by a carefully worked relieving window.
descriptions.NUR2879: Single-tower nuraghe. The corridor leading to the circular chamber, which is without a vault, has on its left a wide staircase about 1 metre in width.
descriptions.NUR2750: Single-tower nuraghe. The corridor leading to the circular chamber, which lacks a vault, has a staircase about 1 metre wide on the left. Nearby is another nuraghe called Lobaos II, visible in the photo.
descriptions.NUR5088: damaged nuraghe near a complex of domus de janas
descriptions.NUR3844: It lies in the municipality of Florinas (SS), and is a circular single-tower nuraghe with the entrance unusually oriented to the north-east. Very ruined. An old mule track passed practically alongside it, but is now completely disused.
descriptions.NUR3003:
Complex nuraghe, with a bilobate bastion.

The central tower is equipped with a mezzanine.
descriptions.NUR3322: The name means "open stone". The monument is in a state of severe degradation.
descriptions.NUR6175:
The nuraghe, which stands at an altitude of about 794 m, is of mixed type, meaning it has features of both corridor nuraghi and tholos nuraghi. It consists of a central tower against which a three-lobed bastion is built.

Around the nuraghe there is a village of huts and, a short distance away, two giants' tombs and a dolmen.
descriptions.NUR821: Unfortunately the nuraghe Longu is no different from the desperate state of most of the nuraghi of Chiaramonti. Its study and architecture are interesting, placing it at the centre of attention because it belongs to the type with a sub-floor chamber. Mario Unali,
descriptions.NUR3504: The nuraghe is a complex structure consisting of a main tower to which two further towers, linked by a straight curtain wall, were added at later stages. The main tower, built of well-worked basalt blocks (especially in the upper parts) laid in regular courses, has its entrance to the north-east, topped by a lintel with a relieving window and raised above ground level.
descriptions.NUR2639: The nuraghe Santu Antine, also called Sa domo de su Re ("The King's House" in Italian), is one of the most majestic nuraghi in the whole of Sardinia and also one of the most important of those still standing. The entire complex is a major example of prehistoric Mediterranean architecture, and its original height is thought to have reached between 22 and 24 metres, the tallest for that period after the Egyptian pyramids and the central tower of the Nuragic palace of Arrubiu, which measured between 25 and 30 metres.
descriptions.NUR5495: The nuraghe Santu Antine, also called Sa domo de su Re ("The King's House" in Italian), is one of the most majestic nuraghi in the whole of Sardinia and also one of the most important of those still standing. The entire complex is a major example of prehistoric Mediterranean architecture, and its original height is thought to have reached between 22 and 24 metres, the tallest for that period after the Egyptian pyramids and the central tower of the Nuragic palace of Arrubiu, which measured between 25 and 30 metres.
descriptions.NUR4116: The nuraghe has a characteristic elongated elliptical plan corresponding to the corridor nuraghe type, and its structure is founded on the natural rock to which it partly conforms. In places the outer perimeter survives up to six courses high, so that one can see how the projection of the basal blocks decreases gradually from bottom to top.
descriptions.NUR6272: In photographs the Longu nuraghe looks like an imposing single-tower nuraghe. Unfortunately there is no detailed description.
descriptions.NUR4313: It is one of many nuraghes in the Tertenia area and preserves the tholos intact.
descriptions.NUR3392: Site accessible only by traversing a difficult path. The ruined monument, difficult to read, retains a section to the east with 11 irregular courses of the wall.
descriptions.NUR3621: The nuraghe Loppelìe still stands in good condition despite the collapses. The entrance, well preserved, is triangular. On the left side of the entrance chamber the intramural stairway opens. Moreover, the nuraghe Loppelìe is worth visiting for the splendid view from the top of the structure, which ranges from the village of Triei below, to the mountains overlooking Baunei, and from the bay of Arbatax to the peaks of the Gennargentu.
descriptions.NUR1938: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The entrance, opening to the south, is lintelled and gives access to the corridor; to its left opens the stairwell of the helical staircase that led to the upper chamber, which no longer exists. The inner chamber is well preserved except for the top of the false dome, which has collapsed. Two facing niches open inside the chamber, oriented respectively east and west.
descriptions.NUR4296: The Lorenzu Origa nuraghe partly incorporates the pink granite spur on which it was built into its wall face. The monument appears as a truncated-cone tower about 11 m in diameter, preserving a surviving height of at least 2.80–2.50 m. The other opening, topped by a lintel, leads into a space that is actually a sort of corridor roofed with blocks laid in steps and may be part of a stairwell.
descriptions.NUR5902: Complex nuraghe of the tancato type, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The building is hard to read because vegetation — shrubs and climbers — covers the structural parts. The main tower, presumably the older one, can be made out; it survives to a height of almost 6 m. This joins a secondary tower positioned to the south of the first. The secondary tower survives to a height of about 4 m.
descriptions.NUR3551:
The central tower dates to the 15th–13th century BC, while the bastion, the outer wall and the curtain wall date to the 13th–late 12th century BC.

Already in the Early Iron Age the finds show a declining use of the site, though it never fell completely out of use.

It was also used for funerary purposes, as attested by finds of the 7th–8th century.
descriptions.NUR3424: A ruined single-tower nuraghe of which only a few courses survive
descriptions.NUR6440: Nuraghe Loschiri, located in the territory of Semestene, a small village in the Meilogu (visible in the background to the right of the image). Partially collapsed, it preserves intact its entrance portal and large internal sections.
descriptions.NUR3252: The nuraghe is situated on the summit of a granitic rock massif; it is a small single-tower nuraghe in an advanced state of degradation, and the dense vegetation prevents access for visitors.
descriptions.NUR2420: The abundant collapse of the structure and the vegetation covering the monument make the site difficult to read, it could be a corridor nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR8889: It lies to the north-east along the provincial road near the boundary with the territory of Ruinas. It stands on a large limestone base and is filled with its own rubble, which makes access impossible. According to local belief it originally consisted of a succession of three superimposed chambers. The remains of a staircase are visible on a ridge.
descriptions.NUR15807:
Single-tower nuraghe. Four courses survive intact. In poor condition. Built of roughly dressed medium-sized blocks. Signs of human spoliation. Already shown on Filippo Nissardi's nuraghe map (in Pinza G. 1901).

The hillock occupied by the nuraghe includes a stretch of Roman cobblestone paving identified to the north-west of the monument. The dense vegetation covering the site makes it impossible to detect any remains or traces of a possible village.
descriptions.NUR2696: The single-tower nuraghe is equipped with a mezzanine or mezzanine floor, built above the corridor leading to the chamber.
descriptions.NUR5821: Nuraghe whose southern side has collapsed but still retains the tholos intact
descriptions.NUR11538: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and bastions, probably with a second tower. Nearby are the remains of a settlement and the Giants' Tomb of Li Mizzani. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR11592: This nuraghe, already recorded in the EEM of 1922, is placed on Taramelli's Archaeological Map a short distance to the west of Nuraghe Pischedda. The monument, which already in the 1930s appeared almost completely destroyed – "Only the base remains, to a height of one metre" – now leaves no trace at all. It was also known as S. Giuseppe.
descriptions.NUR5375:
The nuraghe is largely destroyed. It was built on a rocky knoll at the outermost edge of the Anghelu Nieddu valley.

Built of medium and small boulders, it must have been a small single-tower nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5612: The complex nuraghe consists of three parts built in different periods: the central tower, whose construction phase dates to about 1000 BC; the four-lobed bastion with its courtyard, built between the 9th and 7th centuries BC; and the outer wall with its four external towers, erected between the 7th and 6th centuries BC.
descriptions.NUR19514: The place takes its name from the fact that a nuraghe once stood here, of which no trace remains. It was demolished around 1960, when the present Castelsardo–Santa Teresa Gallura road (SP90) was built; the stone was used for that work.
descriptions.NUR5807:
Nuraghe with attached village of huts.

The tholos is still intact.
descriptions.NUR5641:
It preserves an intact tholos.

Single-tower basalt nuraghe about 10.80 m high; from the entrance, 1.60 m high, you enter the corridor and immediately on the left the stair with 13 steps.
descriptions.NUR2724:
Complex nuraghe.

Of the nuraghe, located on a modest hill (563 m. a.s.l.), only a few courses of the central tower remain.
descriptions.NUR1578: Damaged nuraghe of which the shape is not recognizable
descriptions.NUR1247: It is in very poor condition and surrounded by dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR2506:
Angius with the name “Macariu 1849. Taramelli. and 1883 land register. Also Girillis.

It is a single-tower nuraghe built of trachyte, its structure hard to read because of the dense vegetation. Inside, the outline of the tower is partly distinguishable. Next to the nuraghe are structures probably belonging to the village. The area also contains several pottery fragments.
descriptions.NUR1649: An apparently single-tower nuraghe cleared of vegetation in 2022. It was previously recorded as a single-tower nuraghe, but it now seems more likely to have been a four-lobed one. A considerable quantity of Roman pottery (terra sigillata) lies around the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR1652:
The nuraghe is in very poor conservation conditions (only a maximum of two courses remain) and is completely covered by vegetation.

Around it there is a vast scatter of baetyls, laterites, and coppi.
descriptions.NUR5733: It is a complex structure consisting of a main tower (or central tower) and two subsidiary towers flanking it to the south. Its entrance has partially collapsed, making access difficult.
descriptions.NUR16976:
Structures belonging to a complex nuraghe of the three-lobed type, built of polygonal basalt blocks. The building has been heavily robbed; only two or three courses survive in elevation, depending on the stretch.

The bastion, three towers and part of the curtain wall can be made out, against which large heaps of rubble lean. In place of the central tower a large excavation dug by mechanical means is visible. The whole structure is covered by a considerable depth of soil.
descriptions.NUR3690: Located at the top of the hill known as Montes. It commands a wide view of the landscape.
descriptions.NUR4588: Single-tower, collapsed and stripped, with only the ruins scattered on the ground.
descriptions.NUR5654: Structures belonging to a complex tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The central tower has its lower chamber intact and the base of the upper one; the northern part of the bastion is visible, with two towers, while the whole southern part is covered by vegetation. The other two towers, not yet located because they are hidden by vegetation, may lie to the south of the central tower.
descriptions.NUR2051: A complex nuraghe, probably three-lobed, is in such a state of decay that it is almost impossible to identify its structural elements. Around the nuraghe, over a wide area, lie fragments of Punic and Roman pottery indicating the presence of a settlement.
descriptions.NUR1927:
In a dominant position, a few metres from the northern bank of the Rio Merchis – which marks the boundary between the municipal territories of Borore and Norbello – less than 400 metres SE of the Nuraghe s'Istrampu and about 250 metres SW of the domus de janas of Ortigosu.

The monument appears as a hill strewn with rubble and covered by dense shrub vegetation. The collapse and the vegetation make a correct planimetric definition of the monument very difficult.
descriptions.NUR2079: Single-tower nuraghe covered by sand. In its surroundings are visible traces of habitation and a well dug into the rock.
descriptions.NUR4953: Nuraghe Maistu Peldu (commonly called De Su Par e Pelda) still has two small towers standing, each 2 metres high. The collapsed vault reveals the interior of the tholos, about 1 m deep. The ashlars, which are fairly large, suggest that the site may be a watchtower nuraghe controlling the entrance to the Chia valley. In front of it stands a menhir, the "praying menhir", De Su Par 'e Pelda, visible from provincial road 72.
descriptions.NUR18100: The position is approximate. The nuraghe is marked on the maps of the former Catasto.
descriptions.NUR5501:
It is a bilobed nuraghe built of large trachyte blocks, roughly worked and laid in irregular courses.

Leaning against the central tower, which survives to a height of about (???) metres, is a second, slightly elliptical tower on the east side. From above, part of an internal niche in this tower is visible, faced with perfectly squared limestone blocks.
descriptions.NUR3164: Along the road to Erula, the Nuraghe Majore rises on a height, protected by walls and on the north-east side by a sheer drop. A single-tower nuraghe, still in excellent condition, its tholos is almost intact.
descriptions.NUR5498:
The Maiore nuraghe (14th–9th century BC) is a single-tower type, currently standing more than eight metres high, with a clear taper towards the top; it has a single entrance on the south-east side. From the entrance a corridor leads to the central ground-floor chamber, which has a tholos roof, while on the left a stairway gives access to the upper level.

Because the tower suffered a major collapse before the 1980s, restoration work became necessary.
descriptions.NUR2931:
Built entirely of granite, it is of the central-corridor type, with a mixed layout that combines the plan of corridor nuraghi and tholos nuraghi with a central corridor and paired chambers; the structure is massive and irregular. The tholos is intact.

The bastion is reached by a staircase accessible from the courtyard. The entrance leads into a central corridor, covered by an ogival vault, which runs the full length of the building and opens onto a large courtyard.
descriptions.NUR5535: Considering the characteristics of the minimally worked stones, their small size, and the type of collapse that gives them an elongated form, it is possible this structure represents a proto-nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR6421: It is located within a private farm. Surrounded by vegetation, it is partially eroded but still used as a shelter for sheep.
descriptions.NUR20311: It is a simple nuraghe with the typical truncated-cone shape, probably a single-tower tholos nuraghe. It is built of large granite blocks. About seven courses can be counted at the highest point, but it is clear that others lie below the floor level.
descriptions.NUR2840: Nuraghe characterized by a calcareous lintel, white on dark walls. The tholos has collapsed inward.
descriptions.NUR3048: Nuraghe characterized by a calcareous lintel, white on dark walls. The tholos has collapsed inward.
descriptions.NUR3292:
The monument is in the Mandras locality (Campeda), 600 metres north-east of the Mura Sauccu nuraghe and less than 300 metres west of the Mura Sauccu B nuraghe.

It is a single-tower nuraghe surviving to a maximum height of about 6.50 metres. The masonry consists of large and medium-sized blocks.
descriptions.NUR1011: Single-tower nuraghe. About 100 metres from the monument there is a Roman hypogeum, partly cut into the rock and partly built of brick with a barrel vault.
descriptions.NUR5143: The monument is a single-tower nuraghe, of whose external wall only four courses remain.
descriptions.NUR6220: Concentric-plan nuraghe ... (a short distance from the nuraghe there is another uncertain structure which, in my opinion, dates to the Nuragic period – see photo). At the top the view is breathtaking! A 360° panorama of forest! To the east, in the background, the whole of the Supramonte.
descriptions.NUR6135: The first photos show the section of the tholos, unfortunately half-collapsed. The splendid niche is also visible. It is easily reached even though it is on private land. It lies a few hundred metres from the Romanesque Cathedral of Sant'Antioco di Bisarcio.
descriptions.NUR3916: Nuraghe Mannu stands on the summit of the beautiful Cala Fuili beach. The importance of this site lies above all in the Nuragic village of Nuragheddu, which is one of the largest in Sardinia and consists of more than 200 huts of various shapes and sizes.
descriptions.NUR4853:
It lies west of the village centre, along the boundary with the territory of Villaurbana. It is a simple, single-chamber type. It is undoubtedly the best preserved and presumably among the most recent nuraghi in the municipal area.

Oral tradition holds that this nuraghe suffered a dynamite attack in the 1930s; the arrangement of the dome's ashlars and the condition of the western side would support this theory.
descriptions.NUR1418:
From IGM. The aerial map suggests the polygon is occupied by a modern cottage.

The nuraghe today is probably destroyed or at least not identifiable.
descriptions.NUR19890: Nuraghe of unidentifiable structure. Unfortunately only a few traces of the nuraghe remain because it was completely demolished to make way for a RAI antenna. At the foot of the antenna various boulders lie heaped haphazardly. At the edge of a hollow, next to what must have been the base of the nuraghe, are the remains of a probable hut.
descriptions.NUR868: Complex nuraghe built of schist (Stintino stone). Three towers are still visible, with a massive outer wall encircling the structure. Around the nuraghe there are clear traces of huts and collapses of associated structures. The tholos survives almost intact, except for a few courses.
descriptions.NUR1899: The nuraghe is in a very advanced state of collapse. The full outline of the original tower survives for a maximum of two courses. Given the few remaining boulders on site, it may have been dismantled so its stones could be reused. A few metres away there are boulders that probably belonged to the nuraghe, used to build a yard for watering livestock. At present the nuraghe is completely overgrown with vegetation.
descriptions.NUR4307: Two nuraghe towers very close to each other
descriptions.NUR5791: Nuraghe in excellent condition, although surrounded by vegetation. The internal tholos is intact.
descriptions.NUR579: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and two lateral towers connected by bastions that enclose a courtyard.
descriptions.NUR19469:
The Margone nuraghe stands on the summit of a hill and is largely hidden by dense vegetation, especially prickly pear and wild olive.

Its important function is emphasised by the complexity of the structure: it is a three-lobed nuraghe with a central tower 12 m in diameter. Around it one can trace stretches of polygonal masonry, built of medium-sized limestone blocks, that link three secondary towers to the main tower.
descriptions.NUR4104: A large four-lobed complex nuraghe. Never excavated and lying inside a private property, it is therefore inaccessible. It is distinguished by certain particular artefacts inside it, including a menhir.
descriptions.NUR4158: Ruined nuraghe, part of a larger settlement. The central tower is ruined; it has a fairly broad terrace running all round the main tower. There is a secondary entrance on the north-east. Hut bases are found nearby at the foot of the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR4998: Unfortunately no significant structure remains, as it was completely destroyed together with the village of the same period. On the surface it yields evidence of a hilltop settlement attributable to the early phases of the Middle Bronze Age (17th–16th century BC); indeed, fragments of obsidian, sherds of Nuragic pottery and stone tools have been recovered, indicating the existence of domestic shelters.
descriptions.NUR993: Single-tower nuraghe of large blocks of white limestone, situated in the courtyard of a private house. About three courses survive, with a maximum height of 3 m and a minimum of 2 m. Diameter at the base: 15 m. The structure is collapsing overall; state of preservation: mediocre.
descriptions.NUR5236: This is one of the countless nuraghi destroyed over the millennia by vegetation, ploughing, land reclamation and stone clearance for other uses. It must have been a multi-lobed nuraghe, perhaps with a double frontal addition. But it is hard to say without cleaning and excavation.
descriptions.NUR12069: It is a single-tower nuraghe standing on a rocky rise. From the outside it looks in fair condition at first glance, but inside there is only a heap of rubble; the roof and part of the upper masonry are missing, so the inner chamber is filled with fallen material and cannot be examined in detail.
descriptions.NUR3905: Structures belonging to a single-tower tholos nuraghe. The building, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt, survives for about four courses on the north side, while it has largely collapsed on the south, west and east sides. The inner chamber has collapsed in its upper part and the collapse debris fills the rest. The entrance cannot be identified.
descriptions.NUR4300: It is named after the family that owned the land on which it is situated. The nuraghe is completely collapsed and certainly quadrilobate. It is located 600 m from the palace of Barumini.
descriptions.NUR2599: This is a single-tower nuraghe in a clearly degraded state. Nevertheless, its bulk and the harmony of its construction make it an interesting nuraghe both for its building techniques and its architectural features. It stands on a brown trachyte outcrop, and in places the base boulders merge with the natural rock, giving the structure solidity.
descriptions.NUR3438: Completely buried... and overlooked. In the village it is said that originally it was the largest in the area and that part of the upper tower was removed for building material.
descriptions.NUR18476: The nuraghe takes its name from the locality on the south-eastern slopes of the Giara di Gesturi. It is mentioned by Taramelli in his study of the prehistoric monuments of the Giara; however, the survey carried out in the 1980s no longer recorded any trace of it.
descriptions.NUR3828: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, diameter 11.20 m, with surviving walling 3.20 m high, four courses. Masonry of polyhedral blocks, barely dressed. Already in Taramelli's time the nuraghe was destroyed; only the base remains.
descriptions.NUR2498: Four-lobed nuraghe, with four towers at the corners of the quadrangular bastion and an internal courtyard in front of the central tower entrance. The nuraghe is completely ruined; the remains of its fortification can be seen nearby.
descriptions.NUR11171: Base of a nuraghe near the old fire watch tower, built with schist blocks.
descriptions.NUR11481: Complex nuraghe with settlement; no traces remain on the surface.
descriptions.NUR5452: This nuraghe is laid out longitudinally and has several cavities (presumably towers..) of small size.. four can be seen from the aerial photo, but there are at least five if not more... it is really interesting and it would be worth clearing the parts still standing, today cluttered with the collapse of the upper parts, to understand better how it was laid out; the towers are small and it is not clear whether they were access ramps for an upper structure or something else.
descriptions.NUR3341: Nuraghe completely collapsed, its shape difficult to define
descriptions.NUR3177: Complex nuraghe, covered by dense vegetation; near the nuraghe, a menhir and several giants' tombs, concealed by the thick vegetation, are observed.
descriptions.NUR8289: Nuraghe destroyed at the time of the land reclamation in the area. Large boulders (not found in the surrounding area) remain on the site; they were used several decades ago to build terraces. Pottery sherds probably of Nuragic date and fragments of millstones from the same period have been noted in the area. It is impossible to determine its exact location and dimensions.
descriptions.NUR4489: It is the best-preserved nuraghe in the territory of Tratalias and stands in one of the many medaus, called precisely Is Cuccus. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a surviving height of about 5 m, built of megalithic andesite blocks. The circular inner chamber is about 5.50 m wide, has a tholos with its top missing, and is completely clear of collapse.
descriptions.NUR8243: Nuragic complex with an uncertain plan, in which a very large tower and a series of wall structures of uncertain function connected to it can be recognised. The site was also occupied in the Punic and Roman periods.
descriptions.NUR4071: Near the Massidda or Ghisu medau two small dry-stone buildings with circular plans can still be seen, occupying two eminences overlooking the valley that slopes down to Porto Paglia: they are probably a single-tower nuraghe or a tower-hut and a smaller hut.
descriptions.NUR4597: Near the Massidda or Ghisu medau two small dry-stone buildings with circular plans can still be seen, occupying two eminences overlooking the valley that slopes down to Porto Paglia: they are probably a single-tower nuraghe or a tower-hut and a smaller hut.
descriptions.NUR510: Nuraghe of undetermined type. The nuraghe has an unusual staircase which, about halfway along the entrance corridor, at a height of 2.20 metres from the floor, projects diagonally for over 5 metres with a remarkably steep incline leading onto the terrace. The chamber's vault is intact.
descriptions.NUR2786: Single-tower partially collapsed and covered by vegetation
descriptions.NUR2592: A badly ruined single-tower nuraghe of which only a few courses remain
descriptions.NUR4772: Vittorio Angius calls it Fumìu: "It is a design of such a kind that no idea of it can be given without having drawn it." He goes on to state that several nuraghi make it up: "Above the door opening towards the sirocco-levante there is a loophole, and not far from it a second door opening to the sirocco and two metres high, which however, being high above the ground, looks like a window: on one side of it the gallery within the wall thickness opens, leading to the upper floors or the terrace."
descriptions.NUR4130: Single-tower enclosed within a bastion. Four courses of massive arenite blocks from the wall are visible, with a height of almost 2 metres. Climbing the wall, the top of the tower is seen to be ruined.
descriptions.NUR4691:
The hill is not easily accessible to visitors because it is wrapped in Mediterranean scrub. The car must be left about a hundred metres from the tarmac of the coastal road from Sarroch to Pula. From here you walk up to the nuraghe.

It is hard even to guess the number of towers that surrounded the central one.

However, it is certain that it must have been a multi-lobed nuraghe with an entrance to the south-east, whose central tower had the three typical internal niches.
descriptions.NUR2662: The Mereu nuraghe, also called 'Intro de Padente', built entirely of white limestone with well-squared medium-sized stones, stands on a rise overlooking the surrounding territory. It is a complex nuraghe, consisting of a central tower and two secondary towers further protected by straight bastions.
descriptions.NUR3128: Collapsed nuraghe covered in vegetation. Probable single-tower nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR6473: In total, the ruin still reveals only a few stones that form the basal circle, composed of white, friable limestone. mu
descriptions.NUR5990: It is four-lobed, with a central tower surrounded by a bastion against which the other four towers are built. In places it is quite ruined, yet it still reaches a height of more than ten metres; the ground floor is well preserved, while the upper floor lacks its roof although the masonry survives to a certain height. As often happens in multi-storey towers, the upper floor was characterised by a large window.
descriptions.NUR5007: A single-tower nuraghe largely hidden by vegetation, built on a rocky outcrop that merges with the stones of the wall structure. The site dates to the Middle Bronze Age.
descriptions.NUR10453: It is located in an area containing the Barru nuraghe and the remains of other nuraghes. It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe broken down, fragmented, and buried.
descriptions.NUR15819: Probable location. In a grazing area, hidden by a large thicket of mastic, in poor condition, some blocks are visible. Adjacent to the sewage treatment plant, it may have suffered damage during the recent installation works.
descriptions.NUR8547: Nuraghe partially collapsed with an open tholos
descriptions.NUR11729: Located on a rocky spur near the road between Thiesi and Romana, it dominates the landscape below, where in particular the nuraghe Majore is situated.
descriptions.NUR8206: Nuraghe now almost completely disappeared, of which only a few traces remain visible among the bushes, including two rows of stones.
descriptions.NUR5784: The nuraghe is a complex type, consisting of a central tower enclosed by a three-lobed bastion. It still dominates the Birori plain, from which there is a breathtaking view, even though its surviving height is now only 5 metres. It was excavated in 1995.
descriptions.NUR2421: From the remains that emerge from this nuragic structure located beside the church of Madonna della Pace, I am convinced that this is the Nuraghe of Moddorocco, or that there were two nuraghes.
descriptions.NUR8864: Located on a promontory overlooking the municipal road from Villaurbana to the locality 'S'utturu on cardu'. The tower is largely collapsed and inaccessible.
descriptions.NUR4017: Nuraghe completely destroyed by quarrying activities
descriptions.NUR3694: Complex nuraghe of the tancato type, with a central tower and a secondary tower with bastions. On the IGM map this nuraghe is mistakenly identified as the nearby Sa Tiria nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR2822:
The monument lies less than 400 metres north-east of the village of Sagama, near the southern bank of the Riu Ralzu: beyond the watercourse, about 160 metres away to the north-west, stands the Proto-nuraghe Mulineddu.

It is a single-tower nuraghe with a niche in the corridor and a chamber flanked by a niche.
descriptions.NUR6428: Structures belonging to a single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The inner chamber has collapsed in its upper part. Collapse material lies on the west and north sides of the nuraghe. The structure is accessible only along the entrance corridor, which is 5 m long; to its left a chamber opens, partly blocked, which must have given access to the stair leading to the upper chamber.
descriptions.NUR5444: The monument must have been a far more complex and articulated structure than one can imagine today, looking at the surviving ruins, which nevertheless still retain a semblance of their original monumentality. The first tower, circular in plan, has its foundations set on a bedrock surface; the inner chamber has an oval layout whose elongated end joins the wall face of what must have been the main tower.
descriptions.NUR1866: Nuraghe consisting of a primitive central tower and several towers. The interior of the central tower is filled with earth and fallen boulders. On the east side a lintelled corridor is visible, interrupted by collapse after a few metres. A short distance from the central tower there is a curvilinear wall that probably enclosed a peripheral tower. To the NNW, adjoining the nuraghe, an oval chamber is visible. Numerous pottery fragments of various periods lie on the surface in the area.
descriptions.NUR1701:
A particularly evocative proto-nuraghe for the beauty of its protohistoric architecture. The entrance to the original tholos survives, incorporated into the rocky mass.

On the outside of the granite block, and in plain view, there are hollows that form natural sculptures; inside there is a rock shelter that was probably already used in earlier periods.
descriptions.NUR1692: The nuraghe is located in the COMUNE DI MURAVERA. The entire upper complex, four-lobed with some semi-quadrangular towers, extends along a north-west/south-east axis of about 53 m and an east/west axis of about 20–25 m. The outer curtain wall can be traced only along its eastern stretch and a short southern section: it is an imposing structure with a broad wall thickness that served to close the gaps in the pre-existing natural rock bastion.
descriptions.NUR1863: Complex nuraghe. Traces of at least three towers, probably added concentrically, can be identified. The original tower retains its wall outline, broken to the south by a small opening. The interior is partly blocked by soil and collapse debris. To the south and south-south-east there are two triangular corridors whose outlines, interrupted by collapse, are visible for several metres; one suggests the presence of a stairwell. Clandestine excavations are visible.
descriptions.NUR4627: The Middle Bronze Age material (at most fragments of cooking pots and carinated bowls), almost all of the S. Cosimo facies and found on the surface, comes mainly from Monti Crastu, Monti Atziaddei, Monti Ibera, Monti Porceddu and Monti Acutzu; material of the Monti Mannu facies, which needs further specific study to be better understood, is found only in the Serri locality that gives it its name.
descriptions.NUR4583: The Middle Bronze Age material (at most fragments of cooking pots and carinated bowls), almost all of the S. Cosimo facies and found on the surface, comes mainly from Monti Crastu, Monti Atziaddei, Monti Ibera, Monti Porceddu and Monti Acutzu; material of the Monti Mannu facies, which needs further specific study to be better understood, is found only in the Serri locality that gives it its name.
descriptions.NUR1248: In the immediate area behind the mouth of the Mannu River, the complex nuraghe Monte Aiveghe survives to a height of about 1.2 m with three courses of limestone blocks belonging to the upper parts of the two towers. Around it the remains of at least three huts belonging to the probable associated village can be recognised. A scatter of Roman-period pottery is also attested.
descriptions.NUR3036: Reduced to an extreme state of ruin. Since the 1970s a fire lookout post of the Sardinian Forestry Corps has stood on it. Traces of the nuraghe's construction are evident; it has been stripped by various local people and by various treasure hunters looking for the (siddados=treasures) of the ancient Sardinians.
descriptions.NUR20534: A first, certainly partial, survey suggests that this may be a complex nuraghe, since the insertion of a peripheral tower onto the central body of the nuraghe is quite clear, unfortunately in a very poor state of preservation. The presence of substantial curtain walls can also be seen, hypothetically interpretable as the remains of an outer wall.
descriptions.NUR4920: The Complex lies within the territory of Villaputzu. It comprises the two towers known as N.ghe Monte Arrubiu I and II, which must be considered part of the same structure, and the Nuragic village that spreads out on the plain below. From the summit there is a wonderful view. There are various rocks that take on distinctive shapes.
descriptions.NUR4692: It is elliptical in shape, extends for a length of about 30 metres, has a diameter of about 22 metres and survives to a height of about 4 metres. In the north-west sector of the curtain wall an entrance can be seen leading to an internal corridor that served as a link between the two main towers and was originally roofed with massive slabs laid flat.
descriptions.NUR1533: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a curtain wall, partly overgrown with vegetation around almost the entire perimeter; nevertheless, through the doorway facing south-east one can enter the tholos, which is open at the top. Inside there are two large niches and another doorway to the north-west, half buried in soil.
descriptions.NUR11283: Single-tower nuraghe used as a quarry for the construction of walls and "pinnettas". Today, only a partial row of stones is visible.
descriptions.NUR6228: Complex nuraghe, of which the central tower is preserved in good condition and for almost the entire first level. The tholos is accessible via the entrance corridor, cleared of collapses.
descriptions.NUR4522: The building, of complex type, incorporates an earlier structure within its bastion at the western end of the rocky spur: probably a pseudo-nuraghe, whose ground plan cannot be determined because of its poor state of preservation. The outer wall face is legible only on the north-east side and consists of basalt blocks laid in irregular courses that incorporate outcrops of natural rock.
descriptions.NUR6319: Single-tower nuraghe, eroded and surrounded by vegetation
descriptions.NUR4577: In the territory of Serrenti, the nuraghes with a transverse frontal addition are those of Cannedu and Monti Crabu.
descriptions.NUR4620: The existence of this single-tower nuraghe is assumed, even though very few remains survive.
descriptions.NUR4180: The few known finds from the A1 rock shelter at Monti Crastu, used as a burial and violated by clandestine digging, are attributed to the Abealzu phase. The size and position of the proto-nuraghi at Monti Crastu and Monti Mannu suggest that these may have been the most important centres of proto-Nuragic cantons or sub-cantons in the Campidano, or at least that, together with the other complex proto-nuraghi, they could have controlled a large part of it.
descriptions.NUR4739:
It lies in the municipality of Muravera, a short distance from the Cuili Piras menhirs and near the boundary with the municipality of Castiadas.

More precisely it is a proto-nuraghe.

Of particular interest is an entrance whose lintel survives well preserved.
descriptions.NUR3002: Reduced to total ruin, only the base circle can be traced, where an opening to the north is visible. There are not enough surviving structures for an exact classification into a precise type; it is thought to be a corridor nuraghe. An interesting area because of the presence of large stones set on edge, which gives the impression of standing before a giants' tomb.
descriptions.NUR12554: Apparent, but unlikely single-tower nuraghe, with some signs of other structures in the surroundings.
descriptions.NUR3823: Very ruined, but large blocks of roughly dressed hard limestone remain, showing the construction technique. The entrance is visible to the south-south-east, with the lintel on the ground near the two jambs. The typology of the nuraghe points to its sacredness, linked to the conjunction with the god, since the monument is the prolongation of the mountain shaped like a truncated cone. mu
descriptions.NUR5675:
The enclosure has a single entrance; to its right a passage roofed with covering slabs, which resembles a giants' tomb — a rare feature in the Nuragic age, when tombs were always built near nuraghi but never inside them.

The tower standing on the hilltop has a single chamber with a niche, terraces and bastions defending the doorway, and an annular corridor that probably led to the terrace or to an upper floor.
descriptions.NUR14908: It currently appears as a modest height. Likely a complex nuraghe of "tancato" type (two towers with an intermediate courtyard). Remnants of walls remain. Destroyed by the opening of the municipal road.
descriptions.NUR3167:
Throughout the area there are settlements and hut remains ranging from the Neolithic to the Medieval period.

This nuraghe, too, lies in a state of total abandonment; no restoration work or excavations have ever been carried out to highlight or bring to light any finds.
descriptions.NUR5345: Probable proto-nuraghe with only 4 very irregular courses remaining
descriptions.NUR4134:
This nuraghe lies on the edge of the Teulada military training area.

The geoportal shows that walls still survive around the nuraghe of Monte Idu, built for who knows what reason. The place is magical, both for the presence of the monuments and for the breathtaking scenery it offers the visitor. Its landscape value is exceptional.

The nuraghe appears to be a single-tower nuraghe
descriptions.NUR3737: Part of it is periodically submerged by the level of the artificial basin of Omodeo.
descriptions.NUR2886: Single-tower nuraghe, eroded and enveloped by vegetation, near which a dolmen is reported.
descriptions.NUR4171: There should also be a corresponding Nuragic settlement at the site.
descriptions.NUR6162: Single-tower nuraghe, ruined and collapsed inwards
descriptions.NUR19465: Complex nuraghe of Mont'Elva with an adjoining village. It is reduced to a ruin because of the work on the water mains of the Alta Nurra aqueduct carried out from the 1950s onwards. Still recognisable are: the central tower, partly buried, with a surviving height of about 2 m; a secondary tower, to the south-west of the main one, reduced to just two courses hidden by dense Mediterranean scrub.
descriptions.NUR1873: Called Nuraghe de su casteddu de Monte Maria, a possible fortress nuraghe, set on a granitic base. Difficult to reach, it was visited and catalogued by Lamarmora as early as 1830; a lightning strike is said to have reduced it to its present state. The north and south turrets can be visited; it appears to be a corridor nuraghe that was adapted over time.
descriptions.NUR4037: The remains belong to a small complex nuraghe. The found debris suggests the presence of a small proto-nuraghe, possibly modified or demolished and then reconstructed as a classic nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR21182: Complex nuraghe of which two towers are still visible.
descriptions.NUR8796: Single-tower nuraghe, partially collapsed, situated on a trachyte rise near the Cuga valley.
descriptions.NUR14149: The summit of Monte 'E Mesu is a small oval plateau. At one end stands the eponymous nuraghe, built almost sheer on the rock. On a small natural terrace below the nuraghe there are traces of huts and other evidence of the Nuragic period, such as boulders with bull-shaped carvings, lying in a state of total abandonment and looking, one might even say, weary of the multi-millennial life they carry on their shoulders.
descriptions.NUR553: Damaged nuraghe of which only a buried chamber built in masonry can be observed.
descriptions.NUR3452: Ruined single-tower nuraghe. Part of the tholos survives on the west side. In the past it was altered to house a sheepfold shelter.
descriptions.NUR15828: The nuraghe survives to about 3 metres on the north side and has a diameter of about 10 metres. Built of medium-sized trachyte rough blocks, it is partly covered by vegetation. A scatter of medium-sized Roman material lies on the north-east side of the site.
descriptions.NUR8669: The nuraghe is located on top of Monte Nieddu
descriptions.NUR14885: Single-tower nuraghe no longer visible but noted by archaeologist Daniele Carta in his thesis (ArcheoArte 2012)
descriptions.NUR3930: The monument, subcircular in plan, stands almost at the top of a steep, wooded rise, currently used for pasture. Three blocks of the left-hand doorjamb survive, oriented to the north, and two of the right-hand one. The nuraghe is built of roughly dressed medium and large granite blocks in rough polygonal masonry with frequent use of wedges.
descriptions.NUR3677: The urban plan of Sassari (11 Dec. 2014) designates it as "Nuraghe Arcone I - Monte Palmas".
descriptions.NUR870: Almost on the summit of a small hill stands the nuraghe of Monte Pedrosu. During the First or Second World War it was used as a pillbox, as shown by the concrete masonry added to the top of the archaeological monument.
descriptions.NUR15871: Single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, built of large worked limestone blocks preserved for six or seven courses (height 3.50 m). It has an entrance to the east and a long corridor opening on the left and right into two chambers in the wall.
descriptions.NUR18157: Nuraghe to be verified as it might be a enclosure.
descriptions.NUR8199: Single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical plan. Other wall sections of undetermined function are present. The site was also occupied in Roman times.
descriptions.NUR3908: Reused in the Roman period and as a posting during the Second World War.
descriptions.NUR2165: Remains of a probable quadrangular fortification built by the Nuragic people. It survives as a large megalithic wall running along the eastern edge of the plateau that forms the mountain summit. The wall is broken by an entrance leading to a corridor parallel to the wall and roofed with basalt slabs laid flat. The place name “Sa Rocca 'e su Para” given to this mountain may refer to the use the Camaldolese friars made of the fortress in the Middle Ages.
descriptions.NUR3858:
Only a few boulders of the basal circle survive. They are of hard white tuff that is still friable. It stands right above the curvilinear alignment of the mountain ridge where several domus de janas are visible on the ridge of the same mountain and on the slope.

Nuraghe del monte forato. See Mònte pertùsu.
descriptions.NUR3738: It is a nuraghe of which only a few or no traces remain.
descriptions.NUR4198:
It is hard to interpret because it is not clear whether it consisted of a single tower, which in that case would have been of a large diameter, or of several towers on different levels.

All that can be seen are high walls of massive construction, built of roughly squared blocks and spread over a wide area.

It also appears that the wall faces of the monument enclose a space already bounded by rock outcrops that are incorporated into it in several places.
descriptions.NUR3670: It was marked on the IM map but is now completely vanished.
descriptions.NUR5588: It is a very unusual nuraghe. The only chamber is set into the ground on top of the trachyte mountain, so that you reach it and find the chamber literally under your feet. Access is controlled by an outer wall with the main entrance facing west, while the nuraghe proper faces east, looking out over the cliff that naturally forms an inaccessible place — a strong point for those who favour a defensive function.
descriptions.NUR6432:
The monument stands on the edge of a rise looking towards Montagna di Sant'Antonio; the Nuragic tower is bounded on the west-south-west by the steep profile of the rock, while a quadrangular enclosure opens on the front.

The building is circular, but the western profile tends to be straight for a length of about 5 metres: the sector facing west-south-west cannot be surveyed because of the collapse and the dense shrub vegetation.
descriptions.NUR19591: Few remains of a nuraghe built of limestone.
descriptions.NUR6235: No trace of the nuraghe remains, except for the stone structures that border the properties. Numerous pottery fragments, however, are present.
descriptions.NUR4193: Single-tower nuraghe partially collapsed but with the tholos open. It offers the possibility of climbing to the last remaining course and enjoying the view over Cala Sinzias.
descriptions.NUR4615: The nuraghe consists of a main tower, two additional structures joined to it, remains of the outer wall along much of the perimeter, and the remains of several huts. It is not well preserved except for the main lintelled entrance with its relieving window and the remains of a staircase. A few dozen metres to the north-west there is a cave used as a necropolis. The skeletal remains have been studied and date to the Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR1862: A single-tower nuraghe with its top missing, built of limestone blocks, whose perimeter is broken on the south side by the collapse of the outer wall face. The interior of the chamber is not visible because it is hidden by vegetation and filled with earth and debris.
descriptions.NUR3742: One of the numerous nuraghes in this region, located near three giants' tombs.
descriptions.NUR3351: Damaged nuraghe, of which only a few courses remain buried and entwined by vegetation
descriptions.NUR3363: Single-tower nuraghe of tuff, with a megalithic wall attached that encircles the promontory. Located within a private farm.
descriptions.NUR2958: A ruined nuraghe near which stands a Nuragic spring, in good condition. It consists of a rectangular lintelled entrance (about 0.95 x 0.90 m) giving access, via a stair of four steps with a tread of 24 cm, to a dromos (length about 1.00 m; width 1.06 m; height 1.82 m).
descriptions.NUR14988: Nuraghe completely collapsed and buried, such that its structure cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR6271: The nuraghe, or probably the proto-nuraghe Monte Uri given its features, appears imposing, leaning against and therefore erected in symbiosis with a large granite boulder; it preserves an intact tholos and from its position dominates the Oschiri countryside. For us it was a great surprise to see it, admire it and be able to confirm that where this place-name occurs, remains of very ancient monuments are generally found. (ArcheoUri)
descriptions.NUR2856: Single-tower nuraghe with its tholos intact
descriptions.NUR5241:
The nuraghe, situated on the summit of the hill, is very damaged.

It consists of a circular tower and an elliptical, eccentric curtain wall elongated towards the south-east, where the entrance is presumably located.
descriptions.NUR4232:
It is more precisely a proto-nuraghe.

In the vicinity there are also a special giants' tomb and a domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR615: The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR4532: Most of the proto-nuraghi at Serrenti are small and, as far as can be seen, elliptical or irregular in plan. Those at Monti Mannu, Monti Atziaddei, Monti Crastu and Sa Corona appear larger, the last two perhaps enlarged or rebuilt between the Middle and Late Bronze Age. Around this proto-nuraghe there are traces of a small village.
descriptions.NUR9877: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and two lateral towers joined by straight walls, with a courtyard between them as a linking space. In the immediate vicinity the remains of a Bronze Age stone quarry can be seen.
descriptions.NUR13290: This is the nuraghe Monti di Deu, still partly buried, in a good state of preservation; it stands on the summit of Monte di Deu on the Limbara massif, on the Calangianus side.
descriptions.NUR3270: Only faint traces of two towers added tangentially remain.
descriptions.NUR10510:
Nuragic settlement, attested by a demolished single-tower nuraghe and Middle Bronze Age pottery.

Decontextualised and illegible site, although the recovery of the materials found on the spot, the relevant documentation, and the contextualisation of the whole are desirable.
descriptions.NUR4663: Simple proto-nuraghe, of which only very little remains
descriptions.NUR4481: Proto-nuraghe with a village around it. The size and position of the proto-nuraghi of Monti Crastu and Monti Mannu suggest that these may have been the most important centres of proto-Nuragic cantons or sub-cantons in the Campidano, or at least that, together with the other complex proto-nuraghi, they may have controlled a large part of it.
descriptions.NUR4617: Single-tower nuraghe of which only some traces remain
descriptions.NUR8198: Nuraghe of uncertain type built on the tip of a limestone hill featuring karst caves used from the Neolithic period onwards. Three rows of stones, up to 25 metres long, are clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR4622: Single-tower, of which only a small portion remains.
descriptions.NUR5909: South-west of the hamlet of Lu Bagnu, on the plateau south of Monte Oschiri, stands the nuraghe of the same name. It is completely hidden by soil and vegetation, making the plan hard to read, but it is certainly a complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and a tower to the north-east; the extent of the hill covering it suggests the presence of other towers. The tholos of the central tower is intact, visible only from above where traces of a second floor are evident.
descriptions.NUR10024: Nuraghe with a central tower and an additional tower facing it. The nuraghe is located near the cemetery where the large statues of Monte Prama have been found.
descriptions.NUR4598: The proto-nuraghi of Monti Proceddu, Monti Tellura, Monti Acutzu and Monti de su Marchesu were very probably placed to guard the borders of districts of the Trexenta, whose most important centres must have been in the present municipal territories of Guasila or Samatzai; the one at Sa Corona (Bruncu de is Angionis Birdis) must have controlled at least the proto-nuraghi of Monti Atziaddei (?), Genna su Carru and those of Monti Cuamnaxi (Coa Margine) and Sa Corona di Villagreca.
descriptions.NUR10617: Nuraghe of undetermined type; only a few remains are left on the site among the vegetation. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR4025: This nuraghe has also been completely destroyed; only traces of a single course of a single-tower nuraghe about 9 metres in diameter remain. Many potsherds and basalt lava querns were found on the surface.
descriptions.NUR4437: In 1788 the community council of Villaputzu complained that the cove of Murtas, where the sea penetrated a long, deep inlet, was unguarded. Corsairs hid "behind large boulders at an ancient nuraghe called Nuraxi de moros", which they used as a base for raids: in 1767 they enslaved two farmers; in 1779 two peasants; in 1781 four; in 1788 two men who were making charcoal for their own use.
descriptions.NUR4046: Damaged nuraghe, with the upper part of the tholos collapsed. Set within a forest.
descriptions.NUR5297:
Complex nuraghe, perhaps three-lobed, built of large blocks of local andesite.

Among the vegetation some stone heaps and traces can be seen that probably belong to hut structures.

Reoccupation in historical times is clear, to which numerous pottery fragments, mostly of Roman date, found on the collapse and in the surrounding ground, belong.
descriptions.NUR4676: The nuraghe is situated on the summit of the hill. Single-tower with a staircase. Completely with its top missing.
descriptions.NUR20336: The nuraghe and adjacent village are situated behind the hill that hosts the Nuragic sanctuary of Santa Vittoria di Serri.
descriptions.NUR2582:
Report: name check:

On the IGM maps it is wrongly called Muggiaglio. The name is Egra e Mele.
descriptions.NUR6468: Nuraghe composed of trachyte blocks; only the lintel remains, the rest has been destroyed, probably its stones were used for the dry-stone walls in the area.
descriptions.NUR4753: The nuraghe is in very poor condition, nestled within the dense forest of Scala Argiolas, an ancient entrance to the high plateau of Giara.
descriptions.NUR3049: Originally built of medium-sized basalt blocks, it uses the bedrock as a foundation. At present it is almost illegible because of the conspicuous collapse, held in place by vegetation consisting of wild olives and prickly pears.
descriptions.NUR12245: Single-tower nuraghe made of granite blocks, with in situ evidence of trachyte ashlar finely worked for decorative purposes.
descriptions.NUR2603: The nuraghe is almost entirely collapsed. Only the entrance with lintel remains.
descriptions.NUR21169: The whole structure makes use of the natural rock. The nuraghe is in poor condition. Part of it has collapsed; a magnificent lintel and some walls remain. There is also a corridor leading to a chamber of which only a slight raised area survives.
descriptions.NUR20322: Single-tower, difficult to access, partially collapsed, with the tholos destroyed.
descriptions.NUR3592: It is one of the three nuraghi that stand around the perimeter of the artificial lake of the former Madau estate. The basal circle consists of cyclopean boulders that give it an imposing presence, almost as a guardian of the surrounding valley, which is itself heavily settled and rich in other fine remains. Nuraghe della collina dei cervi.mu
descriptions.NUR3656: Like many others, in total ruin. Enough evidence of the ancient construction can still be distinguished, with some boulders of the basal circle visible. Unfortunately, in the 1960s several sites in the area disappeared because of land-reclamation works, but above all because of the construction of the reservoir dam, which never fully served its intended purpose. Nuraghe of the hill of the deer. See Montìju de chèlvos I.mu
descriptions.NUR6146:
On a rocky spur stands the corridor nuraghe, rectangular in plan, built of pink trachyte boulders. The interior of the monument is not accessible because of the many collapses.

The giants' tomb lies to the south, about 500 metres from the nuraghe; only part of the inner wall face of the chamber and traces of the peristalith are visible.

On an area of about 2000 sq m around the giants' tomb, numerous structures are visible, of which only the basal courses remain.
descriptions.NUR3461: The Mura Craba Nuraghe is located near a quarry, about 2 km east of Bauladu. It is a single-tower nuraghe built with basalt blocks in good state of preservation.
descriptions.NUR3552: It is the collapsed nuraghe, reference point for the beautiful and nearby giants' tomb.
descriptions.NUR6253: Nuraghe surrounded by vegetation and eroded
descriptions.NUR6125: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal basalt blocks. Despite the dense vegetation the circular plan can be made out, and about five courses, though quite irregular, are visible on the north-west side. The entrance, on the east, has a collapsed right jamb and a lintel set at an angle.
descriptions.NUR2517: Complex nuraghe, eroded and enveloped by vegetation. Its outline is difficult to define. It could be four-lobed.
descriptions.NUR11113: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The structures are covered by a large fig tree and bramble bushes. Despite this, the building is in fair condition, partly because it has been used as a livestock shelter, an activity that has led to some internal alterations. The lintelled entrance faces south-east. On the left side of the entrance passage opens the stairwell, now blocked by collapse debris.
descriptions.NUR6183: The nuraghe is probably of a complex type and equipped with an outer wall, although the extensive collapse and the vegetation covering it prevent a more precise assessment.
descriptions.NUR18759: Of the monument, only some base courses remain, while the entrance has been incorporated into a modern hut.
descriptions.NUR6429: The nuraghe retains an intact tholos, but the collapse at the entrance means it cannot be visited. The chamber has four niches, making it one of the very few nuraghi known so far with this feature.
descriptions.NUR6057: The monument is a single-tower, single-chamber nuraghe. Its entrance and the whole of its base are badly damaged, although clear traces of a staircase and a guard niche remain. The north-western wall face is the best preserved, standing about six metres high with eight courses of roughly dressed blocks. Along the corridor, itself practically destroyed, the traces of two facing niches can be seen.
descriptions.NUR3173: Only the outer perimeter of this nuraghe is clearly visible. The rest of the structure is barely discernible. Its plan is rectangular with very rounded corners, and its maximum height to the north is 4 m with six courses of roughly dressed boulders. The western flank consists of a rock face that drops sheer into the valley.
descriptions.NUR2633: Single-tower nuraghe, covered by a layer of vegetation, whose tholos is still intact
descriptions.NUR2939: Single-tower nuraghe of simple type, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The building, camouflaged among the dense vegetation and overshadowed by a large clump of prickly pears, retains about six courses of superimposed blocks. The entrance, to the south-east, has a large, well-squared monolithic lintel. The jamb blocks are also quite carefully worked.
descriptions.NUR590: Complex nuraghe of the tancato type, with a central tower and a secondary tower.
descriptions.NUR5633:
The main monument stands on a plateau in a commanding position. It is a single-tower nuraghe built in regular courses of well-worked trachyte blocks. The entrance, oriented S-SE, has been horribly altered into a pointed-arch opening, because the nuraghe was long used as a pigsty.

Above it the relieving window survives. A corridor 4 m long and 1.00–2.00 m wide, corbel-vaulted in the first part and flat-lintelled in the second, leads into the chamber.
descriptions.NUR5601: Single-tower nuraghe, in poor condition; traces of an intra-mural staircase and lateral niches are visible. At the best-preserved point the nuraghe rises for about 3 m with six courses of roughly dressed boulders.
descriptions.NUR5674:
The nuraghe is surrounded by a square wall, inside which the circular remains of huts can be seen, perhaps forming a small village.

The upper part of the perimeter of the enclosure wall shows several stretches of a walkway cut into the thickness of the wall.
descriptions.NUR6205:
The skill with which the basalt blocks have been laid is immediately striking. Swallowed by the earth and wrapped in greenery.

The south-east entrance is topped by an enormous lintel and leads into the chamber, where access is blocked by the collapsed tholos.

It must have been an elegant single-tower nuraghe, in a strategic position "guarding" a small, lush valley.
descriptions.NUR6314: There is a considerable quantity of potsherds in the area. Visible amid the dense vegetation, one hut is still intact; a first tower and a second, perhaps the remains of a multi-lobed structure; a magnificent well or cistern with a basalt ring at the mouth.
descriptions.NUR3638: The monument, inside the village of Sagama near the parish church, is a single-tower nuraghe with a stair, a corridor niche and a central chamber flanked by three niches arranged in a cross.
descriptions.NUR2341: Nuraghe Muromoi overlooks a village of huts. It is a complex nuraghe that is hard to read because it is hidden by a conspicuous collapse. A central tower and the traces of lateral towers built with roughly dressed andesite blocks can nevertheless be made out. A small village of huts extends to the south-east.
descriptions.NUR3884: Its name comes from the place-name of the land, which in turn refers to the muzzle of the Bull god present in the domus de janas not far away, but also very probably to the more recent medieval or even nineteenth-century period, from the noise made by the waterfall of the same name in winter. “Su mummuttu de s'abba cando sicche addobat dae punta de sas roccas aintro de sa peschina, faghet unu murrunzu mannu. mu
descriptions.NUR1914:
A complex nuraghe, difficult to read in its ground plan because of the dense vegetation and the conspicuous collapse, made up of large andesite blocks.

Traces of a village of Nuragic huts can be seen, especially to the south-east, and of an open-air Neolithic village in the area between the nuraghe and the Neolithic hypogeal necropolis of Serra Maverru.
descriptions.NUR12140:
The Murruzzone or Thiortorro Nuraghe. It was not easy to spot because it is surrounded by brambles, but it lies almost on the valley floor near some springs. A surviving wall about 4 m long remains, and inside it a circular niche whose entrance faces east, accessible from the inside and measuring about 2 m.

Most of it is probably still buried.
descriptions.NUR4427: It has been restored recently, although much of the complex has yet to be excavated. It must certainly have been an imposing structure, since it was originally formed by as many as five towers around which the village huts stood.
descriptions.NUR3684: The main nucleus of the Pidighi archaeological complex lies inside the Municipal Park of the same name; it consists of two nuraghi (Pidighi and Muru Accas) with their respective settlements and their respective water sources...
descriptions.NUR6184: A complex tholos nuraghe with lateral additions, with a clearly legible main tower and two further towers added. One of these is legible, though covered by vegetation, the other only discernible beneath the dense scrub. The main tower survives in fair condition and has a lintelled entrance oriented to the south-east. On the IGM maps the nuraghe is marked as Serra Crastula.
descriptions.NUR3982:
It is a medium-sized single-tower nuraghe. The building style is the one typical of the sites in the area.

It stands on a small rise a short distance from the Pardu river and commanded a good view over the lower part of the valley formed by the same river.

The site is not in very good condition. The entrance side is intact, but the interior has almost completely collapsed. Only the corridor and the internal staircase can be made out. The vegetation is dense, making the site difficult to visit.
descriptions.NUR21135: The structure is completely missing its top and shows only faint traces of wall faces. Illegal excavations have severely damaged the structure.
descriptions.NUR5400: Nuraghe of which only very little remains externally, collapsed and never studied
descriptions.NUR6379: It is a nuraghe with a regular lintel and a relieving window. In the corridor, 4 m long and 1.2 m wide, the stair is on the left while the guard cell is missing. The eccentric chamber, 4 m in diameter, is enhanced by two equidistant niches, narrow and deep… The nuraghe is surrounded by a double concentric wall of two faces, 3 m thick in total.
