On one side the wall breaks off; on the other it is 5 m high and has a small tower 6 m in diameter with a flat-lintelled entrance facing south-east.
descriptions.NUR3663: It consists of only a few remains.
descriptions.NUR1883: Four-lobed nuraghe with a very complex structure. Central tower with at least four connected towers linked by a curtain wall that encloses a large courtyard.
descriptions.NUR2746: The nuraghe is almost entirely collapsed. Only the entrance with lintel and traces of two corridors remain. A niche is also visible in the rear corridor. The Budas nuraghe is an example of a proto-nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5901: A complex tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The structures are overgrown with vegetation, but a central tower and an added tower with a courtyard can be made out, of the so-called tancato type. The added tower appears to be smaller than the central tower. From the top of the latter the interior of the chamber can be seen, still well preserved except for the collapsed upper part.
descriptions.NUR10920: At Scivu, by the beach of the same name, stands the nuraghe known as Nuraghe Narocci or Cancedda. The nuraghe sits on the hill of Punta su Nuraxi, 226 metres above sea level, overlooking the valley that slopes down to the coast. The structure consisted of at least four towers and covered a large area. Some of the scattered material has been found even at the foot of the hill.
descriptions.NUR3000: The nuraghe, an archaic corridor type, built of large polygonal blocks of local basalt, has a quadrangular–elliptical plan. It shows two communicating entrances, on the north and south sides respectively. The entrances are lintelled and vaguely trapezoidal. The internal corridor is visible and in excellent condition, with the usual roofing of slabs laid flat.
descriptions.NUR2827: The monument is a single-tower nuraghe with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a central chamber flanked by three niches in the classic cruciform layout. The masonry consists of large boulders in the lower courses and progressively smaller stones towards the top. Around the nuraghe are remains of the village to the east and a stretch of outer wall to the north.
descriptions.NUR19672: Situated on the hill of the same name, from which it overlooks the Bechida valley and part of the coastal strip that leads northwards to the Nuraghe Artora, the structure is poorly preserved. It consists of a circular wall face of modest dimensions that appears to have belonged to a large hut, built of local granite. A large quantity of collapse debris is visible outside the walls.
descriptions.NUR6233: Single-tower nuraghe, surrounded by Indian fig trees and vegetation. It retains the fine entrance portal with a cracked lintel and dangerous condition, the tholos and the staircase leading to the upper level.
descriptions.NUR4451: Single-tower nuraghe surrounded by dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR4316: Near the remains of this nuraghe there is a sacred nuragic well that has miraculously survived the surrounding quarrying activities.
descriptions.NUR3350: Single-tower nuraghe, ruined, collapsed and overgrown with vegetation
descriptions.NUR5448: An enormous, tall building of huge, very dark basalt blocks, cyclopean, worked just enough to fit them together and give the structures perfect circularity. The central tower, very broad, and two other towers are visible, one to the south-east and the other to the north-west, plus a stretch of wall linking the central tower to the north-western one. The maximum visible height of the tower walls reaches 3 metres. The eastern part of the complex is covered with earth and vegetation.
descriptions.NUR8834: It stands 7.50 metres high over 21 courses, with a diameter of 11 metres, and is characterised by a very tall tholos with thick walls. A Nuragic–Roman–medieval village, later abandoned because of plagues, adjoins it; on the north-west side there is a wall face running for perhaps a hundred metres along a natural cliff.
descriptions.NUR6119: Located on a picturesque natural crag near the Nieddu nuraghe. It appears ruined and hard to interpret because only a few courses remain in situ. The main tower and a smaller secondary tower, probably added later, are visible.
descriptions.NUR5604:
It stands on a small rise from which the surrounding view can be appreciated. It is a single-tower nuraghe about 11 metres high with a tholos roof. Built of large blocks of dark basalt which, together with yellow lichens, give it its characteristic colouring (hence the name: in Sardinian nieddu means black, dark).

The tower has two openings: an entrance at the base, still partly buried, and, almost at the top, a large window.
descriptions.NUR20051: It stands on the summit of the hill of the same name. At first sight it looks like a single-tower nuraghe partly buried, but it is probably a multi-lobed one. The lintel above the entrance is very unusual, being slightly curved. The main entrance has a pointed vault. It too is semi-buried, for its lintel is only a few centimetres above the ground.
descriptions.NUR4762: Of the nuraghe Niu e Crobu nothing remains but a squalid testimony. Indeed the monument lies unknown amid the vegetation and a fence that robs it of its dignity, forced to look on as a reservoir clad in its own stone sits beside it, so as not to spoil the environmental impact… ignorance knows no bounds.
descriptions.NUR3075:
Tholos nuraghe.

The main tower currently preserves its chamber, which is sub-circular in plan and filled with collapse debris from the tholos and the upper part of the wall face; a first block marking the start of the corridor is visible. About 8.50 m to the south there is a secondary tower surviving to a height of five courses, laid in polygonal technique and in an irregular manner.
descriptions.NUR1895: A probably multi-lobed nuraghe whose exact structure cannot be determined; the massive collapse and the dense vegetation on the hill where the monument stands prevent its understanding. To the south, although filled with earth and collapse boulders, an oval chamber is visible, exposed by the action of looters. From NW to NE a curvilinear wall, about 9 m high, set against the rocky ridge, could be part of the central tower's wall face.
descriptions.NUR3068: Part of the nuraghe has been altered and adapted for the construction of a pinnetto.
descriptions.NUR6221: The Nolza nuraghe is a large four-lobed nuraghe, formed by four corner towers joined by straight bastions and a central tower still standing 13 metres high. Archaeological investigations, begun in 1994 and still in progress, have made it possible to distinguish several construction phases, characterised by alterations and adaptations. In a first phase the nuraghe was built of local schist, the material of which the central tower and two of the corner towers still consist.
descriptions.NUR3281: It should have been a perfect three-lobed structure.
descriptions.NUR4049: The Norampè nuraghe is literally almost entirely vanished, only a few stones integrated into the rock remain, testifying to its excellent and prominent location.
descriptions.NUR21109: Damaged and demolished by vegetation encroachment. Difficult to interpret.
descriptions.NUR21108: Damaged and demolished by vegetation encroachment. Difficult to interpret.
descriptions.NUR21103: Damaged and demolished by vegetation encroachment. Difficult to interpret.
descriptions.NUR21106: Damaged and demolished by vegetation encroachment. Difficult to interpret.
descriptions.NUR21104: Damaged and demolished by vegetation encroachment. Difficult to interpret.
descriptions.NUR21105: Damaged and demolished by vegetation encroachment. Difficult to interpret.
descriptions.NUR21107: Damaged and demolished by vegetation encroachment. Difficult to interpret.
descriptions.NUR2594: Complex nuraghe with traces of a village surrounding it, featuring significant collapses on the slopes. From here there is a prominent view and control over the village, which includes a temple at Irru.
descriptions.NUR3887:
Sa Pedra de Nunnale. A picturesque and colossal tower of bizarre shape, at the base of which stands the eponymous Nuraghe. The nuraghe, though imposing, appears incredibly tiny compared to the immense rock that looms over it.

This single-tower nuraghe is built of barely dressed megalithic blocks, even larger at the base. Around the rocky mass it is possible to make out the huts of a small village.
descriptions.NUR5617: The Nuraghe Nuracale is a four-lobed type, consisting of a central tower, or central tower, surrounded by four smaller towers held together by massive straight walls. The main entrance, located in the east bastion, gives access to the internal courtyard, shaped like a half-moon, onto which open the entrance of the central tower and of the south-east and north-east lateral towers, while the other two towers were linked to the courtyard by two long corridors cut into the bastions.
descriptions.NUR4937:
The Nuraceddeu nuraghe shows a curious worked and shaped stone that forms the junction between the straight stretch of the bastion and one of the nuragic towers.

It is a genuine "nuragic special building piece".

This nuraghe, which may hold other interesting features, lies in the territory of Gesturi.

The bastion of the nuraghe has masonry built with well-worked stones.
descriptions.NUR11487: Single-tower nuraghe and settlement, destroyed due to the construction of the railway. The exact location is not known. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR10443: Multi-lobed nuraghe with an outer wall and a straight curtain wall, built of basalt blocks; a Republican Roman settlement on the ruins of the nuraghe. Traces of the nuraghe came to light during roadworks for the construction of the flyover piers: the site was extensively documented and is now completely hidden.
descriptions.NUR5566: This complex nuraghe consisted of a tall central tower and three towers joined by a bastion, now not very well preserved. The tall central tower, on the other hand, is in perfect condition, with a surviving height of 14 m, not much less than its original height. It rises on two storeys, both intact and each roofed with a tholos.
descriptions.NUR2224: Of the monument, only the first two courses of the base remain. It could belong to the nuraghe Nuradorzu.
descriptions.NUR2849: Nuraghe of which only a few courses remain
descriptions.NUR3234: The structure composed of basalt blocks is rubble and collapsed. The remains are scattered over a wide area covered with vegetation.
descriptions.NUR6340: "Nuraghe Su Nuragheddu, or de Sa Taula, or de Su Coddu 'e Su Nuraghe. It stands near the Rio di Posada, in a narrow gorge between cliffs, guarding a pass; it is destroyed, but clear traces of the nuraghe remain. On land belonging to Deiana Serafino."
descriptions.NUR12455: Structures belonging to a single-tower tholos nuraghe. Hard to make out in the dense vegetation, the nuraghe preserves about three basal courses of large polygonal basalt blocks. The rest of the structure has collapsed and the debris fills the lower part. Despite the poor condition, the remains can be interpreted as a small simple nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR1263: Area where ancient maps indicated the location of the nuraghe Nuraghessu; in this area one or more dolmen are present.
descriptions.NUR3979: Built of limestone blocks on a rocky outcrop, it consists of a main tower, an added section where the remains of a corridor can be seen, and the remains of several huts on the west side. It is not in a good state of preservation.
descriptions.NUR4105:
The Nuraxeddu nuraghe stands on a hillock that is now isolated in the middle of a stretch of land used as pasture for sheep flocks.

The masonry is built of roughly dressed parallelepiped blocks laid in fairly regular courses.
descriptions.NUR4209: The megalithic structure is currently located within a sheepfold.
descriptions.NUR16535: The remains of the nuraghe are hard to make out; it has certainly been dismantled and the ashlars may have been used to build the retaining walls and boundary walls found in the area where the nuraghe probably stood. From the booklet “Ritratto di nuraghe eredità di un'isola …” by Sara Muscuso we read: “All that remains of the nuraghe is a curvilinear wall face made up of one or two courses.”
descriptions.NUR17160: It was indicated on ancient cadastral maps. Probable location, no traces are identifiable.
descriptions.NUR18260:
Marks the boundary between the municipal territories of Serrenti and that of Villagreca.

Recorded in the historical cadastral map.
descriptions.NUR2500:
Complex nuraghe built of the local volcanic rock. Largely covered by vegetation and hidden by collapse, stretches of walling from the towers that made up the building can be made out. One part has been disturbed by illicit excavations.

At the foot of the hill, to the north, a hypogeum, perhaps an air-raid shelter.

It is likely that on the summit of the hill, in the private land enclosed by fences and inaccessible, traces of the protohistoric cluster of huts may survive.
descriptions.NUR4477: Remains of a nuraghe upon which Roman to medieval period settlements have been superimposed.
descriptions.NUR4239: Possible origin of the name: nuraghe of the scolca, which in the Judicate period was a guard post. On a small rise at 70 m above sea level there is a heap of stones and basalt boulders, traces of tombs, Roman pottery and obsidian flakes.
descriptions.NUR5671: The nuraghe was built in the advanced phase of the Middle Bronze Age (1500–1400 BC) on a granite base surrounded by a series of massive boulders, adapting the building to the irregular shape of the hill. It is a four-lobed nuraghe, with a central tower and four other towers added concentrically. Access is made easy by a ramp leading to the entrance, which in turn opens into a long corridor with corbelled walls forming a pointed arch.
descriptions.NUR3981: Ruined nuraghe, buried and hard to define.
descriptions.NUR5167: Nuraghe reported, embedded in vegetation and not visible from the outside
descriptions.NUR3771: Single-tower with circular plan (diam. 12.80 x 12) and a maximum remaining height of 2.55 m.
descriptions.NUR3054: It is a nuraghe more than partially collapsed. It appears as a haphazard heap of stones, which, on its least damaged side, retains three courses of the original foundation.
descriptions.NUR3144: It is a corridor nuraghe of difficult detection due to its poor state of conservation and the rubble from collapses that prevent its reading.
descriptions.NUR9632:
Corridor nuraghe with an indefinable plan because of its irregularity, and a profile that juts out and recedes.

The main entrance, facing south-east, is rectangular (height 1.70 m – width 1.40 m) with a sturdy lintel and leads into a corridor that cannot be traversed because of the collapse; a secondary entrance, collapsed and blocked, seems to open to the south-west.

The wall face survives to a maximum height of 3.60 m with six horizontal, irregular courses; the blocks are polygonal and only roughly dressed.
descriptions.NUR1969: Scant remains of a small nuraghe
descriptions.NUR5800:
The nuraghe consists of a main building with a three-storey central tower, against which a bilobed bastion on two levels is built, enclosing a courtyard and two secondary towers. It is surrounded by an outer wall provided with towers and by a sacred area.

Its tower has the largest diameter of any known nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5582: The nuraghe Ola is a single-tower nuraghe about 12 m in external diameter and 10 m high, dating to the Recent Bronze Age. What is particularly striking is the use of different building materials: on the outside the base consists of 12 courses of granite blocks, while above them sit 13 courses of trachyte.
descriptions.NUR19510: Of the Olai nuraghe in this pile of stones, currently only the foundation is visible.
descriptions.NUR4380: Complex nuraghe, with a frontal addition, surrounded by a village
descriptions.NUR4632: Single-tower nuraghe with an addition not easily legible. Surrounding village.
descriptions.NUR4636: A single-tower nuraghe of which very little remains
descriptions.NUR20232: Only a few courses of the nuraghe remain. Located in a position of observation and signaling, it provides a view spanning 360 degrees over all the surrounding mountains and nuraghes.
descriptions.NUR3650: Particular structure with a staircase on the left and a niche on the right side of the corridor. Nuraghe likely restored in successive phases.
descriptions.NUR3320: It is completely surrounded by dense vegetation, which prevents access. It is a four-lobed nuraghe built with basalt blocks.
descriptions.NUR3217: Nuraghe type undetermined, set amidst dense vegetation, not accessible internally.
descriptions.NUR1029:
The nuraghe stands on the summit of a hill, a short distance from the domus de janas of the same name and from Nuraghe s'Aspru.

Of the monument, perhaps an enclosure rather than a nuraghe, two or three courses survive on the west and north sides, to an average height of 2 metres, together with other stones scattered on the ground. The masonry incorporates the natural rock into its circuit and must have enclosed a diameter of about 11 metres. The stones are large and only roughly dressed.
descriptions.NUR5651:
It is a complex nuraghe, built of basalt, on a small rise composed of at least three towers and surrounded by a village.

The foundations of the towers and of what must have been the huts are clearly distinguishable. The central tower still stands partially. Climbing to the top of the tower one can indeed see the interior chamber. Debris accumulated inside and outside, however, prevents access from the base.
descriptions.NUR2995:
The archaeological site stands on a rocky cliff of granitic nature, bounded by three spires lying about 30 and 50 m apart.

The area covers about 2.0 ha; the settlement is hard to read in plan because of the vegetation and its very poor state of preservation.

The site is surrounded by an outer wall that encloses the nuraghe, the two watchtowers and, in the centre, the Nuragic huts, while other huts lie outside the wall on the east side.
descriptions.NUR2782: It is visible from the SS131 and immediately strikes you as a special nuraghe. Special because it combines the features of a nuraghe with an elongated, upturned-boat-shaped chamber and a truncated-cone nuraghe. On entering, you find yourself in the long chamber, which has two large niches and is about 7 metres high; at the far end a doorway leads to a staircase that, plunging into darkness and enclosed by the nuragic walls, spirals up to the upper floor.
descriptions.NUR13372: The Orgono nuraghe at Ghilarza is a remarkable monument whose structural development tells the evolution of Nuragic architecture: from the archaic nuraghe with an elongated, upturned-boat-shaped chamber to the truncated-conical tower with a circular tholos chamber. The consolidation and excavation work carried out so far has allowed at least partial recovery of the monument, which was already seriously unstable and in danger of collapse.
descriptions.NUR3176: Around it one can see the remains of the ancient village and the granitic rocks in their varied shapes. Near the building, of which only a few courses and the lintel facing Monte Novo remain, the traces of the granite quarries are very evident. Within an area of 1 km there are nine domus de janas; some lie near the Nuraghe, the others, on the same granitic outcrop, lie near the Sau family farmhouse.
descriptions.NUR6448:
The nuraghe is a single-tower nuraghe built with large, well-worked boulders.

The entrance is topped by an imposing lintel and leads into a corridor with a niche on the right and the stairwell on the left; the latter is largely filled with rubble. At the end of the corridor the circular chamber opens, its tholos vault still intact, containing three symmetrically placed niches.
descriptions.NUR19708: A small single-tower nuraghe a short distance from the settlement of Siniscola to the north, and presumably belonging to the nearby village of Ghiramonte. The structure is badly damaged by a quarry that extends to its feet. Only a section of the wall face to the south-east is visible; fragments of Nuragic pottery can be seen on the ground nearby.
descriptions.NUR2590: It is located on the hill overlooking the commune of Silanus. It is a complex nuraghe, mainly built of granite. The central tower, originally about 12 metres high, remains almost intact and was originally flanked by two or three additional bodies. The nuraghe features two superimposed tholos connected by a main staircase and a secondary, hidden staircase with a mezzanine. At the base of the nuraghe, remnants of other nuragic constructions are visible, still insufficiently studied.
descriptions.NUR5764:
This is a three-lobed nuraghe of particular importance because of its position, size and state of preservation. It lies in the Marghine sub-region, in the territory of the municipality of Bortigali, at an altitude of 785 metres, from which a vast portion of central Sardinia can be seen.

The site stands at the foot of Monte Cuguruttu (867 metres), in a position that ranges from the nearby Monte Santu Padre (1,025 metres) to the more distant mountains
descriptions.NUR3460:
The tower, circular in plan (diam. 10.65 x 10.12 m), survives to a maximum height of 4.40 m on the north-east side, while the minimum is 3 m on the south-west. The masonry consists of trachyte blocks roughly dressed with some care and laid in fairly regular horizontal courses. The wall thickness is 3.30 m on the north-east, 4 m on the south and 3 m on the north-west.

The interior of the nuraghe is entered through a rectangular doorway (h. 1.70 m – w. 0.90 m), lintelled, oriented to the south-east and slightly splayed inwards.
descriptions.NUR6096: Nuraghe type undetermined; it features a tower with the tholos still intact, surrounded by remains of collapse within the dense undergrowth.
descriptions.NUR5563: Likely complex nuraghe today partially collapsed and difficult to read.
descriptions.NUR4721: Ruins of the base drum of a classic single-tower nuraghe in polygonal masonry, with a maximum surviving height of about 4 m, an internal chamber roofed with a tholos and provided with a small subsidiary niche, and an entrance stair – unfortunately completely destroyed – defended by an opposing guard chamber. The building, already dismantled in Roman times, was reused, incorporating five fragments of figured statue-menhirs that already existed in the area.
descriptions.NUR3506: Because of the collapse, which affects the entrance itself, it is not possible to enter the chamber. The polygonal masonry consists of well-shaped granite blocks with frequent use of wedges of the same stone. The base, by contrast, has a much more compact structure than the upper part of the monument, with large, roughly worked blocks.
descriptions.NUR11739: Because of the collapse, which affects the entrance itself, it is not possible to enter the chamber. The polygonal masonry consists of well-shaped granite blocks with frequent use of wedges of the same stone. The base, by contrast, has a much more compact structure than the upper part of the monument, with large, roughly worked blocks.
descriptions.NUR4267: Damaged nuraghe with multiple towers, undecipherable, part of a larger settlement.
descriptions.NUR663: Damaged nuraghe of which a good height of about 3 metres is preserved.
descriptions.NUR5191: The finds show that it was occupied from the Middle Bronze Age to the Recent Bronze Age. It is built of large limestone blocks and preserved a chamber with two niches and a staircase. Now the collapse blocks the entrance. Near the nuraghe the remains of a hut can be recognised, consisting of a circular room and an atrium.
descriptions.NUR3295: In very poor condition of conservation, completely ruined, only a few courses remain visible.
descriptions.NUR5843: The Ortei nuraghe is a three-lobed type, consisting of a central tower, still in a good state of preservation, and two lateral towers whose remains are almost completely buried and overgrown with vegetation. The peculiarity of this nuraghe lies in the fact that the chamber of the central tower, which has a circular plan, is provided with three particularly deep niches, especially the central one, which has a large lintel with a small window above it.
descriptions.NUR4208: It is a quadrilobate nuraghe (Sardara commune) completely demolished, of which only a few courses of the mural basement remain.
descriptions.NUR2398: Half-ruined. Twelve courses of stones remain, with a breach to the south-east, perhaps the entrance. The prismatic shape of the stones made it easy to fit them together, so they are joined precisely, but they are not laid in horizontal layers. The outer wall is vertical and hard to reach, so it is not easy to get inside.
descriptions.NUR2376: Half-ruined. Twelve courses of stones remain, with a breach to the south-east, perhaps the entrance. The prismatic shape of the stones made it easy to fit them together, so they are joined precisely, but they are not laid in horizontal layers. The outer wall is vertical and hard to reach, so it is not easy to get inside.
descriptions.NUR6376: Around the nuraghe lies an extensive Nuragic village; most of the huts are now reduced to heaps of rubble, but large enclosures remain with walls higher than usual that in places look like ramparts, so it was probably a fortified settlement.
descriptions.NUR5740: Set in a striking wood of monumental wild olives, the nuraghe has a complex, four-lobed plan, with a corridor, an access ramp in the upper part, and a trapdoor leading to an underground chamber. The only accessible lateral tower is the one to the north, and it is visible from the upper part of the central tower.
descriptions.NUR12021: Single-tower nuraghe in partial good condition, located on the slope of a small hillock.
descriptions.NUR15904:
Designated by IGM with the nuraghe symbol, it is now disappeared.

It is likely that it belonged to a hut from the village or to a giants' tomb.
descriptions.NUR16879:
A single-tower nuraghe (mostly remains) is present on the ridge of the hill Cuccuru S. Eremilis, very close to the road.

Position to be verified
descriptions.NUR15664: Complex nuraghe of the four-lobed type. Traces of a central tower and three added towers with the bastion are visible, of which only the foundations survive in very poor condition. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR3145: Of complex plan, it is built of basalt in a structure of well-squared blocks laid in regular horizontal courses so that the joints of the upper blocks fall at the mid-point of the lower ones. The stronghold probably consists of three towers enclosing a small courtyard with an entrance to the south-west.
descriptions.NUR6457: The Nuraghe di Ozzilo lies in the territory of Aidomaggiore. It is a corridor nuraghe, entered from above because the interior is choked with rubble from the collapse. The chamber inside is filled with collapse debris that has affected part of the "navetiform" vault. Two giants' tombs lie a short distance away; one of them has unfortunately been partly destroyed.
descriptions.NUR18858: The Nuraghe di Ozzilo lies in the territory of Aidomaggiore. It is a corridor nuraghe, entered from above because the interior is choked with rubble from the collapse. The chamber inside is filled with collapse debris that has affected part of the "navetiform" vault. Two giants' tombs lie a short distance away; one of them has unfortunately been partly destroyed.
descriptions.NUR18860: The Nuraghe di Ozzilo lies in the territory of Aidomaggiore. It is a corridor nuraghe, entered from above because the interior is choked with rubble from the collapse. The chamber inside is filled with collapse debris that has affected part of the "navetiform" vault. Two giants' tombs lie a short distance away; one of them has unfortunately been partly destroyed.
descriptions.NUR3268: Single-tower with the tholos collapsed inward
descriptions.NUR3521:
The nuraghe Paddaggiu, "pagliaio", lies less than one kilometre from "dall'elefante".

It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe but is in fact a complex nuraghe, consisting of a central tower and a bastion with two lateral towers that are barely legible. The peculiarity of this nuraghe is the presence of a chamber set above the entrance corridor, originally reached by a staircase inside the right-hand niche of the main chamber. The tholos and the staircase leading to the upper floor survive intact.
descriptions.NUR15018: Single-tower nuraghe with a dismantled and buried village, the structure of which cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR4621: The nuraghe Paiulu (IGM) or Paiolu stands perched on a basalt bastion at Costa Pisu, on the west flank of Monte Arci, on the boundary between the municipal territories of Oristano, Palmas Arborea (Tiria) and Villaurbana.
descriptions.NUR18218:
It has a single entrance oriented to the northeast.

It is now covered with soil and sand, although at the top of the nuraghe the top section remains, from which part of the internal walling is visible.
descriptions.NUR21110: Now only large stones have remained, moved and reused in the nearby retaining walls.
descriptions.NUR3876: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The monument preserves three to four courses of blocks of the outer wall face, reaching a maximum surviving height of about 2.60 m. At present it is not possible to identify the entrance, partly because brambles and mastic partially cover the remains of the nuraghe. The inner chamber has collapsed and the material that formed it completely fills the remaining parts of the monument.
descriptions.NUR10446: Unidentified nuraghe. Area with finds attributable to a settlement with a nuraghe, the nuraghe has been demolished. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR2419: Completely dismantled. Probably partly still present beneath the vegetation, which shows stones placed without order.
descriptions.NUR9482:
The monument, located on the immediate northern outskirts of Birori, has a circular plan (diam. 12 x 12.30 m) with an average surviving height of only 2.75 m and two courses; the blocks, polygonal and roughly dressed, are laid in horizontal courses.

Because of its very poor state of preservation it is not possible to identify the internal structure of the monument.
descriptions.NUR8488:
Built of limestone and sandstone blocks, it consists of a central body with two towers, an outer wall, and a village of huts.

The oldest structures, dated to the 15th–10th centuries BC, are the main tower and some huts. The tower, with its entrance to the ENE, survives to a height of 8 m. The inner chamber preserves its tholos vault intact.

In the back wall opens the ogival stairwell that led to the upper floor and the terrace.
descriptions.NUR2954: Single-tower that remains half-submerged, completely buried.
descriptions.NUR5433: Present on topographic maps but evidently destroyed in the past. The sheepfold visible in the photo is not a nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR11648: Also known as "nurarchei" according to A. Tarameli (1915).
descriptions.NUR19667: Single-tower nuraghe with an attached village. The original tower survives, its interior choked with collapse and vegetation. About four complete courses of the original structure remain. To the south there is a curtain wall with an entrance topped by a lintel; because of collapse and vegetation its function cannot be determined. To the north-west of the tower a cyclopean wall is present, breaking off abruptly, apparently the north wall of a corridor.
descriptions.NUR4281: Complex nuraghe consisting of 3 towers connected together. The structure shows heavy damage caused by tomb robbers.
descriptions.NUR2684: Single-tower nuraghe with its top missing and encircled by vegetation, with a domus de janas located nearby.
descriptions.NUR2270: Single-tower nuraghe of large roughly dressed limestone blocks with the entrance facing south-east. The superstructure survives to a maximum height of 2.50 m. The stair is to the left of the entrance. The nuraghe is very hard to see because it is covered in vegetation.
descriptions.NUR6078: Damaged nuraghe, of which only a small portion remains at the junction of three borders.
descriptions.NUR3868: The monument, in a very poor state of preservation, does not allow the original layout of the structures to be identified; one can only hypothesise, judging by the line of some wall stretches on the south side where two courses of granite blocks survive, that it was a simple tholos nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR8946: The Pastoris nuraghe is a simple type, situated to the north-east of the settlement, near the municipal water reservoir, next to which some buildings belonging to a livestock farm were erected a few years ago; these do not really harmonise with the Nuragic presence.
descriptions.NUR3599: It is a single-tower nuraghe 9.90 metres in diameter whose entrance, still intact, leads into a corridor now open to the sky, off which the guard chamber opens, also intact. The circular chamber (diameter 3.50 m) has lost its top at 3.50 m above the present floor; it has no niches, and the doorway to the stair that led to the upper floors opened above ground level.
descriptions.NUR999: The Nissardi in 1901 (map included in G. Pinza's volume) indicated a giants' tomb slightly south-west of the Paule Tolta nuraghe: a nuraghe that is indeed located within the perimeter of the airport.
descriptions.NUR19589: Single-tower nuraghe built of a mixture of calcareous and arenaceous stone, while the lintel is made of trachyte. The chamber is bordered by three niches.
descriptions.NUR8430:
Situated on the southern bank of the Rio Berchida a short distance from the sea, it appears as a shapeless heap of collapse from which the upper part of the central tower can be glimpsed, and it can be inferred that additional structures were present.

On one side of the structure several courses of blocks roughly hewn from the local granite are visible, and damage caused by clandestine excavation is clearly evident.
descriptions.NUR3791: A few megalithic stones indicating a probable nuraghe, perhaps a circle. Witnesses certainly report that many stones ended up forming a hardcore layer during the reclamation of the marsh. Nuraghe of the marshes, of the swamps. See Paùles and Cunvéntu nòu.mu
descriptions.NUR5348:
The tower, truncated-conical in shape, shows a marked structural subsidence on the south side running from the entrance up to the top where the masonry is missing, also affecting part of the tholos.

From the entrance, oriented south/south-east and lacking its lintel, you enter a corridor that splays inwards with a partially surviving ogival roof. On the left side of the corridor the stairwell opens, roofed with flat slabs, of which three blocks remain.
descriptions.NUR4126:
The nuraghe forms the central nucleus of an articulated system of enclosures, the first of which is a massive wall that in several places incorporates the natural rock. Inside this perimeter a second courtyard develops in two semicircular arms that lean against the tower.

The tower itself has a slightly elliptical plan and its perimeter wall also incorporates stretches of natural rock.
descriptions.NUR1350: Probable complex nuraghe completely collapsed and fallen.
descriptions.NUR6232:
It is a single-tower nuraghe from which much of the plain below can be seen.

The nuraghe is completely ruined and on private land, but access is not difficult.

The courses below the lintel are buried.

The tholos has completely collapsed inwards, but through the rubble the spiral staircase can be made out on the left of the entrance, and a second staircase whose course is not easy to follow.

It is still worth a short visit.
descriptions.NUR1813: nuraghe Peddalzos, in the area between this one and the nuraghe Cheas, should be where the famous giants' tombs mentioned, studied and sought by G. Lilliu, are located.
descriptions.NUR3037: Historical memory, passed on by relatives and friends who gladly accompany me to the sites and tell me facts and stories attributed to their fathers and grandfathers, often guides me. The nuraghe is practically non-existent, but my guide's assurance is so strong that I am convinced it is true, because he himself has seen it directly.
descriptions.NUR11289: In this case too I must record the near-total absence of the site. Only a few boulders remain, but they still attest to the site's ancient presence. It is a place where you can try electromagnetic applications aimed at bodily well-being.
descriptions.NUR5942: More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe, and it is circular in plan.
descriptions.NUR5887:
Small nuraghe, located on a high crag of Monte Dominigu.

Nearby, to the west of the nuraghe, is the megalithic circle of Monte Dominigu. In the maps of the defunct land registry it is marked as Nuraghe San Leonardo.

On the current Sardinian Region CTR it is named "Nuraghe Sa Pedra Pertunta".
descriptions.NUR3894: A singular construction set exactly on the rocky summit of Pedras Serradas, barely distinguishable. It is a kind of semicircular nuraghe. Some consider it a circular nuraghe, others the remains of a nuraghe after the collapse of the ground beneath. The view over Giorrè is priceless.
descriptions.NUR3630: It is a bilobate complex nuraghe in granite with traces of a wall that encloses the monument. It is situated between the rocks at 245 m, on top of a hill.
descriptions.NUR3259: It is in a state of complete ruin. Some of the basal stones, though barely visible, are discernible and embedded in the natural rock, forming a single unit with the entire structure.
descriptions.NUR3043: Not easily reached because it stands on a high, particularly striking ridge, it comprises a complex nuraghe. The ruined structure is hard to read owing to the abundant collapse; courses of limestone blocks are visible.
descriptions.NUR6171:
Only a few courses are still visible at the Peidru nuraghe, a probable single-tower nuraghe located on the SP8 near the old cantoniera of Ponte Oinu.

An interesting boulder with three holes can be seen at the base of the monument.
descriptions.NUR5773: This is the second nuraghe named Peppe Gallu in the territory of Uri, after Peppe Gallu di Cuga. The associated village, which was very extensive, has been destroyed by agricultural mechanisation. It is a proto-nuraghe with a circular corridor. It has two raised entrances, above the level of the surrounding ground, which could be reached by wooden or rope ladders.
descriptions.NUR11480: Complex two-tower nuraghe with settlement. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR4838: Nuraghe of which only faint traces remain
descriptions.NUR3775: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. Of considerable size, it survives to a maximum height of about 5.40 m. Built of polygonal blocks of local basalt, it is well preserved on its western side, while the eastern side is partly collapsed and covered with vegetation. The entrance can be identified on the east side, but it has collapsed and is reduced to a simple opening.
descriptions.NUR6385: Nuraghe immersed in vegetation, eroded and partially buried. The entrance is visible but buried down to almost the lintel.
descriptions.NUR15009: Complex nuraghe, partially eroded and buried.
descriptions.NUR2120: Complex nuraghe composed of two simple towers added laterally and joined tangentially, oriented SSE and NNW. The SSE tower has its interior choked with collapse; on the south side there is a break in the wall outline. The second tower, oriented NNW, does not preserve its full perimeter, which is interrupted in several stretches by collapse probably caused by the dense vegetation there. Other building masses are present but not clearly definable because of collapse and vegetation.
descriptions.NUR545: The nuraghe stands on the summit of an isolated, modest elevation. The area is covered by vegetation that is almost impenetrable. Some alignments of granitic blocks are visible.
descriptions.NUR980: Complex nuraghe probably surrounded by a ring of walls, with traces of walls around it.
descriptions.NUR3757: The Perda Lada nuraghe stands on a hill used for grazing and cultivation, very close to the Crastutorro nuraghe. All that remains of the monument are large granite blocks which unfortunately do not help to identify the type of monument or its various features, perhaps also because of the stone-clearing work that has affected the area.
descriptions.NUR2628: Single-tower tholos nuraghe, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The internal chamber has collapsed in its upper part, but still survives to a height of about 3 m. Inside it two facing niches can be made out, one to the west, the other to the east. The entrance, no longer existing, must have faced south, as can be deduced from the surviving structures. The outer wall face survives to a maximum height of 4 m.
descriptions.NUR4638: A ruined single-tower nuraghe of which very few remains can be seen
descriptions.NUR3085: It is located in the territory of the comune of Urzulei at an elevation of 1,030 metres. It was a complex nuraghe, of which only a few ruins remain. Nearby are also important giants' tombs.
descriptions.NUR15070: Single-tower with its top missing and buried
descriptions.NUR10873: The tower is missing its top and the perimeter has an irregular shape. The internal diameter varies from 4.2 to 5.6 m. Presence of clandestine excavations.
descriptions.NUR5575: Nuraghe reported on Wikimapia but under deletion. To be verified.
descriptions.NUR5426: There are some subsquared granite blocks, on two courses, attributable to a nuragic structure.
descriptions.NUR5089: Unidentified nuraghe, located on the summit of a hill between two valleys, now reduced to a heap of large ashlar stones.
descriptions.NUR4630: It stands on the left-hand side of the Samatzai–Serrenti municipal road in the locality of the same name, on a slight rise of the plateau. It is a single-tower nuraghe with an external diameter of 10 m and a wall thickness of about 2 m. The basal course, formed of large limestone blocks quarried from the surrounding area which is rich in such outcrops, survives almost intact all round the circumference.
descriptions.NUR5465: The Nuragic village of Perdu Isu (one nuraghe and traces of about 11 huts) and the cistern-like cache known as "Su scusorgiu" lie at an altitude clearly above 1000 m a.s.l. The village stands on the crest of one of the tacchi, in visual contact with the better-known site of Serbissi and with the valley where the complex of "Is Tostoinus" stands.
descriptions.NUR1008: It appears as a heap of stones and a few large blocks of red sandstone, situated on ground excluded from cultivation and grazing, near the Anghelu Ruiu necropolis. State of preservation: poor.
descriptions.NUR5486: Erased, buried, little known and never excavated, it is visible while travelling along S.S. 131.
descriptions.NUR5822: This nuraghe has a partially collapsed tholos; once inside you find the stair entrance on the left and three niches with "stipetti" in the central chamber. The niche on the right, at first sight a normal niche, contains a stair leading to a mezzanine above the nuraghe entrance, with an opening from which you can see the entrance corridor. The mezzanine has a window looking onto the central chamber.
descriptions.NUR3817: Nuraghe, probably a simple tholos type. The structures are very difficult to interpret because of the dense vegetation, the poor state of preservation, and the presence of recent structures leaning against the remains of the building. A few aligned polygonal blocks can be seen, while the rest consists of a heap of jumbled blocks overlain by small stones.
descriptions.NUR3058: The nuraghe is completely invisible, partly because of the vegetation but mainly because its stone components have been dismantled and reused to build dry-stone structures nearby (also abandoned). This also makes it hard to locate.
descriptions.NUR2855: It is a complex nuraghe located on the hill known as Pettu 'e Murtas, from which it takes its name. Nearby are the remains of some huts, all of Nuragic age.
descriptions.NUR3743: Single-tower nuraghe today destroyed by agricultural mechanization
descriptions.NUR11146: Single-tower nuraghe greatly modified by agricultural mechanization in the 1950s.
descriptions.NUR3409: Collapsed single-tower nuraghe. Some people mistakenly call the nearby Molafà nuraghe "Piandanna".
descriptions.NUR1575:
Single-tower nuraghe, preserves almost intact the tholos roof of the chamber.

It is one of the few nuraghes equipped with a mezzanine or mezzanine floor on the entrance corridor.
descriptions.NUR3558: Enormous single-tower nuraghe, not accessible, built on a rocky ridge; walls up to 4 metres high remain above ground. Reached on foot via the road to the Forestry Service lookout. One of the highest points in the area, it commands a beautiful view.
descriptions.NUR15926: The nuraghe is located on the summit of a high hill, from which the view perfectly extends over the area of S'Adde 'e S'Ulumu,
descriptions.NUR5516: The nuraghe takes its name from “pibiri”/pepper. The monument and the surrounding area were investigated scientifically in the early 2000s. The main body, built of limestone, consists of a central tower and at least two additional towers linked by straight curtain walls. The spiral staircase is visible. The main body is enclosed within an outer wall made up of several towers connected by both straight and curved walls.
descriptions.NUR4377: Probably dismantled after the construction of the adjacent houses.
descriptions.NUR2578: The nuraghe stands about 400 metres north-west of Nuraghe Biriola, while 350 metres to the east there is a Roman cemetery, attested by about ten cinerary urns of different shapes cut into the outcropping rock. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a niche, a corridor staircase and a central chamber flanked by two niches. The tower, circular in plan, has its top missing at a maximum height of 5.80 m with 11 courses, while a large collapse has affected the perimeter wall facing north-north-west.
descriptions.NUR3543: It is undoubtedly the most imposing and best-preserved nuraghe in the Solarussa area. The layout is that of a tancato nuraghe, with a main tower and a secondary tower separated by a courtyard. The main tower is in good condition, with its tholos vault substantially intact. The secondary tower has partially collapsed, while the internal courtyard is blocked by the collapse debris.
descriptions.NUR3017: During the Nuragic period the area was densely inhabited due to its highly strategic location: near the lake stand numerous nuraghes, including one known as Sa Pigalva.
descriptions.NUR4873: Complex nuraghe of modest dimensions, apparently undisturbed as it is covered by vegetation. The central tower and other aligned curtain walls are clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR5261: As far as can be seen through the vegetation, it is a single-tower nuraghe with a curtain wall; I believe it is well preserved despite the collapsed tholos, though it still requires excavation and cleaning.
descriptions.NUR14825: The area preserved the settlement, which was brought to light in the early 1980s. The land was expropriated and archaeological investigations were started, uncovering a series of rooms for domestic use occupied at least until the early medieval period, the traces of a complex nuraghe, and what has been identified as a sacred well, still to be excavated.
descriptions.NUR3224: Nuraghe apparently single-tower. It could belong to the category of "uncompleted nuraghes".
descriptions.NUR1181: The nuraghe is a single-tower structure on two levels, elliptical in shape, which makes use of natural rock masses in which it is embedded. Due to poor conservation, its form is not clearly legible.
descriptions.NUR3910: Structures belonging to a single-tower tholos nuraghe of which three or four courses of the outer wall face survive to a maximum height of about 2.50 m. The inner chamber has collapsed and the collapse material fills it. Built with polygonal blocks of local basalt. No entrance can be identified. The structures are largely covered by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR20200: Disappeared from maps and censuses, it has reappeared thanks to the geological mining map drawn by engineer C. De Castro in 1889 and the drone survey carried out by the Assoc. Cult. Limen Sarrabus-Gerrei.
descriptions.NUR5379: A tower remains, its interior collapsed and inaccessible. A staircase appears to have been present. It is surrounded by an elliptical wall with a residual height of about 3 m and 7 courses.
descriptions.NUR6164: Located in the territory of Mara, what appears to be a large monolith visible from the SS292 just before the Bonuighinu junction is intriguing. The probably complex nuraghe is unfortunately almost completely swallowed by vegetation, but what strikes me is discovering that the monolith is what remains of a cyclopean outer wall shaped like a V.
descriptions.NUR5527: It is a complex nuraghe, consisting of a central tower and four attached towers that are not very prominent. The central tower is the only one in good condition, with two superimposed floors, the lower one intact and the upper one missing its tholos roof. On the upper floor there is a large window facing the entrance side.
descriptions.NUR12510: Single-tower tholos nuraghe, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The structures are almost completely covered by vegetation. The superimposed blocks of the southern side can be seen, surviving to a height of just over 2.50 m. The rest of the building cannot be observed because of poor visibility. Piles of collapsed blocks are visible on the small slope to the south of the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR4530: Single-tower nuraghe built of large blocks, situated on top of the hill. On the hill slopes there are tall wall structures of the same period. The site was used from the Bronze Age to the Roman period.
descriptions.NUR4060:
The monument has a fairly complex plan characterised by successive additions to the main body; the latter has an elliptical plan with a maximum diameter of 13.5 m and is provided with two entrances, to the north and south-west, which give access to two corridors that join at right angles at the centre of the central tower.

Two structures abut the central tower: one is on the north side, the other must have encircled at least two-thirds of the whole.
descriptions.NUR20415: In the centre of the village, research has shown "the existence of important portions of the Nuragic building still preserved around the water reservoir built on the site in the 1920s. Although the ancient building was used as a foundation for the modern one, the excavations have brought to light extensive portions of a tower displaying a massive fabric of polygonal basalt blocks".
descriptions.NUR1845: The monument lies about 200 metres north-east of the Nuraghe Figu and less than 350 metres south-west of the Nuraghe Bighinzone. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, a wall thickness of 4.00 m on the east side and 3.60 m on the west, and a height that varies from 3.05 m to the north-north-west, with six courses, to 1.75 m to the south-south-west with three or four courses. The masonry consists of polyhedral blocks laid in horizontal courses that are not always regular.
descriptions.NUR5934: Nuraghe belonging to the category of "uncompleted nuraghes", relatively common in this area.
descriptions.NUR3796:
Even though it is reduced to a major ruin, the importance of this feature can be grasped; it belongs to the group of nuraghi with an underground chamber, still accessible.

Literally "nuraghe of the cows' urine". See Pìsciu 'àccas.

Cf. MAURO MAXIA, I nomi di luogo dell'Anglona e della Bassa valle del Coghinas, ed. Il Torchietto, Ozieri 1994, pp. 73-74 for the entry "Anglona".
descriptions.NUR5068: Nuraghe Piscu, situated inside the municipal archaeological park since 1982, runs alongside the SS 128 towards Mandas. Piscu is the monument most representative of the Nuragic civilisation of the Trexenta.
descriptions.NUR2676: It retains the tholos intact except for a few upper courses.
descriptions.NUR1777: A row of subterranean wall face remains.
descriptions.NUR5482: Four-lobed nuraghe, largely covered by vegetation. The central tower is still accessible from above. It shows to be a much larger complex than it appears at first glance.
descriptions.NUR4909: Four-lobed, whose excavations have yielded many intact artefacts. The lifespan of the nuraghe appears to be very short.
descriptions.NUR15032: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure cannot be defined. Part of it lies beneath a public reservoir.
descriptions.NUR5754: The building stands in a strategic position on the limestone plateau of Sas Seas (482 m a.s.l.), from which it dominates the surrounding territory. The ground plan of the nuraghe cannot be clearly defined because of the collapses. Inside the structure part of a rectangular chamber survives that was probably originally roofed with a truncated ogive. The same roofing system has been hypothesised for the Fodde nuraghe at Bolotana.
descriptions.NUR4730: Almost completely destroyed. The presence of large stones along the sides of the small hilltop indicates the existence of a nuraghe. Dense vegetation covers what remains.
descriptions.NUR4365: Nuraghe completely destroyed. On the small hilltop, small stones are visible, covering together with earth what was once the nuraghe, which no longer exists.
descriptions.NUR3327: Remains of structures belonging to a single-tower tholos nuraghe. The building, now almost completely destroyed, consists of a few blocks from the basal course and part of what must have been the left jamb of the entrance, oriented to the south. The building material is local basalt. Nearby, heaps of stone material from the nuraghe's structures can be seen.
descriptions.NUR3857: The nuraghe remains isolated at the top of a rocky massif inside a large quarry.
descriptions.NUR4756: The site comprises a main tower, a sub-elliptical structure that must have served as the entrance, and remains of an outer wall all round the perimeter. The various rock outcrops complete the masonry and dictate the ground plan. The sub-elliptical structure, on the south side, probably formed the entrance to the complex and linked the interior rooms by a corridor, now blocked by collapse. A terrace can be made out in the north-western area.
descriptions.NUR6244: It is a complex building consisting of a main tower with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a chamber flanked by three niches arranged in a cross, plus an addition that is not easy to interpret typologically. The tower has a circular plan (diameter 11 m on the north-south axis) and survives to a maximum height of about 6.50 m.
descriptions.NUR5960: Single-tower nuraghe, preserves the tholos intact. The lintel above the entrance measures approximately 3.30 m x 0.90 m x 1.85 m, weighing about 16,000 kg.
descriptions.NUR5629: The nuraghe is a complex type, with a central tower at the centre of a four-lobed bastion with a straight-curved profile enclosing a vaguely rectangular open-air courtyard. The whole structure measures 22.00 x 20.00 m (W-E / N-S axis), while the maximum surviving height is 6.20 m to the south-west and the wall thicknesses are 6.40 m to the south-west and 2.80 m to the north. Of the towers, only the one to the east is detectable, accessible from the courtyard through a corridor with steps visible in the final stretch.
descriptions.NUR4659: Single-tower nuraghe, of which megaliths remain, regularly "arated" in which few cossi of the Late Bronze Age.
descriptions.NUR19694: Located at a short distance from Sa Unta and Sa Tumba, in the area of Sculta 'e Muru, it appears as a heap of stones in complete disuse.
descriptions.NUR5916:
A corridor nuraghe with an elliptical plan, built in polygonal technique with red trachyte boulders.

The short southern side survives to a height of about 3 m and contains the entrance, topped by a granite lintel, which gives access to a small sub-circular chamber that led to a second room through another entrance with a granite lintel.
descriptions.NUR3727: June 2021, report. The foundation has collapsed and the stones have been propped up with iron rods; if you enlarge the image, the rods can be seen.
descriptions.NUR14700: It is a nuraghe left incomplete, notable for the size of the lintel above the entrance.
descriptions.NUR5805: Buried nuraghe, whose layout is difficult to determine. It was certainly a complex and multi-lobed structure. The name suggests its probable function as a watchpost at an embarkation point during the Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR4019: There is no trace of the nuraghe remaining, apart from a large amount of rubble from the collapse, hidden by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR5320:
Nuraghe situated on the double and secure landing at Porto Pirastru.

Currently, only the walls and a concrete foundation of a recent installation remain.
descriptions.NUR14527: The highest part of the Posada crag was occupied by a corridor nuraghe, and on its south-eastern slopes, at a noticeably lower level, a village also stood, probably arranged on terraced levels. The village began about 90 m in a straight line from the nuraghe and extended from an altitude of about 42 m down to about 25 m above sea level, over a difference in level of around 17 metres. (Sanciu 2010)
descriptions.NUR873: The site consists of a three-lobed nuraghe, still mostly buried, and of structures probably dating to the Roman period.
descriptions.NUR3928: Probable location. Today only the basic megalithic structures of the nuraghe remain, and it is quite conceivable that most of the stones that once stood above them ended up, duly broken up, in the walls of the Villa La Favorita.
descriptions.NUR5313: Single-tower nuraghe in good condition, with entrance and tholos partly buried but relatively intact.
descriptions.NUR6018:
Complex tholos nuraghe, of the tancato type, with a central tower, a small courtyard and a secondary tower. The complex is built of polygonal blocks of local basalt, but is distinguished by the extremely careful working of the entrance blocks (jambs and lintels).

The central tower has a maximum surviving height of about 4 m, while the added tower has largely collapsed and survives to a maximum height of just over 3 m.
descriptions.NUR2872: Only a few large boulders that formed the basal course remain of the monument, which is largely covered by a farm track built over it; from these it can be deduced that the ground plan was circular.
descriptions.NUR3913: Structures belonging to a complex nuraghe of the tancato type with a main tower and a secondary tower linked to the first by a small courtyard. The nuraghe is built of polygonal basalt blocks. The secondary tower, to the south of the main one, is covered by vegetation and survives to a height of 3–4 courses. It is not possible to locate the entrances or enter the complex because of the collapses and the dense vegetation growing on the ruins.
descriptions.NUR3837: It is a simple tholos nuraghe whose outer plan is not visible because it is completely buried. The course of the corridor (max. length 3.40 m) and the sub-circular shape of the chamber with a niche on the left side can be made out. The building is constructed with courses of granite blocks that become progressively smaller towards the higher courses.
descriptions.NUR4479:
A nuraghe in the territory of Ulassai, in the province of Ogliastra, is the second largest after the nuraghe s'Ulimu in the same municipality. It belongs to the complex in the "Neuletta" area, where besides it there are two other nuraghi and a small megalithic village, called Nuragheddos in the local Sardinian.

The nuraghe was built in the period between the Middle Bronze Age and the Final Bronze Age, therefore around 1400–900 BC.
descriptions.NUR2942: Diroccated nuraghe, it is distinguished by its proximity to several other Nuragic megalithic monuments.
descriptions.NUR1882: The nuraghe is completely ruined, reduced to a heap of blocks about two metres high.
descriptions.NUR4943: Nuraghe in basalt blocks. Unfortunately, the high residual volume is not properly exploited and the site is neither legible nor accessible, also due to dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR786: Only small portions of the wall of the nuraghe remain. The collapse makes it impossible to read the plan.
descriptions.NUR5614: Of the nuraghe, which is in very poor condition, only a few large trachyte boulders remain; they formed the basal course and today barely convey the idea of the circular ground plan.
descriptions.NUR3891: Single-tower nuraghe. Only the first three or four basal courses, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt, are legible on the side facing west. The structures are covered by dense vegetation and can be seen only from the farm track that runs alongside them.
descriptions.NUR2536: At first sight a single-tower nuraghe, in reality a complex one with buried structures covered by vegetation. The original tower preserves its entire perimeter circuit. On the SE side there is perhaps a raised entrance. The interior of the tower is blocked by boulders and earth. To the SE an obvious attempt at illicit excavation has exposed the outer wall face of the tower. To the S and SW circular curtain walls can be seen that may belong to two further towers.
descriptions.NUR3569: Nuraghe in poor state of conservation.
descriptions.NUR2189: Single-tower nuraghe with its top missing, of which only the imposing portal remains.
descriptions.NUR2190:
It is located in the municipality of Bolotana.

Single-tower nuraghe with a chamber.

The nuraghe is cut by a recent wall.

The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR2769: Ruined, in poor condition, covered by vegetation and partly buried, it remains interesting for its position right against the coastal cliff. Some internal chambers are visible but cannot be entered. It is certainly a single-tower nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5944: Single-tower nuraghe. The entrance is completely blocked by collapse debris; the inner chamber is visible from the top of its summit. It stands on a hill covered with wild olives near the springs of S'ena Ruia.
descriptions.NUR5169: A proto-nuraghe later remodelled into a nuraghe. On the highest hills of Serrenti, overlooking the valleys that lead to the Trexenta, stand the simple proto-nuraghi of Monti de su Marchesu, Monti Acutzu, Monti Ibera and Monti Proceddu.
descriptions.NUR5961: Single-tower in excellent condition, with walls 8/9 metres thick, internally inaccessible, with ancient oak trees surrounding it. It offers a magnificent view down to Gallura.
descriptions.NUR3278: It stands on a rise, in a panoramic spot overlooking much of the Ogliastra territory. Of the structure, which is in poor condition, only a few courses of limestone blocks are legible.
descriptions.NUR4067: Located in the Su Fonnesu area (Teulada), at about 300 metres above sea level. It stands on a sharp peak, locally called "punta acuccia", which from a distance looks very much like a pyramid. The stones used are predominantly granite. The view is excellent, especially over the Gulf of Palmas.
descriptions.NUR2163: Single-tower nuraghe, completely ruined; the opening of an intra-mural staircase that led to the lower floor can still be seen, now filled with collapse debris. A breach in the wall towards the outside, to the east, is also visible, where a large window may have opened.
descriptions.NUR16090: Damaged nuraghe, of which only a few courses of the wall face remain
descriptions.NUR2502: A semi-destroyed nuraghe, surmounted by a fire lookout post, with few visible remains. Excellent panorama ranging from the nuraghe Seruci to the large beach of Porto Paglia/Punta S'Arena/Plag'e Mesu/Fontanamare as far as Pan di Zucchero.
descriptions.NUR8432: The nuraghe survives to a height of about two metres, has an internal diameter of about 7 metres, and a single opening facing north-east that overlooks the approach to the upper end of the valley and the small plateau on which the San Giacomo giants' tomb stands.
descriptions.NUR8634: Small atypical single-tower nuraghe, belonging to the Appiu village context. It stands at the end of a path that leads from the village to the Giants' Tomb, two small dolmens, and finally this small nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR17302: On the summit of the hill lie the ruins of a small nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR19710: It appears as the most imposing monument preserved in the area. That it was a complex structure is almost certain, given the massiveness of the masonry which stands out compared to other monuments; inside the chamber a niche is still visible, positioned to the north-west, and slightly offset to the west a small access space can be seen that seems to belong to a staircase.
descriptions.NUR11633: Largely buried but recognisable. Currently being recovered by the Superintendency for Archaeological Heritage, funded by the Porto Rotondo Consortium. The so-called Nuraghe, after archaeological excavation, turned out to be a Punic coastal watchtower (4th century BC).
descriptions.NUR10880: This is a complex nuraghe over which the buildings of the Boggio anti-ship battery were superimposed during the Second World War. The wall face of the probable central tower is clearly visible from the outside.
descriptions.NUR2524: Remains of a complex nuraghe built in basalt.
descriptions.NUR8266: A single-tower nuraghe overlooking the Rio Santu Milanu valley in an area reused in the medieval period.
descriptions.NUR2752: Of the nuraghe only a few courses remain, barely visible from the area of the subterranean sanctuaries below. The nuraghe rises above a calcareous spur from which it commands the surrounding valleys.
descriptions.NUR3323: The nuraghe was in close topographic and cultural connection with the giants' tombs of Biristeddi, located about 250 metres away.
descriptions.NUR3478:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan (diam. 12.50 m) and an entrance facing south-east; the tower survives to a maximum height of 4.80 m on the south-east side, with six courses, while the minimum height is on the north-west side at 2 metres with three courses. The masonry consists of carefully worked blocks laid in regular horizontal courses.

In the surrounding area the circular structures of numerous huts from the Nuragic settlement are clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR9484:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan (diam. 13.30 x 13 m): the wall thickness is about 4 metres, while the surviving height is 1.75 m with three courses.

The entrance, facing south-east, leads into a corridor (length 4 m – width 1.50/1 m) in which the existence of the stair and the opposing guard chamber can be discerned.

Of the circular chamber only the base diameter (5 m) can be measured, while it is not possible to determine whether it was lined with niches.
descriptions.NUR6331: Irregular-plan complex nuraghe. Its perimeter wall face encloses a single expanse of collapse debris, from which remains of the central tower emerge to the west. The complex is enclosed by a megalithic outer wall that protects it on the west and, in part, on the north.
descriptions.NUR3620: Probable nuraghe tower, of which only the lintel of the entrance and the rubble heap remain.
descriptions.NUR14332: Nuraghe located within the urban centre, single-tower, partially collapsed
descriptions.NUR3787: Complex nuraghe. Access to the upper level via a staircase passing beneath the SE tower.
descriptions.NUR2561: Complex nuraghe, never studied, located within a private property, surrounded by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR640: The nuraghe stands on a small hill where some wall structures of uncertain origin are also visible, some of which run into a dry-stone wall of more recent construction. The nuraghe's structure cannot be determined, given its very poor state of preservation; it may be a single-tower nuraghe built of trachyte.
descriptions.NUR15898: The site is hard to locate because of the Mediterranean scrub. On the slope along the road there is a substantial scatter of pottery, probably Roman. Traces of collapse are visible around the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR4353: A tholos nuraghe whose north tower is clearly visible. The south tower has collapsed on the seaward side. An artificial entrance dug by curiosity-seekers is present.
descriptions.NUR2830: It is fairly well known to the local population because the lintel of the main entrance draws attention for being made of white limestone, probably from the Giombachis or Iscala Ilvena area. Here too one must speak of an advanced state of decay owing to the many collapses that the cyclopean monument has suffered. Some constructional and architectural details are nevertheless still evident.
descriptions.NUR3867: Archaic corridor nuraghe. The building stands on a valley floor just 4 m from the watercourse called Riu e'Sa Tanca, on its eastern bank. It is completely covered by vegetation, in particular dense bramble thickets growing abundantly along the stream banks make observation difficult. Some large polygonal basalt blocks laid one on another can be seen on the north and east sides.
descriptions.NUR3902:
The complex stands on the summit of Monte Colbu overlooking the plain of Olbia.

The nuraghe, surrounded by a wall that originally must have exceeded 5 metres in height and has two entrances (one to the north and one to the south), is a single-tower type. The entrance corridor contains a small niche and part of the stairwell that led to the terrace of the upper floor. The central chamber, which has a small well, was covered by a tholos.
descriptions.NUR5749: Complex nuraghe belonging to a much larger settlement, which has never been the subject of archaeological excavations.
descriptions.NUR8431: Situated on the side of the ravine of the same name where the stream of the same name flows during the rains, it originally stood on an isolated spur in a raised position above the valley below. Some courses of medium-large blocks are present. A few metres further downstream large quantities of collapse are visible; the structure is now almost completely destroyed.
descriptions.NUR1930: Single-tower nuraghe, with traces of a settlement. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR3925: Single-tower nuraghe consisting of a chamber with an intact tholos roof and an internal staircase connecting the various levels that form the complex structure.
descriptions.NUR2912:
It is a nuraghe that is hard to classify typologically because of the collapse and the dense shrubby vegetation covering it.

The masonry consists of medium-sized stones laid in regular horizontal courses. The few features observed do not help to understand the ground plan of this structure, which excavation might reveal to be a proto-nuraghe rather than a classic tholos nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR6417:
Four-lobed nuraghe.

In the vicinity there are also two giants' tombs and a nuragic temple with a sacred well.
descriptions.NUR2999: It lies within the municipal territory of Pozzomaggiore (SS). It is a large proto-nuraghe, almost completely destroyed. There is an entrance covered in scrub and a corridor about 10 metres long with a height of 2 metres. In the upper part an entrance is still visible. Numerous boulders lie all around.
descriptions.NUR5662: Nuraghe partially collapsed with intact tholos
descriptions.NUR2961: The monument is a single-tower nuraghe built of medium and large blocks laid in regular courses. The nuraghe is not in a good state of preservation. The south-east entrance, which has collapsed, leads into a corridor whose left wall shows the access to the stair (also collapsed). The chamber is circular in plan and survives to a maximum height of 9 m.
descriptions.NUR3635: It is a single-tower nuraghe standing on a cliff that overlooks the whole area of the Tirso river below the village of Villanova Truscheddu. The tholos has collapsed inwards and the nuraghe is not maintained and has never been investigated.
descriptions.NUR16343: Giovanni Lilliu defines the Nuraghe Ruinas as the highest in Sardinia. At an altitude of 1205 metres, above the nuraghe there is a wonderful panoramic view over the surrounding territory and the ruins of the numerous circular huts that surround it (at least 200).
descriptions.NUR4648: Ruina Tassa is a single-tower nuraghe. Like Luas and Friorosu, it stands on a limestone base. The whole area shows an unusual abundance of squared stones, used in enclosures, suggesting the existence in ancient times of a village of considerable size.
descriptions.NUR5737: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The nuraghe, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt, has largely collapsed on the south-east side, while it is still in good condition to the north and south-west. The entrance was probably to the south but is no longer visible.
descriptions.NUR5706: The Ruiu in question is an abandoned single-tower nuraghe completely overgrown with vegetation, but we still managed to force our way through the scrub to get inside. The tholos is not intact and unfortunately the vegetation has taken over.
descriptions.NUR6061: The ground level should have the tholos intact.
descriptions.NUR5734: It is one of the many nuraghi scattered across the territory of Torralba; this one lies near the railway that runs from Mores to Torralba station. It is a complex nuraghe, consisting of a central tower with a frontal addition of two secondary towers linked by a solid wall face. It is dated to the period between the Middle and Final Bronze Age (1600–1000 BC).
descriptions.NUR3533: Nuraghe along the road. Partly collapsed. The tholos is open and essentially visible in section, showing its constructional features.
descriptions.NUR3703: It is a single-tower nuraghe with the characteristic shape of a truncated cone and two superimposed chambers…. Access is through the central doorway facing south-south-east; it has a central chamber with corbelled courses closing the dome, and three side cells arranged orthogonally (90°) to the entrance. A clockwise spiral staircase leads up onto the nuraghe directly above the central chamber, where the superstructure of the second chamber is still clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR14208:
The nuraghe is a single-tower tholos nuraghe, built of roughly dressed trachyte stones, with a circular base 12 metres in external diameter, a surviving height of about 6 metres, and walls sloping at 7 to 11 degrees.

The entrance, oriented to the south-east as in most nuraghi, is topped by a lintel made of two separate blocks and leads into the corridor, roofed with transverse slabs.
descriptions.NUR4170:
More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe.

Attached to the nuraghe, a boundary wall was built for a villa.
descriptions.NUR6292: Nuraghe with a system of outer walls surrounding it, visible from the adjacent path.
descriptions.NUR3944: It is a complex nuraghe that was demolished to make way for the Roman settlement.
descriptions.NUR5935: The nuraghe Abba Noa stands on a granite spur at an altitude of 178 m and has the particularity of being built in mixed masonry: both local granite and basalt from the surrounding hills were used in its construction. The complex plan consists of two diametrically opposed towers joined by a bastion, straight on the west side and curvilinear on the east, running along the edge of the summit.
descriptions.NUR1255: Location according to ancient maps of this nuraghe, of which today only scattered stones remain.
descriptions.NUR538: Single-tower nuraghe and settlement (Santu Sadurru). The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR539: A ruined single-tower nuraghe, not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR1864: Complex nuraghe of which the central tower and a bastion, perhaps three-lobed, survive. The original tower retains almost its entire outline. The interior of the tower is filled with collapse and vegetation. To the NNE there is a curving wall that reaches its maximum height to the ENE, where five courses survive; it may be a tower. To the W–SW a wall can be made out, probably belonging to a lateral tower. A further tower was probably located to the SE. Ceramic fragments are present, attributable from the Nuragic period to the medieval period.
descriptions.NUR6413: Built on a slight basalt outcrop less than 200 metres south of the Riu Corte, the monument is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, now largely demolished around its outer perimeter. Because of the collapse, the construction details of the corridor and the chamber cannot be made out.
descriptions.NUR3559: Four-lobed, topless nuraghe, partially buried, shows the lintel, which stands out for its considerable size.
descriptions.NUR1896: One of the six coastal nuraghi on the island of Sant'Antioco — a single-tower nuraghe with an adjoining probable hut or other room — stands on the rocky outcrop of the same name, in a strategic position in the cove “Su Portu de su Casu”. A few courses of the original tower and a short stretch of walling to the east of it survive. The line of the inner face of the chamber can no longer be traced, as its interior is completely covered by vegetation and collapse.
descriptions.NUR3544:
The nuraghe is a single-tower nuraghe with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a chamber flanked by two opposing niches. The external ground plan is not fully definable because of collapses and dense shrub vegetation.

The tower, about 12 metres in diameter, survives to a maximum height of 5.30 m (8 courses).

The masonry consists of basalt blocks, medium and large, roughly dressed with some care and laid in regular horizontal courses.
descriptions.NUR18107:
The nuraghe stands on the northern edge of a modest trachyte plateau, from which it overlooks the whole valley below. Not far from it lie the Runara dolmen and the Pittigheddu nuraghe.

The nuraghe is in very poor condition, having been used as a stone quarry to build several enclosures that stand right up against the building, making it extremely difficult to follow the plan of the ancient structure.
descriptions.NUR2725: It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe in good condition with the interior still intact. Surrounding it, traces of a settlement are visible.
descriptions.NUR827: The construction is atypical and hard to classify: it is not a nuraghe, yet it is difficult to call it a hut. Traces of later human intervention from various historical periods can be found, and these have certainly altered the original structure, creating the difficulty of classification.
descriptions.NUR4803: The complex corridor nuraghe Sa Conca ‛e sa Cresia originated as a corridor nuraghe in the Middle Bronze Age and was remodelled into a tholos nuraghe in the Recent Bronze Age. The surrounding areas were landscaped in the 1990s. From the tholos one enters corridors dug by tomb robbers that lead inside the tholoi. Outside, to the west and south, two elliptical vaulted structures, now ruined and of uncertain purpose, are reported.
descriptions.NUR4551: Proto-nuraghe of circular or sub-circular form
descriptions.NUR3318: It stands on the summit of the mountain of the same name.
