Hard to reach by climbing the slopes from the village of Bottidda below, it is more easily reached from the nearby road to Foresta Burgos. From its ruins one can admire the view over the valley below, known as "Su Campu".
descriptions.NUR16533: A complex structure, almost entirely buried. The nuraghe is enveloped in dense vegetation and, moreover, a fence has been installed on its summit that prevents the eastern part from being seen.
descriptions.NUR4578: Mixed nuraghe, of which only little remains, partly covered by vegetation. Possibly enlarged and restored.
descriptions.NUR536: Almost hidden by the dense undergrowth of shrubs.
descriptions.NUR5506: Complex nuraghe, partially collapsed and surrounded by vegetation. The tholos is intact, surrounded by a significant outer wall.
descriptions.NUR19521: Nuraghe on the SSW slope of Monte Arbus, on the hillside facing the S'Acqua sa Canna area. Complex nuraghe with a three-lobed bastion and an internal courtyard. The towers of which traces remain are positioned to the N, SSE and SSW. Because of the collapses and the vegetation it is difficult to make out the outline of the walls clearly. By contrast the outline of the courtyard is well defined; at first glance it appears pentagonal; in some stretches up to three rows of boulders of various shapes and sizes survive.
descriptions.NUR2763: Single-tower nuraghe; located inside a military area. The tholos survives intact. The site is now accessible (it is still advisable to ask for "authorisation" at the "Bechi Luserna" Barracks).
descriptions.NUR15026: Complex nuraghe, partially eroded and buried, for which it is not possible to define the structure.
descriptions.NUR12457: Circular single-tower nuraghe with the entrance to the south topped by a lintel stone. The central chamber, oblong, is distinguished by the unusual presence of four niches: one on the left side, one at the back opposite the entrance, and two (as a pair) on the right side. All have a semi-elliptical plan; the section is trapezoidal, like that of the entrance passage. The cone survives to an external height of about 3 m.
descriptions.NUR3920: Structures belonging to a nuraghe, presumably of the archaic, corridor type. The monument lies inside a private courtyard on the northern outskirts of the present-day village of Bonarcado. Four or five courses of polygonal basalt blocks can still be seen among recent structures of small blocks and cement that lean against the nuraghe. The building technique of the few visible remains would suggest the nuraghe's antiquity.
descriptions.NUR2765: Single-tower nuraghe at Sa Cordiola. The outer walls are well preserved, but the interior has collapsed. It has the unusual feature of a double name: the first is "Sa Cordiola", the second is "Giustalassa", the name of the neighbouring locality.
descriptions.NUR5955:
Single-tower, single-chambered. With its top missing, the chamber completely filled with collapse debris. The south-east side of its outer wall face, where the entrance opened, has completely slipped away. The highest surviving part of the monument reaches three metres in height and consists of six courses of roughly dressed boulders.

The well-finished entrance lintel lies isolated on the ground a short distance away.
descriptions.NUR1279: The nuraghe is located at the end of a valley on a small rocky spur.
descriptions.NUR4917: Mighty and fascinating even under a grey winter sky, the Nuraghe Sa Dom 'e S'Orcu rises from a massive rocky outcrop amid a superb landscape, with broad views over the whole of the Parteolla as far as the Gulf of Cagliari and the Iglesiente mountains. It dates to the 2nd millennium BC and is the principal monument in the territory of Dolianova, where numerous other prehistoric remains are present.
descriptions.NUR4802: The Nuragic fortification consists of a tholos tower enclosed in a courtyard which in turn is protected by an outer wall provided with five further towers. The entrance lies to the south and leads into a small courtyard where several rooms are found that were used for metal smelting, as shown by the bronze-smelting waste discovered all around. The central tower has an elliptical plan; inside, on the right, a stairway branches off leading to the upper floor.
descriptions.NUR3711: Situated in the valley of the Rio Siniscola, a short distance from the river mouth, it has a rectangular plan with an internal elliptical chamber, survives to a height of about 2 metres, and is built of white limestone with schist inserts.
descriptions.NUR1262: Remains of the nuraghe Sa Domo Ezza
descriptions.NUR8463:
This nuraghe has unique features, such as the three different helical staircases that led from the ground up to the upper levels.

Today, very little of what once stood remains. The height of the central tower and the massive scale of the building can be inferred from the diameter of the tower, the imposing size of the ashlars, and the extent of the whole footprint of the main structure.

In this case, too, a village of considerable size must have developed around it.
descriptions.NUR19665:
The nuraghe is very large and I believe it has more than one tower.

It has suffered many collapses; an aerial photograph taken with a drone would be appropriate.

From the nuraghe there is a broad view over the whole surrounding territory as far as the sea.
descriptions.NUR3786: Remains of a nuraghe, possibly never completed
descriptions.NUR3356: A short distance from the megalithic circle are the basal remains of a simple circular nuraghe of the advanced Nuragic period, and a little further downhill the Ochila domus de janas, some of them richly decorated with symbolic and architectural elements in relief. The megalithic enclosure consists of ten (plus an eleventh lying overturned in the centre of the area) irregularly parallelepiped megaliths set side by side, forming a semicircle 9–10 metres in diameter.
descriptions.NUR4870: It is a singular corridor nuraghe, complex and irregular, composed of three large megalithic bodies set side by side and various secondary structures. It has a surviving height of over 6 metres and was built on the outcropping rock with polyhedral basalt blocks laid dry in polygonal masonry. The nuraghe can be dated, in its first construction phase, to the Early Middle Bronze Age.
descriptions.NUR5355: The imposing single-tower nuraghe Sa Fraigada stands a few dozen metres from the summit of Monte Cresia and is the largest in the area. The ancient Nuragic building has suffered major collapses, making its ground plan hard to understand; the lintelled entrance, presumably on the east side, is not visible. The circular tower is about 8 metres in diameter and can still be seen to a surviving height of 3.70 metres on its south-western side.
descriptions.NUR10494:
The nuraghe is a complex type, consisting of a central tower against whose front a bastion with two secondary towers enclosing a central courtyard has been added – with a complete refacing of the structure.

The main tower (diam. 18.00 m) has an entrance oriented to the SE (width 0.80–1.20 m) surmounted by a lintel with a relieving window.
descriptions.NUR5073: Single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical plan. Several courses are visible. In the area there are large lumps of clay and other wall structures that suggest the existence of a settlement of huts.
descriptions.NUR19526: The area where the nuraghe is thought to have stood has been completely altered, I would say devastated, during the Second World War, when the probable structures belonging to the monument and to the village of the same name were dismantled and adapted for a military position.
descriptions.NUR4575:
The construction is extensive and complex. The area outlined in red is the highest and is well enclosed by typically Nuragic walls up to two and a half metres thick.

All around, however, the existence of other walls can be discerned; they defined a much larger surface, with terraces stepping down towards the impluvium to the north.

The building dominated the valley, now completely built over, which takes its name from the little church of Santa Barbara.
descriptions.NUR20346: It is located above the Church of Santa Lucia. Only little remains visible, particularly a wall of the tower (I believe it is a single-tower nuraghe) on the northern side and some varied courses.
descriptions.NUR8369: It is a complex structure built of squared limestone blocks, in which an inner chamber is clearly visible; its archaeological deposit has been disturbed by looters. Inside, three niches with ogival vaulted roofs are clearly visible, as is the entrance, positioned to the south-east; to the right of it a short blind corridor can be seen, in front of which a small niche opens.
descriptions.NUR5502: Complex nuraghe visible seasonally depending on the water levels in the Cuga basin. A considerable village once surrounded the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR2858: Near provincial road 25 to Aidomaggiore stands the tancato nuraghe called “Sa Jua”, shown here in the fine photographs of Nicola Castangia. Professor Pittau derives its name from the Latin “iuga”, meaning a herd of cattle. I would point out that in ancient Egypt cattle were also called “iwa” (jua), plainly similar to the term “ju” or “juale” used in Sardinian for the yoke.
descriptions.NUR2555: Complex nuraghe with a main tower and two additional towers with a courtyard, built of limestone. Traces of a settlement.
descriptions.NUR4136: Given its commanding position over the surrounding countryside, it is thought to have been a very important and complex nuraghe. Unfortunately, only two curved stretches of wall are now visible, one to the north and the other to the south. Many basalt lava querns have been found nearby.
descriptions.NUR3647: Complex nuraghe; the central tower is visible, and inside it there are three niches. It has been heavily disturbed by agricultural mechanisation and the incessant activity of tomb robbers. An extensive village was attached to it, reaching as far as the giants' tomb of Sa Pedra Longa.
descriptions.NUR4509: Small complex nuraghe, not otherwise definable
descriptions.NUR3328: Damaged nuraghe, of which three courses and the entrance portal remain.
descriptions.NUR6255: Damaged nuraghe, of which only a few courses remain
descriptions.NUR2504: Single-tower nuraghe, built with calcareous stones, of which only one to two courses of stones of the external wall face remain.
descriptions.NUR3680: Single-tower nuraghe partially collapsed. Most of the walling remains on one side.
descriptions.NUR3528: The village consists of several well-built huts equipped with basins, drainage channels and ovens. Some scholars think these huts were cult rooms, others that they were part of a residential village.
descriptions.NUR1383: The Nuraghe Sa mandra e sa Giua no longer exists; it has been levelled, and its ashlars were used to build dry walls and the Roman settlement.
descriptions.NUR5911:
The archaeological complex "Sa Mandra de sa Jua" – literally "enclosure of the yoked oxen", which in a broader sense indicates fertile land – occupies a modest rise overlooking the Rio Mannu di Ozieri.

The multi-layered site was occupied continuously until the Middle Ages and has been incorporated since the 1960s into the San Nicola district, which lies about 4 kilometres from the town of Ozieri.

The Monument
descriptions.NUR3398: Composite nuraghe. At present it is impossible to read its plan because the whole site has been churned up by mechanical diggers, even though until a few years ago it was possible to go inside by lowering oneself from above. One thus entered a long corridor with corbelled walls; a further bulldozer operation has probably piled more material against the nuraghe and blocked the entrance. The hope is that the burial has protected it from this devastation.
descriptions.NUR3849:
Possible single-tower nuraghe; the doubt arises from its small size, but it could be a small nuraghe placed on a height with the sole role of a lookout.

Near the structure there are two tombs, perhaps of Roman date, built of limestone slabs; inside, two skulls and other human bones can be seen.
descriptions.NUR9274: Single-tower nuraghe of large trachyte and limestone blocks; the monument retains its intact tholos. Inside are three niches arranged in a cross; the tholos is about 5 metres high. Beside the nuraghe the Nuragic well is still present and is still used today by the landowners.
descriptions.NUR15145:
A buried Nuragic building, partly hidden by Second World War anti-aircraft positions. Between south-west and east there are traces of the Bronze Age village.

Chronology: Nuragic Bronze Age (for the nuraghe and the village); contemporary period (about 1942-43: for the military position).
descriptions.NUR6308: The Nuraghe Murartu or Sa Menta lies in the territory of Silanus, about 2.2 km from the village. It is almost completely hidden by vegetation. Of complex type, part of the central tower emerges for a height of 2 metres.
descriptions.NUR5571: It has the characteristic of being built with both limestone and trachyte stones, like the nearby nuraghe Corvos; however, whereas the latter shows a clear separation between the part built of limestone and that of trachyte, in the nuraghe Sa Menta stones of different nature are mixed in the wall face without any criterion.
descriptions.NUR3885: A few blocks of the basal perimeter in white limestone. The entrance is visible and little else, all within a dense thicket of fetid anagyris (sa giolva). The name should derive from the place-name of the land. Hill of the liburni, a shrubby legume known for its hanging pods and the unpleasant odour given off by its leaves when touched. Shepherds believe that the leaves of this plant give a bitter taste to goats' milk. See Nuraghe sas giòlvas. mu
descriptions.NUR5508: In total state of ruin, it is named after the toponym of the land or the owner of the land itself. mu
descriptions.NUR3207: Complex nuraghe consisting of a tower with an additional body, built in trachyte.
descriptions.NUR1605: Complex nuraghe heavily collapsed, making it difficult to determine its original form.
descriptions.NUR3939: The nuraghe Sa Murallia takes its name from a massive wall leaning against the original structures on the downhill side; it is largely hidden by deposits, layers and structures that have been built up against or over it over the centuries. In the same period and in later phases, the first settlements sprang up beside these nuraghi, sometimes enclosed by imposing oval or circular walls that are still partly visible today (Tradori, Araganzola, Maganzosa). (from the Narbolia municipal website)
descriptions.NUR5646: It lies on the boundary between the municipal territories of Nuoro and Orani, south of the main town. The transformation of the land does not allow a certain identification of the rest of the settlement, of which there is nevertheless a record.
descriptions.NUR3413: Single-tower nuraghe forming part of the complex of nuraghi at the locality Su Padru.
descriptions.NUR3798: The nuraghe stands on a small hill beside the church of the same name (17th century). It is in fair condition, rising to about 4 metres, with a south-facing entrance that is partly blocked. Inside, two pointed-arch niches can be seen. Single-tower nuraghe built of basalt blocks.
descriptions.NUR2943:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a guard niche, a probable stairwell, and a chamber with three niches arranged in a cross.

The tower, circular in plan (diam. 12.70 m), survives to a maximum height of 5 m on the west side, with 7 courses, while the minimum height is about 2 metres in the section affected by the entrance, to the south-east, which has completely collapsed. The masonry consists of roughly dressed trachyte blocks laid in horizontal courses with numerous packing wedges.
descriptions.NUR3335: Inaccessible with the tholos collapsed inward.
descriptions.NUR3983: A central tower surrounded by a wall emerges for up to four courses, to a height of over 2 metres. The whole is in turn linked to circular and straight walls that emerge from the ground but only for the upper base of the ashlars of the top course. Most of the nuragic complex is buried under earth. About 7–8 metres to the north-east of the tower there may be a sacred well.
descriptions.NUR13682: The Nuraghe Santu Juanni or San Giovanni lies about 1 km north of Villaurbana in the territory of Siamanna. It is a single-tower nuraghe built of roughly dressed basalt blocks. The entrance corridor is lintelled and leads to a chamber where the tholos is still intact. The upper floor, now collapsed, is overgrown with shrubs and prickly pears.
descriptions.NUR4233: It is a tower with a circular outer perimeter, a maximum diameter of about 10 m, and an internal chamber that is approximately elliptical, as far as can be judged from its present state of preservation. The whole northern sector is badly damaged, and the east and west sides have been affected by illicit excavations that caused further gaps in the perimeter, later patched by an attempt to “restore” the masonry in the eastern quadrant carried out by the Sisters of the Good Shepherd.
descriptions.NUR3370:
The monument consists of a central tower against which, on the north-western side, a second ruined tower leans.

The main tower, built of basalt blocks of various sizes, survives to a maximum height of about 8 metres. An internal staircase leads to the upper level. An extensive village, indicated on the surface by stone rubble and numerous ceramic finds, extended around the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR895: San Leonardo is an old Gallurese village that grew up near the church of the same name, a typical Gallurese country church flanked by a small cemetery. The remains of the San Leonardo nuraghe show that the site was also inhabited in the Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR3948: Nuraghe partially enclosed by the walls of the small church dedicated to San Lorenzo, on the north-east side of the structure (the side facing the village), some remains of the S. Lorenzo nuraghe are still visible.
descriptions.NUR4200:
The Santu Scioni, San Lussorio nuraghe stands in the countryside of Pabillonis, on a hillock from which much of the Campidano plain can be seen towards Monte Linas and above a bend of the Flumini Mannu.

Originally it must have consisted of a central tower and a series of other towers that are now by no means easy to identify, since all the wall structures have been levelled and covered by human activity around the sacredness that the site still retains today.
descriptions.NUR19523: Destroyed nuraghe, of which only a small amount remains
descriptions.NUR3352: Of the nuraghe only the foundation remains.
descriptions.NUR13469: Built of basalt blocks, the construction has a trilobate layout, with a central tower and three secondary towers arranged around a sickle-shaped courtyard. The structure was surrounded by a massive outer wall – clear traces of which survive – composed of five towers and straight curtain walls, except on the north side, which was naturally protected by the Giara ridges.
descriptions.NUR4178: At the site of 'su pranu', a complex nuraghe in poor state of conservation, hidden and almost inaccessible to visitors. Nearby, the remains of a village are clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR4729:
Partially brought to light in December 2002, the Sanna nuraghe takes its name from the furriadroxiu of the same name that stands at its feet in the countryside between Santadi and Piscinas. The excavations allowed the Superintendency staff to discover a Nuragic complex, until then forgotten, and to find it in an excellent state of preservation and in a dominant position over the surrounding territory.

Today it is almost abandoned and damaged by the very excavations.
descriptions.NUR5446: The nuraghe has been destroyed, only some traces of the wall face remain observed in different areas of the hillside.
descriptions.NUR4259: The San Nicola nuraghe is considered the oldest in the entire area, dating back to 1600 BC. The nuraghe awaits further study and is still buried up to its summit.
descriptions.NUR4072: All that remains of the nuraghe are some courses arranged in a circular order that formed the base of a single-tower.
descriptions.NUR2647: It takes its name from an old church. It stands on a small promontory on the right bank of the Riu Mannu. The lintel is broken and the whole monument is in a state of complete decay and abandonment. There were two entrances (one has collapsed) and several sacrificial stones. The peculiarity of this nuraghe is that the tholos, perfectly intact, was built with dark boulders formed from agglomerations of fossil shells. A rarity, since no trace of this type of material is found in the area.
descriptions.NUR21148: Nuraghe partially collapsed and invaded by vegetation, located at the edge of the village, near a rural chapel.
descriptions.NUR4871: The San Pietro nuraghe stands on the summit of a hill on the immediate outskirts of the village of Ussaramanna and takes its name from the church of the same name, which has now disappeared. A complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and a quadrangular bastion with towers oriented towards the four cardinal points.
descriptions.NUR3946: Three-lobed nuraghe serving as a foundation for the church of San Saturnino.
descriptions.NUR8429: The nuragic complex consists of nine towers, three belonging to the central structures and six to the robust outer wall. Its absolute peculiarity is the direct superimposition on its structures of the ruins of a small country church, dedicated to the eponymous saint and dating to the early 17th century; eleven burials found in the area around the sacred building belong to its period of use. On the hill of San Sebastiano, traces of a Punic occupation are legible.
descriptions.NUR4600: The church was built on the remains of a nuraghe called Nuraxi Mannu, and Nuragic remains are found throughout the village. The decision to build the church stemmed from a desire to give sacred continuity to a particular place. The church is a small building with a rectangular plan and a single nave. In the white façade, a round-arched doorway with a frame opens, surmounted by a small circular oculus.
descriptions.NUR19697: Located in the San Simplicio valley, on the ground surface only a few fallen stones remain.
descriptions.NUR5816: It is a complex nuraghe, consisting of a main tower surrounded by a four-lobed bastion that includes four corner towers and an open courtyard. In the north-eastern area the remains of the outer wall and the ruins of the annexed settlement are visible.
descriptions.NUR5660:
The building, one of the best known on the island, is a complex type, consisting of a central tower and a four-lobed bastion with an open courtyard.

It was defended by an outer wall, recorded by General Della Marmora, which is now barely legible on the ground surface.

The bastion (height 8.80 m) incorporates four towers linked by curtain walls with a concave-convex profile, built of roughly dressed basalt blocks laid in horizontal courses.
descriptions.NUR4697: Almost imperceptible remains of a nuraghe
descriptions.NUR3464: The simple nuraghe was transformed into the "a tancato" type. A second, smaller building was added to the front of the original tower, linked to it by two curtain walls with a broken line that enclose a courtyard. Known for the occurrence of the "light of the bull" phenomenon.
descriptions.NUR2516: Single-tower nuraghe with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a chamber with three niches arranged in a cross. The tower, circular in plan, survives to a maximum height of 12.25 m over 21 courses, while on the south-east side it reaches 11 m with 19 courses. At the top the diameter is 10 metres. The masonry consists of well-worked basalt blocks laid in regular horizontal courses.
descriptions.NUR3725:
It is a large proto-nuraghe with a single tower, equipped with some auxiliary structures, built with enormous basalt blocks.  

Due to collapses, access to the interior is possible only partially.
descriptions.NUR4582: In 1942 a stonemason from Donori, while breaking up a block of granite to obtain building stones, found 53 coins beneath the block bearing the effigy of Emperor Antoninus Pius, that of Trajan, of Empress Faustina and other rulers with indecipherable names. The nuraghe must have been very large, because despite being considerably damaged and covered by shrubs and various stones gathered nearby, the quantity of scattered boulders is considerable.
descriptions.NUR6206: The complex nuraghe of Santa Barbara lies about three kilometres from the village. Built of basalt, it is a four-lobed type and is surrounded by an extensive village. An excavation campaign carried out in 1986 investigated part of the village, in particular a hut. The hut was circular, built of Sinis sandstone; the floor, however, was of tufa. Near the hut a rectangular basin with two communicating hollows was found.
descriptions.NUR2990: More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe or corridor nuraghe; due to an internal collapse, it has become impossible to visit it from the entrance.
descriptions.NUR1249: According to the map in the publication "L'Altare preistorico di Monte d'Accoddi" by Ercole Contu, the correct name of the nuraghe should be "Camusina", which moreover appears on the IGM map as "Camuscina". It is in very poor condition and completely covered by dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR4428: The single-tower nuraghe currently preserves a standing height of five or six courses, and the ground plan of the lower chambers is quite easy to make out. On the west side of the corridor the stairwell opens, still retaining eight steps in place, which originally curved following the circular line of the perimeter wall.
descriptions.NUR4791:
Along the road from Samatzai towards S. Pietro.

Collapsed complex nuraghe, situated on a gentle slope with a central tower and two smaller ones. It has an elongated plan with the three towers arranged on the same longitudinal axis oriented north to south. A short distance from the central tower the basal structures of three circular huts are recorded, certainly belonging to a small surrounding village. The structures are built of marly and basaltic materials.
descriptions.NUR2303: Almost entirely dismantled, a few ashlars and wall segments of the original structure survive, their layout rendered indecipherable by the dense vegetation and a widespread state of decay. R. Ledda reports the discovery of primary mineral smelting slag, no longer in situ.
descriptions.NUR15281: Nuraghe coincident with a medieval settlement
descriptions.NUR4028: The nuraghe of Santa Lucia di Assolo stands in the countryside, within the archaeological area that includes the rural church dedicated to the same saint. It has a single-tower structure of truncated-conical shape; at present the base is visible, consisting of four superimposed dry-stone courses made of large stone blocks.
descriptions.NUR4513: The archaeological area lies on the edge of the Santa Lucia basalt plateau, east of the Monte Arci massif. It includes two complex nuraghi with a village, set about 50 metres apart. The nuraghe to the east is also complex, in better condition than the previous one; it preserves the central tower chamber, with its top missing, with several niches in the walls and the stairwell opening off the entrance corridor.
descriptions.NUR4447: The nuraghe is part of a complex that also includes a second nuraghe about 50 metres away. It must have been particularly grand, judging by the extent of the rubble. Within the collapse covering the central tower a tholos chamber of considerable height can be made out: the upper part of the entrance passage, with the angular cross-section typical of archaic-type nuraghi, can still be distinguished in the profile of the chamber.
descriptions.NUR11169: The best-known nuraghe is undoubtedly the one found in the Santa Maria area during excavations beneath the sacristy of the country church; its foundations were discovered in 1843 and some nuragic boulders are incorporated in the low wall enclosing the churchyard.
descriptions.NUR5903: Single-tower nuraghe with the tholos still intact
descriptions.NUR6390: Single-tower nuraghe with the tholos partially collapsed inward. Located beside a sheepfold.
descriptions.NUR4593: Single-tower located within the private park of the Sardara Thermal Hotel. It is partially buried and access to it cannot be identified.
descriptions.NUR10048:
Nuraghi that have disappeared completely or almost completely over time; this is one of them, and it lies near Morimenta, not far from the nuraghe Santu Sciori of Pabillonis.

Other archives mention the ruins of a little church, but there is very little of a church to be seen.
descriptions.NUR2716: What remains of a single-tower nuraghe dating from a period between the Middle and Late Bronze Age. Diameter of about 12 m and height of about 2 m.
descriptions.NUR1858: The nuraghe lies within the territory of Villaputzu. It appears as a sub-circular building of which only a few structures are visible, owing to demolition carried out to obtain wall ashlars for the construction of the adjacent church. On the northern side a semicircular building is annexed.
descriptions.NUR5939: This complex nuraghe, with five towers and a curtain wall as long as 450 metres, rises imposingly on the eastern edge of the Abbasanta plateau. The general layout of the Santa Marra nuraghe is complex and three-lobed, with a concave-convex perimeter, similar in type to the Santu Antine nuraghe at Torralba and the Losa nuraghe at Abbasanta, but reworked in an original way.
descriptions.NUR2285: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan. The nuraghe stands on a basalt platform on the summit of Monte S. Antonio, to the south-west of the rural chapel dedicated to the Saint. The monument rests on the sheer edge of the height, which acts as a natural bastion for the nuragic tower along the whole western arc, before sloping down towards the NNE where the building rests on the open ground.
descriptions.NUR4757: Built of limestone and marl blocks, the nuraghe has a four-lobed ground plan, with a central tower and four outer towers oriented to the cardinal points... surrounded by an outer wall, and the remains of four more towers. A sacred well lies inside the complex.
descriptions.NUR10524: The nuraghe that once stood near the church forecourt has been demolished and no trace of its former presence remains. Some shaped blocks are incorporated into the church dedicated to Santa Petronilla. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR6155: The nuraghe has a base diameter of 12.60 m and, although demolished in its upper parts, survives to a height of 8.60 m. Through the south-facing entrance one enters the corridor, on the right of which opens a rectangular niche and, on the left, the stair, still passable, which led to the upper chamber, now destroyed. The corridor leads to the fine circular chamber, 4.15 m in diameter, off which three niches open in a cross formation.
descriptions.NUR4776: Near the remains of a church dedicated to the saint after whom this nuraghe is named. Built of basalt blocks in polygonal masonry, it has a surviving elevation of about 3 metres. It is covered by several bushes that prevent the entrance from being identified.
descriptions.NUR21126: It is possible to assume the location of the nuraghe indicated by Taramelli on the slope of the hill. The nuraghe was already demolished at the time of Taramelli and is no longer visible today. Exact location not established.
descriptions.NUR5802: Two single-tower nuraghes placed at a short distance. The second is about 70 m to the north-east.
descriptions.NUR4537:
The collapses affecting the Nuragic monument make it impossible to identify the entrance.

Collapses are also visible in the upper part, preventing any view of the inner chamber.

In this area a few courses of stones can be seen leaning against the bedrock.

On the northern side, next to the central tower and a rock outcrop, there is a structure with an entrance that appears to belong to a courtyard or a Nuragic hut.
descriptions.NUR19463:
Located in the hinterland of the town of Porto Torres, the Sant'Elena nuraghe is one of the best preserved in the municipal area.

The monument occupies the summit of a low rise covered by very dense vegetation.

The central tower has a diameter of about 12 m and a surviving height of 4 m from the present ground level.

The masonry consists of 13 courses of superimposed blocks of white limestone, carefully dressed.
descriptions.NUR1531:
The nuraghe is a single-tower nuraghe with a sub-elliptical plan, built of roughly dressed trachyte blocks, collapsed on the south side and partly buried, and completely overgrown with vegetation.

Of the central chamber only traces of the staircase and a niche can just be made out.

On the side facing the valley one can see what must have been an opening in the outer wall.
descriptions.NUR14946: Damaged nuraghe, of which only a very small amount remains
descriptions.NUR8539:
The complex consists of a nuraghe and a village of huts. The nuraghe comprises a central tower refaced by a bastion with a straight-convex-curvilinear profile that incorporates two minor towers to the ENE and SSE.

The village, dating to the early Iron Age, extends to the NW of the nuraghe. The dwellings, sub-circular and sub-rectangular in shape, are arranged in "blocks" with several rooms that generally connect onto a central courtyard.
descriptions.NUR1703:
The prehistoric settlement spreads out, adapting to the rock formations, over three natural terraces, the first straight and the other two curvilinear.

These natural features have been reinforced by massive wall bastions built of large and medium-sized ashlars laid with heavy chinking. The proto-nuraghe, built of ashlars laid in irregular, heavily chinked courses, conforms to the morphology of the rocks.
descriptions.NUR4187: The nuraghe consists of a single circular tower and is not in a good state of preservation. The building was constructed using medium-sized, roughly dressed blocks of metarenite (schist). The tholos survives with a maximum diameter of almost five metres and a height of less than two. The nuraghe is reached by an uphill path, steeply sloping, set in Mediterranean scrub.
descriptions.NUR8566: The site of Sant'Uanni lies on a hill a very short distance from the village of Dolianova. Besides the remains of a multi-lobed nuraghe and the basal part of a church that bear its name, some finds attributable to the Nuragic and Roman periods have been discovered, suggesting the presence of both a Nuragic and a Roman settlement.
descriptions.NUR2030: The nuraghe is built on several levels. The oldest part is the central tower; an outer bastion then surrounds the central tower and links it to a second tower. The boulders making up this bastion are of considerable size. The only accessible part is a corridor on the second floor of the central tower, with a “donkey-back” or inverted ship’s-keel roof, whose south entrance is topped by a huge lintel with its relieving window.
descriptions.NUR2959: The monument stands in a hilly area, in land used as pasture about 100 metres south of the rural church of San Giacomo. It was originally built on a granite outcrop which presumably incorporated some parts of it. The plan is sub-elliptical and only a stretch of curvilinear basal wall survives.
descriptions.NUR2699: Nuraghe eroded and surrounded by vegetation, of which three or four courses remain.
descriptions.NUR2043: Remains of a nuraghe located near the millenary olive tree of "Sa Tanca Manna"
descriptions.NUR3945: The church stands on the right bank of the River Temo, a few hundred metres east of the village of Bosa (OR). Built in the medieval period, its foundations rest on the ruins of a nuraghe, like most early Christian and early medieval churches.
descriptions.NUR1002: Built on a hillock overlooking the Riu Filibertu, the San Marco nuraghe has been incorporated into a farmhouse; during the Second World War military structures were built against it, recorded until the 1970s but no longer visible today.
descriptions.NUR2274:
Traces of a nuraghe and a Nuragic village, with finds from the Roman period as well.

The monument stands on a granite crag overlooking a large wooded area, about 1220 metres north-east of the village of Lei. Around the Nuragic building, especially to the east, the remains of a village can be made out and the ground is scattered with pottery of various periods. A short distance away, traces of Roman buildings were found in 1867.
descriptions.NUR3811: A rural penetration road runs along the hillside, though one must still climb uphill on foot (no paths or trails are present).
descriptions.NUR4715: The Santu Millanu nuraghe is a single-tower nuraghe surrounded by a four-lobed bastion barely discernible.
descriptions.NUR960: It is a ruined nuraghe of which only little remains.
descriptions.NUR5695: It is a ruined nuraghe of which only little remains.
descriptions.NUR2113: Single-tower nuraghe, preserved for only a few courses.
descriptions.NUR4121: Inside a large tancato in the locality of S. Pietro, next to a farmhouse, little of the nuraghe remains. The building appears to have been erected on top of the nuraghe. The materials used are large blocks of sandstone. The ruins have yielded several hundred fragments of Nuragic pottery, stone tools, flakes and microliths of obsidian, food remains, etc.
descriptions.NUR13544: The tombs of the archaeological complex lie on the south slope of the hill from its base almost to the summit, where the ruined remains of a single-tower nuraghe are found instead. Unrecorded nuraghe. A wall with a portal of apparent Nuragic date reported to the NurNet editorial team by Mauro Tavella.
descriptions.NUR20136: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and an added tower linked by a wall. The central chamber is flanked by two niches. Around the nuraghe are traces of a settlement. Archaeological excavations have been carried out. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR4032: Complex nuraghe with walls made of dressed ashlar stones and of similar thickness. Damaged, collapsed, and partially buried.
descriptions.NUR3833: Complex nuraghe, presumably of the front-addition type. The nuraghe shows numerous structural alterations after its initial construction. A main tower with two secondary towers added to it can nevertheless be made out.
descriptions.NUR4827: The original nuraghe was likely quite tall. Currently, the tholos has collapsed inward. Note the presence of two giants' tombs located close to the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR3872: The IGM map marks it as Longu, which actually lies further east, a few hundred metres away. It consists of several courses of polygonal cyclopean blocks whose neat arrangement is astonishing. It shows an opening to the north with a lintel that incorporates the beginnings of an arch. The surrounding area is of interest.
descriptions.NUR3383: On the maps of the former Catasto, the nuraghe is called "Mesu 'e Tancas Paulis".
descriptions.NUR3859: The nuraghe stands on the summit of a hill, from which the view extends over the whole surrounding territory and especially over the valleys below and the course of the Rio Mannu. It lies inside a cultivated olive grove.
descriptions.NUR2654: Built on the edge of a trachyte bastion, overlooking a natural route, about a hundred metres north of a giants' tomb situated downhill, the monument is a single-tower nuraghe with a stair in the corridor and a chamber flanked by three niches. To the west, in the sector not naturally defended by the vertical rock face, are the remains of a massive outer wall, while the rocky profile on which the tower stands also appears to be reinforced by coursed wall structures.
descriptions.NUR12297: Nuraghe completely stripped and immersed in vegetation, never studied
descriptions.NUR3824: Reported as a nuraghe, it turns out to be a high pile of stones. Very useful for hikers because, coming from Magola along the cliff edge, it marks the turning point to pick up the path below the walls. Watch out for sheepdogs!
descriptions.NUR5962: All around the monument the Nuragic village extends over a wide area, with in particular two huts in a good state of preservation. At the south-west edge there is a pond (Paule – from which the site takes its name) which very probably served as a water reservoir.
descriptions.NUR5672: Single-tower nuraghe in relatively good condition with the tholos intact. It is located at the boundary between two fields and is accessible only through a privately owned plot cultivated as a garden.
descriptions.NUR19207: It could belong to the category of unfinished nuraghes, of which there are many examples between Macomer and Sindia.
descriptions.NUR3832: Single-tower nuraghe completely collapsed. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR5211: "Monte sa Perda", it is thought there was another nuraghe that dominated the whole gulf of Palmas, probably destroyed for the construction of "su forr'e sa cracina" (lime kiln) situated in the immediate vicinity.
descriptions.NUR5298: Possible corridor nuraghe, rectangular in plan, entrance to the south-east, helical staircase on the left leading to the second level now collapsed. Studied by Lamarmora in 1830.
descriptions.NUR10868: Small circular structure, built using Nuragic technique and classifiable as atypical nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR6262:
Archaic nuraghe, corridor type. The building stands on a solid rocky base controlling the southern bank of the Rio Cispiri. The nuraghe is built of polygonal blocks of local basalt which, in the basal courses, are of considerable size.

In visual contact with various nuraghi such as Zenna Uda, Muschiu, and Serra Crastula.
descriptions.NUR19413: Nuraghe completely collapsed, of which only a few traces remain on the surface.
descriptions.NUR16110: Mixed-type, tancato complex nuraghe, with a central tower and two added towers. The central chamber, slightly elliptical in shape, has two niches and a roof of slabs instead of a tholos, which brings it closer to a proto-nuraghe. Built of granite. The position of the nuraghe is not confirmed; it is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR813: Destroyed nuraghe and today no longer visible
descriptions.NUR6369: Single-tower nuraghe visible only when the waters of the Cuga basin recede. It is one of the 20 nuraghes in the Cuga valley.
descriptions.NUR14948: Nuraghe almost completely disappeared, named by Prof. S. Ghiani in “La Trexenta Antica”. At the base of the hill there is a large rock with artificial cavities.
descriptions.NUR5490: Hidden from view by a granite outcrop, the nuraghe appears half-destroyed. A menhir stands on the spot, from which the settlement and the region probably took their name. A village is likely present.
descriptions.NUR4258: Nuraghe dominating the landing points and the area below the coast. Walls in good condition. Open tholos, probably collapsed.
descriptions.NUR5621: Usanis, located at the top of a rocky spur, was a complex structure composed of two towers.
descriptions.NUR9876: A ruined single-tower nuraghe; in the surrounding area the traces of a quarry and a settlement can be seen.
descriptions.NUR4295: The nuraghe Maletta II, built at 264 m above sea level, is now almost completely destroyed by the continuous agricultural work that has affected the whole area, one of the most intensively exploited in the Sinnai countryside, and preserves only a very fragmentary stretch of the basal course.
descriptions.NUR13096: Nuraghe with a village almost completely covered by earth and vegetation. The most visible part has been destroyed by excavations. Surrounded by greenery and many rivers, other nuraghi are visible from here, including Sa Dom'e S'Orcu.
descriptions.NUR2523: Nuraghe no longer visible; a house was built on the site in the early 20th century, now in ruin, using basalt blocks from the original nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5636: It may be a proto-nuraghe, and it is almost square in plan.
descriptions.NUR5854: The Costa nuraghe, commonly called Sa Reggia, comprises a complex nuraghe, a surrounding village and a massive outer wall. The nuraghe consists of a central tower and a bastion of four secondary towers enclosing a courtyard. The central tower (14 metres in diameter) is built of polygonal basalt blocks in the lower part and well-worked blocks in the upper part.
descriptions.NUR5968: The nuraghe S'Argara is certainly one of the most important at Su Pranu; it is a four-lobed nuraghe, with four towers at the corners of the quadrangular bastion and an internal courtyard facing the entrance to the central tower. From its summit, on the clearest days, one can survey almost the whole of Sardinia's western coast, from Capo Caccia as far as Capo Pecora in the Sulcis.
descriptions.NUR2164: Fortification or nuraghe also called Staderis or Giolza. It lies in the Montiferru, near the summit of a high spur of bare, rugged rock facing Monte Urtigu, where the remains of an imposing megalithic wall survive with seven courses of roughly dressed basalt boulders. The straight line of the ruin suggests an original quadrangular defensive structure around the level top of the rock, rather than the wall face of a hilltop nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR2076: Nuraghe in very poor condition and hidden by thick undergrowth
descriptions.NUR2078: Single-tower nuraghe, enveloped in dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR2077: Single-tower nuraghe, the few remaining fragments are covered by dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR6332: In good conservation conditions it is possible to visit it, although access to the upper level is not possible due to the collapse of the stairs.
descriptions.NUR5117: Discovered by the great cartographer A. Lamarmora in 1840. It is covered in dense mastic vegetation, has collapsed inwards and filled with earth over time. The stones used for the construction are white with yellow patches of dry moss. The surviving height of the tower exposed to the north is about three metres. If visited in summer, the desert-like landscape of the area adds to the fascination of this imposing megalithic monument.
descriptions.NUR5174: It is largely buried. One can thus make out a central tower with an irregularly circular perimeter, containing a central chamber, also circular. Along the outer perimeter of the monument stretches of walling can be seen that suggest something about its more complex articulations; for example, to the east-north-east one might hypothesise terracing works, if not the actual presence of huts or enclosures.
descriptions.NUR10436: The nuraghe stands in an area where an Ozieri culture settlement (4th millennium BC) and a stone cist tomb of the Bell Beaker–Bonnanaro facies (late 3rd–early 2nd millennium BC) have long been known. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR6203: Near the village of San Salvatore, within a private property, the nuraghe is in very poor condition, but the remains of a significant Nuragic settlement are clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR2216: Only a few remains of the nuraghe are left.
descriptions.NUR2902:
We approach the south-east wall with the internal wall face of the nuraghe, past the "guard niche" on the right and the start of the helical staircase on the left.

These two chambers are inaccessible because the interior has completely collapsed and is full of ashlars. The clear trace of their course remains, however, with the upper part of the staircase re-emerging above the entrance passage after completing the circuit of the tower.
descriptions.NUR2720: A single-tower tholos nuraghe built of local basalt blocks; its outer wall face survives for about four to five courses with a maximum remaining height of about 2.50 m. The interior is completely filled with collapse debris. The building must have been of considerable size (diameter over 13 m) with several superimposed chambers. It now stands next to a modern building made of concrete blocks.
descriptions.NUR5616: It is also known as Sas Coas from the place name of the ground adjacent to Sas Baddes. It is a single-tower nuraghe whose tholos has collapsed, leaving the interior of the central chamber with its three canonical niches open to the sky. It has certain peculiarities not found in other nuraghi that make it unique.
descriptions.NUR11145: Single-tower nuraghe on a hilltop with only a few courses of stone preserved. From this nuraghe you can clearly see the Nuraghe su Stiddiu, Nuraghe su Bobboi, and the hill where the Nuraghe di Crabili Simoni stood, with the megalithic altar at its foot. A few hundred metres from the nuraghe lies the Mitza Aramu spring.
descriptions.NUR1921: Situated about 300 metres north-east of the Nuraghe Su Figu and less than 600 metres south-east of the Nuraghe Columbos, the monument is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, a maximum surviving height of 3.65 m and five courses. The entrance, facing south-east and with a rectangular opening, is raised 0.40 m above ground level by a threshold slab and is topped by a well-finished lintel resting on jambs that stand out from the rest of the masonry for the better dressing of the stones.
descriptions.NUR4015: The monument's wall structures are clearly visible: those of the central tower, plus other towers, plus a probable one. The outer wall with its lintelled entrance is clearly visible. The central tower's structure survives for as many as seven courses.
descriptions.NUR3799: On the limestone plateau of sas cudinas to the north-east stands the single-tower nuraghe of roughly squared stones, of which only a few basal circles survive. It overlooks the whole valley of the rio Iscanneddu, the plain of Mamucada, and the fertile Orria Pitzinna.
descriptions.NUR3211: Damaged nuraghe, of which only a few courses remain
descriptions.NUR3204: It retains the tholos intact except for the closure slab.
descriptions.NUR1226: It is a nuraghe with a square-plan chamber that was never finished; only the base has been built and the lintel has been set over the entrance. It is interesting because all around lie the boulders ready to be used on the nuraghe, making it valuable for understanding the building technique employed.
descriptions.NUR1819: location of the remains of the nuraghe Antoni Letzesa sea
descriptions.NUR11237: A few white limestone blocks of the basal perimeter. The entrance and little else can be seen, all within a dense thicket of fetid anagyris (sa giolva). The name should derive from the place-name of the land. Shepherds believe the leaves of this plant give a bitter taste to goats' milk. See Nuraghe sas giòlvas.
descriptions.NUR6192: DIRROCCATO NURAGHE WITH ABOUT FOUR COURSES OUT OF TERRA
descriptions.NUR5389:
It is located within the territory of the comune of Quartu Sant'Elena (CA).

Of exceptional form, the nuraghe is now almost completely destroyed.
descriptions.NUR1499: It may be a nuraghe whose construction was never completed.
descriptions.NUR2572:
A single-tower tholos nuraghe. The building stands on the summit of a bend in the Rio Cispiri and rests on a solid rocky base partly incorporated into the structures, as can be seen on the north-facing side.

The nuraghe is well preserved on the north and north-east sides, with an external wall face of large polygonal basalt blocks reaching a maximum surviving height of about 12 m, while the south and west sides have collapsed.
descriptions.NUR2611:
Position verified with GPS. The nuraghe is partially collapsed and the entrance is blocked by debris from a collapse.

It still reaches a maximum height of about 8 metres.
descriptions.NUR2577: “Nuraghe Sas Melas, a short distance from the hill called Fruncu Sas Patatas, at the ford of Rio Minori. It is the best nuraghe in the municipality; it still has two storeys; solid construction, accessible doorway like the corridor and the lower chamber; shepherds’ refuge; the stair leads to the upper storey, with a domed cell; windows wider than they are high. In the lower chamber a stone table. On land belonging to the heirs of Luca Piras, son of Angelo.”
descriptions.NUR5650: Single-tower nuraghe of trachyte blocks; three courses survive. It appears destroyed and completely hidden. It takes its name from the mountain on which it stands, where a convent of nuns stood in ancient times.
descriptions.NUR3822: It lies a short distance from Lake Cuga; as the photos show, two or three courses of the foundation stones remain, giving a clear idea of the internal layout of this single-tower nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5956: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The interpretation is based on the circular plan of the monument, although its poor state of preservation and the vegetation cover make it impossible to observe other characteristic details. The entrance cannot be identified. Much of the material from the collapse of the nuraghe has been reused to build contemporary enclosures leaning against the ancient structures.
descriptions.NUR1227: Ruined nuraghe submerged by the floral scrub
descriptions.NUR5121:
The megalithic complex consists of a central body, built of rubble laid in irregular wall courses; vaguely quadrangular in plan, it contains three small circular chambers.

These rooms, enclosed within the wall face (about 2.10 m high) that defines the central body, quadrangular in plan, have been subjected to conspicuous illicit excavations carried out at an unknown date by looters.
descriptions.NUR8370: The monument, built of limestone, has an internal diameter of about four metres, small by known standards, but not excessively so when compared with the width of the spur on which it stands, which extends for just over six metres before ending at the edge of a cliff.
descriptions.NUR15711:
The nuraghe lies less than 100 metres north-east of Nuraghe Ordari.

The monument is not clearly legible.

The masonry survives on the west side for 3.20 m with four courses of large basalt stones, only roughly dressed and laid in irregular rows.

A better-finished stone, rectangular in shape and measuring 1.90 m long, 0.78 m wide and 0.56 m thick, appears to be the lintel of the entrance, which can no longer be identified in any way.
descriptions.NUR5711: The nuraghe S'Aspru, one of the largest in the Goceano, is in poor condition and partly unstable. It is a complex nuraghe whose central tower stands in the middle of a rectangular courtyard and is enclosed within a circular bastion to which three further towers were later added; these towers are not accessible. Inside the central tower there are three niches and a corridor leading to the staircase that goes up to the upper floor, where a second chamber with a tholos roof is found.
descriptions.NUR15024: The remains of the nuraghe are located inside the Orguglioso Castle.
descriptions.NUR12035: Nuraghe now almost completely destroyed. Only a heap of stones remains.
descriptions.NUR5593: It lies in the municipality of Lodine (NU). A single-tower nuraghe reduced to a heap of ruins. It is situated very close to Sos Nuragheddos 1. Further information can be found in the book *Archeologia in Barbagia* by M.A. Mele.
descriptions.NUR2384: Remains on a rocky outcrop from which the valley below is visible.
descriptions.NUR728: The complex nuraghe has completely collapsed and is buried. The ashlars were probably removed for the construction of a building nearby. Traces of a village lie all around.
descriptions.NUR6459: Nuraghe named after the locality: "Sa tanca 'e su padru". Of imposing dimensions but completely ruined and not discernible anymore. Until a few years ago it allowed access to the interior.
descriptions.NUR3522: It seems to be one of those nuraghe classified as unfinished.
descriptions.NUR3658: It is in a very degraded state. Covered in brambles and scrub, it is inaccessible. Built of trachyte. From the outside a small window is visible, high up, facing east. The walls still standing are about four metres high.
descriptions.NUR14952: Nuraghe completely dismantled according to S. Ghiani in La Trexenta Antica.
descriptions.NUR2962: Single-tower nuraghe. On the IGM map this nuraghe is confused with the nearby Nuraghe Molas. Around the nuraghe there are traces of a village or settlement.
descriptions.NUR5110: Single-tower nuraghe with a small village adjacent.
descriptions.NUR4955: The nuraghe stands on the hill of Cala Francese, in the locality “Serra is tres portus”. It may originally have been a complex nuraghe built of limestone boulders. The outline of the original tower survives discontinuously; its interior is covered by collapse and vegetation.
descriptions.NUR730:
At Sa Turricula the first phase of the Nuragic civilisation is recognised. The site comprises the nuraghe, the village and, a short distance away, two giants' tombs, a well, and the Funtan'e Casu dolmen.

Sa Turricula does not allow an easy reading of the structures. It is choked with vegetation but, once you reach the top of the hill on which it stands, you enjoy a breathtaking view over the whole surrounding territory.

The nuraghe probably belongs to the corridor nuraghe type.

Nearby are
descriptions.NUR16244: It is an almost inaccessible site with a clear view of much of the nuraghi of the Ogliastra plain. I think it is a multi-lobed nuraghe, but between the vegetation and the collapse it is illegible. The photo I sent is the only part facing south from which anything can be understood; the rest is embedded among natural rocks and, I repeat, with the collapse nothing can be made out. The area is scattered with small terracotta ashlars. (Report by Daniele Murgia, Triei)
descriptions.NUR4948:
Single-tower nuraghe built of squared andesite blocks in fairly regular courses, in a fair state of preservation. The entrance faces east but the chamber is not currently visible because of the collapse of the monument's walls and roof.

To the south a wall runs in a straight and curving line, perhaps belonging to a recent sheepfold, now dismantled.
descriptions.NUR1599: Nuraghe that might belong to the category of "uncompleted"
descriptions.NUR8040:
The stronghold was built in a strategic position: from the top of the hill on which it stands one can see the Campidano plain, the Linas mountain range and several nuraghi in the territory of Pabillonis. Of considerable size (it covers an area of almost 4,000 square metres), it consists of four towers linked by a rhomboidal curtain wall.

Because of the partial collapse of the towers, only one is accessible today.
descriptions.NUR6092: Single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical plan, the layout of the nuraghe is difficult to read.
descriptions.NUR6075: Single-tower nuraghe with a chamber bordered by three niches, built in basalt. Traces of a settlement.
descriptions.NUR1217: Damaged nuraghe, completely surrounded by vegetation
descriptions.NUR2621: Single-tower nuraghe situated at an altitude of 250 m a.s.l.; it is practically the site that stands highest of all its kind, and probably performed a very important function in its context because it dominates the Cuga valley, where there are more than 15 nuraghi in a few square kilometres.
descriptions.NUR5396: Besides the Iscalas nuraghe, the site contains Roman-period wall structures and prehistoric menhirs. The nuraghe, of which only a few stretches of masonry now survive, had a circular tower built of medium and large polygonal boulders laid without mortar.
descriptions.NUR4415: Built on a rise from which it overlooks the surrounding area, it can be seen from the hairpin bends of the SP 6. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a base diameter of about 10 m, built of schist blocks. Part of the masonry on the south side has collapsed, and the entrance, also on the south, is ogival and gives access to the inner chamber, which lacks its tholos roof; a niche is visible inside it.
descriptions.NUR3816: The quadrilobate nuraghe of S. Caterina is located in the municipality of Osilo, just metres from the ruins of the church of S. Caterina.
descriptions.NUR20367: An 19th-century local history document (Emanuele Atzori) records that a nuraghe ruin stood in the centre of Capoterra (it was probably completely destroyed already in the 19th century), of which no trace remains today, not even in living memory. The public document (dated 23 September 1844) in fact notes the presence of a ruined nuraghe at Sa Gruxi Santa (apparently more or less where the square of the same name now stands).
descriptions.NUR3057: Structures belonging to a mixed-type complex nuraghe, consisting of an archaic corridor nuraghe linked to a single-tower tholos nuraghe. The complex as a whole is very imposing, formed by a large building with an elliptical – sub-quadrangular plan with rounded corners, about 22 m long and a little over 17 m wide, oriented N–S.
descriptions.NUR19700: It overlooks the Monte Ozzastru valley, a short distance from the Porchiles nuraghe, and only the base of the monument is visible.
descriptions.NUR1901: The complex nuraghe, of which ruins of the central tower and two curtain walls on two different levels survive. The original tower retains its outline almost intact. The two curtain walls are visible on the side facing north-east of the central tower; they follow a curvilinear course for several metres, interrupted from north-east to north-west by a substantial collapse that starts from the central tower.
descriptions.NUR636: The nuraghe, probably of complex structure, is now covered by dense vegetation and preserves only a few courses of the original building. A cyclopean wall of circular shape, about 10 m in diameter, is attached to the nuraghe. Its state of preservation is very poor.
descriptions.NUR1830: The nuraghe stands on Monte Perdas de Fogu at 230 m above sea level. It is a complex nuraghe of which the wall faces of the central tower survive. The entrance to the monument, trapezoidal in shape, lies to the SSE. A narrow corridor with an ogival cross-section leads directly into the central tower's chamber.
descriptions.NUR16025: The nuraghe is partly collapsed and likely destroyed during the works for the construction of the municipal road.
descriptions.NUR15314: The building material of the structure, of which the top of central tower A and some wall profiles emerge for a few metres, is basaltic andesite. A dense thicket of mastic covers the exposed part of the structure, showing a curvilinear profile of the bastion which, from satellite images, appears to be at least multi-lobed owing to the addition of at least two secondary bodies.
descriptions.NUR4667: The nuraghe has been completely levelled for the construction of the Church of Santa Greca. In aerial views, the circular outline at ground level is still clearly visible and likely represented its original foundation.
descriptions.NUR5708: Corridor nuraghe, also known as Runalgalva.
descriptions.NUR4414: The nuraghe, built of basalt blocks, is in fair condition. It consists of a main tower and two others leaning against it, though the structure of one is unrecognisable because of collapse. Through a lintelled entrance you enter the main tower, where a niche and the remains of a staircase can be seen. From the nuraghe there is a splendid view over the bay of Cea.
descriptions.NUR5657: Single-tower nuraghe in good condition near a small agricultural farm
descriptions.NUR5828: From the old road to Sorradile, turning left, 1 km from the village, near a bend in the Riu Binzas, the remains of a circular nuraghe about 12 metres in diameter can be seen: only the basal course is just visible, formed of large, unworked trachyte boulders.
descriptions.NUR5874: A ruined single-tower nuraghe of which half the perimeter wall survives for seven courses.
descriptions.NUR5958: It is a nuraghe that is particularly dear to me, not least because it was the site of a find of an object that I donated to the Sanna Museum in Sassari, and which has unfortunately disappeared. I have monitored the nuraghe over the years and reported its imminent collapse. I have visited it inside and I believe I am one of the few who know the nature of its masonry.
descriptions.NUR13375: The nuraghe stands in a commanding position over the broad Modolo valley, in the Planargia region of north-eastern Sardinia. The building, of particular interest and grandeur, is a corridor nuraghe. It has an irregular elliptical plan, crossed longitudinally by a through corridor with opposed entrances.
descriptions.NUR5484: Nuraghe Senis Mannu is reached from the Church of San Giovanni after about one kilometre of road. This nuraghe, built at an altitude of 302 m above sea level, is a megalithic construction in which a tower erected thousands of years ago by stacking blocks of sedimentary rock stands out. The tholos has collapsed at the centre. From the top of the nuraghe there is a good vantage point: to the south the tabular profile of the Giara and to the north the hill of Santa Vittoria.
descriptions.NUR16861: Not recorded, it is located on private land.
descriptions.NUR15764: From the aerial photograph it appears to be one of those nuraghes belonging to the category of "uncompleted" ones.
descriptions.NUR4324: Complex nuraghe composed of a central mastio and two towers with a courtyard.
descriptions.NUR3080:
It is probably a corridor nuraghe against which various elongated huts and numerous dry-stone walls were later built, making it particularly difficult to survey.

From this heap of rubble overgrown with vegetation a circular tower (diam. 11–12 metres) emerges, with a surviving height of 4 metres.

At the top, where the tower is missing, short stretches of corridor can be made out, but they cannot be defined because of the collapse.
descriptions.NUR4366: It is located within a military zone, access to which is forbidden to the public.
descriptions.NUR659: A place of rare beauty. The site, particularly evocative, includes a complex nuraghe with an attached village, a cave with two entrances, two giants' tombs, and two single-tower nuraghes.
descriptions.NUR4346: Nuraghe almost completely destroyed, of which only a single course remains visible. Almost entirely covered by the collapse and vegetation, its plan cannot be established.
descriptions.NUR6256: Single-tower nuraghe in excellent condition, with its tholos intact. Surrounding traces of other towers and huts are visible.
descriptions.NUR3588: Single-tower nuraghe reduced to a ruin. A single stretch of circular wall survives, 4 metres high, with seven courses. The monument is almost completely destroyed and its materials have been reused to build enclosures and livestock shelters in recent times.
descriptions.NUR1285: We are faced with only a few elementary basal circles of the construction, which appear with stones arranged in courses, some of which are disordered and affected by collapse. Interesting are certain constructional details that highlight even more the genius loci of those who commissioned its building.
descriptions.NUR3011: The nuraghe "Serra de Chigulas" was formerly known as "Su Tangarone" and is mentioned in the book of Canon Spanu. The monument has a complex plan.
descriptions.NUR5301: Some courses of large stones can be seen, together with part of the summit, which includes a blocked access. At 40 metres to the east, the remains of a "sacred" well.
descriptions.NUR537: Nuraghe "a tancato", with a central tower and an additional tower connected by bastions. Traces of a settlement. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR20140: This nuraghe is unique in the Pattada area, because it is built of boulders that are distinctly smaller than average, except for the beams and lintels. Its structure suggests that it is a proto-nuraghe (1800–1600 BC).
descriptions.NUR3987:
The ground plan of the whole structure must have been rather irregular and adapted to the natural lie of the rock, which was incorporated for long stretches into the building.

The surviving structure extends along a north–south axis 7.35 m long and an east–west axis 7.80 m long, and retains an elevation reaching up to 1.90 m above ground level.
descriptions.NUR6101: USAI (2014, p. 42) includes it within the typology "the 'small nuraghes' probably unfinished".
descriptions.NUR5985: The largest nuraghe in the territory of Illorai, mentioned by Taramelli, G. Lilliu and Angius-Casalis, consists of a central tower probably of two storeys with its tholos still intact; on the south side is the courtyard with the entrance partly collapsed; on the north-east and north-west sides are the two lateral towers (with collapsed tholoi) but their internal walls are in excellent condition. Collapses inwards are minimal, while those outwards are substantial. Contact AGRIS for access to the area.
descriptions.NUR4655: This singular monument, composed of two superimposed towers, stands alone on a very high and impressive cliff overlooking the great valley of the Rio S'Acqua Callenti, right near its junction with the Flumendosa valley.
descriptions.NUR4003: The namesake nuraghe near the unique monument, composed of two superimposed towers, stands alone on an extremely high and impressive cliff overlooking the great valley of the Rio S'Acqua Callenti, right near its junction with the Flumendosa valley.
descriptions.NUR6216:
The nuraghe stands on the summit of a high watershed whose north and east slopes are very steep, while to the west, a few metres from the nuraghe, the hill ends in a high cliff.

It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, 10.30 m in diameter. Very little of the nuraghe survives because of the substantial collapses it has suffered over the centuries.

Further reading:

Bibliography: E.E.M. 1922, p. 104; MERELLA 1996-97, vol. V, pp. 770-773, fig. 37, pl. XXIII.
descriptions.NUR5312: Remains of nuraghe or nuragic huts
descriptions.NUR5637: Single-tower nuraghe completely collapsed and looted. Only some stones of the outer wall face and the circular base alignment remain; no other elements are detectable.
descriptions.NUR1900: Complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and probably two other towers. Unfortunately the original structure is hidden by a conspicuous collapse and dense vegetation. Leaning against the central tower, on the front side, the structures of two probable towers can be glimpsed. To the north-east a rectangular room built in cyclopean masonry is visible, with a flat-lintelled roof.
descriptions.NUR19661: Nuraghe in a very advanced state of collapse, making it difficult to determine its structure. To the north-west a few courses can still be seen in their original position, but even these do not help to establish its layout.
descriptions.NUR5151: Collapsed remains of a probable single-tower nuraghe
descriptions.NUR15803: The area of potsherds at Serra Ona can be delimited to the east of the nuraghe in the surrounding fields used for agriculture. They are small and medium-sized fragments of Nuragic and Roman date with a medium degree of abrasion. They are distributed unevenly and, because the fields are ploughed, they concentrate especially in the headlands where the plough turns.
descriptions.NUR1888:
The Serra Paulis Nuragic complex now survives only as a ruin, with four wall structures already identified by Struglia around the 1980s.

Its dominant position over the whole territory allows a 360° view.

The site was probably reused in the Roman period as a foundry workshop, given the considerable remains of materials burnt and deformed by fire found in situ.
descriptions.NUR3492: A ruined nuraghe, not easily reached, stands on a hill at as much as 982 m above sea level. The Serra Pirisi cave is an area that is not particularly extensive, measuring about 1.5 km in length, located in the Su Canale area, in the Supramonte of Baunei. Despite its small size, compared with other areas, it contains a considerable number of cave entrances, among them Lovettecannas, the deepest in Sardinia with a vertical drop of -520 m.
descriptions.NUR2941: Complex nuraghe, apparently four-lobed with the tholos of the central tower intact
descriptions.NUR6111:
It appears as a large heap of rubble covered by dense shrub vegetation that in no way allows the ground plan of the monument to be read.

The surrounding ground is strewn, over a wide area, with the remains of the Nuragic settlement, which was also reused in Roman times, as shown by the potsherds scattered on the ground and several cippi.

The nuraghe was defended by an outer wall that still survives for about sixty metres in length and to a height of about 1/1.50 m.
descriptions.NUR2604: The monument, partly hidden by dense vegetation, is of the corridor type with an elliptical plan, built of medium and large granite stones and preserved to a maximum height of 4 m on the north side.
descriptions.NUR1907: Very little information exists about the Serra Su Parone nuraghe because it has been almost completely dismantled. It is perhaps a single-tower nuraghe of which only a few traces remain; a stretch of the tower wall survives discontinuously, consisting of two courses of trachyte boulders. Its state of preservation is very poor.
descriptions.NUR3682:
Only a few basal courses of the nuraghe remain visible, up to a maximum height of about 2 m, formed by large polygonal basalt blocks laid in a circle.

What survives of the inner chamber is completely blocked by collapse debris and covered by a dense layer of vegetation, with brambles and shrubs. The entrance, no longer visible, faced south.
descriptions.NUR3445: Structures belonging to a single-tower tholos nuraghe. The building stands on a low rise in a commanding position over the surrounding plain. Three to four courses of the outer wall face, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt, can be seen, while the inner chamber is destroyed and not visible. The maximum surviving height is about 2 m.
descriptions.NUR5970: Among the numerous nuraghes in the region, Serrese is particularly notable for having the tholos in good state of preservation.
descriptions.NUR6689: The nuraghe is multi-lobed, consisting of a central tower surrounded by five towers, some of which are in a good state of preservation. The towers have lost their tops; originally the tower summits must have been crowned with stone battlements, which were recovered at the base of the structures during the most recent archaeological excavations carried out on the monument following the collapses.
descriptions.NUR3076: Nuraghe with staircase in good state of conservation.
descriptions.NUR575: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and two lateral towers connected by bastions and featuring a courtyard. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR862: The nuraghe is hidden beneath an impenetrable layer of vegetation.
descriptions.NUR5775: Complex nuraghe with frontal addition and lateral development: the added structures are arranged not only in front of the main tower but also to its sides. There are two minor towers, linked to the main one by curtain walls; the courtyard lies between them as a connecting space.
descriptions.NUR4999: Little of this nuraghe remains: the first two courses of the foundation on the north side, and the upper part of the basalt ashlars in curvilinear courses at the other cardinal points. Clearly the nuraghe is not to blame. Whatever can be documented is documented.
descriptions.NUR3989: It was a smaller tower (about 8 m in diameter) than the nuraghe de Susu. It probably served as a lookout. It was certainly reused in the Roman period, as shown by the presence of terraces, pit graves and lithic material in the area. After bulldozer work during reforestation, few traces remain.
descriptions.NUR4195: Little or almost nothing remains standing; a portion of the outer facing of the south side can be distinguished, and all around a very large number of scattered blocks from the collapse. It is classified as a single-tower nuraghe with a circular base and an external diameter of about 11 metres.
descriptions.NUR4280: The nuraghe, built of schist, is constructed with quadrangular blocks laid in regular courses, set in a layer of ochre-coloured clay. It consists of a main tower and an adjoining chamber joined to the first by a short curtain wall. In the inner wall face of the tower various voids can be seen that must have served to anchor a wooden mezzanine. At the foot of this nuraghe lie the huts of the Nuragic village.
descriptions.NUR10460: Certainly a central-tower nuraghe of note. The central tower soars, and from what can be made out it must have been a four-lobed nuraghe with a village around it. The tholos has collapsed inwards.
descriptions.NUR3425:
The monument lies less than 900 metres south of the Nuraghe Suerzu.

It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular, slightly flattened plan, with a surviving height of 2.15 m over four or five courses of medium and large stones, only roughly dressed and laid in irregular courses.

Because of its very poor state of preservation, the collapse and the shrub vegetation, it is not possible to determine the position of the entrance.
descriptions.NUR5905:
It is a single-tower tholos nuraghe of trachyte with some elements in granite, circular in plan and about 11 metres in diameter, surviving to a maximum height of 5 metres.

The monument has an entrance topped by a lintel, a corridor with a trapezoidal cross-section that gives access to a niche and the stairwell, as well as the central chamber with two opposing niches; however, the whole is difficult to reach because of the collapses.
descriptions.NUR5738: One of many nuraghes, hidden beneath the earth, in the Oschiri area.
descriptions.NUR4841: Nuraghe currently under excavation. It is thought to consist of a central tholos and four surrounding towers enclosing a courtyard. An extensive village of numerous huts, also used in Punic and Roman times, spreads around it, protected by a massive system of walls up to 6 metres thick. Great importance attaches to the discovery inside the village of a glass-working workshop. The site is not open to the public.
descriptions.NUR2817:
Situated 500 m from the village along the road to Sarule, the circular-plan nuraghe was probably a single-tower type.

Today only the basal course of squared trachyte blocks is visible, and to the north a stretch of the second course.
descriptions.NUR19896: It is in a state of complete abandonment, overgrown with vegetation, partly buried but mostly collapsed, also due to the action of tomb robbers. A nuraghe with at least two chambers or smaller towers leaning against the main tower and an entrance certainly oriented to the south-east. It is mentioned as a nuraghe with a smelting furnace. In visual contact with the nuraghi S'Omu 'e S'Orku, Monte Eghedda and Brandanu.
descriptions.NUR5540: Of the nuraghe tower only very little remains. The lintel and three courses. Around the ruins of a small village.
descriptions.NUR4238: Together with the nuraghe Cabonu, it lies at the border between the territories of Ussaramanna and Turri.
descriptions.NUR8195: Nuragic structures are difficult to read as they are either stripped or covered by more recent construction phases at Medau Canè. The site was inhabited during the Bronze Age, in the Nuragic culture.
descriptions.NUR3242:
A single-tower nuraghe on the basalt plateau of Su Gollei, in the area of S'Iscampiatorju. It is a perfect tholos. The south-facing entrance, with the stair on the left and the guard cell on the right, leads to the central chamber.
