To the east there are traces of a first outer wall in a crescent shape, leaning against the nuraghe itself; further east a second outer wall surrounded the Nuragic village.
descriptions.NUR6327: Single-tower nuraghe with a giants' tomb nearby
descriptions.NUR3657:
At present a circular tower (diam. 1.50–2 metres) can be seen at the centre of an irregularly quadrangular fortified bastion that follows the rocky contour of the hill.

The entrance to the bastion, on the south-east, has a rectangular opening (width 0.80 m – height 1.05 m above the fill) and is topped by a massive lintel. This doorway leads into a short corridor (depth 2.50 m – height 2.05 m – max. width 1.75 m) that turns left and then stops where it has collapsed.
descriptions.NUR19549: Three courses of roughly dressed limestone blocks survive. The stair opening and perhaps the chamber roof are visible on the summit. The south-east side of the entrance has collapsed. Military structures lean against the north and north-east sides. Partly enveloped in Mediterranean scrub, the nuraghe is in a good state of preservation. It is a single-tower nuraghe, originally accompanied by a village. Structures currently reused are also reported in the immediate vicinity.
descriptions.NUR988: On a hill, consisting of a central tower and a bastion, with a large village that the dense vegetation conceals almost entirely. Two large huts survive, one identified as the 'meeting hut'; at least four more can be glimpsed in the scrub.
descriptions.NUR4574: The Sisini nuraghe stands on the summit of a low hill in the countryside at the entrance to the hamlet of the same name. It has an original and uncommon plan that follows the model of sacred wells. It consists of a tower with a circular base preceded by a massive square bastion.
descriptions.NUR6427:
Imposing three-lobed nuraghe with the two added towers collapsed but the main tower in good condition, although largely buried. It must have served to defend the nearby village with the nuraghe of Pettu 'e Murtas, only 200 metres away as the crow flies, and to guard the Badde valley below.

For further information:
descriptions.NUR634: Situated about a hundred metres north of the Rio Merchis and less than 300 metres west of the proto-nuraghe known locally as “Nuraghe Magossula”, the monument is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan (diam. 13.70 x 11.70 m) that survives to a maximum height of 2.00 m with four courses on the north side, while on the south-west there is only a single course and on the south-east, where the entrance must have been, the wall face is entirely absent.
descriptions.NUR16022: Damaged nuraghe of which it is not possible to indicate the form
descriptions.NUR19581: Single-tower nuraghe with a chamber bordered by at least one niche, built in trachyte.
descriptions.NUR3227: The central tower, almost completely destroyed (maximum surviving height 2.70 metres), is built, like the rest of the visible structures, in polygonal masonry, using exclusively granite blocks. On the south side a trilithic structure survives that could be interpreted as the remains of the entrance to a mural staircase giving access to the tower's terrace or to a possible second chamber.
descriptions.NUR5717: Complex nuraghe with village. Ruinous and hard to read because it is covered by collapsed masonry. It occupies an area used for agriculture and pastoralism. Built of granite blocks, its central tower and two lateral towers are visible.
descriptions.NUR5027: "Nuraghe s'Omu e s'Orcu" lies near Santa Giusta. The Nuragic stronghold consists of a bilobed central tower, characterised by a lateral tower and a second tower situated in the central part of the complex; the towers are circular, about 7.50 m in diameter, and built of medium- and small-sized quadrangular and polyhedral ashlars laid, with chinking, in regular courses.
descriptions.NUR5290: The site is partially eroded. Only the entrance corridor and part of the staircase remain. It is thought that the use of the nuraghe may date back to 1550 and continue until 900 BC.
descriptions.NUR4474: The site stands on a gentle hill at the edge of a plateau where sherds of pottery from various periods abound. We are at 194 metres above sea level and seven other nuraghi are visible all around. The structure is undoubtedly complex: the central part, although damaged, preserves an almost intact niche, a room filled with collapse debris, and some wall remains that suggest further rooms and structures around it. The building material is granite.
descriptions.NUR5730: Characterized by a large Nuragic settlement to which several archaeological excavations have been carried out.
descriptions.NUR6208: The tower, circular in plan (13.20 x 13.50 m at the top where the roof is missing) with its entrance facing south-east, survives to a maximum height of 9.30 m, while the average height is about 8.50 m. The masonry consists of carefully worked trachyte blocks laid in regular horizontal courses with occasional chock stones.
descriptions.NUR5969: The nuraghe appears to be formed by three towers; inside, three niches can be seen. On the left a staircase leads to the upper floors, and around it the remains of the Nuragic village are visible, with some red stones from the area. To the left of the nuraghe lies a small necropolis.
descriptions.NUR3672: Nuraghe never excavated, almost completely buried
descriptions.NUR3206: Single-tower nuraghe, the entrance is not visible; its diameter is about 9 metres. It belongs to the complex of nuraghes at Su Padru.
descriptions.NUR1007: A single-tower nuraghe of limestone, about half covered by vegetation, stands on the edge of a cultivated area inside a bend of the Riu Filibertu. State of preservation: good. The existence of a surrounding village is hypothesised.
descriptions.NUR6044: Remains of the nuraghe Sos Iscaledos, greatly damaged.
descriptions.NUR818: Single-tower nuraghe belonging to the complex of nuraghi at Su Padru. Partially destroyed
descriptions.NUR5808: Among the nuraghes in the Mores area, this one is the best preserved and most intricately structured, thanks to its three towers connected by a bastion. Surrounding it, traces of the ancient village are visible.
descriptions.NUR6141: It is a single-tower nuraghe that still has its tholos intact. It almost certainly belongs to the type with a sub-floor chamber, which is easily recognisable. The entrance has collapsed but it can be entered carefully by sliding over the lintel astride the guard chamber.
descriptions.NUR6247: In a total state of ruin, a few boulders of the basal circle survive, identifying its type. The boulders are large and the chamber has collapsed together with a mass of debris that has accumulated over time. Prickly pear plants and thorny shrubs have colonised the site.
descriptions.NUR6089: The exact name of the nuraghe (with the mezzanino above the entrance corridor) should be S'Olteri.
descriptions.NUR5382: Nuraghe destroyed by the scolopi fathers in 1730 for the construction of some buildings in Chia. Eighties-era construction further erased all traces.
descriptions.NUR4738: The oldest nuraghe in the Villa Sant'Antonio area is Nuraghe Spei, a corridor nuraghe with a central body consisting of an ellipsoidal structure measuring 22 x 7.5 m, on whose eastern side open the three lintelled entrances of the internal tholos chambers, which are connected to each other by intermural passages. On the opposite side a second, larger ellipsoidal body abuts it, also with three lintelled entrances, now blocked.
descriptions.NUR8749:
It is striking that the monument is not signposted in any way, in an area where, moreover, there is a sign for every sheepfold. The wall looks out over the Boncaminu plain, and from it one can see the village of Lu Brandali and the site towards La Colba.

The wall looks out over the Boncaminu plain, and from it one can see the village of Lu Brandali and the site towards La Colba.
descriptions.NUR2485: Remains of a simple single-tower tholos nuraghe built with basalt blocks from Montiferru. The structures survive to a height of 5–6 courses. The nuraghe stands on the summit of a dune of what was, until the 1950s, the Is Arenas desert. It has direct visual contact with the large four-lobed nuraghe of Tradori, on the opposite side of the road.
descriptions.NUR3909: Built of polygonal blocks of local basalt, it survives only in a few courses, to a maximum height of just under 2 m. The trapezoidal entrance, fitted with a monolithic lintel and oriented to the south, can be seen. The nuraghe stands near the crossing of the Rio Strampadorzu, where the stream forms a small waterfall.
descriptions.NUR11156: Unfortunately only a few boulders remain, but they still show the presence of the monument. Like most sites in our municipality it has been robbed, and it bears witness to the intense human occupation of the area. Part of the surrounding territory is known by the same name as the nuraghe. m.u
descriptions.NUR2873: The few remains of the nuraghe have ended up, following land reclamation and improvement works, beneath a blanket of brambles and other shrubs, and behind a curtain of barbed wire. Nevertheless, traces of the monument are evident through the large stones of the basal circle.
descriptions.NUR6066: Again, with no concrete evidence of foundations or anything else, we must rely on the historical memory of those who pass on orally what they heard from their forebears. Concretely, one must admit that in the 1970s and 1980s numerous land-reclamation and improvement works took place, affecting many sites reduced to shapeless heaps of stones. Probably a bachelor's nuraghe. See 'Ajanu.
descriptions.NUR2894: The nuraghe stands on a low hill in an area now used for pasture and arable land. Its very poor state of preservation makes it impossible to determine its type or analyse its architectural development. A stretch of the outer perimeter survives, forming a semicircle. The blocks that make up the masonry are of granite, only roughly dressed and of medium–large size; in the short visible stretch they are laid in irregular courses.
descriptions.NUR4808: The area around the Nuraghe Su Angiu is further enriched and distinctive due to the nearby Punic and Roman villages, the remains of which are still visible today.
descriptions.NUR587: Single-tower nuraghe, near which traces of a settlement and a sacred well are found.
descriptions.NUR2501:
Complex nuraghe of which only some wall stretches of the towers and probably of an outer wall are visible. The collapse and the dense vegetation make it difficult to interpret the spatial development of the complex.

A modest Early Neolithic village extends to the south-west.

The complex shows interesting superimpositions, including the ruins of an old medau with buildings constructed of dry-stone walls.
descriptions.NUR6163: Subtrapezoidal in plan, it stands on a granite outcrop. It is built of large granite blocks laid in polygonal masonry. The only well-worked block is the lintel, with a sub-triangular section shaped to divert the thrust of the overlying structures onto the jambs. On the more accessible sides, to the west and east, the nuraghe is enclosed by a curtain wall, of which the west stretch survives for about 17 m.
descriptions.NUR11260: Single-tower nuraghe, half-destroyed, at Su Billianu in Uri
descriptions.NUR12817: Of this nuraghe only a small amount remains, just a few large stones arranged in a circular form. Perhaps the first course of stones from the foundation.
descriptions.NUR11150: The shape of this single-tower nuraghe is still clearly visible, although only a few stone blocks have survived.
descriptions.NUR5972: Locally also known by the place name of the land "serra porcheddos". It would appear to be a single-tower nuraghe, even though the whole surrounding area shows a high probability of survey evidence. — Tripod Nuraghe. For other nuraghi whose names refer to objects of use or connected with worship, compare Nuraghe Trìbides, Cogàlzos, Manos d'òro.mu
descriptions.NUR19714: The nuraghe is easy to locate because it lies near the tanks of the drainage plant of the Central Sardinia Reclamation Consortium. Large schist blocks outcrop on the eastern slope of this hill, but a more detailed reading of the site is not possible because its state of preservation is very poor.
descriptions.NUR3067: The nuraghe is now reduced to a heap of massive ashlar stones, though the base circumference is still discernible.
descriptions.NUR6201: The place name certainly dates from the medieval period and is due to the fact that the nuraghe rises on the very outermost hilltop, directly overlooking the valley below. Several stone circles, variously collapsed, are still visible. The interior can be visited, and the entrance, rigidly oriented towards the south-south-east, can also be seen.
descriptions.NUR3365: Nuragic hut. It is circular, built of flat stones of various sizes laid one on another in courses that corbel inwards towards the centre. The wall is conical: about 60 cm wide at the base and about 40 cm wide at the top, with a surviving height of about 130 cm. To the south-east the wall breaks off for about 100 cm (perhaps the entrance) where the structure has collapsed, probably because of wild olive and mastic trees.
descriptions.NUR6381: Nuraghe partially buried with a special lintel, worked and currently broken into two. Nearby is also a dolmen of the same name.
descriptions.NUR5833:
The building is a single-tower nuraghe that retains its chamber, accessible via a corridor with a stair and a niche, and provided with three subsidiary chambers.

The tower is built in its lower courses with large blocks; above these are set smaller boulders, carefully dressed and laid in regular horizontal courses.

Several light openings, triangular or quadrangular, arranged almost in a spiral, are visible on the outer wall face.

A short distance from the nuraghe a domus de janas has been cut.
descriptions.NUR3359: It has a fine intact tholos and, at a height of about four metres, two niches that certainly communicated with the staircase leading to the upper floor. The boldness of the construction is evident, since the two niches should weaken the ogival structure, which instead appears solid and strong in all its beauty. Part of the upper floor, accessible from the outside, is also visible.
descriptions.NUR4613: Single-tower nuraghe incorporated within Medau Su Conti. In recent times it was used as a support for the masonry of a house. It is partly stripped of its outer stones but overall retains a good height. It is the only accessible nuraghe in Carbonia, even though it lies inside a fenced plot.
descriptions.NUR2545: Something cyclopean stands before something wonderful. The site is known as a nuraghe but it does not have all the features of the structure that would allow the monument to be identified with certainty. It could be a ceremonial circle. The boulders are about 5.00 m x 0.90 x 0.90. Unable to achieve the proper connecting curvature between one boulder and the next, they have been regularly chamfered. I believe I have located the quarry not far from the site. mu
descriptions.NUR4388:
It stands on a high rocky spur whose shape has strongly influenced the appearance of the monument, which in its surviving part shows a portion of an internal room with a sub-rectangular plan and rounded corners.

The surviving wall face of this room is about 3 m long and 1.55 m high.

For the rest, the whole nuraghe is reduced to the collapse alone, which is very extensive and located mainly on the southern slope.
descriptions.NUR5428: the rock that is visible at the site) and a landslide of medium to small stones
descriptions.NUR5162:
The structure is badly damaged and only a circular alignment of large stones, set on the natural rock, remains, with an estimated maximum diameter of 11 m; no other details or planimetric articulations can be determined.

The surviving basal course consists of large, roughly dressed blocks whose dimensions range from a maximum of 1.04 m long by 0.41 m high down to a minimum of 0.35 m by 0.17 m.
descriptions.NUR3538: Archaic corridor nuraghe with an ellipsoidal–sub-quadrangular plan, built of polygonal basalt blocks. A few basal courses remain visible for less than 2 m in height. The nuraghe stands on a solid foundation of outcropping bedrock that forms an integral part of the structure.
descriptions.NUR6196: It is also known as Matzone (Maxia records Massone). Su crastu covaccadu probably comes from the presence, not far away, of a giants' tomb that had a trilithon and a cist covered with a flat lintel, hence su crastu covaccadu. It is a single-tower nuraghe and its features cannot be made out because it is completely covered by plants and bushes. However, the Nuragic spring that supplied drinking water (so the owners told me) until a few years ago is noted.mu
descriptions.NUR10641: Single-tower nuraghe whose layout is hard to determine because of the collapses and the dense vegetation. Even so, the outer wall face of the central tower can be made out. A probable refacing is visible on the west side of the central tower, with two or three courses surviving in places.
descriptions.NUR4487: On the main summit of the rocky ridge, beneath the remains of a modern rectangular structure, the ruins of a probable nuraghe are visible, almost unrecognizable.
descriptions.NUR6384: Single-tower nuraghe with access to the collapsed tholos.
descriptions.NUR3266: Significant difficulty discouraged by the ascent. Several abrupt drop-offs. At certain points, walkways and ropes are provided to serve as handholds.
descriptions.NUR4945: Built of squared limestone blocks, it stands at least six courses high and has a well-defined, legible façade even from a distance. It was investigated in the 20th century with unsystematic excavations undertaken by the then Honorary Inspector Cornelio Puxeddu. About 25 m west of the nuraghe and at a lower elevation, a building of uncertain purpose was erected in modern times; it has a cemented stone wall with an iron door and an upper skylight.
descriptions.NUR10883: It is an archaic construction of presumably oblong shape extending on a north–south axis for a presumed length of 20 m and a width of 13.40 m. The building is erected entirely on the pre-existing bedrock with a steep slope towards the north. The south façade consists of two courses of large, rough granitic-marl blocks without any dressing, of uneven size and superimposed with an irregular archaic technique without any alignment on horizontal planes...
descriptions.NUR6435: The nuraghe Su Cuttu stands on the Alghero–Ittiri provincial road. It is a single-tower nuraghe that has suffered considerable disturbance. Only a few boulders remain in their original position. It belongs to the complex of nuraghi in the Cuga valley.
descriptions.NUR3098: Nuraghe forming part of the complex of nuraghi in the Cuga basin. Apparently bilobed, but a third, semi-destroyed tower beneath the lake waters cannot be ruled out. All around, the remains of a vast Roman settlement are clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR2946: The Nuraghe Su Guzzu is a single-tower nuraghe built of limestone blocks with basalt reworkings. It lies about 7 km south of Paulilatino and, together with the Nuraghi Forreddos, De Mesu and Codas, forms a quadrilateral between the territories of Zerfaliu and Paulilatino. The lintel giving access to the inner chamber is very interesting; the tholos is intact but unfortunately the chamber is cluttered with a good deal of collapse debris.
descriptions.NUR10511:
Single-tower nuraghe destroyed during the clearing of the field for cultivation, although traces of ceramic finds can still be detected during survey.

The site is hard to read because of the cultivation; it would therefore be desirable to recover the materials found on the site and document them in order to reconstruct the site, even if only partially.
descriptions.NUR15214: Indeterminate nuraghe; only a few courses survive, immersed in lush vegetation that makes the layout of the structures hard to read. Several wall stretches, probably belonging to huts, are present in the area. Various pottery fragments are also found in the vicinity.
descriptions.NUR3220: Some know it by the place-name "runda de suerzones" but also "de sa paghes" because on that site, in the mists of time, two families ended a feud. The monument is in an advanced state of decay. Nevertheless, important features can be observed that make it a "unicum" in the archaeological landscape of which I have information. The surrounding area is interesting. mu
descriptions.NUR3936: Corridor nuraghe particularly eroded. The corridor is composed of a flat band with stone slabs. Transversal niches have been carved.
descriptions.NUR19703: Located in the channel between Monte Alibertu and Cammeddare, the nuraghe appears almost destroyed and further data cannot be recorded.
descriptions.NUR3564: A single-tower nuraghe built on a spur of granite rock, following its contours and in places incorporating it. The interior of the nuraghe is filled with backfill earth and large blocks that belonged to the masonry. The nuraghe stands in a commanding position on the coast with a broad view over Tavolara and Capo Ceraso. It is a watchtower of which five courses of stone survive on the outside and about two metres of masonry inside.
descriptions.NUR3871: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The nuraghe is built of polygonal blocks of local basalt and survives for 2–3 courses laid in a circle to a maximum standing height of about 2 m. The entrance, fitted with a well-worked monolithic lintel, like the blocks of the jambs, faces east. The passage between the inner chamber and the entrance can still be traced, although the whole upper covering is missing.
descriptions.NUR6347: The monument stands on the basalt plateau that extends at the southern foot of the Marghine chain, south of the Rio Tossilo. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a niche, a corridor staircase, and a central chamber flanked by two opposing niches. The tower, circular in plan, survives to a height of 2.90 m on the north-west side, with 6 courses, and 2.20 m on the north-east side with 5 courses. The masonry consists of medium and large blocks, carefully worked and laid in regular horizontal courses.
descriptions.NUR2567: Located about 300 metres from the nuraghi Sas Casas and Columbos, respectively to the west and south-east, the monument is a single-tower nuraghe with a niche and a corridor staircase, and a central chamber bordered by three niches arranged in a cross. The tower, circular in plan, survives to a maximum height of 4.70 m with seven courses to the south-east, while the minimum height is recorded to the south-west at 0.40 m with only a single course: the wall thickness ranges from 4.25 m to 4.75 m.
descriptions.NUR1174: Single tower of irregular shape in basalt and porphyry (Inglese)
descriptions.NUR4138:
A rather massive towered structure can nevertheless be distinguished. This tower stands off-centre in relation to a kind of walled “enclosure” that appears to have been very thick and abuts it on the northern side, while a facing of large blocks involves the western sector of the tower.

Another outer wall is visible from north-west to south-east, almost doubling the tower’s perimeter.
descriptions.NUR5897: The monument, built in polygonal masonry with granite stones, is of the corridor type and has a sub-circular plan; the entrance leads, through a small lintelled corridor, to a central circular chamber without a roof, which gave access to two further chambers, now inaccessible because of collapses.
descriptions.NUR6029: It is a fine example of a single-tower nuraghe where the tholos is still intact. Continuing up the staircase, which winds clockwise, certain constructional features emerge that are similar to other sites in the territory of Chiaramonti — a distinction made today that did not exist three thousand years ago, since the territory was a contiguous extension of that of Ploaghe. m.u
descriptions.NUR5504: It spends most of the year beneath the waters of Lake Cuga. Destroyed single-tower nuraghe; only a few courses of the original structure are visible. During the excavations before the dam works, the archaeologist Contu found an important Nuragic model boat here.
descriptions.NUR3679: Complex nuraghe, completely buried and destroyed; only three courses of about 1.20 m in height remain of the main structure, with a diameter of about 9/10 metres.
descriptions.NUR568: Poor visibility and the vegetation cover prevent a proper reading of the monument. Part of the east and north sides can be seen, with a wall face built of large polygonal basalt blocks laid in four to five courses to a height of 3–3.50 m. The whole building is buried to a considerable depth, especially on the western side. The inner chamber has collapsed and the surviving part is filled with collapse debris, as can be seen from the top of the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR3232: The tower is almost completely destroyed; the interior, where there are three niches, is easily accessible. The best-preserved part of the tower stands about 4 metres high. It is easy to reach and lies about 300 metres from the road. Around the nuraghe there is a magnificent prickly-pear garden.
descriptions.NUR4075:
It stands imposing in the locality of Pauli on a limestone plateau. The monument consists of a central tower almost 7 metres high, against which two further added structures lean, now almost completely collapsed. From the entrance you enter the main chamber, partly covered by collapse debris.

The nuraghe is surrounded by an outer wall and the remains of a village, whose huts are used as goat shelters. A few hundred metres away lie the remains of two giants' tombs.
descriptions.NUR2739:
The nuraghe S'Ulivera is of mixed type; it has corridors, and above them rises a tholos chamber with niches that has partly collapsed.

Around the nuraghe some remains survive of what was once a village. A few metres away, several well-worked basalt boulders are visible, which almost certainly belonged to a building of cultural significance.
descriptions.NUR3166:
It is a single-tower nuraghe in a state of serious deterioration. The perhaps improper description comes from the fact that these monuments speak and shout like living beings. History of our forebears, of a great people who managed to express their own culture of peace and solidarity among small shepherd-kings federated in a single great state. What was said elsewhere for the many monuments in the territory of Chiaramonti applies here.

(photo Mario Unali)
descriptions.NUR3203: Single-tower nuraghe, attached to a colonial-era farmhouse. Very close to the asphalted road.
descriptions.NUR9750: The Su Mamuccone nuraghe is today completely ruined, standing on a calcare monolith near the homonymous sheepfold, located in a position optimal for having an elevated view of the entire area.
descriptions.NUR12621: Partially destroyed and located near the industrial zone of Portoscuso.
descriptions.NUR6430: It is a complex nuraghe in poor state of conservation.
descriptions.NUR15861: The nuraghe stands on a rocky ridge west of the Domus de janas and is completely hidden by dense vegetation. The outline of the central tower can barely be made out, but a few partially visible courses suggest a single-tower structure.
descriptions.NUR2812: Simple-type nuraghe, completely ruined, reduced to a heap of rough blocks, about two metres high.
descriptions.NUR5881: It is reported in historical memory of those who worked on the construction of the artificial basin at Madau in the second half of the 1900s. There are no on-site evidences of other types of constructions or foundations.
descriptions.NUR19212: Single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan and a remaining wall face reduced to 2–3 courses.
descriptions.NUR1297: Like the Oes nuraghe, it does not have a traditional tholos roof but one made with wooden substructures.
descriptions.NUR2280:
It is a coursed Nuragic construction that rests on the rugged profile of the hill, which dictates its irregular plan. At the top a small chamber filled with collapse is visible; no entrances or other structural elements can be seen.

It should be noted that building on this rocky spur, where movement is extremely difficult and dangerous, is hard to understand: it looks more like a lookout post than a defensive structure.
descriptions.NUR17157: In the historical dictionary by Goffredo Casalis, the nuraghe is listed as Sa Corti deis Bacus.
descriptions.NUR8618: Nuraghe/proto-nuraghe characterised by a sturdy, broad central tower and the remains of two other towers that are barely visible. The nuraghe stands on a hilltop, in a natural stronghold that commands an extensive view, so that the ruins of the castle of Las Plassas can easily be seen with the naked eye.... traces of Punic/Roman pottery suggest the overlapping of several civilisations.
descriptions.NUR3542: On a hillock beside the Atzara–Belvì provincial road, blocks of granite have been found, almost completely buried and arranged in a circle, which are thought to belong to a nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR2021: The nuraghe is completely collapsed and only some residual stones remain of the entire structure.
descriptions.NUR736:
Single-tower nuraghe.

It stands on private land and is partly in good condition.
descriptions.NUR3751:
The monument appears as a large sub-circular enclosure (diam. 18 m), with a wall thickness of 2.50–3 m and a maximum surviving height of 1.50–2 m, showing two courses.

The masonry consists of large polygonal blocks laid in horizontal courses.

From what can be seen, it is most probably a corridor nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR14956: Nuraghe now completely vanished but studied by Silvestro Ghiani in the 1940s. S. Ghiani in “La Trexenta Antica.”
descriptions.NUR6095: Complex nuraghe, the architecture cannot be determined due to the poor state of the structure.
descriptions.NUR4102: The nuraghe Su Nuraxi of Gonnosnò lies about 400 metres east of the village, near the industrial area. It is a single-tower nuraghe largely destroyed and covered by its own rubble and vegetation. Only a few courses remain.
descriptions.NUR4591:
Single-tower nuraghe now called “Su Nuraxi”, though it was once better known as “Cocconi”.

A second tower is suspected to have existed in the past. A distinctive feature is that a Byzantine burial complex has been brought to light inside the central tower: a sacred use from which the monument evidently never strayed. Indeed, another of its long-standing names was “Sa Parrocchia”.
descriptions.NUR11472: Remains of the Nuraghe Su Oi. Currently only the base course remains.
descriptions.NUR5439: Very eroded nuraghe with a tholos and collapsed walls
descriptions.NUR3471: The nuraghe, located in a grazing area on a granite outcrop, is irreparably destroyed. Its lintelled entrance can still be seen, filled with collapse debris. As for the chamber, again because of the collapsed state of the nuraghe, only a short stretch on the northern side can be made out.
descriptions.NUR15225:
Popular memory records the existence of a complex nuraghe beneath the Su Pisu Fort.

The reconstruction commissioned by the Region for the Phoenician Sulky project shows a Nuragic village on the hilltop overlooking the harbour and the ancient city.
descriptions.NUR2308: Proto-nuraghe of sub-triangular form, built of basalt. It is located a short distance from n.ghe Su Pranu in the westward direction.
descriptions.NUR6045: It is in a fairly advanced state of ruin, yet the monument retains some features that make it a distinctive building. Indeed, in our area there are several other nuraghi that have an opening to the north. "Nuraghe del gallo" or "di Pullo", the Latin name. In popular imagination the rooster is an apotropaic representation of the devil.
descriptions.NUR5505: Almost nothing of the tower remains.
descriptions.NUR9246: Proto-nuraghe with multiple towers, almost completely destroyed. With its height it dominates the entire area of "Su Padru". The name derives from the fact that the nuraghe is situated on a very sharp hilltop, from which Punzu Rudu is seen.
descriptions.NUR9630:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan (diam. 9.60 m) reduced to a heap of ruins. The wall face, made of medium-sized stones laid in horizontal courses, survives to a maximum height of 2.20 m with 3–4 courses.

Because of the collapse it is not possible to know the internal layout of the monument.
descriptions.NUR5522: Complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and four lateral towers enclosed within a large outer wall provided with ten towers, for a total of at least 15 towers. Seven of the outer wall's towers are visible, while the others lie buried under the mantle of earth. In the excavations of recent years the structures belonging to the complex nuraghe have been brought to light, of which two of the lateral towers are discernible.
descriptions.NUR18066: Nuraghe with a sub-rectangular plan (13.40 m long on the NS axis and 10.60 m wide on the EW axis), characterised by straight long sides and convex short sides. The nuraghe is completely destroyed and practically illegible. It lies in the territory of the municipality of Ittiri.
descriptions.NUR3954: Destroyed nuraghe and no longer visible
descriptions.NUR2060: The nuraghe is completely ruined, reduced to a heap of blocks about 2 metres high. Impenetrable because of the dense vegetation. A complex structure with a Bronze Age settlement and remains of Punic-Roman houses.
descriptions.NUR5712:
The nuraghe stands on the edge of the Corte plain, south-west of the town. You follow the Nuoro–Orani farm track and stop at the little bridge that crosses the Rio Su Saju.

On the left, about 200 metres away (near the shepherd's hut), lies the nuraghe. The site occupies a dominant position over what was a possible access route to the Corte plain and made use of the water from the nearby stream, which in ancient times was much more abundant.

Altitude 510 m a.s.l.
descriptions.NUR5158: We find it listed in the map of the 1844 State General Census, as Nuraghe Numassi.
descriptions.NUR4916: The nuraghe, built of blocks laid in courses of differing shapes and sizes, is a complex type with the particularity of the fusion of the central tower, originally single, with six later buildings, joined to one another by curtain walls, which surround it.
descriptions.NUR14921: Nuraghe. It is located on top of a hill near a pond, adjacent to a building. Covered with stones and vegetation.
descriptions.NUR2869: Nuraghe built into a stone masonry and tholos structure between emergent rocky masses.
descriptions.NUR4813: One may suppose that the natural terrace was provided with some raised chambers that supplemented the natural cavities and were later demolished. The nuraghe stands out against the present-day village of Morgongiori, guarding the valley. For this reason it can reasonably be assigned the function of controlling the territory and maintaining visual contact with the lava bastion of Funducarongiu behind it, in which the cave of Scaba 'e Cresia, the subject of this study, opens.
descriptions.NUR1823: Complex nuraghe, probably of the "a tancato" type with a courtyard and an added tower, built of limestone. The majestic wall faces of the main tower survive largely intact. Inside, on the SSE side, a trapezoidal lintelled opening is visible, preceded by a passage whose course is interrupted by the collapse of the structures. Tampering by looters is evident.
descriptions.NUR6309: Complex nuraghe with a unique plan. Known in the IGM incorrectly as "Giaga 'e Puliga" (which is the name of a nearby nuraghe).
descriptions.NUR16020: Single-tower with tholos, built in basalt
descriptions.NUR3941: Nuraghe on an acrocoro from which the Coros is seen. Single-tower, built with local limestone ashlar, its tholos has collapsed inward.
descriptions.NUR3314: Single-tower nuraghe belonging to the complex of nuraghi at the site Su Padru. Currently very modified.
descriptions.NUR5388:
The construction, which looks very rough, is also incomplete and reduced to only three basal courses at the best-preserved points.

Other ruins and wall alignments come into view as one moves from the road into the dense vegetation.

In general a very rough building technique is found, using large granite blocks merely rough-hewn into elongated parallelepiped shapes, laid in irregular courses that are now very disjointed.
descriptions.NUR4249: Complex nuraghe with three towers, probably added. Calcare ashlar. Nearby are the remains of a village and two giants' tombs.
descriptions.NUR4250: The Nuraghe Bruncu Mannu of Villa Sant'Antonio stands on a rise a short distance from the SP 37. At first glance it looks like a single-tower nuraghe whose top is missing and whose interior is invaded by the flowing crowns of several shrubs. Along the perimeter the entrance can be made out, topped by an interesting lintel. The interior is choked with collapse debris.
descriptions.NUR1175: Complex nuraghe with a central single-tower nuraghe and a quadrangular perimeter wall with four towers.
descriptions.NUR5466: Complex nuraghe. Only a few remains of the central tower and bastions survive; it was demolished to build the nearby state road. Many finds from the Roman and early medieval periods attest to the monument's use in those periods as well.
descriptions.NUR2947: The monument, of simple type, stands at the edge of a small clearing on a granite outcrop that is incorporated into the walls for long stretches. Its outer plan is vaguely elliptical, with a lintelled entrance leading into a corridor 3.50 m long; to the left of this corridor another lintelled doorway presumably gives access to a staircase, or at any rate to a beaten floor that in ancient times must have led to a terraced space.
descriptions.NUR5872: Single-tower nuraghe with a tholos, unfortunately in advanced state of degradation, protected by a large outer wall with a deep underlying drop, of which today only a fortress remains inaccessible.
descriptions.NUR2583: With the filling of the artificial basin at Oliai, it is found on the summit of a small island.
descriptions.NUR3311: The complex consists of a proto-nuraghe, a village and a giants' tomb. The proto-nuraghe, of the "corridor" type, has a vaguely ellipsoidal plan and abuts a granite outcrop. The masonry is made of large polygonal blocks of granite.
descriptions.NUR12182: Inside there is a lintelled corridor, a semicircular niche, the staircase leading to the upper floor, and the central chamber; the latter, originally roofed with a tholos but now uncovered, has the classic circular plan with three niches arranged in a cross. The outer wall, up to 4 m high, is built of medium-to-large trachyte boulders.
descriptions.NUR18933:
The monument, of complex type, consists of a central tower and a bilobed bastion.

The central tower is entered through a lintelled doorway. The bastion probably enclosed two towers, one to the east and the other to the south-west:
descriptions.NUR3593: It lies within the municipality of Nuoro. It is not the only Nuragic site in the town, but it is the only one to have been systematically excavated. Around the nuraghe the remains of a village dating to about 1600 BC (the early Nuragic period) are visible; it originally consisted of more than 200 huts. Historical sources also report the presence of several domus de janas along the hill.
descriptions.NUR3803: Nuraghe site located just a few metres from the cliff formed by the Rio Carrabusu. The state of conservation is precarious and the structure is partially buried.
descriptions.NUR4923: More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR17939: Within a farm, it is in good conservation condition and access is possible from the top.
descriptions.NUR3926: Structures that are hard to read because of the dense vegetation, probably belonging to an archaic corridor nuraghe. A few blocks of the upper part can just be made out among the vegetation. The plan appears vaguely elliptical, with a straight section facing south, in which a doorway with a monolithic lintel opens onto a flat-roofed corridor about 4 m deep. The nuraghe is built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. A
descriptions.NUR2719:
A single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal basalt blocks.

The building is completely covered in brambles and climbing vegetation, so that only a few stretches of the external wall face can be seen. From above one can observe the collapse debris filling the inner chamber. Modern and contemporary structures, enclosures and shelters, lean against the nuraghe on the west side.
descriptions.NUR11484: Complex nuraghe with settlement, village. If this designation is incorrect, it might refer to a nuraghe without a name, listed as number 480 by van Dommelen. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR6367: A ruined single-tower nuraghe overgrown with vegetation. About five courses of the masonry survive.
descriptions.NUR4647: Currently, in the site we can observe an old stone enclosure, below which several stones belonging to the nuraghe are visible.
descriptions.NUR3013:
The monument stands on top of a steep hill, partly covered by dense woodland and used for grazing. The single-tower nuraghe has collapsed on the east side, so the entrance is not visible.

It survives to a maximum height of 5.50 m and a minimum of 1 metre, with wall faces built of granite blocks laid in irregular courses.
descriptions.NUR3809:
Reduced to a state of total ruin, most probably as a result of road excavation and land improvement works. It merges with the one not far away at Pedru Canu.

Nuraghe della smilace (Smilax aspera). This is very probably a Paleo-Sardinian term. It indicates that when the name arose the monument was covered in smilax, a thorny climbing plant.
descriptions.NUR5620: The nuraghe Thorra, like the nuraghe Sas Melas, stands on a low hill rising at the bottom of the valley, surrounded by higher ground; from this position it closely controls an important ford on the Rio Torra, a tributary of the Rio Mannu. Three hundred metres away to the west lies the eponymous giants' tomb, recorded by Taramelli who, strangely, makes no mention of the nuraghe at all.
descriptions.NUR2543: The nuraghe is a complex building consisting of a central tower against which a bastion with three secondary towers linked by curtain walls with a concave-convex course has been built: two towers stand on the front, the third is set off-centre to the right (towards N). The bastion has a curved eastern front (height 5.00 m) in the centre of which the entrance opens (width 1.10 m; height 1.60 m), now partially blocked.
descriptions.NUR1241: Nuraghe situated atop a mass of granite dominating the Gulf of Arzachena Cannigione
descriptions.NUR5739: Reduced to a great ruin, it still shows some constructional features of that period. The foundation traces and part of the wall fabric are clearly visible. Land-improvement work has contributed greatly to its disappearance by piling up the stones.
descriptions.NUR3614: The nuraghe Tinteriè appears to be a single-tower nuraghe with very irregular masonry. It has a circular plan 12 m in diameter and preserves its entrance intact; this leads into a curvilinear corridor 4.50 m long roofed with flat slabs. On the left inside the passage is the stairwell, while the interior is blocked by collapse.
descriptions.NUR5589: Four-lobed, rock-cut. The upper and lower chambers are visible through a breach in the upper surface layer. Surrounding them, traces of the settlement are visible.
descriptions.NUR9808:
The remains of this nuraghe lie on a trachyte outcrop overlooking the Rio Tossilo, near the bend where the Birori–Cobercada road passes the nuraghe Urighe.

Unfortunately, only a few large boulders survive, arranged in a double row on just a few stretches. No survey is possible.
descriptions.NUR2775:
Reduced to the level of a ruin, only a few circles of vaguely dressed, disorderly stones in courses remain. The remains poorly show the constructional features, despite some stretches of courses still in order.

Nuraghe of the Ginestroni site, in Logudorese Tirià. See Tiriàles.
descriptions.NUR6063: The “Tittiriola” at Bolotana is a single-tower nuraghe built of basalt blocks, bounded by an outer wall and set within a village whose traces are still appreciable. It has an internal stair chamber that is currently impassable because of collapses, and on the upper part, corresponding to the entrance, a large window surmounted by a lintel is clearly visible. Near the structure a sacred well is visible that appears to have been covered over in relatively recent times.
descriptions.NUR5855: It is located within the territory of the comune of Pozzomaggiore (SS). Partially destroyed, about 2 metres high, covered with debris.
descriptions.NUR5820: Of the monument, in very poor condition, only some fragments of the first base course are visible, in pink trachyte.
descriptions.NUR3042: Single-tower nuraghe on top of a basalt outcrop, a natural fortress. Inside, a shelter for shepherds was built. Today it is abandoned.
descriptions.NUR5577: The Tolinu nuraghe, set in a fine position on a plateau overlooking the Tirso valley, is an imposing complex Nuragic monument composed of a large central tower of truncated-conical shape surrounded by a bastion that incorporates several smaller towers.
descriptions.NUR3283:
Complex nuraghe considerably buried.

The central tower, which retains intact the tholos, reaches a height of about 10 metres on the northern side.
descriptions.NUR5669: It preserves the intact tholos covered by a large slab. It is a complex structure with a lintelled entrance and a partially collapsed stairwell. On the left an opening leads to another tower in good condition but with the ashlars fallen from the tholos inside it. To reach the upper floor one must use the side facing north-east, from which to admire the 360° panorama over the village with huts still distinguishable amid dense vegetation and among the various collapses.
descriptions.NUR17857: Only a few traces of the nuraghe remain, as the stones were removed to build a road.
descriptions.NUR6191: The nuraghe is built of soft trachyte blocks, not very large. The foundations rest directly on the bedrock, which also forms a natural bastion that was then finished and completed by the nuraghe's builders by adding large blocks. Nearby the base of a Nuragic hut is visible. Single-tower nuraghe with village and outer wall with probable seven towers
descriptions.NUR3041:
The monument lies less than 200 metres south-east of the giants' tomb of Santu Bainzu, which must have been the reference funerary area.

It is a single-tower nuraghe at the centre of a large village bounded by an outer wall that can only be traced in part. The tower, circular in plan (13.12 x 2.75 m; diameter at the top of the surviving masonry 11.90 m), with wall thicknesses of 4.30 m to the east and 3.60 m to the north-west, survives to a maximum height of 7.25 m and 12 courses to the south-east.
descriptions.NUR3237:
The nuraghe, set in Mediterranean scrub, is a fine prehistoric single-tower building constructed of black basalt stones of fairly regular size.

The inner chamber, reached through a well-preserved corridor, has two side niches and a terrace, situated at a height of about eight metres, accessible via a flight of steps.
descriptions.NUR6263: The Nuraghe Tradori is built of black basalt. The entrance has a pointed arch and is very low. The chamber, from which two low corridors lead off, is circular in plan with a very high false dome (tholos) that is still intact. Outside the nuraghe there is a stretch of walling made of large stones; on its outer face, facing south-east, a passage opens that descends deep down and appears to reach beneath the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR4963:
In the municipal territory of Gonnosnò stands the nuraghe Tramatza which, together with the nuraghe Emmauru, overlooked the valley of the rio Figu, a winding watercourse among the hills at the foot of the plateau.

Only a few traces of the nuraghe remain; the original structure was a single-tower nuraghe with a truncated-conical shape, built by superimposing stone blocks, and contained the main chamber inside, connected to the outside by a narrow corridor.
descriptions.NUR4880: Embedded within the vegetation of this nuraghe, only a few courses remain. It has never been excavated or studied.
descriptions.NUR5218: It is a three-lobed complex nuraghe, with a central tower, three perimeter towers arranged in a triangle and joined by straight-curving curtain walls, and an internal courtyard with an entrance facing south-east. Finds of female-headed incense burners, draped figures and anatomical votives testify to a probable cult of the goddess Demeter.
descriptions.NUR620:
Nuraghe consisting of two towers and a courtyard on the south side. Built of large roughly dressed blocks of red trachyte. A megalithic double-faced wall runs south from the nuraghe, of which about 35 m of the basal courses survive. To the north, and partly to the east and south, a village of huts extends, of which various basal circles remain.

A few metres west of the nuraghe there is a well now blocked by collapse debris.
descriptions.NUR6059: Likely a three-lobed nuraghe, if not even four-lobed; the planimetry is almost impossible to read due to the poor state of preservation.
descriptions.NUR2546: The name would suggest a possible three-lobed structure, almost entirely destroyed, of considerable dimensions. Above the main tower there is an entrance covered by bushes.
descriptions.NUR3046:
The monument appears as an artificial hill at the base of which the material produced by clearing the surrounding fields has been piled up.

Its very ruined state, the fact that it is buried, and the rubble that partly covers it do not allow a correct reading of the building's ground plan; nevertheless, it must have been grand and of complex type, as the very name Tresnuraghes attributed to it also suggests.
descriptions.NUR1344: It lies within the municipal territory of Nuoro. The region takes the name Intranuraches because three massive nuraghi stand on three rocky "mammelloni". Unfortunately the nuraghe is in poor condition and looks more like a fortification, built by making full use of the granite outcrop.
descriptions.NUR2323: Covered with stones gathered from a collapse.
descriptions.NUR3484: Unfortunately, the nuraghe is covered by vegetation. It is believed to have a well-preserved tholos.
descriptions.NUR17385: Single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, of which only a single course of limestone blocks laid in a curvilinear line survives, 4 metres long. To the north-west a stretch of wall is visible, made of blocks set in a row for a length of about 3.20 metres.
descriptions.NUR3963: It is submerged beneath the waters of Lake Omodeo.
descriptions.NUR3700:
It consists of a few basal circles that nevertheless define its construction character precisely; this character belongs to a broader human context in the surrounding territory with numerous other features close by. Its function as a lookout, or if you prefer as a defensive post, is paramount.

- Nuraghe del mestolo. In the matter of kitchen utensils it is curious that this nuraghe lies about one kilometre as the crow flies from Nuraghe Cogàlzos (see entry) which means "spoons (of bone)". See Truddàriga.mu
descriptions.NUR2754: The possible staircase is visible. The tholos has collapsed.
descriptions.NUR6102: Quadrilobate nuraghe, the central tower (with a mezzanine) retains intact the tholos roof of the chamber.
descriptions.NUR717: Submerged nuraghe in the basin of the lake on the hillside
descriptions.NUR6365: Damaged nuraghe, with three courses remaining. Likely nuraghe belonging to the category of "uncompleted" nuraghes.
descriptions.NUR5610: It is a tholos nuraghe with an outer wall, located near the village and in a precarious state of conservation.
descriptions.NUR5792:
The Nuraghe Tunis is in a precarious state of preservation, particularly the central tower and the southern parts of the four-lobed bastion; of the latter the two northern towers can be seen, with stretches of the three adjacent curtain walls, and the eastern boundary wall of the courtyard with the large window connected to the staircase leading to the wall-walks.

Around the ruins of the bastion, stretches of straight walls and parts of circular buildings emerge.
descriptions.NUR5397: The Tuppedili nuraghe, situated along the road to Mandas, is also of particular archaeological importance. Still awaiting full study, the site has so far yielded a large number of artefacts datable to the Nuragic and Roman periods.
descriptions.NUR3821: Structure of uncertain interpretation built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The building stands on a small natural rocky spur and has an elliptical plan. It measures about 17 m in length and about 11 m in width at the central point. The northern, western and eastern parts consist of one to two courses of large and medium-sized polygonal blocks, while the southern part has three courses built with the same technique.
descriptions.NUR3199: Single-tower nuraghe, with part of the tholos remaining and the access portal restored.
descriptions.NUR6423: It is a single-tower nuraghe with its roof collapsed.
descriptions.NUR5895:
Even though the present state is nothing but a series of collapses affecting the site in its entirety, I must admit that it inspires interest and respect for the majesty of the cyclopean stones, few of which are still in situ. The state of devastation is evident.

Nuraghe della Tortorella. mu
descriptions.NUR792: Nuraghe in good condition, built of red granite stones. Equipped with a spiral staircase. Likely part of a complex nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5409: The nuraghe Tutturuddu stands on the first promontory after the nuraghe Nuridda, guarding a path that descends towards the village of Tuili. Only a few traces of this Nuragic monument survive. The name Tutturuddu comes from the Sardinian word tutturu (rolling pin), referring to the shape recognisable in the remains of the ancient structure.
descriptions.NUR5728: A ruined, never-studied nuraghe of which a few courses remain. A singular and remarkable worked stone near the proto-nuraghe, above a few completely unidentifiable ruins, could be interpreted as a fragment of a shaped tumulus originally located above a domus de janas with a façade, or as a covering element of a giants' tomb.
descriptions.NUR10197: It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe. Survey is difficult because thorny shrubs have colonised the whole structure. Traces of the Nuragic village huts are clearly visible, scattered around the central tower in a limited area, not as incorrectly reported by others.
descriptions.NUR2097: Nuraghe of uncertain type built on a rocky spur, utilizing its elevations; characterized by a powerful collapse, particularly located to the north-northeast. Situated at 418 m.
descriptions.NUR3600: The nuraghe Tuvurunaghe, built of trachyte on the edge of a rocky plateau, has a single-tower layout with an almost intact tholos roof. It follows a "classic" plan: three cross-shaped niches and a helical staircase opening to the left of the entrance corridor, which is partly blocked by fallen stones. Near the nuraghe several circular hut bases are visible, indicating the presence of a settlement.
descriptions.NUR3239: Single-tower nuraghe, built of local basalt blocks. The outer wall face survives to a maximum height of about 4 m. The entrance is identifiable to the south-east, from the remains of the entrance passage, with the stairwell opening on the left and a niche on the right, leading to the inner chamber. The latter survives to about half its original height and has a large internal niche facing south.
descriptions.NUR5624: It is a “corridor nuraghe” standing at the centre of a broad outer wall within which the ruins of a large village can be made out. The monument stands on the basalt plateau that stretches between the settlements of Dualchi and Borore. About 180 metres to the north-east lie the remains of the giants' tomb of the same name, while to the north-west is the giants' tomb of Putzu Iu.
descriptions.NUR3280: Nearby are also some nuragic huts.
descriptions.NUR2622:
Other towers, perhaps five in number, lean against the central tower. The whole complex is hard to survey because of the trees and tangled thorny bushes that block access (just as well!). Inside, almost the entire structure can be visited and the harmonious development of the whole massive and majestic construction can be appreciated.

The word ùi, which is probably Paleo-Sardinian.
descriptions.NUR6348: Single-tower nuraghe, ruined with its tholos collapsed and overgrown with vegetation
descriptions.NUR3004: Structures belonging to an archaic-type nuraghe, a corridor nuraghe. The building is made of large polygonal blocks of local basalt. The plan is vaguely quadrangular, although the monument cannot be read accurately because it is completely overgrown with vegetation.
descriptions.NUR3861: A single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. Almost completely destroyed, it appears as a heap of basalt stones. The first two courses of the base can be made out on the south side.
descriptions.NUR3736: A tholos nuraghe, presumably single-tower, although its poor state of preservation and the dense vegetation cover prevent a full reading of the monument. Built of polygonal basalt blocks, the outer wall face on the west side survives to a maximum height of about 3.50 m. The nuraghe has been heavily robbed, as can be deduced from the heaps of large blocks on the plateau to the north of it.
descriptions.NUR9159: Through a gap between the large ashlars of the upper part of the outer wall face, one enters the corridor that housed the helical staircase giving access to the upper part of the tower. In fact, the corridor ends against two large lintels that are completely buried. The nuraghe is in very poor condition. It is partly enveloped by mastic shrubs and prickly pears, the cause of the collapses and the burial, up to about two metres from the floor level.
descriptions.NUR2614: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan (SE-NW axis 11.75 m; E-W axis 11.50 m) and a wall thickness of 2.70 m to the NW and 3.85 m to the west; the maximum surviving height is on the NW side, at 3.60 m over 8 courses of well-worked, medium and large basalt boulders laid in regular horizontal courses.
descriptions.NUR2984: The monument was demolished by a bulldozer. What remains is a spread of ashlar fragments belonging to the wall masonry.
descriptions.NUR3777: A single-tower nuraghe with ten courses of porous basalt still in place. It lies in the territory of Sorradile (OR); its present position is curious, for after the Omodeo artificial reservoir was built the monument stands on the lake shore, subject to the continual fluctuations of the water level.
descriptions.NUR4972:
The Urceni nuraghe complex was built at 900 m on the summit of a rocky spur.

A well-preserved architectural monument of great merit for the skilful symbiosis between the built element and the natural element. Several holm oaks grow in the area.

One is faced with a well-preserved architectural monument of great merit for the skilful symbiosis between the built element and the natural element. Several holm oaks grow in the area, partially obscuring the view of it.
descriptions.NUR15924: It is located on the summit of a hill, precisely at the intersection of two watersheds. From this fortunate and strategic position, the nuraghe dominates the entire surrounding plain.
descriptions.NUR2985:
It is a circular single-tower nuraghe (diam. 13 x 13.50 m) with a corridor niche and a provisional chamber of two niches; the existence of a staircase is probable but not certain.

The tower survives to a maximum height of 5.54 m and is built of medium-sized blocks, roughly dressed and laid in horizontal courses that are not always regular.

A corridor 4.25 m long leads into the circular tholos chamber (diam. 4.20 x 4 m), now reduced to a maximum height of just 3.10 m with 7 courses.
descriptions.NUR11587: Of this monument, reported by Lamarmora and other authors but not by Taramelli, every trace has disappeared. It seems to have been located not far from the railway and to have been destroyed by the very works connected with the building of Borore railway station.
descriptions.NUR6411: In Florinas, among cultivated fields, we find this small proto-nuraghe known as Urzeghe, "characterized by a corridor-like structure with parallel corridors attached to a small circular tower."
descriptions.NUR2658: Usanis, located at a short distance from Osidda and situated at the top of a rocky spur, was a complex structure composed of two towers.
descriptions.NUR3126: Nuraghe partially collapsed, with a dozen courses still standing, located beside two rural buildings
descriptions.NUR5497: Single-tower nuraghe and traces of a settlement.
descriptions.NUR8747:
At the head of a dominant ridge overlooking the beds of two watercourses that fed the pond behind the harbour, before it was transformed by the present buildings.

Remains of Nuragic towers beside the abandoned house.

There were probably two towers, contiguous, one of them built on a granite outcrop, exactly like all the other Nuragic towers of Santa Teresa. The perimeter of the tholos is clear, collapsed inwards and filled with ashlars for at least three metres in height.
descriptions.NUR5770:
The nuraghe, of complex type, consists of a central tower around which a three-lobed bastion was built enclosing a courtyard.

The towers have a curvilinear profile, as in the nuraghe Santu Antine at Torralba.
descriptions.NUR3829: Corridor nuraghe. The structures are completely covered and hidden by dense marsh vegetation. The building stands on a small alluvial rise between the Rio Cispiri and a parallel stream. As for the structures, only a few courses of polygonal basalt blocks can barely be made out.
descriptions.NUR12843:
Destroyed nuraghe located on the summit of the hill of the same name.

Unfortunately, little remains of this monument, but it is still of considerable significance.
descriptions.NUR573: Nuraghe "a tancato": on the front face of the main tower there is a wall of irregular shape that encloses a smaller tower and a courtyard situated between the two towers.
descriptions.NUR4076: Oral sources insist that a nuraghe stands on the summit of Bruncu Zinnibiri, without specifying whether it is a single tower or a more complex structure. Immediately below the few ruins of the “nuraghe” the village extended, also the target of continuous illicit digging; one of the surveys carried out led to the discovery of a cultural deposit near which charcoal remains were observed and where abundant ceramic material was collected.
descriptions.NUR505: Oral sources insist that a nuraghe stands on the summit of Bruncu Zinnibiri, without specifying whether it is a single tower or a more complex structure. Immediately below the few ruins of the “nuraghe” the village extended, also the target of continuous illicit digging; one of the surveys carried out led to the discovery of a cultural deposit near which charcoal remains were observed and where abundant ceramic material was collected.
descriptions.NUR534: Nuraghe in very poor condition and completely covered by undergrowth.
descriptions.NUR617:
Zinnuri, in a municipal rural park characterised by centuries-old olive and wild olive trees and a rural shelter. Around the spring there is a picnic area with wooden tables and benches and a car park.

The nuraghe Zinnuri and the spring of the same name are found here.
descriptions.NUR17032: Marks the boundary between the municipal territories of Siamaggiore, Solarussa, and Tramatza.
descriptions.NUR3574: Single-tower nuraghe, around the traces of a settlement. At this site the famous bronze tablets of Tzricottu were discovered.
descriptions.NUR3971: Single-tower nuraghe in an advanced state of decay.
descriptions.NUR2557: Complex nuraghe of quadrilobate type, the central tower is surrounded by bastions with four towers enclosing a courtyard. Around it, traces of a settlement and a wall remain.
descriptions.NUR3721: Complex nuraghe formed by a central tower onto which an added body is grafted, consisting of two lateral towers linked by a curtain wall and with an intermediate courtyard from which the central tower is accessed.
descriptions.NUR3246: Complex nuraghe with an adjacent giants' tomb and a spring, called "Roia Zrighidanu", which flows into the Riu Pizziu further downstream. It is a settlement used up to the Imperial Roman period, and the rectangular structures in the area of the nuraghe probably date from that period. Five hundred metres from the nuraghe, the researchers Dyson and Rowland report a Roman necropolis with at least 32 cist tombs.
descriptions.NUR5687: Nuraghe Zuanne Orane lies about 5 km north-west of Norbello, a short distance from the road leading to the church of Sant'Ignazio. It is a single-tower nuraghe built of basalt blocks in a fair state of preservation.
descriptions.NUR6312:
The nuraghe has been dated between the 14th and 12th centuries BC.

It is notable for the use of large basalt blocks carefully squared, in particular the jambs and lintel of the entrance.

At the entrance, on the left, is the ramp that led to the upper terrace, while on the right there is a niche in the walling. In the chamber one can see the three large ogival niches in the walls, the central hearth, and the tholos that forms the ceiling, still intact.
descriptions.NUR3634: Nuraghe probably unique because composed of two adjacent towers similar in type and dimensions.
descriptions.NUR5208: Single-tower, of limited architectural value but of significant strategic importance, as it allows control over the entire Gulf of Palmas.
descriptions.NUR4404:
Nuraghe now completely demolished, of which a single course of part of the foundation remains.

Among the evolved nuraghi of Serrenti, this one at Nuraxi and the one at Bruncu Siliqua belong to the concentric-addition type. Nuraxi is four-lobed, similar in form to Su Nuraxi at Barumini (Lilliu's Lower Nuragic I phase), while Bruncu Siliqua has a central tower 14 m in diameter and at least three secondary towers.
descriptions.NUR13635: This nuraghe was identified through a letter sent to Nurnet by a reader of the page. The nuraghe appears to have been destroyed and incorporated into a large rural building. This is the origin of the name "Medau Mannu".
descriptions.NUR4118: Destroyed by the construction of modern buildings.
descriptions.NUR4394: Of this nuraghe no traces remain as it was completely destroyed during the construction of a vineyard.
descriptions.NUR10339: It is an age-old wild olive tree, certainly the oldest in the territory of Chiaramonti. In summer hundreds of sheep shelter beneath its branches, and at night hundreds of birds and other animals roost in it. I personally reported it to the Sardinian Forestry Authority, which has taken it into its care. I am its godfather.
descriptions.NUR714: Its position relative to the terrain's orography is really strange! Or rather, it is clear as day, since the fortified wall facing it on the slopes of Monte Zennaru declares its function of control and surveillance.
descriptions.NUR1551: It is a hilltop surrounded by a wall probably of the Nuragic period, partly buried, never investigated, near which the baetyl (the Bulzi warrior's head) was found. From it one commands all the not few nuraghi that existed in the surrounding area.
descriptions.NUR9214: The sources available to us report that the proto-nuraghe was studied by the archaeologist Ercole Contu, before the construction of the Cuga dam, around the 1950s/60s; unfortunately the same texts tell us that the body of the nuraghe was dismantled for study precisely because it had unusual forms. Subsequently, with the approval of the Ministry, it was used as a foundation for the Cuga dam. The tower was 6 metres high.
descriptions.NUR6843: In the countryside around Samatzai there are several scattered menhirs. Many of them, once standing, now lie overturned at the edges of paths and farmland; some have become and are used as boundary stones between one village and another, like the one still visible on top of the hill Bruncu sa Furca, where a prehistoric village may have stood. This standing stone is 1.30 m high, with a quadrangular section, rounded at the top, and without any particular signs of working.
descriptions.NUR12847: Nuragic village with remains of Roman-period dwellings, most of which were destroyed by the commune during the eucalyptus reforestation.
descriptions.NUR13499: Inscribed stones, petroglyphs with concentric circles and cups
descriptions.NUR19421:
A spring above a travertine limestone cliff produces a constant dripping down a sheer wall overhanging the bed of the Flumendosa. The continuous flow of water has created limestone concretions and allowed lush maidenhair fern to grow.

This unusual cascade falls into a pool suitable for swimming in the summer months. The dripping is heavy in winter, gentle and tranquil in summer.
descriptions.NUR8513: Vast and complex archaeological site, comprising at least two villages, a probable necropolis with an associated building that may have been of cultic use, and nearby also a furnace.
descriptions.NUR17274: Nuragic gate that leads to the rock above the cliff.
descriptions.NUR16903: It is located within the territory of the comune of Uras; given the construction technique used, it is likely that the structure dates to the Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR19607: The well, situated to the south of the cave and a short distance from it, is oval in shape. It was cut into a rock outcrop that defines its north side and, partially, the east and west sides. A masonry structure built of parallelepiped blocks completes the east and west sides and the whole of the south side.
descriptions.NUR19229: The monument is in a good state of preservation. It consists of a rectangular lintelled entrance, from which a flight of four steps leads down to a dromos. The ceiling of the dromos is covered with a flat arch of limestone slabs, while the side walls are of dry-stone construction. At the far end of the dromos is the doorway giving access to the well chamber proper, which is permanently full of water.
descriptions.NUR13049: Well of undefined period, often indicated as Roman but possibly Nuragic.
descriptions.NUR16967: The Nuragic well/spring was built at the edge of a rocky outcrop with trachyte ashlars. It is ovoid in shape and descends to an approximate depth of about 2.50 m. The wall on the north side continues from ground level for a rise of about 2 m and for an equal width. In recent times a watering trough for livestock was built nearby.
descriptions.NUR15788: Well located a short distance from the nuraghe Unia, along the catchment of a stream, of probable Nuragic origin
descriptions.NUR17002: Nuragic well concealed. It has been completely sealed with bricks and cement to make it undetectable.
descriptions.NUR16834: Nuragic sacred well currently under study and excavation. The reconstruction is hypothetical.
descriptions.NUR12566: It is located within the municipal territory of Pula (CA) inside the archaeological area of Nora.
descriptions.NUR11028: A well of probable Nuragic date and probable sacred use, situated 70 m west of the quadrangular tower. The well is built of well-shaped ashlars in limestone and volcanic rock, has the remarkable depth of about 30 m, and has yielded a large quantity of material of Nuragic, Punic and Roman date.
descriptions.NUR20286: Probable Nuragic well in poor condition and relatively isolated. It still has an active perennial spring. Noted and photographed by Sergio Melis.
descriptions.NUR8645: Remains of two sacred wells of the Nuragic period, set about 150 m apart. The first well is almost entirely buried. The second is in excellent condition, with an entrance formed by a semi-buried staircase. Its cylindrical shape has a diameter of about 2 m and a depth of about 3 m; it is built of stone blocks laid in horizontal courses. The presence of two sacred wells suggests a sacred centre of considerable importance.
descriptions.NUR8644: see sacred well Bau Crabas I
descriptions.NUR11928: The sacred well was excavated by diggers using a backhoe, and they found numerous bronze objects sold on the black market. The current state of the well is very poor, covered by moss and mud.
descriptions.NUR10424:
Sacred well, situated inside the 13th-century Romanesque chapel dedicated to Saint Anthony of Padua.

Access is through a hatch to a flight of steps leading down to the sacred well, which lies perfectly positioned beneath the Christian altar.
descriptions.NUR10004:
The monument stands in the marly basin of Coni at the foot of the Valenza hill, in the historic region of Part'e Alenza, between the Marmilla and the Sarcidano. The sacred well of Coni, built of basalt blocks in pseudo-isodomic masonry, although lacking a vestibule, follows the classic architectural scheme of Nuragic wells.

The monument consists of a descending staircase protected by a corridor (2.60 m long) and an underground chamber that encloses the spring vein.
descriptions.NUR8161: The village consists of three sacred wells and a series of circular huts. The best-preserved well lies in the northern sector of the area. Built of local schist blocks, it abuts a small natural rock face to the south-west. The entrance to the chamber is off-centre relative to the axis of the tholos. The latter has collapsed on its northern side. The area in front of the well's entrance chamber is bounded by a series of curvilinear walls at different levels.
descriptions.NUR10849: The village consists of three sacred wells and a series of circular huts. The best-preserved well lies in the northern sector of the area. Built of local schist blocks, it abuts a small natural rock face to the south-west. The entrance to the chamber is off-centre relative to the axis of the tholos. The latter has collapsed on its northern side. The area in front of the well's entrance chamber is bounded by a series of curvilinear walls at different levels.
descriptions.NUR11536: From Tharros.info. Position not precisely defined
descriptions.NUR2666:
It dates to the 11th century BC. A temple built of isodomic limestone ashlars, it is a work of fine architecture. The outer walls are decorated with rows of bosses carved on the ashlars. Water is channelled into the well through channels and from there into an external basin.

It has some affinity with the Predio Canopoli well at Perfugas.
descriptions.NUR12846: The Nuragic sacred well of Is Molineddus lies in a valley rich in springs. From the little information Spano was able to gather, it consisted of a rectangular building with an entrance on the west side, built of large blocks laid dry. Behind the building a spring rose from the rock and collected in a round well, also made of large stones.
descriptions.NUR11026: The “rotunda” of Sa Corona Arrubia in the territory of Genoni, also known locally as “Santa Maria S'Ungroi”, is a unique sacred building of the Nuragic period at Sa Corona Arrubia-Genoni. Of the monument, mentioned by Taramelli who considered it a Nuragic sacred well, the entire base ring survives, consisting of an isodomic basalt wall face with two and in a few places three courses preserved, with a small niche and a few blocks belonging to a bench.
descriptions.NUR12657: Built by the Sardo-Nuragic people, the well is presumably about 2,700 years old. It was discovered in 1883 during earthworks for laying the state railway tracks; it is assumed that valuable finds were lost. Of the original 40 steps, 22 remain. Various finds such as rings and coins were recovered, all now kept in the Cagliari Archaeological Museum.
descriptions.NUR20022: The sacred well of Nanni Ecca lies on private property; a fence more than 2 metres high protects a large private area, and within a scrubby patch are the remains of the well, which retains its entrance and part of the chamber but lacks the "cupola".
descriptions.NUR13616: Sacred well temple, one of the most refined in Nuragic Sardinia, follows the layout with a vestibule leading into a stairway that connects to the well chamber. The building is constructed of perfectly worked limestone ashlars laid in regular courses. The vestibule, rectangular (width 2.70 m; depth 1.88 m), with a perfectly paved floor, has two bench-seats along the walls, each formed from two worked blocks.
descriptions.NUR8697: The Sa Linnarta complex, a three-lobed nuraghe with numerous associated huts and a beautiful sacred well, is, according to experts, one of the most important Nuragic sites in the Baronia.
descriptions.NUR13310: The archaeological site stands a few dozen metres from the Christian-medieval one, set among centuries-old olive trees. It is divided into two areas: in the first you will find a sacred well temple, dating to the Final Bronze Age (12th century BC), embraced by a sacred enclosure (themenos) shaped like a keyhole. Built of finely worked basalt ashlars with precise techniques, the temple is a jewel of perfect geometric forms.
descriptions.NUR13620: The well consists of a rectangular, paved atrium that leads to the stairwell through a strongly tapering trapezoidal passage; the stairwell, about 6 metres long, leads down to the underground chamber, which is sub-circular and covered by a tholos, where the water table is intercepted. The structure is built of local marl blocks, regularly squared, bush-hammered and laid in staggered courses with earth inserted between the bedding planes.
descriptions.NUR8615:
Built of granite blocks, it consists of a circular courtyard, a vestibule – a small space linking the courtyard and the well – and the well itself, reached from the vestibule by several steps; the spring lies 17 steps down.

Excavated completely in 1938, the sacred well of Sa Testa has an overall length of 17.50 metres. It was a place of worship for spring waters. Numerous finds came to light during the excavations, such as Punic-period incense burners.
descriptions.NUR12964: Rock-cut chambers used and modified from the Neolithic. Nearby are the remains of a Nuragic village. Sacred well dismantled with mechanical equipment. Some sandstone blocks and T-shaped ashlars remain. Where the well or temple once stood there is now a crater.
descriptions.NUR20122: “Su Posidu”, meaning treasure. A very unusual well set between two enormous granite boulders, about 60–80 centimetres apart and 5–6 metres high. A series of schist steps, set between the two rock spurs, deliberately worked and cut, form a double staircase that allowed easy access to the central part of the well, where the precious liquid was found: water, what treasure was as precious to the people of that time as water?
descriptions.NUR17300: Situated in the locality of the same name, in the countryside around the village, a Nuragic sacred well of which only a few remains are visible today. The monument is of isodomic type and therefore of very refined workmanship. Numerous blocks of the sacred building can be recognised scattered near a recently built well that has effectively replaced the ancient one.
descriptions.NUR8115:
