Romanzesu is one of the most important settlement and cult complexes of Nuragic Sardinia, with about a hundred huts, five cult buildings — a sacred well temple and four "megaron" temples — and a large ceremonial enclosure. It is built of local granite.

The area develops around the sacred well temple, built into the rock from whose fissures spring water emerges. It has an access stair and a circular chamber built with regular courses of carefully worked blocks.
descriptions.NUR10744: The sacred well, or well temple, is undoubtedly the most evocative example of a sacred building among those so far discovered and studied in the Mediterranean basin. This type of building, belonging to the rich Sardinian civilisation, dates back to the long and varied Nuragic period. It was conceived as a place for performing the various rites connected with the water cult.
descriptions.NUR7034:
consisting of domus de janas of the horizontal-projection and pit types (1, 2, 3, 4), the other of pit-type domus de janas (5, 6, 7).

Tomb 1 is particularly remarkable, the result of several construction phases: originally of the pit type with an antechamber and a large main chamber, it was later given a long access corridor in place of the pit and enlarged to the right of the main chamber, incorporating three small burial chambers from a neighbouring tomb.
descriptions.NUR21001: An interesting site in the territory of Villa Sant'Antonio. Situated about 2 km south-east of the village, it shows probable remains of domus de janas, channels, cup-marks, basins and a symbol that the locals believe refers to fertility. The whole ensemble suggests a probable cult area of the pre-Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR19819: Remains of a megalithic circular structure with an apparent entrance portal.
descriptions.NUR20253: Likely domus de janas, currently used as a dog kennel. It is probable that other domus de janas existed in the area, now destroyed due to building activities.
descriptions.NUR20142: Reported by a resident of Osilo. The domus is not photographable, hidden by brambles and shrubs. To be verified.
descriptions.NUR21163: Fountain whose architectural form recalls several clearly nuragic analogies
descriptions.NUR17888: On site the carved stones belonging to the nuragic fountain still remain, presumably the nuragic fountain was destroyed during the works for the construction of the water trough complex.
descriptions.NUR21172: It consists of a façade and a small courtyard. On the façade there is an architrave lintel opening for the collection of water. The space has a semicircular plan and walls that gently slope inwards.
descriptions.NUR21179: Generally known as Su Corrazzu dessu Estiu, it is so large that its circuit measures no more than a hundred ordinary paces, and it is built of enormous stones with the wall about 30 palms high on one side and half that on the other. Inside and around there is a great mass of ruins. The simple folk who live there believe an evil angel dwells within, so many fear to approach it, and only the most courageous dare go there in September to search for some marvellous flower of prodigious virtue that benefits whoever picks it. But all who have gone have laboured in vain, because the spirit of the place hides it. This place and this spirit are the subject of wondrous tales among the people of Fluminimaggiore, and anyone who tries to dissuade them speaks in vain.
descriptions.NUR3169: A small isolated hill in the middle of ploughed fields. Many maintain that a nuraghe lies completely covered with earth inside it. The upper crowning of stone ashlars also suggests this.
descriptions.NUR20343: It is a couple of hectometres from the church of Santa Lucia. At first glance it looks like a single-tower nuraghe, but it could simply be the top of a large complex nuraghe buried inside a hillock formed over the millennia. What is visible is somewhat ruined: a few courses, a cavity that may be the top of the central tower or the end of the stairwell.
descriptions.NUR14925: Well, probably belonging to a Nuragic village. It is located on the top of a hill, inside a vineyard.
descriptions.NUR19605: South of the nuraghe and near the village huts there is a rectangular structure cut into the ground to a visible depth of about 150 cm, about 120 cm wide and about 250 cm long, lined with trachyte boulders of various sizes. The interior is almost entirely filled with collapse boulders and vegetation, making it difficult to determine its dimensions and structure correctly.
descriptions.NUR21140: Giants' tomb destroyed, from which two lateral walls remain; traces of excavation by tomb diggers are evident.
descriptions.NUR20350: Heaps of ashlars typical of an ancient settlement abandoned and covered by woodland, and various stretches of wall, mostly circular: on the south side there is a wall about 5 metres long, almost straight, and a small circular wall further down, while on the west side of the settlement we find a circular wall of large blocks in 2–3 courses, suggesting a Nuragic date.
descriptions.NUR21141: It is an unidentifiable structure without an appropriate archaeological excavation. Limestone slabs set vertically, adjacent, tall but not very thick, are visible; a semicircular structure emerging from the ground, built of limestone blocks and with two openings. A long circular row, perhaps delimiting the structure, at the top of which cavities covered by a few slabs can be seen. Further west, a structure with two adjacent vertical limestone slabs positioned to the north, with another slab to the right while to the left there is a wall of ashlars. Traces of tomb-robbers' digging are evident.
descriptions.NUR2672: It has a quadrangular plan with a rounded profile and a maximum surviving height of 3.65 m on the south-east side, with five courses, while on the north-west it is 2.00 m with four courses. The masonry consists of large, barely dressed boulders laid in very irregular horizontal rows. The building has two coaxial entrances, the first to the ESE and the second to the WNW, linked by a corridor that runs orthogonally to the structure's long axis.
descriptions.NUR12270: Located on the edge of a cliff, less than 400 metres north of the "Pattada" nuraghe, now reduced to a heap of rubble, it is covered by shrub vegetation.
descriptions.NUR14235: The nuraghe has an irregular elliptical shape; the total circumference is about 50 m. This massive structure is crossed lengthwise by a corridor 15.2 m long, running right through with opposed entrances and lined on both walls by wide openings that lead to large niches — that is, cavities — or to the stairwell that gives access to the upper floor. The straight corridor has a trapezoidal section with a flat ceiling formed by 11 slabs.
descriptions.NUR2980: The proto-nuraghe Su Cannuju (ex S'Alzola Trigale) has a quadrangular plan, with a single longitudinal corridor.
descriptions.NUR1250: Known as Coarittos nuraghe, but there is no trace of that type of monument.
descriptions.NUR20116: The structure is built onto a natural rocky outcrop and forms an enclosure about 50 by 32 metres with an average height of about 3 metres. Access to the interior was through two lateral portals on the north and south sides. The entrances are followed by a walled corridor. Inside, a large granite boulder, which some say has the features of a mother goddess, leads them to hypothesise a temple function for the area.
descriptions.NUR1939: It is described as a nuragic enclosure by A. Moravetti.
descriptions.NUR3761: Situated about a hundred metres south of the Borore–Sedilo provincial road, the Pedru Feghe enclosure is roughly circular, with a surviving height of 2.45 m to the north-west and 2.05 m to the south-east, with four and three courses respectively, while the wall thickness varies from 1.45 m to 2.46 m. The masonry consists of medium- and large-sized polyhedral blocks laid in fairly regular horizontal courses.
descriptions.NUR20132: It is hard to say whether this was a village. Because the site lies on a steep slope, sediment has covered the structures. The area has never been excavated. Massive walls, tens of metres long and very thick, run downhill towards the river, while others run parallel to it. One particularly striking feature is an extensive wall made of two parallel lines of walling separated by a ditch about two metres wide.
descriptions.NUR21160: The reliefs at Sa Icu in Dorgali are on the basalt cliff overhanging the Cedrino, 1.2 km east of provincial road no. 38, and are attributed to the Chalcolithic. They consist of 57 geometric figures covering an area of 10 x 12 m, carved mostly in high relief (only one is incised) on three basalt blocks that protrude on average 30 cm above ground level. The figures depict: simple parallelepipeds, truncated terraced pyramids of three tiers with simple rectangular plans or with a semicircle on the longer side of the base parallelepipeds.
descriptions.NUR19917: Natural monument, eroded into columns and protected by rock overhang.
descriptions.NUR8234: Cave currently blocked by a collapse that prevents access. Inside, some ceramic fragments have been recovered, assignable to the culture of Bonu Ighinu.
descriptions.NUR8232: A shelter characterized by various rooms, one of which was inhabited from the Early Neolithic, later used for funerary purposes. The artifacts found can be attributed to the Cardial culture.
descriptions.NUR19647: A tafone that may have been used in prehistoric and protohistoric times as a shelter/dwelling by human families. Here too the walling built by humans to reduce the opening is clearly visible. At least two other more or less similar tafoni in comparable condition lie nearby.
descriptions.NUR19649: Tafone/luttoni – a rock shelter probably used in prehistoric and protohistoric times as a shelter/dwelling by human families. Its identification is not certain for lack of thorough study, so information is scarce. The only clues pointing to such an identification are other rock shelters nearby (three to be exact) and a giants' tomb a short distance away.
descriptions.NUR12969: Su Scusorgiu: "The Treasure". In this storage room, 40 complete pre-Nuragic swords were found. They are now on display at the Archaeological Museum of Cagliari.
descriptions.NUR7363: The hypogean necropolis of "Sa Perda Puntunta", better known as "Roccia dell'Elefante", consists of two domus de janas: the first is in the upper part of a large trachyte boulder and only traces of three chambers remain; the second tomb opens a little lower down on the same boulder, consists of four small cells, and is interesting and very well known for the presence of bull's-head protomes carved on the walls of the first chamber.
descriptions.NUR11032: It consists of two large outcrops of rock near the SS 131 state road. The smaller of the boulders that make up Perda Longa is thought to have been used as a "sacred stone" in the Ozieri culture period, as shown by the cupmarks carved in it and the remains of obsidian tools and pottery found around it. From: Biddas e nuraxis de su sattu de Serrenti de su Brunzu de mesu a su Ferru I, by Daniele Carta
descriptions.NUR3767: The I.G.M. marks it as a nuraghe, but there are strong and well-founded doubts about classifying it as such. It stands on the boundary between the territories of Chiaramonti and Ardara, in the area called Pittiri, at an altitude of 440 metres above sea level, and on the boundary with the areas of Truncu Nieddu and Serra di Monte Pittu. The construction is atypical and hard to classify: it is not a nuraghe but difficult to class as a hut.
descriptions.NUR19679:
The cave, about 30 metres long, has two entrances oriented north–south.

Inside, traces of wall structures and numerous potsherds are visible. The archaeological deposit shows intensive occupation from the Early Bronze Age.
descriptions.NUR12863: Megalithic enclosure with inside a toppled menhir.
descriptions.NUR12848: Nuragic village almost entirely covered by debris, vegetation, and stones from cleared lands.
descriptions.NUR8474: Remains of about twelve huts and a perimeter wall.
descriptions.NUR1935: The nuraghe is semi-subterranean, probably single-tower and single-chambered. The outer wall face is exposed in places. The inner face retains three courses that completely roof the circular chamber. The entrance lintel has been set into a dry-stone wall.
descriptions.NUR8088: The giants' tomb Sa Dom 'e S'Orcu is one of the best-preserved Nuragic monuments. Built on a slight rise in the ground, it is of the coursed exedra type. The apsidal tomb body, aligned on a SE–NW axis, is 15.20 m long. The masonry consists of medium-sized, well-worked basalt blocks laid in regular courses. In some parts of the walling the use of levelling wedges can be observed.
descriptions.NUR9868:
There are not enough elements to define it as a nuraghe. It appears to be a simple wall of roughly squared megaliths, like a rudimentary fortification for a guard post (?).

Nuraghe delle macerie. The rubble implied by the name is that of the nuraghe from which the locality takes its name. See Carràlzu. Ardu Pinzone = cardo. mu
descriptions.NUR14129: The site has yielded a two-chambered hypogeum burial cut into the southern wall of the plateau, whose upper part shows a slab of natural rock that, seen from the front, gives the monument a megalithic appearance; a small dolmen; a giants' tomb; a spring; a megalithic wall with traces of later adaptations; and a corridor nuraghe. The corridor wall includes boulders of considerable size, some of which bear linear incisions.
descriptions.NUR7997: The site dates to the Bronze Age and is built entirely of finely worked basalt rock. The structure consists of a perimeter wall that is almost totally destroyed: only the base of the well is visible, as it lacks the tholos roof (which is difficult to reconstruct), even though the chamber has remained intact. Nine steps can be counted descending downwards until they reach the water about two metres underground.
descriptions.NUR8708:
The temple of Sant'Anastasia stands near the church of the same name, in the upper part of Sardara, at the foot of the ridge that rises towards the hill of Pran'e Cuaddus, in the central Campidano.

The sanctuary, one of the most important in Nuragic Sardinia, centres on the sacred well temple.

The temple, dated to the Late Bronze Age (13th–12th century BC), is set within an articulated settlement of both civil and religious character that is still being excavated.
descriptions.NUR7106:
The site dates to about 3000 BC and was used for about 1500 years, from the time of the Ozieri culture to that of Bonnanaro.

It takes its name from the large number of skeletons (more than 200) and the rich assemblage of weapons – datable to about 1650–1600 BC – consisting of swords and daggers in arsenical copper (19 in all). The swords, with triangular blades, range in length from 27 to 66 cm and show some similarities with the swords of the El Argar culture (Spain).
descriptions.NUR8265: Sacred area of probable Nuragic origin, reused in Punic and Roman periods, where abundant building materials and ceramics are found.
descriptions.NUR11927: These are the remains of a sanctuary built in megalithic technique, set in the centre of the saddle about 100 metres from the other site to the east; at present the dense vegetation allows only four or five menhirs lying on the ground a few metres apart to be visited. I remember from a visit I made to this site many years ago that the menhirs were far more numerous, but now the thick vegetation makes it impossible to tell whether any others survive.
descriptions.NUR12888: The excavation revealed a rectangular building divided into two rooms and set inside an enclosed area. It is thought that the building had a religious function. The excavations yielded finds datable between the 8th and 7th centuries BC. The setting is bleak and typical, with abandoned military structures (built inside the sanctuary), an abandoned restaurant and a large tarmac car park.
descriptions.NUR17761: It consists of a Nuragic village, a circular temple and a megaron temple, and, upstream, a series of springs, wells and channels for capturing, collecting and channelling water towards the sacred area situated downstream.
descriptions.NUR11041: In the fissure there is a staircase of squared basalt stone, one metre wide, composed of three flights, two visible and the third covered by debris, separated by two landings. All the steps consist of two squared basalt blocks cut 'to measure' and laid with a wedge-shaped block inserted between them. Some have circular hollows cut into them, interpretable as cup-marks with a lustral function; on others, mammillary reliefs stand out.
descriptions.NUR14230: The archaeological site was discovered in 1985, entirely by chance, during clearance work for a vineyard. Excavations, which continued until 1988, identified the main core of the sanctuary, consisting of the sacred well, a rotunda that characterises part of the large building in isodomic masonry, and two cylindrical structures, interpretable as altars.
descriptions.NUR9171: This, so they say, is the area where the Castle of Burgos was initially being built at sa Pattada in Illorai, before that site was abandoned and the castle was definitively erected at Burgos... but I don't think so! ...to me it suggests something more archaic, perhaps Nuragic, ...some kind of ritual area!
descriptions.NUR8333: Two Nuragic huts are in a good state of preservation; the rest of the village is a ruin. On the south-west edge lies the pond (Paule – from which the site takes its name), which probably served as a water reservoir.
descriptions.NUR20375: On the site a few large slabs can be seen, partly embedded in the ground, partly broken and not in situ, which may belong to a dolmen-type structure. Although no archaeological material is found on the ground, the shape and size of the blocks suggest that the site should be included among areas at risk. The name recalls other dolmen toponyms.
descriptions.NUR6833:
A folk tale tells that these rocks are a married couple turned to stone by the deity for mocking the sound of the bells coming from the nearby church of Masullas during the feast of Sa Gloriosa.

It seems that in the past these statue-like rocky blocks, which geologically are nothing other than submarine lava outcrops, were worshipped by the proto-Sardinians as fertilising deities.
descriptions.NUR19417: Its entrance was narrowed and adapted in the Nuragic period so as to make it hard to find and extremely easy to defend in the event of an outside attack. The rather steep dromos, with a final drop of 8 metres, was altered by adding a retaining wall and creating an access via a narrow, steep staircase of 18 steps. Inside, traces of Nuragic-period use are clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR19681: The cave is reached by a staircase built with Nuragic technique and covered with lintels for sixteen steps, very similar to the one used inside nuraghi. The cave consists of two large chambers and a small single-cell room at the top of the cavity. On the floor of the cave there are ceramic fragments of the Nuragic period. The site is generally classified as a hypogean temple or as a refuge.
descriptions.NUR10129: Inside a lentisco trunk, probably ready for transport to the client, the sarcophagus (2.00 x 0.90 x 0.90 m) is made from a single monolithic brown trachyte of considerable size.
descriptions.NUR19894: North-west of the nuraghe Sa Scrocca Manna, a probable menhir of prismatic shape with a triangular base lies on the ground. The boulder has a flattened front face, probably produced by pecking the surface. The two rear faces show signs of working and smoothing.
descriptions.NUR19892: In the area of Monte Sa Scrocca Manna, on the boundary between the municipalities of Sant'Antioco and Calasetta, there are several structures that originally most likely formed part of a Punic and/or Roman settlement. Unfortunately, during the Second World War military works irreparably damaged their walls. Some stretches of walling, still fairly well preserved, survive, together with various squared and moulded ashlars reused in the military constructions.
descriptions.NUR10195: It takes its name from the place-name of the land. Like most of the nuraghi and other features at Chiaramonti, it too is in a state of degradation that is irretrievably compromised. Certain particularities emerge that lead me to consider it as belonging to the nuraghi with a basement level.
descriptions.NUR1501: It is a sarcophagus similar to those of Su Cannau and Sos Terrelas. Ready for a burial, or simply ready to be delivered to the client? Roman period or simply medieval? Or belonging to the Judicate period, part of the personal or family estate of one of the judges or kings of Torres or of Logudoro.
descriptions.NUR5262: The giants' tomb of San Liberno – which, moreover, is perfectly oriented towards the sunrise on the winter solstice – is only one of the many archaeological features in the municipality of Sarroch. A monument unfortunately violated by an electricity pylon
descriptions.NUR8671: Nuraghe with remains of a village and a Roman settlement.
descriptions.NUR19683: The monument, situated a short distance from the Giants' Tombs of Su Piccante and Su Ittichinzu and the nearby village of Lettu Rucratu, stands at the foot of a hill where it appears as a small spring cut into the ground, where the water table presumably emerged naturally, and lined with blocks of rough basalt.
descriptions.NUR7038: The domus de janas of Pranu Efis or S'acqua Salida, at Pimentel, are easily reached. After travelling about two kilometres along the road linking the village to Guasila, you turn left onto an unsurfaced track which leads to the necropolis after 300 metres. Some of the tombs still show traces of red ochre paint, and one in particular contains a profile resembling a bull's-head protome.
descriptions.NUR10026: Popular belief mixed with the clear memories of the old ancestors and confirmed by the regional Sardinian newspaper of the time “l'ISOLA”, reports the news of a small village where some tombs were found. Among the finds a figurine in the shape of a woman, (ocarina, or Mother Goddess?). MU
descriptions.NUR832: It is the only one in the entire territory inaccessible due to environmental incompatibility: the monument is presumed to have disappeared entirely. mu
descriptions.NUR5209: The site is completely ruined and buried. The existence of a village, probably Nuragic or pre-Nuragic, over a wide area is evident. Apart from a few spreads of ashlars, only a few walls of a hut or a nuraghe are visible.
descriptions.NUR14671: The site includes an undefined structure (WHAT COULD IT BE?) at the edge of a sheer drop; on the front it once had (now disappeared) a hollowed-out boulder like a holy-water stoup, a tiny domus de janas, the giants' tomb of Pascaredda; a dolmen, the Monti Di Deu nuraghe, the Agnu nuraghe, and the Nuragic spring of Li Paladini. The Pascaredda tomb and the Agnu nuraghe are easily reached; everything else has been left to itself and is hard to locate and reach.
descriptions.NUR12958: A village already inhabited in the Iron Age. According to the PUC the site continues to be affected by quarrying activities and, in particular, by a large dump of equipment and inert materials. A quarry where 10,000 tonnes of toxic waste from Portovesme S.r.l. were illegally buried.
descriptions.NUR6806: Three metres high. Broken transversely at mid-height and chipped at the base by the impact of a mechanical ploughshare, it tapers at the top into a kind of smooth, sub-oval mask. The design continues linearly along the sides, and at the top appears almost crowned by a distinct pair of bull's horns. The monument is unique on the Island, and perhaps in the sculptural art of continental megalithism as well.
descriptions.NUR6790:
Inside a pastoral farm, at the centre of a circular sheepfold bounded by a dry-stone wall, stands a unique and exceptional proto-anthropomorphic menhir fixed in the ground. The pillar, 1.77 m high, shows a summary rendering of a head set off from the body below by a short neck, and may symbolically evoke the phallic symbol.

It lies 500 metres north-west of the hypogeal necropolis of Monte Ozastru.
descriptions.NUR11035: In Serrenti, nuragic villages are often located near a nuraghe, as in the case of the site of Bruncu Pubusa; in other cases (Giuanni Acca, Sattu Divisu, Bruncu Abis, and Sa Serra) they are located without any nearby nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR18711: Stele with an arched stele placed at the post for a metal gate
descriptions.NUR6793: Menhir / carved stele with concentric circles
descriptions.NUR10863: Elliptical building, slightly raised on an artificial platform. Function to be verified.
descriptions.NUR4726:
On the summit of the limestone outcrop at 191 metres above sea level stands a monumental Nuragic complex that makes use of the natural rock ledge to the west and a sheer drop on the eastern slope.

The monument covers an area of about 1000 sq m and extends in plan along a longitudinal axis oriented north-west–south-east, with a probable entrance to the north.

From north to south the following can be identified: a tholos; a sub-rectangular block; a semicircular room; walls following a curvilinear course.
descriptions.NUR10857: Archaeological trace corresponding to the area of the trigonometric point.
descriptions.NUR6838: Su Putzu Nuragic village, composed of about one hundred huts surrounding a well temple, exactly Su Putzu.
descriptions.NUR13565: The slow retreat of the water, caused by drought, reveals what normally lies submerged. All around, clear Nuragic traces are visible, such as the sacred huts and other rooms typical of the period. On a small promontory stands another nuraghe, “Sa tanca 'e sa Mura”, and a little further on a third, “Tudera Alto”, of which, unfortunately, only a few of its cyclopean stone courses have survived.
descriptions.NUR12616: Remains dating to the Nuragic period located on the Red Island, about one kilometre from the coast of the commune of Teulada. The area falls within the Capo Teulada military zone.
descriptions.NUR8276: The site, dating to the Late Bronze Age (1300–1000 BC), is a complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower to which eight further towers were subsequently added, forming a bastion. The bastion is surrounded by a megalithic wall equipped with five towers fitted with loopholes. The construction mainly used granite boulders, a material available on the spot.
descriptions.NUR19915: In the area, where a site of Nuragic origin probably existed, a lime kiln was built which, in recent times, was reused as a dwelling. Adjoining it are the ruins of a recently built house. The kiln was most likely built at the end of the 19th century or the early 20th: many other kilns erected on Sant'Antioco date from that period.
descriptions.NUR19911: From the second giants' tomb, moving 50 m westwards, one finds an area where the presence of polyhedral boulders of various sizes, only roughly dressed, suggests a zone set aside for worship.
descriptions.NUR19913: From the second giants' tomb, moving 450 m northwards, one finds an area where the presence of polyhedral boulders of various sizes, only roughly dressed, suggests that a cult area was located there.
descriptions.NUR19909: Against an enclosure of probable Nuragic origin stands a block of red trachyte that at first glance looks like a hatch or an entrance slab. Irregularly parallelepiped in shape, its visible face shows a surface on two offset levels. In the upper level, at the ends, there are two holes, one round and the other rectangular.
descriptions.NUR19907: About 200 m from the second giants' tomb there are buildings of Nuragic origin whose function cannot be determined, mainly because of later alterations carried out at different times (some of them recent) and the lack of archaeological study. The surviving structures of probable Nuragic origin consist of an enclosure with cyclopean walls built of roughly dressed boulders, and the remains of two probable huts.
descriptions.NUR19903: Two giants' tombs once stood in this area, one of which has been completely dismantled. In the area where the tomb presumably stood, about ten ashlars remain scattered inside a mastic thicket. Given the raised ground level, part of the tomb may still lie buried.
descriptions.NUR19905: Two giants' tombs stood in this area, about 100 m apart. The second is the one that survives in a more legible state, although for most of its extent it is covered by vegetation and its walls are blocked by collapse. The tomb whose structure is harder to make out very probably has a rectangular chamber built of large boulders of various sizes, only roughly dressed.
descriptions.NUR8099:
The monument consists of an atrium and the spring itself from which the spring water flows.

The atrium is a rectangular space measuring 5.15 by 1.80 m, bounded on the sides by two benches of equal length built of basalt blocks and, on the left side, by a section of walling 2 by 3 m made of well-squared ashlars laid in regular courses. The floor is paved with blocks of the same kind.
descriptions.NUR19931: Between 1950 and 1960, a calcination oven was built, whose structure was very likely constructed using stones belonging to the village.
descriptions.NUR19927: To the south-east of the village are the remains of two or more tombs, probably of Punic or Roman origin. In one of these tombs the landowner saw about ten small skulls brought to light by clandestine excavation. Human bones are still present inside the tomb today. The tomb structure has been completely destroyed and most of the worked stones have been reused for other purposes.
descriptions.NUR19924: The probable Nuragic village, about 200 metres west of the nuraghe, appears to consist of about 10 huts, two rectangular and the rest round. Unfortunately all the structures are in very poor condition and in some cases barely distinguishable. The huts were built of small and medium-sized polyhedral boulders laid dry. Several pottery sherds are present in the area.
descriptions.NUR8755:
The nuraghe has yielded an extraordinary Nuragic altar. Three construction phases can be identified.

The first, perhaps of Middle Bronze Age I (16th–15th century BC), saw the laying out of a bastion and an outer wall with corridors and cells.

In the second, of Middle Bronze Age II (14th century BC), a sinusoidal trilobed bastion was superimposed, together with a new outer wall of four towers linked by irregularly straight curtain walls.

In the third phase the outer wall was provided with another tower and curtain walls.
descriptions.NUR14793:
Nothing of this monument remains, as it was buried over time and subsequently covered by houses and streets.

Some sewer excavations and the accounts of the inhabitants indicate the presence of a complex nuraghe and the village. We are also 300 m from the site of the warriors' tomb of Sant'Iroxi, known for the two hundred skulls and the swords.
descriptions.NUR5867: Site located in the Su Pranu area on a truncated-pyramidal hill. Here are found the remains of a nuraghe or, more probably, a small temple, attested by votive material found at the base of the site and along the ridges of the hillock; on its south-facing flank there are hypogeal tombs that are difficult to reach.
descriptions.NUR4974:
The monument displays a ground plan and architecture among the most extraordinary produced by the Nuragic culture. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.

The complex shows various construction phases characterised by the use of local stone: the basalt of the Giara, which largely predominates, and calcareous marl.
descriptions.NUR8556: Apart from the central tower, the complex is largely buried, making it difficult to interpret the parts that compose it. Around the nuraghe several circular rooms can be seen, perhaps the remains of a village. Also nearby is what may be a sacrificial area, called by the people of Samatzai “Sa piscedd' 'e su casu” because its particular appearance resembles a cheese form.
descriptions.NUR11735:
Su Nuraxi Serra Manalgiu, about one kilometre from the old "Ortuabis" railway station, in the territory of Meana Sardo.

Around the nuraghe there are many fallen stones and many holm oaks, which keep it good company.

Of interest one can observe a wall built with rows of stones of the same height and a chamber with a collapsed vault.
descriptions.NUR19751: The pond north of the Noccus nuraghe, about 200 m away, was formed by using a natural, roughly circular depression in the ground, bordered by rocky banks for about two-thirds of its circumference. The north and south-west banks show clear signs of human intervention: large boulders were placed on the embankment to hold back rainwater and at the same time increase its capacity.
descriptions.NUR12834:
Site where a proto-Sardinian healing god was worshipped.

Rectangular-plan temple built of large blocks, with a spring that collected in a round well. Taramelli judged that all the elements of a sanctuary with a healing character were present: a therapeutic spring and a temple to the healing deity, where the most remarkable find in Sardinian archaeology came to light. The bronze column base with inscriptions in Greek, Punic and Latin dedicated to the god Eshmun.
descriptions.NUR13502: Probable Nuragic water source from a perennial stream
descriptions.NUR19568:
The name is linked to a legend: after a human skull was found inside the cave, it was thought to belong to one of the unmarried mothers who, it is said, were shut inside as punishment until they died of suffocation.

More recently, human remains accompanied by coarseware pottery fragments have been found there. It is clear that Su Secretu is a small natural cave that must have served for funerary depositions.
descriptions.NUR8480: Neolithic period - Ozieri culture. Entrance to the western shelter - asset identification code: 95059055
descriptions.NUR19624: “Human presence on the island of Sant’Antioco is attested from the 5th millennium BC13 in rock shelters, caves, lithic scatters and tombs.” A tafone that, because of its size, was used as a rock shelter. Human use is clear, also shown by stones of various sizes, some still in their original position and others in large numbers nearby, which probably formed a wall partly closing the opening.
descriptions.NUR19781: A tafone which, because of its size, was probably used as a rock shelter. Various stones of different sizes, some still in their original position and others at the edges of the tafone, suggest the presence of a wall partially closing the opening. A few small potsherds of indeterminate use are present nearby. The existing vegetation prevents the detection of any further traces.
descriptions.NUR19626: “Human presence on the island of Sant’Antioco is attested from the 5th millennium BC in rock shelters, caves, lithic scatters and tombs.” A tafone which, because of its medium-sized opening and its not very large interior surface, as well as its volumes, may have been used as a pantry, considering that it lies near a hut. Here too some stones remain in their original position forming the wall that partly closed it off.
descriptions.NUR19759: A tafone of very particular workmanship, probably used as a burial, given the presence of several stones beneath the tafone that probably formed part of the closing wall. A folk legend tells that a chest containing a treasure, a “Scrixoxiu”, was hidden/walled up inside it.
descriptions.NUR1327: It is an interesting Nuragic structure featuring the corner junction between the perimeter walls. Experts describe it as a megaron Greek type.
descriptions.NUR12714: The building, probably Nuragic, shows straight wall lines that enclose a rectangular shape oriented on a north–south longitudinal axis. It seems plausible that stones taken from the ancient building were used for the later enclosure and hut; at first glance its shape and evident features recall a megaron temple.
descriptions.NUR19900: Included in the Municipal Urban Plan. There are no authoritative scholarly sources on the structure. Local oral tradition says it has an entrance on an inclined plane/steps for a couple of metres down to a base, then a vertical drop of about 20/25 metres. The landowners in that area sealed the entrance with a large boulder/slab.
descriptions.NUR19736: Well constructed with stones of different sizes; the external structure is completely ruined, probably belonging to a temple of a spring-water well.
descriptions.NUR8489: The monument is built at the foot of a rocky outcrop where a spring vein is present. The structure is made of trachyte boulders of various sizes expertly worked. Access to the well is through a vestibule leading to a staircase that ends in the well chamber; this has a façade preserving a rectangular entrance opening surmounted by a lintel. Because of collapses and its precarious state the site has been fenced off.
descriptions.NUR14575: The temple of Antas is a Punic-Roman temple dedicated to the worship of the eponymous god of the Sardinians, Sardus Pater Babai (Sid Addir for the Carthaginians). It lies about ten kilometres south of the village of Fluminimaggiore, in an area where Carthaginians and Romans settled, attracted by the abundant lead and iron deposits in the territory.
descriptions.NUR14805: A temple dedicated to Astarte, the Punic goddess of love, fertility and war. What made her places of worship famous was their association with a particular practice, that of sacred prostitution.
descriptions.NUR12446: The main sacred building consists of two rooms: a sub-rectangular atrium (originally fitted with a bench) probably covered by a gabled roof, and a circular cell accessible from the atrium, originally with a tholos (false dome) roof. In the centre of the cell are the remains of a hearth showing several phases of use, and against the wall face a bench-like embankment.
descriptions.NUR10788:
Domu de Orgia of Esterzili is the largest Nuragic "megaron" temple known so far.

The building is enclosed within an elliptical perimeter (48.50 x 28 m; wall thickness 1.50 m) reduced to the single foundation course, with an entrance to the west.

This and other information:
descriptions.NUR11967: The temple, built of irregular blocks of granite, porphyry and more rarely limestone, consists of two quadrangular rooms leading into a circular chamber that preserved an altar inside reproducing two nuraghe towers. Outside, a structure with an irregular rectangular plan yielded an extraordinary deposit of votive bronzes, dedicated to the deity during the cults.
descriptions.NUR15758: Discovered in 1881, it was buried and then rediscovered in 1982 by the Superintendent.
descriptions.NUR10637: To the north-east of the nuraghe a well is visible, its masonry built of polyhedral boulders of various shapes and sizes. The wall face of the north side is hidden by vegetation and at first glance appears to have collapsed. Around the well lie many boulders that probably belonged to the original structure.
descriptions.NUR10638: To the south-east of the nuraghe, leaning against a rocky spur, is the structure of a well cut into the rock. It appears as a long cavity built in a semi-circular shape with boulders of various shapes and sizes. All around are fallen boulders, probably belonging to the well's original structure.
descriptions.NUR19817: To the east of the nuraghe a structure is visible that at a cursory glance looks like a well, though it is very degraded. Its interior is completely covered with fallen stones, and what remains of the walling appears to be made of polyhedral boulders, mostly small in size.
descriptions.NUR10097: In the Nuragic period, during the Final Bronze Age, a small sacred well temple dedicated to the water cult was built. The building follows the ground plan typical of this type of monument elsewhere on the island, consisting therefore of a vestibule, a stairwell, and an underground chamber. The circular chamber, originally roofed with a tholos, and the stairwell, which survives with six steps, have wall faces built of perfectly fitting isodomic sandstone ashlars.
descriptions.NUR10448:
Nuragic well in the territory of Guasila about which no significant information exists.

It is simply noted that the construction is of isodomic masonry and has, in its upper part, a crowning of T-shaped ashlars, a feature found only in far more famous monuments of the highest quality.
descriptions.NUR12619:
Nuragic sacred well with a circular chamber, originally covered by a tholos vault, now lost, preceded by a staircase of which seven steps remain.

The hypogean structure is built of andesite blocks laid in concentric courses, eight of which survive.

Groundwater still collects at the bottom of the chamber. The monument now stands inside a small fenced area.
descriptions.NUR10654:
It was built in the Nuragic period for the water cult. Situated in the locality of Is Pirois, this Nuragic sacred well has the peculiarity of a single-tower nuraghe erected on its summit, built on the false dome that closes the well chamber.

The vestibule is defined by two wall faces composed of granite blocks. From the lintelled entrance one enters the stairway leading down into the well chamber, which is closed at the top by a false dome.
descriptions.NUR10777: The sacred well of Sa Brecca is located in the locality of Sàrrala é Sùsu in the Marina di Tertenia (Ogliastra). The site takes its name from the Rio Sa Brèca (Sa Brècca on IGM maps) and from the goat sheepfold of the same name (Coìli 'e Sa Brèca) that stands on the remains of the pre-Nuragic settlement. The watercourse is one of the most important on this slope and flows out onto the beach of Fògi Mànna.
descriptions.NUR19603: It is a sacred well almost completely buried and partially disturbed by illicit digging. It can be identified in the middle of dense, invasive vegetation that nevertheless does not prevent the presence of wall structures forming the upper part of the well's tholos and the upper structures of the vestibule from being observed.
descriptions.NUR10780: The sacred well is the most important part of the whole sanctuary, so much so that it was the first feature to be recognised and immediately excavated. Dated to the 9th century BC by the archaeologist Anati in 1985[2], the site was built using the cyclopean technique, the same as that used for nuraghi, but unlike them with carefully dressed stones rather than roughly hewn ones. In antiquity the temple was roofed.
descriptions.NUR10708: Immersed in the dense vegetation stands the sacred well “Su Presoni”, so named because tradition says it was used as a prison in past centuries. The sacred well is a building linked to the water cult, composed of an underground part (well chamber) and an above-ground part (atrium) connected by a flight of steps. The monument at Cardedu is well preserved; the side walls of the atrium are still clearly visible to a surviving height of more than a metre;
descriptions.NUR11381: Sacred well of the Nuragic period, of which only the vertical shaft remains.
descriptions.NUR10763: Nuragic village of Su Putzu, composed of about a hundred huts surrounding a well temple, precisely Su Putzu. The temple has a long ramped vestibule; the staircase leading to the spring vein is missing.
descriptions.NUR12218: Lacking visible structures and a vestibule. It consists of the linear continuity of the staircase (28–29 steps) and the water chamber, which together form a rectangular void 8.12 m long and 1.25–1.10 m wide. The "bottle-shaped" section of the well, elliptical in plan (1.82 x 1.25 m, height 5.12 m), also sets it apart from the sacred wells of Sardinia. The internal masonry is of polyhedral type.
descriptions.NUR4793:
Cuccuru Nuraxi is the hill on whose summit a grand complex nuraghe once stood, now largely destroyed.

Even the earliest studies made it possible to grasp the nuraghe's structure. It was the first archaeological excavations, in the early 1960s, however, that gave a more precise definition of the monumental complex. The building consisted of two megalithic towers joined by a curtain wall. Inside, it comprised at least three chambers, one of which formed the main chamber.
descriptions.NUR4142: The nuragic sacred well is a special structure attached to the spring vein; the sacred spring structure is usually composed of a chamber enclosed by stone slabs.
descriptions.NUR11528:
It consists of a temple, an almost completely collapsed nuraghe, a large circular hut, and a series of "tafone" tombs.

The small temple of Malchittu is certainly the most interesting building in the complex, both for its excellent state of preservation and for the singularity of its construction, comparable to only a few others in Sardinia.
descriptions.NUR12954: A Nuragic temple in the territory of Nulvi, almost completely collapsed. At the apex a worked lintel remains that surmounted a doorway, reached by a spiral staircase inaccessible from the inside; the last steps and the covering slabs in a single block survive. From the remains the pediment appears to have been similar to that of giants' tombs. Around it are various remains of nuraghi, a village, and the enclosure wall that ran around the apex of the promontory.
descriptions.NUR20236:
The building dates from the 11th century. The remains of the wall enclosing the precinct are visible. The most precious part lies at the centre of the area, with the basin altar. The building was constructed of large, fine isodomic ashlars. Many are T-shaped.

Two "circular rooms" were joined by a sort of trapezoidal vestibule, provided with lateral stone benches. Like the nuraghi, it possesses the triad of internal perimeter niches, the western one larger, the northern and southern ones smaller and symmetrical.
descriptions.NUR17369: Third domus of the S'incantu complex
descriptions.NUR17373: The arcosolium-type hypogeum with a rectangular basin, cut into the limestone ridge like the domus de janas, showed two distinct deposition levels; the upper one with the remains of 8 inhumations; the lower one with 5 inhumations. The nuraghe has not been located.
descriptions.NUR7242: It was a tomb of the "architectural façade" type. The façade is completely ruined and hidden by vegetation. It now lies beneath the overpass of the new Uri–Scala Cavalli road. Source: Wikimapia
descriptions.NUR11539: A mixed-structure tomb consisting of an ancient pre-Nuragic multi-chambered hypogeum modified to the plan of a Nuragic-period giants' tomb by the addition of a monolithic arched stele (height 3.60 m) with a central doorway and an exedra obtained by shaping the rock bench.
descriptions.NUR6997: The tomb opens a few metres from the remains of a small single-chambered domus de janas (Tomb III); it is very likely that Tomb II was also originally a small domus de janas, later transformed into the form of a façade tomb. The stele now lacks its upper part with the lunette frame, which lies overturned a few metres from the entrance.
descriptions.NUR1475: We are faced once again with an immense loss inflicted on the community and on history, perhaps to gain a few square metres of arable or pasture land. The monument has been reduced to a ruin and few of the building's features can be made out.
descriptions.NUR17736: The tomb body shows its wall faces with difficulty because of collapses and the vegetation covering the front and rear sections. From the visible parts it can be seen that it is built of large, dressed limestone blocks. The apse wall, though covered by vegetation, retains two or three courses of polyhedral blocks. The front part of the tomb is incorporated into a dry-stone wall where a parallelepiped-shaped block can be made out, perhaps the tomb's lintel.
descriptions.NUR17738: The tomb structure is unrecognisable; the few surviving stretches of the courses that formed the tomb are not enough to determine its structure and size. The vegetation growing inside the tomb and the probable intervention of clandestine excavations are the factors that have contributed to its disintegration.
descriptions.NUR12015: What remains of a giants' tomb located in the wooded area of Santa Barbara's pic nic zone
descriptions.NUR11464: Giants' tombs not easily identifiable near the sheepfold Presethu Tortu
descriptions.NUR11465: Giants' tombs not easily identifiable near the sheepfold Presethu Tortu
descriptions.NUR14582: This dolmenic giants' tomb is easily accessible because it is situated alongside the road and near the larger Aidu complex.
descriptions.NUR17698: The tomb is covered by vegetation and can only be found by following the dry stone wall on the western side.
descriptions.NUR8633: Small Giants' tomb, belonging to the Appiu village context. Never excavated, it appears to belong to the cyclopean type of giants' tomb, despite being located in an area where dolmens with arched stelae are predominant.
descriptions.NUR8132:
The Barrancu Mannu giants' tomb, also known as "Sa Tuerredda", displays the classic ground plan of giants' tombs: an apsidal tomb body, a covered corridor, and an arched exedra.

The outer wall face consists of large, roughly dressed blocks of yellow-pink granite topped by irregular courses of variously polyhedral stones of large size.

Of the apsidal circuit, originally finished with ordered rows of tailed ashlars, two or three courses survive.
descriptions.NUR10562: The tomb is not in a good state of preservation. However, the large stele can still be seen in its original position, of which only the lower, trapezoidal part survives, while the arched top is missing; a fragment of it can be seen fallen inside the chamber. Practically nothing of the exedra survives. The burial chamber, also poorly preserved, is built of slabs set vertically into the ground.
descriptions.NUR10640: The tomb, still buried, clearly shows the violations it suffered at the hands of looters. The chamber is rectangular, built of boulders of various sizes, only roughly dressed, laid dry with packing wedges. The entrance, facing ESE, has its doorway completely buried, topped by a lintel shaped like a rectangular block whose sides appear perfectly smoothed. The tomb was preceded by an exedra, of which some boulders remain in situ to the north of the tomb body.
descriptions.NUR14084: The tomb is of the coursed type, built with schist slabs about 1 metre long, of which six courses of the outer wall face of the chamber and eight courses of the exedra survive in situ. The doorway at the centre of the exedra is built in dolmenic fashion, with two slabs set on edge and one above; the relieving window is missing. The exedra joins the outer wall face of the chamber with a concave line.
descriptions.NUR12597: At Funtanazza, on the Lampis family's land, lies the giants' tomb of Bruncu Espis, a place where a Roman village once stood. Well preserved and looked after by the landowners, it has a corridor about ten metres long and a little over one metre wide, and is completely covered by the earth above which some ancient structures still appear.
descriptions.NUR11732: It is in poor conservation. At the Sassari Museum the closure door is on display, but the tomb is incorrectly named Mesu e Rios.
descriptions.NUR10871: The actual location of the site needs to be verified.
descriptions.NUR13517: Giants' tomb with a bilitic stele, of which only the lower part remains; the monument damaged over the years by clandestine diggers and vandals.
descriptions.NUR15051: Dolmen with a collapsed and buried structure, whose layout cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR10392: It is a jewel of architecture, harmonious in construction and full of sacredness. In front of the mound, turned over from below and above, visited several times by tomb robbers, the exedra develops in a double row of roughly worked stones. From the wings of the exedra the circle of single stones begins, with a diameter of 15 m.
descriptions.NUR10537: They are two distinct collective burials that share the same exedra. They are located at a short distance from the homonymous nuraghe situated at the top of the plateau.
descriptions.NUR12960:
The corridor tomb has been attributed to the Nuragic period.

The pottery found during the surveys is of Roman Imperial and Late Antique date. Repeated surface surveys have yielded pottery and bricks, probably belonging to a necropolis.
descriptions.NUR19638: Near the namesake nuraghe on the ridge that descends towards the Stupàra stream there is a giants' tomb built of flat schist stones. The tomb is about 7 metres long and about 2 metres high. No exedra is visible. Its state of preservation is nevertheless fair.
descriptions.NUR21133: Wild olive trees growing in the tomb corridor are demolishing what remains. Branches, foliage and wind-blown sediment have covered the cavities. On the front of this giants' tomb someone had built a kind of hut using some of the exedra ashlars. Today, however, because of the thorny shrubs the tomb is not even easily reachable.
descriptions.NUR16151: The tomb has a rectangular chamber that is completely blocked by fallen boulders and covered in vegetation. In the area in front of the tomb there are boulders that certainly belong to the exedra wall, some still in their original position. Given its present condition it is difficult to determine its dimensions.
descriptions.NUR12614: A prehistoric burial of the Nuragic period. Unfortunately, the tomb has been partially demolished by herders to build a sheepfold.
descriptions.NUR11738:
The burial lies on the southern slope of a gentle incline. The burial chamber is partly visible, and about 3.50 m from it two partly buried blocks can be seen, probable elements of the exedra. The tomb has unfortunately been disturbed by illicit digging that has affected the rear part of the tomb.

As far as can be seen, the latter consists of medium-sized granite slabs, well dressed on the exposed face, and set as orthostats.
descriptions.NUR9875: In an advanced state of abandonment, the wall face running east–west, built of medium-sized stones laid on edge, is still visible. There are few traces of the probable exedra. Worth noting, however, is the presence of a baetyl stone with several holes whose meaning is unknown unless related to the female essence.
descriptions.NUR18918: Of the tomb only the dentilled ashlar and a monolithic arch belonging to the apsidal section remain.
descriptions.NUR8292: On the site there are as many as two giants' tombs of modest size, largely stripped of the stones that originally composed them. The exedra and the burial chamber are still discernible.
descriptions.NUR12233: Of the aforementioned tomb, only a few foundation stones remain, together with a nearby stele, suggesting that there may have been a giants' tomb.
descriptions.NUR9867: Very ruined: vertical orthostats (with transverse cuts) and the tumulus closure and part of the exedra can still be identified.
descriptions.NUR11972: The burial, situated near two nuraghi and a village, still preserves the tomb body. This encloses a burial chamber built of granite blocks of various sizes, shaped obliquely on the exposed face and laid in irregular courses with the use of chocking wedges.
descriptions.NUR12395: A coursed giants' tomb, it stands on the south-west part of a hillock. The tomb preserves the outer wall face, the whole funerary corridor including the back slab and a head slab with a doorway (stele?), much of the east arm of the exedra, and an ashlar with circular hollows lying out of place.
descriptions.NUR20297: The cemetery consists of three corridor tombs and two giants' tombs without stelae. Further details are provided in the document "Recovery of archaeological sites in the territory of Castiadas".
descriptions.NUR9869: Although reduced to a ruin, a few basic elements can be observed that reveal the structure of the monument. The cist is built of various fairly squared stones on which some covering elements rest. The presence of the exedra, composed of stones set on edge, also remains clear, although some of them have fallen to the ground.
descriptions.NUR1479: It is situated on the north-east slope of Monte Sozu, just below Su Casteddu where the nuraghe of the same name stands. It is the largest giants' tomb in our territory of Chiaramonti. The burial cist, about 15 m long, is built of stones of various sizes roughly shaped, and is covered with large trachyte slabs laid flat. Mu
descriptions.NUR10189: Few remaining walls and many uncertainties: frequent help from the historical memory of the elders and the presence of only a few basal remains of the homonymous nuraghe. mu.
descriptions.NUR16146: It has a particular form, because part of it is built upon a huge stone that has been partially cut out and adapted to a funerary function.
descriptions.NUR15228: Datable to the 13th century BC. Belonging to the Albucciu nuraghe. In this tomb the rectangular body, of flat slabs, is surrounded by a mound of rubble. The exedra is reduced to a series of blocks and small slabs that deprive the monument of the sense of grandeur that characterises the other megalithic burials. The wall thickness of the tomb is remarkable, at about 6 metres. The structure has undergone alterations in different periods and has been reused several times.
descriptions.NUR20111: This is probably a coursed giants' tomb in very poor condition: it is almost indistinguishable from the surrounding rocks. The ashlars at the sides of the central doorway, the burial corridor, the courses to the right and left of it, and part of the outer walls can still be made out. It is clear that many of the stones that made up the central body and the vault have been removed and then scattered all around the tomb or thrown down into the central corridor.
descriptions.NUR20009: The orthostats of the large exedra, which lacks its stele, stand out. The stele lies broken on the ground in front of it. A wild olive tree has grown in the stele's place. A small piece of the exedra remains at the apsidal rear, giving an idea of the monument's size.
descriptions.NUR998: The Nissardi in 1901 (map included in G. Pinza's volume) indicated a giants' tomb slightly south-west of the Paule Tolta nuraghe: a nuraghe that actually lies within the perimeter of the airport.
descriptions.NUR12420: The slabs of the burial chamber and a small portion of the outer wall face on the east side are visible. The chamber has been partially dug out by looters, who also excavated in the mass of fill making up the tomb mound, between the left wall of the burial chamber and the course of stones of the outer wall face, wrongly believing that the two walls enclosed a second burial chamber adjoining the first.
descriptions.NUR10130: Only vague remains of the cist's perimeter outline survive, but the feature is unmistakable. Many stones were taken to Castelsardo for the rebuilding of the ancient Medieval Cathedral.
descriptions.NUR10342: Giants' tomb dating to the Middle Bronze Age (14th century BC). In very poor condition of conservation, located very close to the homonymous nuraghe, better known as N.ghe Gorroppu.
descriptions.NUR12419: About 500 metres from the homonymous nuraghe
descriptions.NUR6458: Known as a nuraghe, it is in fact a fine example of a giants' tomb with an attached ceremonial circle. Facing east is the dolmenic exedra that opens into the rectangular stone cist. From the sides of the exedra, large dressed stones radiate in a circle to form the circle for ceremonies. Mu
descriptions.NUR12593: Or at least what is left of it. During the rebuilding of the Sibiri road it was gutted to allow an easier alignment. In effect the bends in the old alignment were removed and the tomb was destroyed. Today a stretch of about 2 metres remains. In short, a victim of "Progress".
descriptions.NUR18425: It lies within the municipal territory of Collinas. The Regional Commission for the Cultural Heritage of Sardinia, by its Decree no. 155 of 14 December 2017, declared the property known as the “Nuragic Tomb of Sa Terra de Su Muru” to be of particular archaeological interest.
descriptions.NUR10190: A few but clear remains of a giants' tomb. The mound still partially in situ, together with two pillars embedded in a dry-stone wall. The surrounding area is rich in Nuragic remains. mu
descriptions.NUR10132: Reduced to the level of a ruin, like so many other sites. I am sorry to repeat myself, but the disappointment of finding a cultural heritage that is not protected and is not taken into account imposes on me the civic duty of publicly denouncing this neglect.
descriptions.NUR10133: Few remains of TdG. The site, heavily anthropized from distant epochs, is presumed to be very rich, like the nearby Pisciu Accas. mu
descriptions.NUR10234: A burial of the Nuragic period built of polygonal trachyte blocks. Little of the tomb is visible because of the vegetation; the corridor and part of the exedra survive. From what the remains and the vegetation allow one to see, the mound has walls of roughly dressed blocks and a final cut stone. It is of interest as the only one of its type known so far: the ashlar with three holes in which three small baetyls were placed during religious ceremonies. mu.
descriptions.NUR10233: The area has been heavily settled since ancient times. The importance of the site stands out from the numerous remains and their particular nature, which find no parallels in other parts of the island. A project focused on the architecture of the giants' tombs is currently being studied by female researchers who will shortly publish a specific book on them.
descriptions.NUR16569: In poor state of conservation, the corridor and several squared stones that originally were meant to form the entrance are still visible.
descriptions.NUR10193: A burial of the Nuragic period built of polygonal trachyte blocks. Little of the tomb is visible because of the vegetation; the corridor and the exedra survive. From what the remains and the vegetation allow one to see, the two arms (running straight) that define the exedra consist of two superimposed wall faces of different widths with a set-back that presumably served as a seat. mu.
descriptions.NUR10188: The surrounding territory has been heavily settled since ancient times, and sites are numerous everywhere. Often, as is the case with the few visible remains, it is not easy to determine their type. The only proof is the historical memory of the elders, with their indelible recollection of their existence.
descriptions.NUR12639:
Important giants' tomb near Sant'Antonio di Santadi.

It appears to be in apparently good condition.

The name is unknown to me, but it is certainly of great historical importance. Found by cross-referencing data from several maps.
descriptions.NUR21111: Feature whose plan is not easily interpretable
descriptions.NUR10199: Modest in overall scale, almost a little treasure; it consists of two walls of nearly squared stone masonry and has a roof made of large natural trachyte slabs.
descriptions.NUR16896: We find it at about 30 metres perpendicular to the secondary road of SS 131, in a state of complete abandonment.
descriptions.NUR18877:
The giants' tomb lies to the south, about 500 metres from the nuraghe; only part of the inner wall face of the chamber and traces of the peristalith are visible.

In an area of about 2000 sq m around the giants' tomb, numerous structures are visible of which only the basal courses remain; in particular a wall stands out that encloses a roughly rectangular area, inside which there are traces of various types of rooms, some semicircular but mostly quadrangular.
descriptions.NUR11723: The Giants' tomb is located about fifty metres to the south of the Nuraghe Figu. Part of the tomb's structure and a small portion of the exedra are visible.
descriptions.NUR21178: Very damaged and difficult to read. Probably dolmenic. It is likely that on the stele there was a dentilled stone typical of the TDG, placed on top of the entrance.
descriptions.NUR11935:
The giants' tomb is covered by dense scrub, and only one covering slab leaning to the north can be seen outside.

Rock shelter opening in a huge granite boulder, a spacious cavity with a wide main entrance flanked by two orthostatic slabs and already partly closed. The main interest lies in the geometric figures on the exposed rock that forms the shelter floor, and schematic anthropomorphic figures on the back wall.
descriptions.NUR20330: Next to the provincial road remains a low row possibly belonging to a giants' tomb, whose typical structure is clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR9180: Situated on a small rise in the countryside of the municipality, a short distance from the new provincial road "Ussana, Donori, Barrali". It is a prehistoric wall structure discovered during a survey beneath a clearance cairn. The wall stretch is straight, 4 metres long and 80 centimetres wide, built of large blocks, of which only the uppermost course is visible. It could also be one side of a tomb of the same period.
descriptions.NUR21177: Cyclopean giants' tomb with a corbelled corridor, of red granite. The corbel slabs are missing. A short distance away some ashlars appear to belong to the apse. The exedra has been destroyed.
descriptions.NUR10870: Two blocks of the exedra are visible, the inner right wall of the chamber. Illyscavated illegally and damaged.
descriptions.NUR8101:
Also known as "Sa Domu 'e s'Orku", it is built of local granite blocks laid in "cyclopean style". It has the unique feature of being oriented exactly to the north.

This giants' tomb is of the "coursed façade" type, typical of the giants' tombs of southern Sardinia; the façade and the exedra, 10 m wide, are built in megalithic masonry; on the right-hand side of the exedra there are three "ritual hearths", circular in shape.
descriptions.NUR13949: The giants' tomb of Iscrallotze is particularly eroded. In appearance, what remains suggests it belongs to the category of dolmenic giants' tombs.
descriptions.NUR11635: Giants' tomb, nuragic, with a corridor and a partial portion of the exedra.
descriptions.NUR13994:
An interesting monument in the territory of Villanova Monteleone, oriented south-west; part of the exedra is still visible, but unfortunately no trace of the stele remains. The well-preserved corridor, built of well-squared trachyte blocks, is 7.10 m long and 2.80 m wide; two slabs laid flat still survive of the roofing.

To the left of the monument a setting of stones covered by a slab can be seen, perhaps a dolmen.
descriptions.NUR9487: The monument, aligned NW–SE, has a rectangular body (length 15.90 m; width 4.60 m), vaguely apsidal at the rear, with a funerary corridor flanked by two pairs of facing niches; of the exedra (chord 5.60 m; arc about 15 m) only the left wing survives in part. But the most interesting feature of this tomb is the presence of the four niches in the corridor, which probably served to hold funerary offerings.
descriptions.NUR8738:
Practically unknown and inside a private property. The monument, excavated and cleared in recent times, is perfectly legible and defined in all its components: the corridor, which preserves its intact floor of granite slabs, the apse and the two wings of the exedra.

It lies to the west of Santa Reparata.

The structure is built on a very slight rise with the exedra clearly raised. A linear bench is present in the front part of the exedra, a feature often found in other giants' tombs.
descriptions.NUR2650: Giants' tomb completely collapsed, with only a few ashlar stones remaining and its location difficult to determine.
descriptions.NUR15382: Around the building extends a large village of circular huts, while a short distance away there are two giants' tombs. There is also record of a well that existed in ancient times, of which no trace remains today.
descriptions.NUR12177:
A burial of the Nuragic period.

The monument is in very poor condition and its construction type cannot be determined. On the ground an alignment of stones is visible (probably belonging to the exedra), while the final stretch of the corridor can be glimpsed buried under a bramble bush.
descriptions.NUR8739: The Lu Brandali nuragic complex consists of a nuraghe with an outer wall, a village, a giants' tomb, a series of "tafone" tombs and rock shelters. To reach the Lu Brandali Archaeological Site from the traffic lights on Via Nazionale in Santa Teresa Gallura, turn left towards Capo Testa; after about 700 m the main entrance is on the left.
descriptions.NUR11622: Only the base of the tomb is visible, and what remains is almost entirely covered by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR20373: Giants' tomb marked in an article by Gallura Oggi, already included in the Geoportal, alongside which a windmill has been erected.
descriptions.NUR10917: A collective burial of the Nuragic period. Of the monument, hidden by the Mediterranean scrub bushes that cover it, the corridor, the exedra, and inside it the dentilled stele that adorned the facade can be made out.
descriptions.NUR13390: A heavily ruined cyclopean giants' tomb, of which part of the corridor and the lintel remain. The monument is of the type known as "coursed", consisting of a burial built in courses of superimposed blocks with an elongated rectangular burial chamber, preceded by the entrance, followed by a dromos, and ending in an apse.
descriptions.NUR13334: A striking dentilled ashlar with three teeth is visible, upon which, likely, the three baetyls representing an unidentified Sardinian triad were set.
descriptions.NUR20299: The TdG consists of two walls, each about 15 m long. Destroyed by tomb robbers. Location uncertain.
descriptions.NUR9181: Giants' tomb located within a large olive grove.
descriptions.NUR9483: Nearby and closely associated with the Miuddu nuraghe, no more than a hundred metres to the south-east, stands a giants' tomb displaying the usual architectural layout of this tomb type: a semicircular exedra (chord 10.05 m – sagitta 2.25 m), a slightly apsidal rectangular body (length 9.75 m – width 2.50 m) and a rectangular burial chamber (length 4.60 m x 0.80 m wide x 0.75 m high above the fill).
descriptions.NUR13674:
It is a burial with a rectangular corridor cut into the rock and provided with a limestone pavement.

The walls of the chamber are built of marl ashlars, originally bonded with mud mortar, laid in horizontal courses, which in the upper part of the wall face have an oblique exposed face. No trace remains, however, of the exedra's hemicycle.
descriptions.NUR11726:
Giants' tomb of the orthostat type in the region of wall ramparts, Muracalzos.

A nuraghe is also present nearby, Muracalzos.
descriptions.NUR14728: The arched stele of this giants' tomb lacks an entrance doorway, so it must have rested directly on the jambs that frame the entrance. Or on a lintel that gave the monument greater grandeur.
descriptions.NUR20020: Giants' tomb, of which only a very small portion remains, almost completely destroyed.
descriptions.NUR12159: It is a tomb with a rectangular burial chamber clearly in a state of degradation, almost entirely covered by moss and difficult to identify; the chamber is about 15 metres long.
descriptions.NUR12821: Partly hidden by Mediterranean scrub, the tomb is oriented north–south, with an exedra facing south of which about three courses survive, composed of large quadrangular granite blocks laid in alternating rows, to a surviving height of 90 cm.
descriptions.NUR9485:
The tomb, of dolmenic type and oriented south-east, has a semicircular exedra (chord 9 m – depth 3 m) bounded by orthostatic slabs, an apsidal rectangular body (length 6 m – width 4 m) and a modest burial corridor (length 3.70 m x width 0.75 m).

At present the northern flank and the right arm of the exedra are incorporated in a dry-stone wall.
descriptions.NUR9486: Of the megalithic tomb, which was very well preserved until the 1970s, only the northern side and the right arm of the exedra survive, and only partially; a short stretch of the burial chamber can also be made out, while a few metres away some enormous slabs that formed the flat-lintelled roof of the tomb are visible.
descriptions.NUR19743: The tomb, because of the collapse of its side structures and the lush vegetation that covers most of it, does not clearly show its layout. However, some ashlars still in their original position suggest a rectangular plan. At the sides and in the surrounding area there are heaps of earth mixed with boulders and rubble that probably belonged to the tomb structure, clear signs of the violation carried out by clandestine diggers.
descriptions.NUR21125: Chance find. Tomb cited in Annalisa Uccheddu's 1995 degree thesis, University of Cagliari, located inside the Villa Siotto Park. Tomb with its top missing and buried. Probable original length about 10 m. Illicitly excavated with the covering removed.
descriptions.NUR21127: Random location. Tomb cited in Annalisa Uccheddu's 1995 degree thesis, UNICA. It lies on land bordering the Villa Siotto Park. The tomb has no covering, is partly buried and free of vegetation. Length about 7 m.
descriptions.NUR9480: The lower register of the stele, slightly trapezoidal (1.02 m – 1.05 m – height 0.98 m), has a frame running along the profile of three sides (0.16/0.18 m wide on the upper line; from 0.18 m to 0.13 m on the vertical sides), raised by 0.35/0.15 m. The thickness of the slab differs on the two sides: on the left, at the lower edge it measures 0.34 m; 0.40 m at the top and 0.56 m in the middle zone; on the right it decreases from the base (59 cm) to the top (32 cm).
descriptions.NUR15064: Tomb with corridor and semicircular exedra
descriptions.NUR9635: The tomb is almost buried under a substantial mound of earth and stones. The basal orthostats follow almost the entire perimeter: a semi-circular exedra (arc 10.40 m – chord 3.80 m) flattened on the south-east side with arms surviving for 6.66 m on the right and 4.45 m on the left; a rectangular body 10.60 m long and 4.20 m wide where it meets the exedra wings; a burial corridor (length 7.20 m – width 1.10 m) bounded by upright slabs.
descriptions.NUR9481: The tomb has the usual architectural layout: an elongated apsidal body (length 14.50 m – width 4/4.30 m), a broad sickle-shaped exedra (current chord 11.70 m – depth 3.25 m) and a rectangular corridor (11.55 m long – average width 1.10 m and 0.55 m at the entrance). In the summer of 1982 the monument was excavated and partially restored.
descriptions.NUR21010: A burial of the Nuragic period. Of the monument, in poor condition and partly hidden by vegetation, only the funerary corridor, the exedra and numerous shaped ashlars remain, showing that the tomb was of the coursed type in isodomic masonry. The ashlars, very carefully made, include the so-called dentilled stele of considerable size, and an element of uncertain definition on which one face has a framed, raised boss.
descriptions.NUR11434: The tomb now consists only of a corridor, oriented along a SE–NW axis, bounded by orthostats and open at the short ends, which are now destroyed. Even in the absence of certain evidence, which could only come from an excavation that would clarify on which of the two sides the entrance opened, it can be assumed that, in keeping with what generally occurs in these tombs, it faced SE.
descriptions.NUR9631:
Of the megalithic burial, of isodomic type and oriented south-east, the funerary corridor can be measured (length 4.20 m – width 1.05 m), consisting of four blocks per side and one at the end, all finely worked; the layout of the exedra and that of the tomb body are less clear.

Among the scattered stones in the exedra area lies a dentilled ashlar: it is trapezoidal (1.85 x 1.15 x 0.75 m high), has a slight rebate and the usual three vertical notches.
descriptions.NUR20033: At 'Perdas de Fogu', on the ridge of a small hill, are the remains of a giants' tomb built of large limestone boulders. The burial chamber is polygonal with an entrance to the south where part of the exedra is visible, having a chord of 12.10 metres. The chamber survives for a length of 6 metres, a width of 1.20 metres and a height of 0.50 metres.
descriptions.NUR15741: Of the monument, largely destroyed, the funerary corridor is visible, composed of polygonal blocks finely finished on the exposed sides.
descriptions.NUR21150: Only the central corridor of the structure remains. Surrounding it are scattered ashlar stones, but not immediately assignable to the tomb.
descriptions.NUR10879: The tomb is set into a rocky slope. The funerary corridor is 7.65 m long. Lacks an exedra. Excavation revealed artifacts dating to the Roman period and below the Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR19651: The tomb shows clear signs of illicit excavation; its structure is hard to make out because most of it is covered by vegetation and soil. The chamber is rectangular and partly buried at the rear; an apse may be present. On the sides and at the back of the tomb there are fallen boulders that certainly belonged to the tomb. Even though it is hidden by the scrub, the wall of the exedra is visible, following a curved course.
descriptions.NUR12236: The site lies in the municipality of Nuoro, in the city's industrial zone. The structure is partly destroyed, but the stones that probably made up the exedra and part of the burial chamber can still be distinguished. The typical U-shape of the megalithic tomb can still be made out.
descriptions.NUR21146: It is a report by an enthusiast, verified by an archaeologist. It appears to be a giants' tomb or a corridor dolmenic, hitherto unknown.
descriptions.NUR13527: The monument stands in the middle of a livestock farm. It is a dolmenic tomb, aligned NW–SE with the entrance to the south-east, its burial chamber tapering towards the rear and open at the front in a broad semicircular exedra.
descriptions.NUR1336: The cista is formed by medium-sized stones set vertically into the ground. There is a single stone that closes the cista; previously, the presence of a baetyl is noted.
descriptions.NUR8658: Also known as "Sa Grutta de Santu Giuanni", it displays the classic ground plan of a giants' tomb. The tomb body (22.10 m), aligned on a north–south axis with the entrance to the south, is bordered on the outside by rows of granite blocks of various sizes. The façade is still partly buried and covered with rubble.
descriptions.NUR10874: The tomb was built with large blocks still partially buried and with exposed faces mostly straight. The exedra is no longer visible and the position of the door can only be hypothesised.
descriptions.NUR20149: Unfortunately, very little of the tomb remains: today the central corridor of the burial chamber can still be made out, its walls once formed by courses of stones laid neatly as in nuraghe corridors; the stones that framed the central doorway are also present, together with many other stones scattered all around. Finally, a single stone slab (or orthostat) survives which, set in a row with many others, formed one of the two wings of the exedra.
descriptions.NUR12077:
The megalithic burial lies less than 200 metres south-east of Nuraghe Pattada, which stands in a higher, commanding position on the sheer edge of an extensive trachyte formation.
