The monument, of isodomic construction, with a coursed exedra and a lintelled entrance, repeats in plan the ground-plan common to this tomb type: a rectangular body with an apsidal rear profile, preceded by a semicircular exedra.
descriptions.NUR9815:
About twenty metres north-west of the large tomb described in record no. 50 lie the remains of a second megalithic burial that has been largely destroyed by a dry-stone wall cutting across it transversely.

Only a short stretch of the rectangular body can be measured (4.30 m long – 3.20 m wide); the construction technique uses orthostats, while several large overturned slabs inside show that the roof was flat-laid.
descriptions.NUR8760:
A few kilometres from the village of Uri, a tall stone stele stands in the middle of a field, giving the site its name: Sa Pedra Longa (The Long Stone). In the past it formed the front of a Nuragic giants' tomb, dating to the Middle Bronze Age (about 1700–1350 BC).

Of the original monument only the monolithic arched stele (cut from a single block of rock) survives; its type and relatively modest dimensions suggest an early date.
descriptions.NUR6890:
A semi-circular exedra oriented to the south-east, bounded by large orthostatic slabs; an elongated body (length 6.15 m – width 3 m at the junction with the exedra – and 2 m in the terminal section) with a burial chamber 4.43 m long and 0.55 m wide.

In the centre of the exedra the lower part of the bilithic arched stele is visible, truly majestic (width 1.10 – thickness 0.22) with a trapezoidal doorway (width 0.24 – height 0.20).

Another arched fragment of the stele lies overturned on the tomb.
descriptions.NUR12307: Only the floor, composed of large stones, a few peripheral stones, and clearly visible exedra remain.
descriptions.NUR9633:
The remains of the megalithic tomb lie next to a dry-stone wall that follows the railway line, just 200 metres south-east of Birori station.

Seven surviving slabs of the semicircular exedra (chord 9 m – rise 2.40 m) are visible on the ground, as is part of its outer perimeter (length 9 m – width 4.50 m); nothing can be said, however, about the burial corridor and the arched stele, whose existence can be considered certain.
descriptions.NUR9634: The only evidence of this megalithic burial is the presence of numerous shaped ashlars of various forms incorporated into a dry-stone wall for a length of about 200 metres. All these monoliths are remarkable for being perfectly worked and shaped, indicating that the destroyed tomb was of isodomic type. Among these stones, most of which have lifting recesses, a monolithic arch is of particular interest (arch span 1.72 m – rise 0.80 m – height 0.68 m).
descriptions.NUR21132: Uncertain location. Illegal excavation. The excavation extends for about 5 m. An apse is visible at field level.
descriptions.NUR11642: Arched stele of a Giants' tomb known as “S'Artare de su Moro”; the base of the stele remains in situ, while the upper part has been broken and incorporated into the wall of the hut.
descriptions.NUR19685: Situated a short distance from the little church of San Giacomo, this tomb too is badly damaged by illicit activity, but particularly monumental aspects can be seen in the working of the material used. The structure is built entirely of isodomic granite blocks.
descriptions.NUR8977: Giants' tomb dating to the Middle Bronze Age with a likely Bilitic stele belonging to the giants' dolmenic tomb, partially buried
descriptions.NUR15614: Completely dislodged structure, the original form of which is barely discernible.
descriptions.NUR12762: This dolmenic tomb, of the Early Bronze Age, is in an excellent state of preservation; indeed it retains the funerary corridor almost intact, with a flat-lintel roof formed by stone slabs laid horizontally along the corridor walls. The large stele consists of a centinated monolith in which the small doorway giving access to the burial chamber is cut. The exedra still preserves several stones set in the ground exactly as they were originally.
descriptions.NUR9812:
Of this megalithic tomb, which must have been closely linked to the nuraghe of the same name, only the upper part of the arched stele survives, in fragments.

The monolith, now incorporated into one of the many dry-stone walls that criss-cross the area near the Serbine nuraghe, measures 1.68 m in height and 1.15 m in maximum width; the frame that defines its outer profile is 0.11 m wide.
descriptions.NUR19797: The tomb is hidden by vegetation, blocked by fallen boulders and earth. Despite the collapse, the entrance can be identified and faces east. The exedra and the apse are hard to make out, also because of the violation by looters. For the exedra, the few clues are some semi-worked stones still in their original position at the sides of what remains of the probable entrance. To the rear, boulders arranged in a semicircle formed part of the apse.
descriptions.NUR19799: The tomb has a rectangular apsidal chamber, with the exedra and entrance facing south. The chamber was built of boulders of various sizes, only roughly dressed, bonded dry with packing wedges. The tomb has certainly been violated by looters; the burial chamber is covered by vegetation and filled with collapse stones and earth. On the east side of the tomb there are collapse boulders that certainly belong to the monument. The west wall is hidden by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR18120: The giants' tomb is located in the municipality of Romana; the remains of the burial are visible today embedded in a dry stone wall.
descriptions.NUR13439: The giants' tomb S'iscra e Lottoni is of dolmenic type, from the Early Bronze Age, and is in a fair state of preservation; indeed it retains the funerary corridor almost intact, with a flat-lintel roof formed by stone slabs laid horizontally along the corridor walls. The large stele consists of a centinated monolith in which the small doorway giving access to the burial chamber has been cut.
descriptions.NUR12436: Giants' tomb completely embedded in the undergrowth, never apparently excavated and totally collapsed. Only a few isodomic ashlar stones remain from the inner wall of the corridor...
descriptions.NUR9048:
The burial – of the coursed type with an arched stele – partly preserves the apsidal tomb body, oriented to the east and built of medium-sized polyhedral blocks of granite and porphyry. The short rectangular inner corridor has walls formed by basal orthostats supporting three courses of roughly dressed blocks; the floor consists of the outcropping rock.

The burial dates to around 1500 BC.
descriptions.NUR9844: Almost certainly present until the 1960s, when major land improvement and transformation works were carried out. The place name "su crastu covaccadu" suggests the presence of a trilith or covering lintels of a probable tomb. mu
descriptions.NUR14239:
The Written Boulder, carved.

Giants' tomb at Santu Micheli whose stele is framed, precisely, by a low-relief border.
descriptions.NUR19688: The tomb is small and built with orthostatic technique. Disturbed by illegal digging, during the excavation and restoration work carried out in 1996 fragments of a carinated bowl of a particular shape were found, which has no parallels in Sardinia; in 2008 various glass-paste necklace elements were recovered.
descriptions.NUR10067: Once again we are faced with traces of a giants' tomb that is recorded only in the memory of the oldest inhabitants. Clear traces of a structure identifiable as a giants' tomb remain on the spot. The cyclopean boulders involved are piled in disorder as a result of land-improvement works.
descriptions.NUR21137: Giants' tomb of Deruta. Located just 50 m from another Giants' tomb in better condition, on which the municipality has carried out minor interventions for cleaning and improved accessibility.
descriptions.NUR20264: Giants' tomb of Deruta. Located just 50 m from another Giants' tomb in better condition, on which the municipality has carried out minor interventions for cleaning and improved accessibility.
descriptions.NUR8306: The giants' tomb Su Niu de su Crobu stands on a rocky rise, not far from the sea, in the locality Sa corona de su crabì. The burial, of the “coursed” type, consists of an apsidal funerary corridor a little over 10 m long and 1.20 m wide on average; the stones composing it are roughly worked, laid in irregular courses and wedged with numerous chocks.
descriptions.NUR21124: The uncovered tomb has the outer profile of the central body with concave wall faces. The exedra has curved wings. The burial chamber is oblong. The facing course of the apse can be seen.
descriptions.NUR8334: Situated on a plateau next to the Caddare stream, the tomb lies a short distance from the Lettu Rucratu site. Before excavation and restoration the burial had suffered heavy disturbance by mechanical equipment that removed part of the chamber and the exedra; it was built with orthostatic technique. The site has yielded material datable to the beginning of the Middle Bronze Age.
descriptions.NUR11964: Giants' tomb with a cyclopean corridor in good condition, while the exterior appears buried and partially eroded.
descriptions.NUR12212: The giants' tomb Su Pranu est is not in an optimal state of preservation, but its fundamental components can still be made out. In the facade only a few blocks of the exedra remain in their original positions; at the centre stands the monumental monolithic arched stele, which has the peculiarity of lacking a doorway. The stele is now broken in two, uprooted and lying overturned on the remains of the chamber. The tomb can be dated to the beginning of the Bronze Age, about 1800 BC.
descriptions.NUR20281: Tomb built of roughly hewn calcare ashlar. Part of the exedra and the corridor remain. The lintel above the door is still in situ.
descriptions.NUR19965: The tomb is completely covered in vegetation; a few aligned blocks can be glimpsed among the grass. The presence of another tomb on the site is reported, to which a pile of blocks glimpsed among the vegetation may belong.
descriptions.NUR8567: The giants' tomb lies next to a river and is largely destroyed. A stretch of the open corridor is visible. The area is interesting because it is rich in springs. Several nuraghi lie near the giants' tomb. It stands at the foot of Bruncu Salamu, where there are several springs, sacred wells and the Nuraghe Sa Dom'e S'Orcu.
descriptions.NUR21173: Three metres of corridor, the headrest to the west, a row of outer blocks, particularly curious is a block with a large cupmark. There would be another stretch of corridor but it is not accessible, let alone documentable, because of trees.
descriptions.NUR6897: The walls are built of rubble of various and medium sizes, roughly dressed, with a cyclopean stone set upright in the ground closing one end. The coverings are megalithic; some are still in situ while others have been torn up by land-improvement works.
descriptions.NUR16899: Easy to find and hard to understand, because of its REINFORCED CONCRETE roof that only the local administrators can fathom, not to mention its pitiful state of abandonment. Apparently the giants' tomb was used as a powder magazine during the construction of the SS131, which is why it was fitted with a reinforced concrete roof and an iron door that is no longer there.
descriptions.NUR14174: The great burial at Zanchia shows the lower part of the bilitic stele still intact, while the upper part lies reclined upon the other stones of the tomb corridor.
descriptions.NUR12959: It was a large stone cist dug into the ground, oval in shape, with its walls lined with stone slabs; inside were the remains of 15 inhumations and various grave goods typical of the Early Bronze Age (Bonnanaro Culture).
descriptions.NUR8925:
Giants' tomb dating to the Middle Bronze Age. Located in the immediate vicinity of the Sa Sinèpida equipped area.

With a possibly Bilitic stele of the giants' dolmenic tomb, partially buried
descriptions.NUR11752: A collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument is built in isodomic masonry with well-squared and finished basalt elements, found both in their original position and incorporated into the surrounding dry-stone enclosure walls. The corridor with the terminal head slab, the exedra with the central slab in which the entrance doorway is cut, and the dentilled stele are visible.
descriptions.NUR11753: A collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument stands next to the tomb of Battos I and repeats both its type and the fine workmanship of its well-squared and finished basalt ashlars, but it is not as well preserved. Among the fallen ashlars the corridor and the exedra can still be made out, while in the apsidal area there are two monolithic arches. The dentilled ashlar is visible on the ground.
descriptions.NUR11754: A collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument, of large dimensions, is barely legible in plan because it is almost entirely buried. Of the orthostatic structure, parts of the outer wall face and the exedra are visible, as well as fragments of the large arched stele lying on the monument.
descriptions.NUR18895: Less than 100 metres south of the nuraghe lies a small giants' tomb, of which only the funerary chamber remains, composed of large granite orthostats, together with traces of the external wall face and the peristalith.
descriptions.NUR18897:
The second giants' tomb, situated 100 m south-west of the nuraghe, instead has a narrow corridor 6.5 metres long inside, without a roof, the peristalith visible only in part, and to the left of the entrance an orthostat about 1 m high and traces of the exedra.

About 500 m west of the nuraghe there is an area where stretches of walling and surface material emerge, probably of Roman date.
descriptions.NUR12205:
A burial of the Nuragic period.

Of the monument, practically destroyed, the funerary corridor can be seen, formed by two parallel alignments of ashlars emerging from the ground. Other ashlars are detectable in the immediate vicinity.

The tomb's construction technique was of the isodomic type, carried out with finely shaped ashlars.
descriptions.NUR11755: The giants' tomb of Brebeghenieddu lies about 400 m north of the nuraghe Columbos at Sedido. The lower part of the stele has been reused as the wall of a small house that is now ruined and roofless. Behind the stele part of the burial corridor can also be seen.
descriptions.NUR18743: Of the monument, currently destroyed, only some worked ashlar stones remain, indicating that the tomb type was coursed in isodomic masonry.
descriptions.NUR18735: Of the monument, currently destroyed, only some worked ashlar stones remain, indicating that the tomb type was coursed in isodomic masonry.
descriptions.NUR11318: Structures belonging to a giants' tomb built of local basalt. The funerary structure stands on a small rise overlooking a small river valley, between the nuraghi Campu Scudu and Piricu (Santu Lussurgiu). Some blocks of the funerary corridor and part of the outer wall face remain visible. The tomb is oriented east–west and survives for a total length of about 8 m. In the front part a few displaced blocks can be seen that originally must have formed part of the exedra.
descriptions.NUR17910:
A burial of the Nuragic period built in courses of polygonal limestone blocks.

Although partly covered by vegetation and fill, the ground plan with its apse and exedra, whose arms run in straight lines, is clearly legible. On the façade, in front of the entrance doorway, a rectangular slab lies on the ground and may be the lintel of the entrance.
descriptions.NUR15645: Giants' tomb, cut-down, belonging to the same named nuraghe and village
descriptions.NUR12190:
A burial of the Nuragic period. The monument is fairly well preserved, though partly hidden by vegetation; its outer profile, the funerary corridor and the right wing of the exedra can be seen.

The construction technique is regular coursed masonry using sub-squared polygonal blocks.
descriptions.NUR6761: Very little of the tomb remains. The baetyls are five and are located in the territory of the comune of Dualchi (NU).
descriptions.NUR10005: The monument stands on the Planu Is Ciaexius plateau, in the Sarcidano, a region of south-central Sardinia. The megalithic tomb of Aiodda, which follows the classic giants' tomb layout, was discovered during agricultural work. The entrance, facing east, is preceded by a large semicircular exedra of limestone orthostatic slabs, about 6 m wide.
descriptions.NUR12410: "Giants' tomb of Araene, of the long cell the dense stones of the sides and large slabs of the roof are seen. In the land of Carta Luca, it was Luigi." From Taramelli's description, the tomb of Araene must certainly have been the best preserved among those in the territory of Lodè; unfortunately the monument was destroyed in relatively recent times, as a result of the usual land-reclamation works, which spared practically nothing.
descriptions.NUR11082: Giants' tomb in very poor condition; the chamber can still be read clearly, while the exedra is partly incorporated into the enclosure wall. It lies inside a fenced plot a short distance from the country church of Santa Cristina. Easily reached.
descriptions.NUR14688: Situated a short distance from the Durane stream, the tomb has a burial chamber about 9 metres long and a broad exedra on the front, 14 metres long. It is built entirely of granite with ashlars laid in regular courses. The central part has the entrance doorway surmounted by the so-called “dentilled ashlar”. The large exedra, provided with bench-seats for pilgrims to rest on, contains a small baetyl to the east, which must have been an object of worship.
descriptions.NUR18889: About 150 metres from the Bigozzi nuraghe, to the north-west, lies the giants' tomb of the same name. Built on a small platform made of small stones, the burial retains the tomb corridor of orthostatic granite slabs; the roof is missing and the apsidal slab lies on the ground, while only a short stretch of the exedra is visible outside.
descriptions.NUR16990:
A collective burial of the Nuragic period.

Of the monument, hidden beneath a mass of mastic trees, only the apsidal area and the terminal section of the corridor remain visible.
descriptions.NUR11526: It is located in the area of Capichera (Arzachena – OT), near a winery producing the fine Vermentino wine. In the immediate vicinity lies the complex nuraghe of La Prisgiona.
descriptions.NUR10721:
It lies in the municipality of Goni (CA).

Although the signage highlights the presence of a giants' tomb, the construction type (the monument has two opposing apses) finds few parallels in a funerary context.

It may be a cult enclosure.
descriptions.NUR17768: Only some stones remain of the tomb.
descriptions.NUR11958: Funerary structure of the Nuragic period. The monument is fairly well preserved and still reveals its various components: corridor, apse, and exedra.
descriptions.NUR18900: 100 metres to the south-east of the nuraghe, traces of a giants' tomb are present: some slabs emerge from the ground belonging to the burial corridor.
descriptions.NUR19078: The monument is quite imposing: it measures 22 m overall; the exedra has a chord length of 18 m and almost all the boulders remain, set on edge, some of them very tall. The burial corridor is 16 m long, 1.30 m high and 1.40 m wide; it is roofed with horizontal slabs, one of which is missing, allowing a view of the interior, whose cross-section is rectangular.
descriptions.NUR11741: The burial lies on the south-western edge of a plateau used for crops and pasture. It is about 1.50 metres north-west of the nuraghe of the same name and a few hundred metres south-east of the open-air site of Ruinacchèsos. The monument has its entrance facing north-west, with some blocks of the exedra nearby. The burial chamber is about 3.55 metres long and rectangular in plan.
descriptions.NUR19341:
1. Of the monument, unusually close to the reference nuraghe, only a stretch of the burial corridor just emerges from the ground of the site.

2. Of the monument, currently destroyed, only a few worked ashlars are visible, indicating that the tomb was of the coursed type in isodomic masonry.
descriptions.NUR12632: The tomb, situated beside a lane and built of courses of large blocks, has its exedra facing south and a partially damaged gallery. Scattered blocks and large heaps of clearance stones can be seen nearby.
descriptions.NUR11439: Described by Lamarmora and Mackenzie, who saw it almost intact, at least in its ground plan, and defined by Pinza as “the elevation of the finest giants’ tomb known in Sardinia”, the giants’ tomb of Imbertighe is now reduced to the arched stele and the wings of the exedra, which consist of three courses of stones.
descriptions.NUR10800: Giants' tomb completely collapsed, with the most significant elements missing. It retains the burial corridor.
descriptions.NUR11488:
The tomb was built in several phases. The first dates to the Early Bronze Age, when the Bonnanaro culture was widespread in Sardinia (about 1800 BC). At that time the tomb must have looked like a cist dolmen covered by a mound.

In the Nuragic period the site was reworked into a giants' tomb by enlarging the burial chamber and adding the exedra, composed of 14 slabs among which the central stele, with its entrance, stands out at almost 4 metres high.
descriptions.NUR11537:
The tomb is built with coursed masonry. The tomb body contains a rectangular funerary corridor, closed at the far end by a single shaped head slab with an arched top.

The exedra survives only in part: the hemicycle is bounded by orthostatic slabs of reduced size, at the base of which runs a low bench-seat, also incomplete, intended to receive offerings.

The rear wall face of the exedra joins the tomb body without a break.
descriptions.NUR18515: Situated off-centre in relation to the Madau funerary complex, and despite its small size, the few visible structures suggest that it retains the characteristics (and therefore perhaps also the construction period) of its "larger sisters". Of the tomb, now half-buried by sediment, the exedra and part of the corridor are visible.
descriptions.NUR11618: Giants' tomb completely collapsed, with only faint traces remaining
descriptions.NUR10619: The tomb is in excellent condition, both inside and out. The façade, built of well-squared medium-sized blocks laid with care, has a low rectangular entrance doorway at the centre (about 50 cm wide and 60 cm high). The burial chamber reaches a height of about 1.80 m at its highest point; the apse that closes the rear of the chamber is also very well preserved.
descriptions.NUR16356: Currently it has been largely buried prior to carrying out interventions for its preservation.
descriptions.NUR10632:
The site where Sa Murta 'e Pizzus stands, at 520 metres above sea level, is beautiful and evocative, set in the greenery and silence of an area little touched by man. Numerous grey-pink granite rocks sculpted by time are present, and the Gulf of the Angels can be seen from the hill.

Near this funerary complex there are some stones marking the circular perimeter of several Nuragic huts,
descriptions.NUR10458:
The distinctive features:

the complete absence, at the entrance of the tombs, of the exedra; the resemblance to an upturned ship's keel that can be seen or compared with funerary monuments called "navetas", typical of the Talayotic civilisation of Minorca and the Balearic Islands.

These large structures are built of limestone slabs laid in courses that corbel progressively further inwards towards the top, and the roof was formed by a series of slabs serving as lintels.
descriptions.NUR10459:
The distinctive features:

the complete absence, at the entrance of the tombs, of the exedra; the resemblance to an upturned ship's keel that can be seen or compared with funerary monuments called "navetas", typical of the Talayotic civilisation of Minorca and the Balearic Islands.

These large structures are built of limestone slabs laid in courses that corbel progressively further inwards towards the top, and the roof was formed by a series of slabs serving as lintels.
